# Architecture

Status: **authoritative**, v1.2, 2026-10-05. This document supersedes the four design proposals it was synthesized from. v1.1 resolves the principal-engineer review of v1.0; Appendix D indexes each finding and where it is resolved. v1.2 incorporates the accepted M0 deviations of `Docs/Decisions/0002-m0-deviations.md` (Appendix D, last paragraph). Where this document and `Docs/CodeStyle.md` overlap, CodeStyle governs formatting and naming; this document settles every topic CodeStyle marks **[Architecture]** (see Appendix A).

The display name "Yggdrasil" appears only in the premake workspace name, the `ENGINE_PRODUCT_NAME` define (editor window titles, and the user-data folder of the Editor and Tests) and documentation. Exported games use their manifest `Name` instead (§14.1). Code says `Engine`.

**Provenance.** Structure and scope discipline come from the simplicity proposal (highest mean judge score). The correctness core comes from the robustness proposal: UI-free `EditorCore`, canonical iteration order, sorted physics events, seeded runtime UUIDs, per-step input latching, serializer-based Play copy, and test infrastructure. The automation layer comes from the AI-control proposal. Renderer verification and quality details come from the rendering proposal. Every flaw and uncovered requirement the judges raised is resolved in the text; Appendix B indexes where.

---

## 1. Goals, non-goals, guiding principles

### 1.1 Goals
- **G1 Spec features.** glTF PBR meshes with materials and textures, gizmo placement, IBL from Poly Haven HDRIs, soft shadows, GTAO, HDR with tonemapping, Jolt physics authored as components and driven by scripts, miniaudio, Luau scripting with entity creation, destruction and prefab spawning, an editor, and export to a standalone runtime.
- **G2 Rock-solid.** Every subsystem is unit-testable without a window, GPU or audio device. Bugs assert, expected failures are values, nothing fails silently.
- **G3 Deterministic.** The same source built with the same toolchain on the same platform, given the same inputs and seed, produces the same state hash. This holds whatever the frame rate, the Jolt thread count and the build configuration (Debug, Release, Dist). Recorded replays and expected hashes are therefore valid in every configuration (§9.1, §15.8).
- **G4 Full AI control.** An agent builds, tests and exports a game through the editor automation API alone. The proof is Tetris and Rolling Ball 3D, built by an agent through automation with a committed transcript and a file-provenance audit, and it is complete: Tetris (M17, rebuilt in place as pixel art in M25, `Docs/Decisions/0036-m25-tetris-pixel-art.md`) and Rolling Ball 3D (M27, `Docs/Decisions/0038-m27-rolling-ball.md`), each built by builder agents through the MCP tools alone, each with its committed `Automation/BuildLog.jsonl` and `Automation/Provenance.json` and a provenance audit that passes from a fresh clone (§13.11, §13.12).
- **G5 Verifiable completeness.** The FeatureTest project mechanically proves that every component, component field, enum value, project setting, asset format, script function, method, property, callback and automation method is exercised, in the editor and in exported Release and Dist builds. A gap fails CI.
- **G6 Honest platform status.** Windows x64 is built and tested on every change. Linux and macOS are compile-targeted and generation-checked locally. Windows is the only verified platform. First-party code stays portable by rule (the `Platform/` layering, no Windows-only shortcuts, the local portability stage's premake generation and clang-cl builds), but Linux and macOS are never verified: the Linux/macOS catch-up was dropped by the product owner, because there is no Linux or macOS machine without GitHub. (`Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decision 10.)

### 1.2 Non-goals (v1)
Each can be revisited through an ADR in `Docs/Decisions/`. The backlog program (`Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md`) schedules some of them, each marked with its milestone below, and confirms others as won't do; until its milestone lands, a scheduled item is still a non-goal.
- Graphics backends other than NVRHI-Vulkan. Ray tracing, bindless rendering, GPU-driven rendering, render-graph aliasing. (Won't do, ADR 0028.)
- GI beyond IBL plus AO and baked probes (dynamic GI won't do, ADR 0028). (Clustered light culling and point-light shadows, scheduled for M23, are built since its W23.1, §8.3 and §8.7. Histogram auto-exposure, colour-grading LUTs, and baked irradiance and reflection probes, scheduled for M26, are built since its W26.1, §8.3, §8.6 and §8.9; TAA and SSR since its W26.2, §8.3; ADR 0037.)
- (Mesh instancing, the block compression of imported textures through CMP_Core, which ADR 0028 approved, and Ogg Opus import, scheduled for M23, are built since its W23.1, §8.3 and §7.4; EXR import and BC6H environment cubes since its W23.2, §7.4 and §8.6.)
- (Skeletal and morph animation, scheduled for M23, are built since its W23.3: glTF skins, joints, morph targets and animations import as Skeletons, AnimationClips and the mesh's skin and morph sections (§6.8, §7.1, §7.4), the Animator and SkinnedMesh components (§5.3) are stepped by the AnimationSystem phase with script-driven layer blending, root motion and animation events (§5.7, §11.3, §11.5), the Skinning pass deforms on the GPU (§8.3), and the editor previews a pose (§12.2, §13.5; ADR 0034 decisions 22 to 33).)
- (Particles and terrain, scheduled for M26, are built: the ParticleEmitter, its presentation-only Particles phase and pass, and the Heightfield asset with the Terrain and TerrainCollider components, its import, physics and queries since its W26.1, §5.3, §5.7, §6.8 and §8.3; the terrain's rendering with its levels of detail and the editor's sculpt and paint tools since its W26.2, §8.3, §12.2 and §13.5; ADR 0037.)
- An animation state-machine graph (animation blending stays script-driven: crossfades are scripts tweening layer weights, ADR 0034 decision 26), native gameplay modules (lifted on Windows by M19, §11.11; a non-goal on Linux and macOS), networking, mobile, consoles, web. Networking, mobile and web stay non-goals; consoles won't do (ADR 0028). (Visual scripting, scheduled for M24, is built since its W24.1 and W24.2: a graph is one behaviour, a `.graph` Script asset transpiled to Luau at import and compiled by the script pipeline, so Dist runs its bytecode with no transpiler (§6.11, §11.12); agents build it through the `graph.*` methods and the editor's Graph Editor canvas submits the same ones, with live values in play (§12.2, §13.5, §13.7; `Docs/Decisions/0035-m24-contract.md` decisions 2 to 16).)
- ImGui multi-viewport OS windows on Linux and macOS (Windows has them since M24's W24.1: a panel dragged out of the main window gets a platform window of its own, drawn through `ImGuiRenderer` on a swapchain registered with the recreation protocol, §8.11, `Docs/Decisions/0035-m24-contract.md` decisions 17 to 21; the other platforms keep every panel docked in the main window, "Windows backends only", ADR 0028), native file dialogs on Linux and macOS (Windows has them since M18 through nativefiledialog-extended's `IFileDialog` backend, ADR 0029 decisions 19 to 21; the other platforms show the editor's ImGui picker, "Windows backends only", ADR 0028), a UI framework beyond `TextComponent` (lifted by M22: canvases, element rectangles, images, text, layout containers and string tables laid out and drawn in scene pixels, ADR 0033 decisions 2 to 11; the interactive UI, with focus and navigation, events, the five widgets, the theme, minimal authoring and the interaction state in the hash, decisions 21 to 36; the text input, fallback fonts with shaping and bidirectional text, and World canvases, decisions 42 to 53; §5.3, §5.7, §8.3 and §11.5; `Docs/Decisions/0033-m22-contract.md`).
- Native Wayland (Linux runs X11, including XWayland sessions), cross-OS export (each host exports for itself), bit-exact cross-OS or cross-compiler determinism. Jolt itself is built cross-platform deterministic (§9.1), but the CRT `pow` behind Luau's general `^` operator is not guaranteed to match across C runtimes. These stay non-goals (ADR 0028).
- Identity code signing and notarization (macOS bundles are only ad-hoc signed, §14.2). Won't do (ADR 0028).

### 1.3 Guiding principles
1. **Pure core, thin effectful shell.** Step scheduling, device scoring, cascade math, light packing, undo, pak layout, input latching and coverage evaluation are pure functions with table-driven tests. Device wrappers stay thin.
2. **One source of truth per concept.** The type registry drives the inspector, serialization, Luau proxies, automation schemas, validation, docs and coverage. The script API registry drives bindings, `Engine.d.luau`, docs and counters. The method registry drives dispatch, the MCP catalogue and coverage. Generated files are committed and staleness-checked by CI.
3. **One path per job.** One mutation path (Commands), one load path (cooked bytes through the same loader in editor and runtime), one scene-copy path (the serializer), one render path (headless equals windowed).
4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed step, seeded RNG and runtime UUIDs, canonical iteration order wherever the order is observable, sorted physics events, simulation time only, precise floating point everywhere, and deterministic transcendental functions on the simulation path (§4.12).
5. **Errors are values at boundaries.** Programmer errors assert. Expected failures return `Result<T>`. Script faults are isolated. Fatal environment failures exit with a documented code.
6. **Parity.** Anything a human can do in the editor, an agent can do through automation on the same code path. No editor feature lands without its automation method and test.
7. **Bounded and located.** Every automation response is size-bounded. Every error carries a code, a location and, where possible, a hint.
8. **Pays for itself.** A new abstraction needs a written justification in its PR. The non-goals list is a scope guard.

## 2. Repository layout and build system

### 2.1 Layout
```
D:/Engine
├─ premake5.lua  Dependencies.lua  AGENTS.md  CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md)  .mcp.json (generated by Setup.py, gitignored)
├─ GameEngineDoc.md                        (the original specification)
├─ .clang-format  .clang-tidy  .editorconfig  .gitattributes  .gitignore
├─ .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, <page>.md (§13.10: a skill and its reference pages)
├─ .github/workflows/ci.yml                (runs Scripts/CI.py only when started by hand, workflow_dispatch, from the program's setup commit; GitHub is an off-site backup only, ADR 0028 decision 10)
├─ Engine/    premake5.lua
│             Config/entt/ext/config.h      (routes ENTT_ASSERT to ENGINE_CORE_ASSERT)
│             Source/EnginePCH.h|.cpp  Source/Engine/<Module>/...  (include root: Engine/Source)
├─ Editor/    premake5.lua (projects EditorCore = StaticLib, Editor = ConsoleApp)
│             Source/EditorPCH.h  Source/EditorCore/...  Source/Editor/...  (include root: Editor/Source)
├─ Runtime/   premake5.lua (projects RuntimeCore = StaticLib, Runtime = ConsoleApp)
│             Source/Runtime/{RuntimeMain.cpp, RuntimeApp.h|.cpp, NoNativeModule.cpp}
├─ Tests/     premake5.lua  Source/TestsPCH.h  Source/TestMain.cpp  Source/Support/
│             Source/Engine/<Module>/*Tests.cpp  Source/EditorCore/*Tests.cpp
│             Source/{Editor,Runtime}/*Tests.cpp (the executables' code)  Source/Golden/*Tests.cpp (§15.4)
│             Source/ThirdParty/*Tests.cpp  (configuration of vendored libraries, e.g. Jolt's version ID)
│             Data/ (fixtures + LICENSES.md)  Golden/<DeviceClass>/*.png
│             Automation/test_*.py  Projects/Breakout/ (dry-run project, M16, §18)
│             Projects/NativeTest/ (native test game, M19, ADR 0030 decision 35)
├─ Resources/ Shaders/{Shared/*.h, Common/*.slang, Passes/*.slang (the IBL passes included), Shaders.json}
│             Scripting/Engine.d.luau (generated)  Templates/{Projects,Scripts}/  Audio/*.sfx (§10.3)
│             Environments/*.hdr (2 x CC0 Poly Haven, 1k)  Fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf (SIL OFL)
│             EngineAssets.json  LICENSES.md  Licenses/ (license texts LICENSES.md references)
│             (editor icons and blue noise are generated in code, §8.4, §12.2)
├─ Vendor/<Lib>/ (as vendored; premake5.lua + VENDOR.md each)   Vendor/premake/bin/premake5.exe
├─ Scripts/   *.py entry points  Lib/ (shared helpers)  Premake/{CompileCommands,XcodeHeaderSearchPaths,NativeModule}.lua
│             ModuleRules.json
├─ Tools/     MCP/{run.py, engine_mcp/, catalog.json (generated), requirements.lock, tests/}
│             Automation/engine_client.py (stdlib JSON-RPC client shared by MCP and tests)
├─ Projects/  FeatureTest/  Tetris/ (M17; rebuilt in M25)  RollingBall/ (M27)
└─ Docs/      Architecture.md  Roadmap.md  CodeStyle.md  ReviewChecklist.md  Backlog.md  Decisions/
              Reference/ (generated: Components, ScriptAPI, Automation, Validation, FileFormats, BuiltinAssets,
                          Methods.json, Schemas/)
```
A game project is `Projects/<Name>/<Name>.eproj`, `Assets/**` (each asset with a `.meta` sidecar), `AGENTS.md` (game notes), `Automation/` (committed: `BuildLog.jsonl`, the MCP transcript, and `Provenance.json`, §13.12), optionally `Native/` (the game's native module: only `.cpp` and `.h` sources, Windows only; ADR 0030 decisions 26 and 30) and `Library/` (cache, autosave, `Editor.lock`, offloaded automation results, the native module's builds in `Library/Native/Builds/`; gitignored).

### 2.2 Premake
Windows uses x64 host tools as well as an x64 target: the workspace sets `preferredtoolarchitecture "x86_64"`. `CheckBuildConfig.py` checks the generated project setting, with a seeded regression fixture (ADR 0019 decision 9).
`premake5.lua` declares `workspace "Yggdrasil"`, `configurations { "Debug", "Release", "Dist" }`, `architecture "x86_64"` on Windows and Linux and `"ARM64"` on macOS, and `startproject "Editor"`. The target, the macOS deployment target, the x64 host tools and `NDEBUG` come from `ApplyWorkspaceSettings()` and `OutputDir = "%{cfg.buildcfg}-%{cfg.system}-%{cfg.architecture}"` from `Dependencies.lua`, which the native module's workspace (`Scripts/Premake/NativeModule.lua`, below) shares. Vendor projects are included under `group "Dependencies"`: `Vendor/GLFW`, `Vendor/NVRHI`, `Vendor/imgui`, `Vendor/ImGuizmo`, `Vendor/Luau` (projects `Luau`, `LuauAnalysis`), `Vendor/JoltPhysics`, `Vendor/miniaudio`, `Vendor/MikkTSpace` (ADR 0010 decision 16), `Vendor/nativefiledialog-extended` (project `nfd`: its Windows backend only, defined on every OS so the portability stage's project sets match, ADR 0029 decision 21), `Vendor/spdlog`, `Vendor/CMP_Core` (M23: Compressonator's BC codecs, `Docs/Decisions/0034-m23-contract.md` decision 13), `Vendor/libogg`, `Vendor/libopus` and `Vendor/opusfile` (projects `ogg`, `opus` and `opusfile`, M23: the Ogg Opus reader under miniaudio's libopus decoding backend, ADR 0034 decision 16), `Vendor/tinyexr` (M23: the OpenEXR reader of the environment importer, its implementation unit `tinyexr.cc`, ADR 0034 decision 14). Header-only libraries (glm, EnTT, nlohmann/json, doctest, cgltf, stb) have no project; their implementation TUs live in Engine (`AssetPipeline/ThirdParty/{CgltfImplementation,StbImageResizeImplementation,TrueTypeRasterizer}.cpp`, `Graphics/ThirdParty/StbImageImplementation.cpp` (ADR 0009 decision 11) and `ImGui/ImGuiGlfwImplementation.cpp`, all compiled without the PCH through `enablepch "Off"`, because premake 5.0.0 has no `NoPCH` flag; ADR 0009 decision 15). The exception is stb_vorbis, miniaudio's Ogg Vorbis decoder: it compiles inside the miniaudio project through the local translation unit `Vendor/miniaudio/miniaudio_vorbis.c` (the stb_vorbis declarations, `MINIAUDIO_IMPLEMENTATION` with `miniaudio.h`, then the stb_vorbis implementation; `Vendor/stb` is on that project's include path), which replaces upstream's `miniaudio.c` (ADR 0015 decision 2). The miniaudio project also compiles upstream's unmodified libopus decoding backend, `Vendor/miniaudio/extras/decoders/libopus/miniaudio_libopus.c`, its own translation unit over opusfile, libopus and libogg (ADR 0034 decision 16).

**Workspace-scope rule (ODR).** `filter "configurations:Dist" defines { "NDEBUG" }` is set at workspace scope (`ApplyWorkspaceSettings()`, which only workspace blocks call) and nowhere else. `NDEBUG` changes the layout of vulkan.hpp's dispatcher (`Vendor/NVRHI/VENDOR.md`), so it must be identical for NVRHI and every consumer. The vendored Luau project additionally defines `NDEBUG` for its own TUs in Release; this is allowed because no Luau layout depends on it and no Luau TU includes vulkan.hpp.

**`Dependencies.lua`** defines `IncludeDir`, `OutputDir`, `ApplyWorkspaceSettings()`, `ApplyFirstPartySettings()`, one `Use<Lib>()` function per library and the Runtime executable's `UseRuntimeDependencies()` and `ApplyRuntimeExecutableSettings()` (below). Each function's defines are copied verbatim from that library's `VENDOR.md`:

| Function | Consumer settings (must match the vendored project) |
|---|---|
| `UseNVRHI()` | `VULKAN_HPP_DISPATCH_LOADER_DYNAMIC=1`; Windows `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR`, `NOMINMAX`; no other `VULKAN_HPP_*`; never link `vulkan-1` |
| `UseJoltPhysics()` | exactly the table in `Vendor/JoltPhysics/VENDOR.md`: `JPH_OBJECT_STREAM`, `JPH_OBJECT_LAYER_BITS=16`, **`JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC` in every configuration**, SSE4.1/4.2 on x86_64 (`/arch:SSE4.2` for MSVC, `-msse4.2 -mpopcnt` for GCC, Clang and clang-cl), `JPH_DEBUG_RENDERER JPH_PROFILE_ENABLED JPH_ENABLE_ASSERTS` in Debug and Release, `JPH_FLOATING_POINT_EXCEPTIONS_ENABLED` in MSVC Debug, `JPH_NO_DEBUG` in Release and Dist |
| `UseSpdlog()` | `SPDLOG_COMPILED_LIB`, `SPDLOG_USE_STD_FORMAT`, MSVC `/utf-8 /Zc:__cplusplus` |
| `UseMiniaudio()` | `MA_NO_ENCODING`; macOS `MA_NO_RUNTIME_LINKING` + CoreAudio frameworks; then `UseOpusFile()`, `UseOpus()` and `UseOgg()`, which miniaudio's libopus decoding backend needs |
| `UseOpusFile()`, `UseOpus()`, `UseOgg()` | links only (`opusfile`, `opus`, `ogg`, in that order after `miniaudio`): no first-party code includes their headers and they have no consumer defines (libopus is built `FIXED_POINT` without run-time CPU detection or intrinsics, opusfile `OP_FIXED_POINT`, both their sources' own) (M23, ADR 0034 decision 16) |
| `UseLuau(analysis)` | include dirs only; `links { "LuauAnalysis", "Luau" }` when `analysis`, else `{ "Luau" }` |
| `UseGLFW()` | `GLFW_INCLUDE_NONE`; platform link libraries from `Vendor/GLFW/VENDOR.md` |
| `UseImGui()` | none (unmodified `imconfig.h`); ImGuizmo include `Vendor/ImGuizmo/src` |
| `UseMikkTSpace()` | include directory only; `links { "MikkTSpace" }`; precise floating point like Jolt (below) |
| `UseNativeFileDialog()` | include directory only (Engine, Editor, Tests; `Platform/Windows/NativeFileDialogWindows.cpp` alone includes `nfd.h`); on Windows `links { "nfd", "ole32", "shell32", "uuid", "user32" }` for the Editor and Tests executables; Linux and macOS link nothing; the Runtime never calls it (ADR 0029 decision 21) |
| `UseHarfBuzz()`, `UseSheenBidi()` | include directories only, no defines (HarfBuzz's `HB_NO_GETENV` and `HB_NO_SETLOCALE` are private to its own translation unit); `links { "HarfBuzz" }` and `{ "SheenBidi" }` in every executable (`UseRuntimeDependencies()` too); precise floating point like Jolt (below); Renderer's text measurement and AssetPipeline's font importer use them privately (M22, ADR 0033 decision 41) |
| `UseCMPCore()` | include directory only (`Vendor/CMP_Core/cmp_core/source`; `Asset/TextureCompression.cpp` alone includes `cmp_core.h`); `links { "CMP_Core" }` for every executable, the Runtime's included (its decode fallback); precise floating point like Jolt (below); no defines (the `CMP_` family stays empty) (M23, ADR 0034 decision 13) |
| `UseTinyExr()` | include directory `Vendor/tinyexr` (`AssetPipeline/Importers/EnvironmentImporter.cpp` alone includes `tinyexr.h`) and the library's own configuration `TINYEXR_USE_MINIZ=0`, `TINYEXR_USE_STB_ZLIB=1` (ZIP and PXR24 inflate through stb_image's zlib, Graphics' implementation; no miniz), `TINYEXR_USE_THREAD=0` and `TINYEXR_USE_OPENMP=0`; `links { "tinyexr" }` for the Editor and Tests executables; Engine, EditorCore, Editor and Tests call it, never the Runtime's projects (M23, ADR 0034 decision 14) |
| `UseRecast()`, `UseDetour()` | include directories only (`Vendor/Recast/Include`, `Vendor/Detour/Include`), no defines (the `RC_` and `DT_` families stay empty); `links { "Recast" }` for the Editor and Tests executables (EditorCore's `Navigation/NavMeshBuilder.cpp` alone includes Recast's headers; EditorCore, Editor and Tests call it, never the Runtime's projects, so no exported game links Recast) and `links { "Detour" }` for every executable, `UseRuntimeDependencies()` included (the Navigation module's private files alone include Detour's headers); precise floating point like Jolt (below) (M30, ADR 0045 decision 2) |
| first-party only | `GLM_FORCE_DEPTH_ZERO_TO_ONE`, `GLM_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL`, `GLM_FORCE_CTOR_INIT`, `JSON_USE_IMPLICIT_CONVERSIONS=0`, `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN`, `ENGINE_PLATFORM_{WINDOWS,LINUX,MACOS}` |

All vendor include directories use `externalincludedirs` with `externalwarnings "Off"`. `Scripts/CheckBuildConfig.py` generates the workspace into a temp directory for every generator and toolset the build or CI uses (vs2026 with MSVC and with clang-cl, gmake with GCC and with Clang, xcode4), parses every generated project and computes each compile unit's effective defines in command-line order (undefines and `-D`/`/D` in compiler options count). It fails if, for any target and configuration, an ABI-relevant define differs between a vendor project and a consumer that includes its headers. The families come from each `VENDOR.md`: `JPH_*`; `SPDLOG_*`; `MA_NO_*`, `MINIAUDIO_IMPLEMENTATION`; `VULKAN_HPP_*`, `VK_USE_PLATFORM_*`, `NOMINMAX`, `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`, `NVRHI_SHARED_LIBRARY_*`; Luau's `LUA_USE_LONGJMP`, `LUA_API`, `LUACODE_API`, `LUA_VECTOR_*`; Dear ImGui's and ImGuizmo's `IMGUI_*`, `ImTextureID`, `ImDrawIdx`, `USE_IMGUI_API`, `IMGUIZMO_NAMESPACE`; GLFW's `_GLFW_*`, `GLFW_DLL`; HarfBuzz's `HB_*` and SheenBidi's `SB_CONFIG_*` (M22, ADR 0033 decision 41: both families stay empty in every project, HarfBuzz's `HB_NO_GETENV` and `HB_NO_SETLOCALE` being private to its own translation unit); CMP_Core's `CMP_*` (none is defined, M23); libopus's `OPUS_*` (its own `OPUS_BUILD` excepted), `CUSTOM_MODES`, `ENABLE_OPUS_CUSTOM_API`, `DISABLE_PTR_CHECK` and `DLL_EXPORT`, and opusfile's `OP_*` (its own `OP_FIXED_POINT` excepted), none of which a consumer defines (M23); tinyexr's `TINYEXR_*`, which the library and its consumers define alike (M23); Recast's `RC_*` and Detour's `DT_*`, empty for both libraries and every consumer (M30: `DT_POLYREF64` and `DT_VIRTUAL_QUERYFILTER` change the layout of Detour's polygon references and query filter, ADR 0045 decision 2); and `NDEBUG` for every library. It also fails if `JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC` is missing from JoltPhysics or any consumer; if a Jolt consumer uses other instruction-set options than JoltPhysics (Jolt derives `JPH_USE_AVX2` and the like from the compiler's `__AVX2__` macros, which `JPH_VERSION_ID` does not encode); or if any first-party, Jolt, MikkTSpace, Luau, HarfBuzz, SheenBidi, CMP_Core, tinyexr, Recast or Detour project uses a non-precise floating-point model (`/fp:fast`, `FloatingPointModel=Fast`, `/fp:contract`, `/Qfast_transcendentals`, `-ffast-math` or any of its components, or any effective `-ffp-contract` other than `off`). The same rules apply to the flags each shared vendor-cache entry a build would link recorded (below). At runtime `JPH::VerifyJoltVersionID()` is checked at startup and a mismatch is fatal. The version ID encodes `JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC`, so a consumer built without the define cannot run.

**Floating-point model (determinism, §9.1).** Every first-party project, JoltPhysics, MikkTSpace, the Luau VM project (`Luau`, whose interpreter and `vector`/`math` libraries run scripts' gameplay arithmetic), HarfBuzz and SheenBidi (M22: shaped text reaches the UI's layout and the cooked fonts, ADR 0033 decision 41), CMP_Core (M23: compressed texture blocks are cooked, and must be identical from the Debug and Release editors) tinyexr (M23: an OpenEXR image's decoded texels, its half-float conversion among them, are baked into a cooked environment under the same configuration-independent key), and Recast and Detour (M30: a bake's NavMesh file is byte-identical from the Debug and Release editors, and Detour's path queries run on the simulation path, ADR 0045 decision 2) compile with precise floating point; `Scripts/CheckBuildConfig.py` checks every one of them (`PRECISE_VENDOR_PROJECTS`; each has a fixture in `Tests/Data/BuildConfig` that the check must fail). On MSVC this is `/fp:precise` (premake `floatingpoint "Default"`), which since VS 2022 never generates FMA contractions. GCC and Clang use `-fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off` on every architecture, and clang-cl the same options as `/clang:-fno-fast-math /clang:-ffp-contract=off`. Clang's default model is already precise, so this is precise without contraction; `-ffp-model=precise -ffp-contract=off` is not used, because `-ffp-model=precise` implies `-ffp-contract=on` and Clang reports the override as `-Woverriding-option`, an error under `-Werror` (for the same reason premake's `floatingpoint "Precise"` is not used). `-fno-fast-math` also resets the `-ffast-math` that premake's xcode4 generator adds for `optimize "Full"` (Dist). The vendored Jolt premake file therefore replaces upstream's MSVC `floatingpoint "Fast"` and its ARM64 `-ffp-contract=on`. That is a build-configuration change recorded in `Vendor/JoltPhysics/VENDOR.md`; Jolt's source stays unmodified (Roadmap M0). Jolt documents the cost of cross-platform determinism at roughly 8 %, which is accepted. In exchange, replays and expected hashes are valid in every configuration. The vendored Luau premake file adds the same options to `Luau` (recorded in `Vendor/Luau/VENDOR.md`; M13 review F01); upstream's `-fno-math-errno` stays, since it changes no value. `LuauAnalysis` only type-checks in the editor and keeps the compiler defaults.

**`ApplyFirstPartySettings()`** (Engine, EditorCore, Editor, RuntimeCore, Runtime, Tests, and a game's native module): `language "C++"`, `cppdialect "C++23"`, `staticruntime "off"`, `warnings "Extra"`, `fatalwarnings { "All" }`, `multiprocessorcompile "On"`, exceptions on, RTTI at compiler default (first-party code never uses `dynamic_cast` or `typeid`; lint-enforced). MSVC adds `/utf-8 /permissive- /Zc:__cplusplus /Zc:preprocessor` and the precise FP model above. GCC/Clang add `-Wshadow` and the precise FP flags above. Windows Debug executables link with `/STACK:2097152` (Luau analysis recursion). Each Windows executable embeds `Engine/Source/Engine/Platform/Windows/App.manifest` (PerMonitorV2 DPI, UTF-8 active code page, long paths).

| | Debug | Release | Dist |
|---|---|---|---|
| Defines | `ENGINE_DEBUG` | `ENGINE_RELEASE` | `ENGINE_DIST`, `NDEBUG` (workspace) |
| Optimize / symbols | Off / On | Speed / On | Full + `linktimeoptimization "On"` (xcode4: `LLVM_LTO = YES`, because premake ignores `linktimeoptimization` there) / On (PDB/dSYM archived in `bin/Symbols`, never shipped; a native game's exported Runtime, which the export links itself, in its project's `Library/Native/Symbols/<Config>/`, §14.2 step 3a) |
| Engine asserts, Trace logs | on | on | off |
| Vulkan + NVRHI validation | on by default | `--gpu-validation` (always on in tests) | never |
| Projects built | all | all | Engine, RuntimeCore, Runtime, vendor (`removeconfigurations { "Dist" }` on EditorCore, Editor, Tests) |
| Runtime kind | ConsoleApp | ConsoleApp | WindowedApp (`entrypoint "mainCRTStartup"`) |

PCH: `EnginePCH.h` (Engine), `EditorPCH.h` (compiled separately by EditorCore and Editor), `TestsPCH.h`. RuntimeCore and Runtime use none. Headers never include a PCH.

**Shaders** are compiled by a dedicated `Shaders` project (`kind "Utility"`, group `Engine`) into `bin/<OutputDir>/Shaders/` (§8.12). Its single custom build rule runs `python Scripts/CompileShaders.py --config %{cfg.buildcfg} --output-dir <bin/<OutputDir>/Shaders>` on `Resources/Shaders/Shaders.json` (with the interpreter `Generate.py` passes as `--python` when it does, `python3` on Linux and macOS otherwise). The rule declares `buildinputs` for every `Resources/Shaders/**.slang` and `**.h` file and `buildoutputs` for a stamp file `bin/<OutputDir>/Shaders/.stamp`, so Visual Studio's fast up-to-date check re-runs it when only a shader changes. `Engine` declares `dependson { "Shaders" }`. The ninja generator is the exception: premake 5.0.0's ninja generator supports neither Utility projects nor `dependson` edges to them, so for ninja `Engine/premake5.lua` attaches the same rule to `Engine` itself and every Engine object depends on the stamp. A prebuild step on the Engine static library is not used, because the IDE skips it when no C++ input changed. Dev builds mount `engine://` at `<repo>/Resources` (the `ENGINE_REPO_ROOT` define) and `shaders://` at the repository's `bin/<OutputDir>/Shaders` (the `ENGINE_SHADER_DIRECTORY` define, from the workspace's `ShaderOutputDirectory`, which stays in the repository's `bin` even with `Generate.py --to`); both defines are absent in Dist. The VFS mounts whole schemes, so the SPIR-V gets its own scheme rather than `engine://Shaders` (ADR 0009 decision 4). Exported games read `engine://Shaders` from `Engine.pak`, which contains the target configuration's SPIR-V (§14.2).

**`Scripts/Premake/CompileCommands.lua`** adds a custom action, `premake5 compile-commands`, that writes `compile_commands.json` (clang-style flags derived from the same project settings) for clang-tidy.

**The Runtime and a game's native module** (`Docs/Decisions/0030-m19-contract.md` decision 30). The Runtime is split: the `RuntimeCore` static library holds the application, and the `Runtime` executable adds `RuntimeMain.cpp` and `NoNativeModule.cpp`, whose `GetLinkedNativeModule` answers no module; `ApplyRuntimeExecutableSettings()` and `UseRuntimeDependencies()` (`Dependencies.lua`) hold the executable's settings and its `Use<Lib>()` set. `Scripts/Premake/NativeModule.lua` is the workspace of one build of a game's `Native/` module, which `Scripts/BuildNative.py` (§2.3) generates below the build's output directory, never `Generate.py`: it includes `Dependencies.lua` and compiles the module's sources with `ApplyWorkspaceSettings()`, `ApplyFirstPartySettings()` and `UseRuntimeDependencies()`, so native code gets the first-party settings (precise floating point, warnings as errors) and the instruction set of the code it runs beside. For the editor it builds `NativeModule.dll` (Debug or Release) with `ENGINE_NATIVE_SHARED_LIBRARY` defined and no library linked (`removelinks { "*" }`); for an export it builds `Runtime.exe`, the same executable as the prebuilt Runtime with the module's sources instead of `NoNativeModule.cpp`, linked with the configuration's `RuntimeCore` and `Engine` libraries from `bin/<OutputDir>/` and the vendored libraries the prebuilt Runtime links (from the vendor cache, below). The non-Dist first-party projects define `ENGINE_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE`, the interpreter `Generate.py` passed as `--python` (empty without one), with which the editor runs `BuildNative.py` by its fixed path (§13.2).

**Shared vendor-library cache** (`Scripts/Lib/vendor_cache.py`; `Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decision 16). Every worktree of the repository compiles the vendored static libraries (the projects whose compiled sources all lie under `Vendor/`) from the same pinned sources with the same settings, so MSBuild builds through `Build.py` link them from one cache instead of compiling them in each checkout. The make, ninja and Xcode builds compile them as before.
- **Location.** `<git common directory>/vendor-cache` (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`: `D:/Engine/.git` for the main checkout and every worktree of it). It is shared by exactly the checkouts of the repository, lies outside every working tree (no `bin/` removal or `git clean` touches it) and is never tracked. Deleting it, or an entry, is safe only while no build runs in any checkout (`Scripts/Locks.py` lists no build holder), since a running build links the entries it verified where they are; the next build compiles and publishes what it needs. Entries are never evicted, so the sets of an older toolchain or vendor change stay until then (an accepted limit, `Docs/Backlog.md` §6). Below `v1/`: `entries/<Project>/<Configuration>-<key>/` (one entry: `entry.json`, the library and its compiler PDBs), `staging/` (compiles in progress), `trash/` (rejected entries) and `populate.lock`.
- **Key.** The first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of an entry's inputs as canonical JSON: the project's generated settings for the configuration (every property, tool setting and compiled file with its per-file settings of its `.vcxproj`, so every define, the ABI-relevant ones of `AGENTS.md` among them, the floating-point model and options, the instruction set such as Jolt's `/arch:SSE4.2`, the sanitizer (`EnableASAN`), the runtime library, optimization and debug-information settings and the platform toolset, `v145` or `ClangCL`), the toolchain (Visual Studio, MSVC tools and Windows SDK versions, and the per-user property sheet `Microsoft.Cpp.x64.user.props` every generated project imports), and the source pin of every `Vendor/<Lib>` directory the project compiles from, includes or force-includes (the version and commit of its `VENDOR.md`, and a digest of every file git lists there, `VENDOR.md` and `premake5.lua` included). MSBuild compiles with exactly that toolchain: `Build.py` removes the variables that would select another (`VCToolsVersion`, `VCToolsInstallDir`, `LLVMInstallDir`, `LLVMToolsVersion`) or add compiler options (`CL`, `_CL_`) from its environment. The key is fail-closed: a vendored project whose include, library, `#using` or forced-include paths, or items, name anything outside `Vendor/` or a path built from an MSBuild property (a first-party configuration header in `Engine/Config`, an SDK's `$(VULKAN_SDK)/Include`), whose content the key cannot digest, is never cached and compiles in the workspace. Paths are relative to the repository root and the output and intermediate directories are left out, so every checkout and every workspace location (in place, `--to bin-int/Asan`, `bin-int/Portability`) computes the same key for the same build. The AddressSanitizer workspace's Release and the clang-cl workspace therefore have their own entries; its uninstrumented Debug and Dist share the plain ones.
- **Publishing.** A missing entry is compiled by `Build.py` under `populate.lock` (other builds wait, then link it), in `staging/` with its own `OutDir` and `IntDir` and without its project references; its library and compiler PDBs move into a staging directory with `entry.json` (the inputs, every file's size and SHA-256, the warnings the compile reported), which is then renamed to the entry's name, so a reader sees no entry or a complete one. Entries are immutable. A failed compile publishes nothing and fails the build with its errors.
- **Verification.** Before an entry is linked, its record must parse, have this format, hash to its key and record exactly the current inputs, and every file must have its recorded size and SHA-256. An entry that fails is never linked: it moves to `trash/` and is compiled and published again. A linked entry's recorded warnings count in the build, so a cache hit passes or fails `Build.py`'s warning rules as compiling the library would.
- **Linking in place.** `Build.py` passes MSBuild `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` (the documented hook that imports a `.targets` file after `Microsoft.Cpp.targets` in every C++ project of a build) with the file it writes into the workspace's `bin-int/VendorCache/`: a cached vendor project builds nothing, every project drops its `ProjectReference` to it, and every linking project lists the cache's library in `Link.AdditionalDependencies`. Build output is never copied between checkouts (MSBuild's `.tlog` files hold absolute paths): consumers link the cache's files where they are, and the linker finds each library's compiler PDB beside it. Debug information and `__FILE__` strings of a cached library name the vendored sources of the checkout that compiled the entry (identical files, by the key). The generated workspace is unchanged, so its project sets stay those of the other generators (the portability stage's check), and a build in the IDE or with `Build.py --no-vendor-cache` compiles the vendored libraries in the workspace.
- **Check.** `CheckBuildConfig.py` (rule 9) finds the entry each Visual Studio target would link for every vendored project and configuration and fails when its record is broken, records other settings than the generated project, or records flags that break the ABI-define, determinism-define, instruction-set, floating-point or sanitizer rules against the workspace's consumers. Entries under other keys (another branch's vendor set, an older toolchain) are never linked and not checked, nor is a project the key cannot digest.

### 2.3 Python scripts (Python 3.10+, stdlib only; `Tools/MCP` uses a venv created by Setup.py)
Every script has `--help`, `--json` output and a non-zero exit code on failure. Every script also works from any directory. A relative path given on its command line is resolved against the caller's directory (`Export.py --out Exports/Game` started in `C:/Games` writes `C:/Games/Exports/Game`): `main()` parses its arguments first, a path through `Scripts/Lib/paths.py`'s `argument_path` type and a tool given as a path or as a name on `PATH` through `tool_argument`, and only then makes the repository root of its own checkout the working directory (`enter_repository_root`; `Scripts/Lib/unittest_runner.py` does the same). `Format.py`'s and `Lint.py`'s `--paths` are the exception: they stay relative to the repository root (to `--root` for `Lint.py`). A relative path a tool prints is resolved against the directory the tool ran in, never against the script's working directory (premake's `Generated <path>` lines are below the repository root it runs in: `premake.generated_paths`). So a script started from another checkout, such as a gate run as `python <worktree>/Scripts/CI.py`, reads or names that checkout's files only where a path on its command line names them. A run a script stops at its timeout or on Ctrl+C ends with its descendants (`Scripts/Lib/process.py`'s `terminate_tree`): on Windows the processes whose recorded parent id is the run's process or one of its descendants and that were created no earlier than that parent, each opened before it is ended, with snapshots taken again until one finds no new descendant; never `taskkill /T`, which follows the recorded ids alone, so that a process of another checkout that is older than the holder of its parent's id (Windows never updates a recorded parent id and gives ids out again) is never ended (R-GPUCRASH's evidence, `Docs/Backlog.md` §3). Elsewhere the run's process leads a process group of its own, which is ended.

| Script | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Setup.py` | Check Python, Git, `VULKAN_SDK` (≥ 1.4.350, `slangc`, `spirv-val`), MSVC via vswhere, Linux packages (`xorg-dev`). Download the pinned premake 5.0.0 into `Vendor/premake/bin/` (SHA-256 verified; the directory is gitignored) when absent. Create `Tools/MCP/.venv` from the hash-locked `requirements.lock`, then write `.mcp.json` with the venv interpreter's absolute path (§13.8), so no `python` on `PATH` is assumed. |
| `Generate.py [--action] [--toolset] [--to <dir>] [--sanitize address]` | `premake5 vs2026` (Windows), `gmake`/`ninja` (Linux), `xcode4` (macOS); then `compile-commands`. `--sanitize address` generates the hardening stage's AddressSanitizer workspace (Release of every project instrumented, workspace scope; used with `--to bin-int/Asan`, ADR 0024 decision 12). |
| `Build.py --config C [--project P] [--workspace-dir D] [--jobs N] [--no-vendor-cache] [--vendor-cache-dir D] [--lock-timeout S \| --no-wait]` | MSBuild via vswhere, or make/ninja/xcodebuild, under the machine-wide build lock (below): `--jobs N` with N at most half the logical CPUs is a capped build (one of the lock's two slots, at most N compilers for the whole build: MSBuild runs up to `-m` projects at once, each with `/MP` at `CL_MPCount`, the per-project compiler count that `Microsoft.Cl.Common.props` makes every project's `/MP` count, so a capped build gets `-m:2` and `-p:CL_MPCount=N/2`, `-m:1` below 4 jobs), more is uncapped (both slots, `/MP` at the logical CPU count), and without `--jobs` the build is uncapped on a free lock and capped with half the CPUs beside one capped build. MSBuild builds link the vendored static libraries from the shared vendor cache (§2.2; ADR 0028 decision 16): each entry is verified before it is linked, and a missing or rejected one is compiled once, published atomically and linked; `--no-vendor-cache` compiles them in the workspace and `--vendor-cache-dir` names another cache; the cache's compiles of missing entries run inside the build, under its build-lock slot and compiler cap. After building Runtime on Windows, copies the app-local CRT (`vcruntime140.dll`, `vcruntime140_1.dll`, `msvcp140.dll` from `VC/Redist/MSVC/<newest>/x64/Microsoft.VC145.CRT`) into `bin/<OutputDir>/Runtime/Redist/`. From M15 (ADR 0024 decisions 2, 5 and 8), after building Runtime on every OS it writes `bin/<OutputDir>/Runtime/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` from the `## Notices` sections of `Vendor/*/VENDOR.md` and `Resources/LICENSES.md`; on macOS it stages the SDK's `libvulkan.1.dylib`, `libMoltenVK.dylib` and `MoltenVK_icd.json` in `Runtime/Frameworks/` and `Runtime/Vulkan/icd.d/`; after a Dist build it archives the Runtime's symbols and map in `bin/Symbols/<OutputDir>/Runtime/`. Before each configuration's build it writes the build stamp (ADR 0030 decision 13): the commit and a dirty flag from git (`rev-parse`, `status` and `ls-files`; dirty means a tracked file that differs from the commit, staged or not, or a file git neither tracks nor ignores below `Engine/`, `Editor/`, `Runtime/` or `Resources/`, which premake compiles or the build copies) into `bin-int/<OutputDir>/Engine/BuildStamp.h`, rewritten only when its content changes, so a commit recompiles `Core/BuildId.cpp` alone (the first stamp of a configuration also removes its `BuildId` objects, built without one); `--json` reports it as each step's `buildStamp`. It takes the source stamps as the build begins, once it holds the build lock, and as it ends, however it ends: `<workspace>/bin-int/SourceStamps.json` records the size, modification time and SHA-256 of every input (every C and C++ file below `Engine/Source`, `Engine/Config`, `Editor/Source`, `Runtime/Source`, `Tests/Source` and `Resources/Shaders`, and every input of the shader rule: `Shaders.json` and each `.slang` file below `Resources/Shaders`), when the latest build began and when the builds last ended with none running. Because the builds compile only what is newer than its objects, an input put back with an older time (a kept copy restored by `mv`, `cp -p`, `shutil.copy2` or an archive, as the proof that a regression test fails without its fix does) would otherwise never compile again while the build reports its projects built: as a build begins, an input whose content differs from the record while its time is not newer than the last end (than now while another build of the workspace runs, or after one was killed) gets the current time, and as it ends, so does every input whose content changed while it ran (it may have compiled the input before the change). The record is written through a temporary file of the build's own under a short lock (`SourceStamps.lock`), and a running build keeps a locked mark in `SourceStamps.running/`, so two builds of one workspace take turns. Only a changed size or time is hashed; an input that stays unreadable (an editor saving it through a rename) or cannot be touched is a warning naming it, and the stamps never fail a build. `--json` lists what they did (`sourceStamps`). Not covered: an input put back during a build, after it compiled, to exactly its content at that build's start and with a time no newer than its objects (Backlog §6). After an MSBuild build that succeeded it compares every linked output it built with the first-party static libraries the output links (its project references outside `Vendor/`): an output older than one is a link MSBuild skipped although the library changed, so Build.py removes it and builds again (a full link) and the step ends as a warning naming it, or fails when the output cannot be removed, the build fails or the output stays older (`staleLinks` in `--json`). |
| `BuildNative.py --project P --kind module\|runtime --config C --out D [--json] [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--lock-timeout S \| --no-wait]` | Windows only (exit code 3 elsewhere, naming the platform; ADR 0028 decision 10). Builds a game's native module (`Docs/Decisions/0030-m19-contract.md` decisions 30 and 35), the `.cpp` and `.h` files below `P/Native/`: first `Lint.py`'s native-module rules (`lint_native_module`, over every file below `Native/` but the `*.bak` backups the editor's writes keep; each finding a `NATIVE_LINT_ERROR`), then the format check that `Format.py --check` makes (with the clang-format 22 it finds and the repository's `.clang-format` named explicitly, since a project outside the repository has none above it, each source that is not clang-format clean is a `NATIVE_FORMAT_WARNING` at its first differing line, quoting the line clang-format writes there or naming its CRLF ending (the repository's style writes LF), as is a missing or failing clang-format; these warnings fail nothing), then, in a capped slot of the machine-wide build lock (below), MSBuild on the workspace `Scripts/Premake/NativeModule.lua` generates below `D` (§2.2): `module` the editor's `NativeModule.dll` (Debug or Release), `runtime` the game's `Runtime.exe` of `C` with the module linked in, which needs `Build.py --config C --project Runtime` first. A compiler or linker warning fails the build; an MSBuild warning about the build itself (MSB8029 below `%TEMP%`) is recorded as a warning. After the compile the sources are hashed again, and a build whose sources changed while it ran (MSBuild read them after the lint) fails with a `NATIVE_BUILD_ERROR`. Writes `D/NativeBuild.json` (kind, configuration, source hash, sources, success, the output's and log's file names, diagnostics; `--json` prints it, `Scripts/Lib/native_build.py` reads and writes it; the source hash is empty only in the record of a build that failed before it could hash the sources) and `D/Build.log` for every outcome once the arguments are valid; `D` must be missing or empty. Exit codes: 0 built, 1 a lint, compile or link failure, 2 usage, 3 no `Native/` or no source, not Windows, the toolchain or the build outputs it links missing, or `--no-wait` refused, 5 timeout. The editor runs it by fixed paths with fixed arguments (`native.build`, `project.export`'s NativeBuild step; §13.2), always with `--timeout 3600 --lock-timeout 1800`, so its build ends within the 4200 s its callers' declared timeouts count (`NativeBuildBoundSeconds`, ADR 0030 decision 30). |
| `CompileShaders.py [--program P] [--force]` | The only place slangc flags are defined (§8.12). |
| `Test.py --suite unit,gpu,golden,feature,automation,export,determinism,games [--config C] [--require-gpu] [--vulkan-api 1.3\|1.4] [--update-golden] [--junit] [--allow-skips] [--editor-report F] [--build-root D] [--sanitizer address] [--debug-heap] [--test-timeout-scale S] [--fuzz-scale S] [--exclude-test-suites S] [--parallel N] [--lock-timeout S \| --no-wait]`; `Test.py --merge-coverage <Editor.json> <Release.json> <Dist.json>` | Runs the suites (§15) in the configurations given by the §15.8 matrix. A run that includes a GPU-using suite (gpu, golden, feature, automation, export, determinism, games) holds the machine-wide GPU lock from its first suite to its end; any other run only waits until no gate runs (below); `--merge-coverage` takes no lock. With the default `--suite all`, a suite that does not take a requested configuration is reported as not run in it; naming that suite together with that configuration is a usage error. The gpu suite runs once per Vulkan API cap (1.4, then capped with `--vulkan-api=1.3`; `--vulkan-api` restricts it to one). JUnit XML into `bin/TestResults/<Suite>-<Config>[-Vulkan13\|-Vulkan14][-Asan][-DebugHeap].xml`. Each Tests process gets `--user-data-dir=bin/TestResults/<report stem>/UserData` (the JUnit file's stem; `Scripts/Lib/paths.py`'s `tests_run_user_data`), so its `Tests.log` and crash reports stay in the checkout and never reach the user's real user-data folder. That folder is never emptied: every run of the suite and configuration in the checkout shares it, and two may overlap (a unit run takes no machine lock), so a run names only the crash reports its own Tests process wrote, each printed as `CRASH REPORT: <path>` and named in the step (`Docs/Decisions/0029-m18-contract.md`, "Milestone review"). A run that ends with a non-zero exit code, no failed test case and no crash report of its own names in its detail, from the log files below that root, the last test case its process started and the last lines that process's doctest thread logged (with `--json`, `lastTestCase` and `lastLogLines`; §15.2). `--debug-heap` (Windows only; the unit, gpu and golden suites, and the hardening stage's debug-heap GPU step) starts each Tests process on the Windows debug heap (`Scripts/Lib/debugheap.py`: under a debugger of the child alone that detaches at the loader's initial breakpoint, so every heap of the process, the graphics driver's included, checks block tails, fills freed blocks and validates parameters while its crash handler still reports a crash); its step names gain ` (debug heap)` and its reports the suffix `-DebugHeap` (`Gpu-Debug-Vulkan14-DebugHeap.xml`), so they never replace a plain run's (`Docs/Decisions/0029-m18-contract.md` decision 37). Without `--require-gpu`, a GPU or golden test case that finds no Vulkan device passes without running and the run ends with the status warning; with it, the test case fails. The automation suite (`Tests/Automation` and `Tools/MCP/tests` in the MCP virtual environment, then the method coverage gate) does the same for its tests that start a rendering editor (`harness.require_gpu`, ADR 0009 decision 33). A gpu run under the 1.4 cap also warns about skipped host-image-copy cases, and a golden run about missing goldens (smoke mode) and about candidates `--update-golden` wrote. Every run fails on, and names, any test case skipped outside the child-process targets (`Test::ChildTargetSuite`), from the Tests binary's `--no-skip --list-test-cases --reporters=xml` listing of the run's selection; `--allow-skips` is contract mode (Roadmap rule 3, `Docs/Decisions/0004-contract-stub-gate.md`). The feature suite runs `Editor --headless --project Projects/FeatureTest --run-tests --strict` per configuration (§6) and fails on a non-zero exit, on a per-mode gate that is absent, unevaluated or failed (`UNCOVERED gate <g> (Editor): <id>` lines), on a skipped case row and on any change under `Projects/FeatureTest` outside `Library/`; with `--junit` the editor's own reports are `bin/TestResults/Feature-<Config>.xml` and `.json`; it needs a Vulkan device and follows the automation suite's rule without one. The determinism suite verifies every `Testing.Replays` file of FeatureTest with `input.replay {verify, strictHash}` in the `--renderer none --strict` editor of each configuration, comparing every state-hash checkpoint on the way, then requires every replay with input events to fail `input.replay {verify, strictHash, withoutInput, continuePastCheckpoint}` in those editors (the input check, §13.6; a replay whose run without input differed only at checkpoints and still reached the recorded final hash is printed as a warning that fails nothing, ADR 0030 decision 3), and fails on a failed verification, a replay that passes its input check, or a hash that differs from the committed `FinalStateHash` or between configurations (JUnit `bin/TestResults/Determinism.xml`; M14 runs the Debug and Release editors, M15 adds the exported Release and Dist runs, whose hashes it reads from the export suite's reports, ADR 0024 decision 10). The export suite (M15, ADR 0024 decision 9; `--config Release,Dist`) exports a copy of FeatureTest from a `--strict` editor with `project.export {testing: true}` into `bin/Exports/<Config>/FeatureTest/`, runs each package's `--feature-test`, evaluates each report's per-mode gates and merges them with the Editor report (`--editor-report`, default `bin/TestResults/Feature-Release.json`); it needs a Vulkan device and follows the automation suite's rule without one. `--build-root` and `--sanitizer address` run the unit and feature suites from the AddressSanitizer workspace, giving every process they start the AddressSanitizer options and the runtime's directory first on `PATH` (ADR 0024 decision 12); the Debug unit run passes `--fuzz-scale=0.1`, so each fuzz case runs the first tenth of its own sequence (at least its minimum), while the Release unit run executes every count and the hardening stage 1,000,000 per reader (the product owner's decision, ADR 0024 decision 14); `--fuzz-scale S` sets another scale. `--exclude-test-suites` (unit suite only) leaves the named doctest suites out of the unit runs: the hardening stage's ASan unit step leaves out `Fuzz`, which its fuzz step runs as a superset. `--parallel N` (unit suite only; `Scripts/Lib/shards.py`, `Docs/Decisions/0060-skerries-engine-program.md` decision 3) lists the run's selection once, skipped cases included (the run's skip check), and runs its unskipped cases in contiguous shards, N at a time, each a Tests process with doctest's `--first` and `--last`, which count only the unskipped cases that pass the filters in the order the binary runs them, so every case runs in exactly one shard. The shards hold about 120 s of measured work each (at least N of them; 100 cases each without a measurement), since a sanitized process keeps the memory its work took, and the next one, the dearest first, starts as one ends. The cuts follow the per-case costs kept in `<git common dir>/test-costs/<report stem>.xml` for every checkout, where a run whose shards all passed replaces the costs of the cases it ran and keeps the others'; each shard's timeout is five times its expected time, at least 1,200 s, within what is left of `--timeout`, which bounds the listing and the shards together; each shard has its own report, output and user data (`bin/TestResults/<report stem>/Shard<k>.xml`, `Shard<k>.log`, `Shard<k>/UserData`), their reports merge into the run's with one test suite per shard (the run's report is removed first, and a run that fails before the merge writes one naming the failure), and a failure, a timeout, a shard the bound left unstarted or a report that holds other cases than its range fails the step naming the shard. `--merge-coverage` runs the cross-mode merge of §15.6 alone and prints one `merge: <rule>: <subject>` line per failure (ADR 0022 decisions 6 and 7). The games suite (M16, ADR 0026 decisions 7 and 8; any of Debug, Release and Dist) runs over the game projects staged below `Projects/` and `Tests/Projects/` (`Projects/FeatureTest` excluded): with none it passes with one step, `games`, and a project on disk but not staged gets one passed step naming it. Staged projects that share an `.eproj` file stem or a Name (the staged `.eproj`'s), compared ignoring letter case, would share their steps, reports or Dist package directory, so they fail the `games` step, each pair named, before any project runs (`games.check_distinct_projects`, ADR 0030 decision 12). **Machine-wide locks** (`Scripts/Lib/locks.py`; `Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decision 16). The checkouts of the repository (the main one and its worktrees) share one machine, so three locks, whose files are in the git common directory (`<git common dir>/machine-locks/`, the same for every worktree), keep them from overloading it:
- **build** (counted): one uncapped build, which holds both slots, or up to two capped builds, one slot each, each running at most its jobs' worth of compilers (`Build.py`'s rule in its row above). The slots go to the waiting builds in arrival order (the queue, below), so a stream of capped builds cannot starve an uncapped one; an uncapped request at the head of the queue also takes a claim file that holds off the capped builds of checkouts whose `locks.py` predates the queue.
- **gpu** (exclusive): one GPU run at a time: `Test.py` with a GPU-using suite, `Scaffold.py`, `Perf.py`, `Hardening.py` with perf, soak, asan-feature or debug-heap, `Export.py` when it renders or smoke-tests, and the MCP bridge (§13.8) from the launch of a rendering editor (`renderer: "vulkan"`) until that editor exits, however it exits, or the bridge itself exits (an editor left running with unsaved changes holds none, below).
- **gate** (exclusive): `CI.py` holds it for its whole run and takes the gpu and then the build lock after it, so its stages begin once the runs that held them have ended. While the gate is held, or a `CI.py` queues for it, every other build or gpu acquisition, every `Test.py` run, every `Export.py` run and every editor launch of the bridge waits.

The order is gate, then gpu, then build, and nothing that holds a later lock waits for an earlier one. A holder exports its locks in `ENGINE_HELD_LOCKS` (`<lock>=<token>` pairs), and a process whose environment names a lock that its file still records and that is still held runs under that hold: it neither waits for it nor takes another build slot. So `CI.py`'s own `Build.py` and `Test.py` runs, the automation suite's bridge tests under its `Test.py`, and `Hardening.py`'s children run under their parent's locks, and a process inside a run that holds any lock never waits for a gate that began after that run (the gate waits for the run instead; waiting for the gate would deadlock). An MCP client that starts the bridge with an environment it curates (the MCP SDK's stdio client passes only an allow-list and the variables it is given) must pass `ENGINE_HELD_LOCKS`, and `ENGINE_LOCK_DIRECTORY` when set, or the bridge waits for the hold it runs under. **First come, first served.** A request that has to wait queues: it takes a ticket, `<lock dir>/queue/<lock>-<sequence>.ticket`, numbered from a counter in `queue.lock` under that file's short exclusive lock, and holds an operating-system lock on its ticket, as a holder does on its lock file, until its wait ends. Only the earliest live requests may take a lock: a gate or gpu request takes it only when no earlier queued request that can take it now waits, and the earlier build requests take their slots first, oldest first, the first one that cannot start yet (an uncapped request beside a running build, a capped one with both slots taken) stopping everything behind it. A ticket whose lock is free belongs to a dead waiter: every reader skips it and the next waiter that lists the queue removes it, so a crashed waiter never blocks the queue. A request that refuses at once (`--no-wait`) takes no ticket and is refused while earlier requests wait, even for a free lock. The gate keeps its precedence: while a gate runs or a `CI.py` queues for it, a gpu or build request outside a run that holds a lock waits, and the queued ones are passed over by the requests that run inside such a run (the gate's `CI.py` and its children, or the children of a run that began before the gate), which would otherwise wait for requests that wait for the gate; each ticket records its request's `ENGINE_HELD_LOCKS`, so every reader can tell. The bridge's wait, which tries the GPU lock without waiting every 250 ms so a cancelled call can end it, keeps one place in the queue for all its tries. A checkout whose `Scripts/Lib/locks.py` predates the queue neither queues nor reads the queue: it still takes a lock only when it is free (and respects the build claim), so it can take a free lock ahead of the queued requests, but it never removes, reorders or waits for a ticket, and the queue waits for it only while it holds a lock or the claim, which the operating system releases when it ends: it can cut in, never deadlock the queue. A long-running process keeps the `locks.py` it imported until it restarts, even in an up-to-date checkout (an MCP bridge started before the queue landed still polls the old way), so running bridges are restarted after the change lands. A waiter that stops polling while its process lives (a suspended process) keeps its place, as a suspended holder keeps its lock: stop it like any process. Every wait polls and reports the holders (pid, worktree, command and since when) and the earlier requests queued ahead of it when it starts, when they change and every five minutes. Whether a lock is held is learned by taking it and letting it go at once, so a free lock can look held for the moment another process probes it: a wait polls a few more times, 50 ms apart, before it refuses, and a waiting uncapped build gives up its claim only for a gate that stays held. The scripts bound it with `--lock-timeout S` (3 h by default; then exit code 5) and refuse at once with `--no-wait` (exit code 3); the bridge waits at most 25 min (below Claude Code's 30-minute idle timeout for a tool call that sends nothing, ADR 0036 friction F14), reports the holder in its progress notifications meanwhile (§13.8), and then fails the launch with `LockUnavailable`, naming the holder, without spawning an editor; a launch whose call the client cancels stops waiting at once and spawns nothing. Each lock is an operating-system lock on its file (`msvcrt.locking` of one byte far past the holder record on Windows, `fcntl.flock` on POSIX), which the operating system releases when its holder's process ends, however it ends: a crashed holder never wedges the machine, and nothing is ever cleared by hand. `Locks.py` lists the holders and the queues; a holder or waiter that should not run any more is stopped like any process. `ENGINE_LOCK_DIRECTORY` replaces the directory (the tests' own locks), and a checkout without git keeps them in `bin-int/machine-locks/`. Processes started directly take no lock: a Tests or Editor binary run by hand, or an editor the bridge leaves running with unsaved changes when its MCP client goes away (its hold ends with the bridge).

---

## 3. Module architecture and dependency rules

All engine code is in `namespace Engine`. Sub-namespaces: `Utils`, `Detail` (CodeStyle), `Automation` (method handler free functions), `ScriptBindings` (Luau C functions), `Lua` (Scripting's checked helpers and protected VM entry points, §11.4/§11.7; `Docs/Decisions/0021-review-fixes.md`) and `Test` (test support). EditorCore, Editor, Runtime and Tests code also lives in `namespace Engine`; editor classes carry an `Editor` prefix where a name would be ambiguous (`EditorContext`, `EditorCamera`).

| L | Module (`Engine/Source/Engine/…`) | Contents | May include | Third-party (public headers / .cpp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `Editor` (exe) | everything |
