A sensor `RigidBody` of Type Static is created Kinematic (§9.2). A `RigidBody` without any collider makes no body, without a diagnostic. Solid colliders on a `CharacterController`'s entity and on its collider-only descendants form no body (the capsule is the character's shape); trigger colliders there still get implicit sensor bodies. Effectively disabled entities make no bodies.
- **Collision groups.** A body's group is the nearest entity at or above its owner with a `RigidBody` or a `CharacterController` (none for implicit static bodies). Bodies of one group never collide and never report each other, so a trigger attached to a moving ball or a character never reports its own carrier.
- **Order.** Bodies in canonical order of their owners (an owner's solid body before its sensor body); a body's colliders are the owner's own in `BuiltinComponents` order, then each gathered descendant's in canonical order. A collider's index in that order is its sub-shape user data (§9.2).
- **Terrain colliders** (M26, ADR 0037 decision 21). A `TerrainCollider` is a solid collider under these rules: it joins the nearest `RigidBody` at or above its entity (Static or Kinematic: a height field is not convex, `PHYSICS_NONCONVEX_DYNAMIC` otherwise), or else the implicit static body that gathers it (a collider-only ancestor's, or its own entity's). The one departure: when its own entity's implicit static body holds it, that body takes the `TerrainCollider`'s `Layer`, `Friction` and `Restitution` instead of layer 0 and the default material, since a terrain is nearly always a root-level static body whose ground layer and material matter; elsewhere they are unused.
- **2D colliders** (M21, §9.9) follow the same rules in the 2D world, `RigidBody2D` in `RigidBody`'s place. A `TilemapCollider` is one collider of its body like `BoxCollider2D`, `CircleCollider2D` and `PolygonCollider2D` (after them on an entity): its sub-shapes are its tilemap's merged boxes (`Asset/TilemapCollision.h`: each chunk's solid cells merged greedily, rows from the bottom up, each row left to right, never across a chunk's edge; chunks in the tilemap's canonical order), every box with the collider's user data, so a tilemap without a `RigidBody2D` above it is one static compound and its contacts name the tilemap's entity (ADR 0032 decision 25).

### 5.4 Reflection registry: the single source of truth
```cpp
enum class FieldType : uint8_t { Bool, Int32, UInt32, Float, Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Quat, Color3, Color4, Bool3,
	String, EntityRef, AssetRef, Enum, Array, Struct, Map, Variant };
struct FieldMeta
{
	std::optional<double> Min, Max, Step;
	std::optional<double> MinMagnitude;      // per component |v| >= MinMagnitude (Transform.Scale)
	std::string Unit;                        // "kg", "m", "deg"
	std::string AssetFilter;                 // AssetType name of an asset-reference field; set by the registry from its TypedAssetHandle type
	bool ReadOnly = false, Hidden = false, Virtual = false, Scriptable = true, Serialized = true;
	RunModes Modes = RunModes::All;          // All | EditorOnly (see §11.4)
};
// Variant fields resolve their schema at run time from the owning object and the key or pointer:
using VariantSchemaResolver = Result<const FieldInfo*> (*)(const ResolveContext& context);

RegisterComponent<RigidBodyComponent>(registry, "RigidBody", "Simulates the entity with Jolt physics.")   // installs the ComponentHostOps
	.Category("Physics").Version(1).Requires<TransformComponent>().Excludes<CharacterControllerComponent>()
	.Field("Type", &RigidBodyComponent::Type, "Static never moves; Kinematic is moved by script; Dynamic is simulated.")
	.Field("Mass", &RigidBodyComponent::Mass, "Mass in kilograms (Dynamic only).", { .Min = 0.001, .Unit = "kg" })
	.Field("Layer", &RigidBodyComponent::Layer, "Physics layer name from project settings.")
	/* ... */
	.Validate([](const RigidBodyComponent& component, ValidationContext& context)
	{
		if (component.Type == BodyType::Dynamic && component.Mass <= 0.0f)
			context.Error("Mass", "must be > 0 for Dynamic bodies");
	});
```
- **Every float is finite.** Readers, reflected setters, script proxies and automation reject NaN and ±Inf with a located error (`/components/Transform/Translation/1: must be finite`), so non-finite values can never reach Jolt, the renderer or a file. `Min`/`Max`/`MinMagnitude` are enforced on every write path, not only in the inspector.
- **`Map`** is a string-keyed map `std::map<std::string, T>` whose value type is any `FieldType`. Keys are written in sorted (canonical, byte-wise) order. The JSON Schema uses `additionalProperties` with the value schema. Patches use RFC 7386 semantics (`null` deletes a key; nested objects merge). The inspector shows an editable key/value table, and random generators produce 0–8 random keys.
- **`Variant`** holds any JSON-representable value whose schema is resolved at run time by the field's `VariantSchemaResolver`. Validation, drawers, undo, random generation and schema output go through the resolved `FieldInfo`. When resolution fails (unknown script field, missing prefab target), the value is preserved verbatim and a diagnostic is raised, so data is never silently dropped.
- The users of these two types are listed explicitly and tested by the registry suite: `ScriptSlot.Fields` (`Map<Variant>`, resolved against its slot's script's field schema per key), `PrefabOverride.Value` (`Variant`, resolved by the target component and field, or the whole component struct for `AddComponent` overrides) and `ProjectSettings.Input.Actions` (`Map<Struct InputAction>`); `TestSuiteSettings.Parameters` (a free-form `Variant` without a resolver, ADR 0006 decision 6); the `components` param of `entity.create` and `entity.update` (`Map<Variant>`, resolved per component name) and the `Components` maps of entity and scene results. The registry suite covers the settings and components, `RegisterMethodsTests` the automation structs. A new use requires a registry-test fixture.
- `TypeRegistry` holds `ComponentInfo` (name, mandatory description, category, version, flags `Serializable/ScriptVisible/EditorVisible/Removable/UniquePerScene/Required/Hidden/EntityLevel/NoShortcut`, `Requires`/`Excludes`, ordered fields, type-erased `Add/Remove/Has/Patch/ToJson/FromJson/Validate/Migrate(fromVersion, json&)`), `StructInfo` (the same without ECS operations: `MaterialData`, `ProjectSettings`, every `*ImportSettings`, every automation param/result struct) and `EnumInfo` (name↔value table; **enums serialize by name**).
- Descriptions are mandatory for every type and field (the builder signature requires them); `GenerateDocs.py --check` fails on an empty one.
- Consumers: serializer (§6), inspector (one drawer per `FieldType`; custom drawers only for `Script` fields, `Prefab` overrides and, from M22, UiRect's anchor presets above its reflected fields, ADR 0033 decision 34), Luau component proxies (§11.4), automation validation and JSON Schemas (§13.4), `Engine.d.luau`, docs, undo (component JSON before and after), the coverage gates (§15.6), and `FuzzySuggest(name)` (Levenshtein over registered names) for "did you mean" hints.
- `using BuiltinComponents = TypeList<...>` is the one list of component types. Startup asserts every listed type is registered. A registry-parametrized doctest checks, for every component and every reflected struct: default → JSON → equal; 200 seeded random in-range round trips (including `Map` and `Variant` fields, with the resolver fed a fixture schema); validation rejects out-of-range and non-finite values; script get/set of every scriptable field; automation set/get; schema validates the serialized output. Adding a component gets these tests for free.

### 5.5 Prefabs
A prefab asset (`.prefab`) is a serialized entity subtree with one root and prefab-local UUIDs (§6.3).
- **Instantiation** (`PrefabInstantiator::Instantiate(scene, prefab, {PrefabHandle, RootID, Parent, SiblingIndex, RootTransform}, …)`, reached for an asset handle through `InstantiatePrefabAsset`; the single path used by the editor, automation and scripts) deep-copies the subtree and derives member IDs deterministically: the instance root keeps `RootID`, and every other member gets `InstanceID = Hash64(RootID, PrefabEntityID)`. `EntityRef` fields and script `Entity` field values that point inside the prefab are remapped with the same function. The root gets `PrefabInstanceComponent`; every member gets `PrefabLinkComponent`. Instantiation never loads another prefab: a prefab document holds its nested instances expanded (below), so the Runtime instantiates it as it is.
- **Overrides.** Each override names its entity by its `Path` (below) and has a `Kind`: `Field` `{Path, Component, Field, Value}`, `AddComponent` and `RemoveComponent` `{Path, Component, Value?}`, `EntityKey` `{Path, Field: Name|Active|Tags, Value}`, which keeps a renamed or deactivated member so across updates, and `RemoveEntity` `{Path}`, which keeps a deleted member deleted (`Value` is a `Variant`, §5.4; files write all five keys in the order `Path, Kind, Component, Field, Value`, an unused one empty or null; `Prefab` version 1's single `PrefabEntityID` migrates to a one-element `Path`). They are derived by diffing the instance against its prefab when a `SceneEdit` commits (`PrefabInstantiator::RefreshOverrides`), never recorded field by field, and compared in instance space, so a fresh instance has none (ADR 0006 decisions 17, 18 and 25 to 28; ADR 0010 decisions 11 and 33). The diff records each `Value` as a file holds it (§6: `0.8`, not the `0.800000011920929` of a `float` field's `0.8f`), so the record a scene file gives back after a save is the one the diff computes, a refresh after a load leaves it unchanged, and a scene whose prefabs are unchanged opens clean, its instances rebuilt without a change (World Tree's brief 21, whose skinned model with a fractional Animator override opened dirty on every open). A `Map<Variant>` (a script slot's `Fields`) is overridden by the keys that differ only, an RFC 7386 patch, so the prefab's edits of its other keys still reach the instance. A Field override of the `Script` component names one slot's member, `Field` = `Scripts/<slot>/<member>` (`Script`, `Fields` or `ExecutionOrder`, `<slot>` the slot's index in the prefab entity's list), while the instance's list has as many slots as the prefab entity's; a list of another length is one `Scripts` override. A slot override follows its slot's index: one whose slot the prefab entity no longer has is stale, and a prefab edit that reorders or inserts slots before an overridden one moves it to whichever slot has that index (M20, `Docs/Decisions/0031-m20-contract.md` decision 19). Root Name, Transform and Parent are always implicit overrides. Entities added under an instance (no `PrefabLinkComponent`) are user children: updates preserve them, and `prefab.apply` adds them to the prefab (below).
- **Deleting members.** A member deleted from an instance in the edit scene is recorded by the diff like every override: one `RemoveEntity` for the top of each removed subtree (a prefab entity without a member whose prefab parent has one), whose prefab descendants go with it and get no override of their own. `entity.destroy` (the editor's Delete included) and `prefab.create {replaceWithInstance}` of a member destroy it, and the commit's override refresh records the `RemoveEntity` on its instance root in the same undo step; with `replaceWithInstance` the new instance's root keeps the member's id as a user child of the outer instance. Updates build neither a removed entity nor its prefab descendants, and `prefab.revert` brings them back with their derived ids (a revert that would rebuild a member over an id another entity took fails as any update does then); a `RemoveEntity` whose entity the prefab no longer has, that names the root or that lies below another removed entity is stale. `prefab.apply` leaves the entity and its descendants out of the prefab, and references to them keep their prefab-local ids, naming no entity. Instance roots, user children and the transient play scene, whose members scripts' `Scene.Destroy` destroys and nothing records, are unchanged (M20, `Docs/Decisions/0031-m20-contract.md` decision 7, replacing the setup's refusal of ADR 0028 decision 16).
- **Live nested prefabs** (M20, `Docs/Decisions/0031-m20-contract.md` decisions 8 and 9). A prefab document holds instances of other prefabs exactly as a scene holds them: expanded, with their `Prefab` and `PrefabLink` components and their overrides, each outermost within the document; the prefab's own root is never an instance root or member itself (`PREFAB_NESTED_INSTANCE`). An instance nested in a document is an instance of its prefab at its root's id: a nested root's id derives at the level that encloses it, `Hash64(enclosing instance root, its id in the enclosing prefab)`, which its `PrefabLink` records as `OuterPrefabEntityID` (null on every other entity), and its members derive from it, so `fold(Hash64, outermost root, Path)` is the id of every entity but the outermost root. Every `PrefabLink` keeps naming its entity's innermost instance (a root, nested or not, names itself). Only an instance outermost in its document records overrides, those of its own entities (`Path` = `[its id in the prefab]`) and of the instances nested in it (`Path` = the nested roots' `OuterPrefabEntityID`s from the outermost level inwards, then the entity's own `PrefabEntityID` unless it is that nested root), sorted by `(Path, Component, Kind, Field)`; a nested root's stay empty. An instance is rebuilt, diffed and applied only from its outermost root, its nested instances following it (the instantiator refuses a nested root, naming its outermost root); `PrefabInstantiator::GetInstanceLevels` and `GetOverridePath` give an entity's levels and path.
- **Update.** When a prefab asset changes, every instance in the open scenes is rebuilt as *prefab + overrides*: the addressed scene's inside the undo step of the action that changed the prefab, and every other open scene's as one "Update Prefab Instances" step of its own history, in tab order, after the change and again after its undo and its redo (`EditorContext::PropagatePrefabUpdate`, ADR 0031 decision 15), so undo stays isolated per scene. `scene.open` rebuilds a scene's instances from the current prefab versions; when that changes an instance, the scene opens unsaved, and its result's `rebuiltInstances` names each changed outermost instance with its prefab (ADR 0038, friction F14). Derived IDs are stable, so external references into the instance survive. Prefab entities that no longer exist, or that a `RemoveEntity` removes, disappear; overrides that no longer match a field are dropped with a warning. An entity's `Field` overrides of one component are applied as one write and the combined component validated once, as `entity.update` with the same fields would (M35, ADR 0050 decision 9; World Tree's brief 13): so overrides valid only together (`UiRect`'s `AnchorMin` and `AnchorMax`) survive a rebuild together, and when the write is invalid the overrides whose fields its error locates are dropped and the rest written again (after an error that locates none of them, a rule of the component that blames a field no override writes, the rest are written one at a time over the component as written so far and only those invalid there are dropped, so a valid override never goes with an invalid sibling). Every dropped override is a `PREFAB_STALE_OVERRIDE` warning, logged and reported in the result of the method that rebuilt (ADR 0050 decision 10): `scene.open`'s `diagnostics`, and the `rebuildDiagnostics` of `prefab.apply`, `prefab.revert`, `asset.import`, `asset.reimport` and `asset.setImportSettings`, and of `edit.undo` and `edit.redo` for the other open scenes that follow an undone or redone prefab write, each naming the open scene, the instance root and the override's place in its record. A new version of a nested prefab (`prefab.apply`, `asset.setImportSettings`, `asset.reimport` and the inspector's import settings) first rewrites every prefab asset that nests it, directly or through others, in nesting order (each after the prefabs it nests, ties in path order; `EditorContext::GetNestingPrefabs` reads the nesting graph from the import dependencies, which list every prefab a document nests, and confirms it in the documents), each document's nested instances rebuilt from the new version keeping the overrides that document records for them (`UpdateNestedPrefabInstances`, `EditorContext::CreateNestingPrefabUpdateCommand`); then the outermost instances of every changed prefab are rebuilt, all as one undo step. A prefab that nests itself, directly or through others, is `PREFAB_CYCLE`: an update whose propagation meets the cycle is refused and changes nothing, `prefab.apply` refuses to add an instance that would close one (below), and `project.validate` reports it on each prefab on the cycle.
- `prefab.apply {instance, level?}` writes overrides back into a prefab: by default the outermost instance's into its own asset (its nested instances' edits becoming their own overrides in that document); with `level`, the overrides within the instance, re-based onto the level's prefab, where the level root's Name, Transform and Parent (its placement) are never written. **Added entities** (M27 friction F04, `Docs/Decisions/0038-m27-rolling-ball.md`): it also adds every entity added below `instance` (an entity of its subtree that is not an entity of its outermost instance: a user child with its subtree, an instance placed there included) to that prefab, at its place among its parent's children, keeping its ID as its prefab-local ID; an added instance stays live there as a nested instance with its record, and at the outermost level a member below an added entity keeps it as its parent. In the same undo step the added entities leave the scene and the rebuild creates them as members of the level's instance, each at `Hash64(level root, its old ID)` (the result's `addedEntities`), so every instance in every open scene gains them and none keeps a copy beside them; undo restores the prefab and every instance. Since an added entity changes its ID, the apply refuses (`InvalidState`, naming both) an added entity that another entity references, unless that entity is added too or, when the level is the outermost, a member of the outermost instance (whose references are written with the prefab and recorded in its space); an added entity whose ID the prefab already uses (`InvalidState`); and an added instance of the prefab or of a prefab nesting it (`PREFAB_CYCLE`). `PrefabInstantiator::GetAddedEntities` lists them, and the inspector shows them beside the overrides, its Apply offered for either. `prefab.revert` clears overrides (on a nested root, those whose paths lie within it); `prefab.create` keeps the instances strictly inside the subtree live, outermost in the new document, unpacking the subtree root's own instance and those enclosing it; `prefab.unpack` removes the link components and keeps the entities, one level at a time: the instances nested directly in the unpacked one become outermost, taking over the overrides recorded for them.
- Scenes store instances fully expanded plus their override records, so a scene loads even if its prefab is missing (diagnostic `PREFAB_MISSING_ASSET`), and the Runtime never resolves prefabs while loading a scene.

### 5.6 Scene lifecycle: Edit, Play, Simulate
```
Edit ──Play/Simulate──▶ Running ⇄ Paused ──Step(n)──▶ Paused        Running/Paused ──Stop──▶ Edit
```
- **Play** creates a `PlaySession` of the editor's active scene (§12.1; the session's played scene): `SceneSerializer::ToJson(editScene)` → `SceneSerializer::FromJson(runtimeScene)` through an in-memory `ordered_json` document. This is the exact path the exported Runtime uses to load a scene, which removes "works in the editor, broken in export" bugs. Budget: a 1,000-entity copy in under 30 ms (Release), tracked warning-only by the hardening stage's perf capture (`Perf.py`'s `playCopy/1000Entities`: the median of 5 lockstep `play.start`/`play.stop` cycles less an empty scene's `play.start`; ADR 0012, ADR 0024 decision 16), never gated, because no outcome may depend on how long anything takes. M20 made the serializer copy faster without changing its output (ADR 0031 decision 6, measured and still warning-only), and the session keeps the copy's document as its start document, which `Scene.Reload` reloads; a registry-based copy won't be built (ADR 0028 decision 2), since the serializer stays the one scene-copy path (§1.3).
- Session setup: physics bodies are created in canonical order, the script VM is created, script instances are created (one per script slot of each Script component, §11.2), `OnCreate` runs for every instance in (`ExecutionOrder`, canonical entity order, slot) order, then `OnStart` for all in the session's startup flush (§5.7 step 2's rounds, in the step view of tick 0 with the fixed delta), whose rounds also start, with their bodies, what the startup callbacks spawn, and right after it a destroy and disable flush in the same view (§5.7 step 8's work), so what the startup callbacks destroyed or disabled, with its `OnDisable` and `OnDestroy`, is gone before tick 0 however the first frames group their ticks (ADR 0038 decision 14); `PlayOnStart` audio starts. The `PhysicsSystem` is created right after the scene loads, so queries and `physics.bodyInfo` work at tick 0. The `AudioSystem` starts its `PlayOnStart` sources in canonical order with their voices held paused until the first `AudioUpdate` phase, so the paused and lockstep state a host applies after creation is in force before a voice can reach a device, and their cursors are 0 at tick 0 (ADR 0014 decision 11, ADR 0015 decisions 5 and 13).
- **Simulate** is Play without the script engine and audio, using the editor camera; physics runs as in Play.
- **Pause / Step(n)** freezes the scheduler; Step runs exactly n ticks (each tick = fixed step + frame phase, as in lockstep).
- **World pause** (M35, ADR 0050 decisions 1 to 5; World Tree's brief 12): not the run state's pause above, which stops every tick, but a pause of the session's world while its ticks, input and UI run on, so a pause menu works over a frozen world. Scripts request it (`Time.PauseWorld(sounds?)`, `Time.ResumeWorld()`, `Time.IsWorldPaused()`) and so does automation (`play.setWorldPaused {paused, sounds?}`, refused while a recording records or a replay plays, so every replay reproduces its pauses from its scripts); each fixed step applies the latest request before anything of it runs, so a tick runs wholly paused or wholly not. While it holds, the world's phases do not run (§5.7's classification), only behaviours whose class sets `RunsWhileWorldPaused` run `OnFixedUpdate`, `OnUpdate`, `OnLateUpdate` and tasks (§11.3), the world's clock holds (`Time.GetTick`, `Time.GetTime`; `play.state`'s `worldTick`) while the session's counts on (`Time.GetSessionTick`, `Time.GetSessionTime`; `play.state`'s `tick`), the world's presentation holds with its clock (a `MaterialParameters` scroll renders at the world's clock, §8.3; ADR 0042's execution-order rule, at batch 1's landing of M31 with M35), and the world's voices, those of every group but `Music` and `Ui` (with today's groups, the `Sfx` group's; a group added later is held unless it is listed as playing on), pause or play on to their end by the pause's `sounds` choice, while the `Music` and `Ui` groups and the session's music play on, so a pause menu, its music and a stinger under a defeat panel sound (§10.2; M40, ADR 0057 decision 14, amending ADR 0050 decision 3). The pause, its pending request and the world's clock are session state, kept across `Scene.Load` and `Scene.Reload` like the time scale (so a pause menu that loads or restarts a scene calls `Time.ResumeWorld` first, or the new scene starts with its world paused and soft-locks unless it has a menu of its own), and form the state hash's world-pause block from the session's first request to pause on (§13.7); `play.state` reports `worldPaused`, `worldSounds` and `worldTick` beside the run state.
- **Session locale** (M38, ADR 0055 decisions 1 to 4; World Tree's brief 17): a session starts in its project copy's `Localization.Locale`, which its host sets from `PlayStartOptions::Locale` (`play.start {locale}`, `input.record {locale}`, a suite's `Locale` or the run's, the Runtime's `--locale`, a replay's header; §6.1), its start locale (`GetStartLocale`), an input like the seed. `Loc.SetLocale` changes the session's locale (`PlaySession::SetLocale`, through `IScriptHost::SetLocale`) and its VM's copy, then delivers `OnLocaleChanged` synchronously (§11.3); the locale is session state, kept across `Scene.Load` and `Scene.Reload`, whose VMs start in it without the callback, and forms the state hash's locale block while it differs from the start locale (§5.1). `play.state` reports it as `locale`.
- **Lockstep** (automation, §13.6): the wall clock is ignored and ticks advance only through `play.step`.
- **Stop** destroys the session (`OnDestroy` for all instances, bodies, voices, VM). The edit scene is never touched during play; selection is restored by UUID, into the played scene's edit selection.
- **Open scenes during play** (ADR 0031 decision 13). Activating another open scene's tab, or closing any tab, the played one included, leaves the session running, as replacing the played scene with `scene.open` does. While the played scene's tab is active the editor shows the play scene; another tab shows its edit scene, and the Game view keeps showing the session. The scene view, its picking, its gizmo and `viewport.frame` follow the hierarchy (`EditorContext::ShowsPlayScene`): in another tab they show, select in, move and frame that tab's edit scene, its gizmo moves recorded in its history as in Edit mode (ADR 0031 decision 23). A played scene that is closed or replaced leaves the session belonging to no open scene, and Stop then drops the play selection. The runtime keeps one scene per session: additive runtime scenes are not built, and `Scene.Load` replaces the session's scene as below.
- **Scene.Load** from a script swaps the session's scene at the end of a frame: the current runtime scene is torn down (including its VM, so state never leaks), the new scene is loaded through the serializer, and the optional parameters table (JSON-serializable) is readable in the new scene through `Scene.GetLoadParameters()`. The new scene's startup callbacks (`OnCreate`, then its startup flush's `OnStart`, then the destroy and disable flush of what they destroyed or disabled) run as the session's do, in the step view of the tick the frame ended with and with the fixed delta, however the frame grouped its ticks (ADR 0038 decision 14). Which frame's end depends on where the request was made (ADR 0038 decision 15, which fixed friction F17), so that the new scene's first tick is the same however the ticks are grouped into frames: a request made in a fixed step (`OnFixedUpdate`, an `OnStart` of a fixed step's start flush, a physics, animation or UI callback, a task, a test case, native code) belongs to its tick, and the frame runs no further fixed step (§5.7), runs its frame phase in the current scene and applies the transition at its end, as lockstep applies it after every tick, the steps the frame did not run staying in the scheduler for the next frames; a request made by a scene's startup callbacks (the session's, or those of the scene a `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload` made current) belongs to the next tick, so the requesting scene runs that one tick and the frame that runs it stops and applies it (a frame of no step leaves it pending); a request made in the frame phase or between frames (`OnUpdate`, `OnLateUpdate`, an evaluation) applies at that frame's end, after its steps, as presentation code's does (§11.3). Until it applies the request only waits, and a second `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload` before then raises `InvalidState` (as one after `Application.Quit()` does), the first one still applying; so a game keeps its own flag once it has requested a transition and requests nothing more, which still matters for two requests in one tick (two behaviours) (`PlaySession::State::CheckSceneTransition`). `Scene.Reload` follows the same rule. The scene's voices go with it, but the session's music (M40, §10.2) is the session's: a `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload` keeps it playing, never held, and a new scene that asks for the clip already playing (`Audio.PlayMusic` in its `OnStart`) keeps its voice, so a track goes on through the doorway.
- **Scene.Reload** restarts the current scene the same way from the document it started from: the session's start document while the scene the session started with is current (in editor play the play copy, so the edit scene's unsaved edits are kept; a suite's or replay's scene; the Runtime's start scene), otherwise the document of the scene asset the last `Scene.Load` loaded, as it was then. Given parameters replace the load parameters; without them the current scene's are kept. `Scene.GetCurrent()` names the scene asset the current scene came from (the open scene's or `play.start`'s, a suite's or replay's, the Runtime's start scene, then each `Scene.Load`'s; a reload keeps it), nil for an editor scene never saved. One transition at a time: a second `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload` while one is pending raises `InvalidState` (ADR 0031 decision 5).
- Edits made during play affect only the runtime scene, are not undoable, are visibly tinted in the UI, and are discarded on Stop.

### 5.7 Step order (`PlaySession`), documented and tested
Fixed step (repeated `StepCount` times per frame, one per tick, until a scene transition requested in a tick ends the frame's steps: the frame then runs no further fixed step, its frame phase applies the transition at its end, and the steps it did not run stay in the scheduler for the next frames, within its per-frame cap; `PlaySession::EndsFrameSteps`, `FixedStepScheduler::EndFrameAfter`, which every loop that runs a frame's steps follows; §5.6, ADR 0038 decision 15):
0. Interpolation snapshot: `TransformSystem::Update` first when a transform changed outside the session's phases since the last update (an automation write at the safe point); then `PreviousWorldTransform ← WorldTransform` for every entity; clear `InterpolationResetTag` (§5.2).
1. Apply injected input events stamped for this tick (and, during a replay, the replay's events); `InputState::LatchStep()`. A recording captures every event applied here (§13.6).
   - 1a. TextLatch (M22 C22.3, ADR 0033 decision 46): `PlayInput::LatchStepText` latches the tick's committed characters (the `Text` events ApplyInput applied, in order) into the step view, so UiInput and the tick's scripts (`Input.GetText`) read the same characters, none on a tick without text; the frame view's text is every step text latched since the previous frame (none in a frame without a step: text is never previewed). Play and Simulate.
   - 1b. UiInput (M22 C22.2, ADR 0033 decision 24): `UiSystem::ProcessInput` reads the step view's pointer (mapped to scene pixels through the output stage), wheel and left stick and the `Ui` settings' navigation bindings, and, against the session's current UI layout, updates focus, hover and press, writes what the widgets change (a toggle's IsOn, a slider's Value, a scroll view's ScrollPosition) and queues the UI events; while the scene has no canvas it reads no input and keeps the interaction state empty. C22.3 (decision 47): a focused interactable text input takes the step's text and its editing keys (fixed keys: Backspace, Delete, Left, Right, Home, End, Enter and KeypadEnter), and while it has focus only the gamepad's commands, the stick, and Next, Previous and Cancel pressed by a control other than its editing keys (Backspace, Delete, Left, Right, Home, End: M22's milestone review) navigate, so a key typed into it never navigates and an editing key bound to Cancel only edits; a gamepad focuses, submits and leaves a text input but types nothing into it (there is no on-screen keyboard: an accepted limit, decision 47's amendment and Backlog §6). C22.3 (decision 50): only while the current layout holds a World canvas, the session casts the pointer's ray through the primary camera at its simulated pose (`ComputeUiPointerRay`: the inverse of the projection render extraction draws the camera with, its PixelPerfectCamera's orthographic one from the snapped position when it holds one, M22's landing), so a scene without one keeps its hash; a Screen canvas's target under the pointer wins, else the nearest World canvas whose rectangle the ray meets within the camera's clip range, with a target at that point, and a pointer outside the scene image reaches neither (`HitTestUiPointer`; scene geometry does not occlude it, an accepted limit); a slider or scroll view on a World canvas drags along its plane; directional navigation stays within one render space (the Screen canvases together, or one World canvas). Play and Simulate; Simulate drops the events.
2. Start flush (ADR 0038 decision 14), in rounds until no instance waits. Each round synchronizes the physics bodies of both worlds (after a `TransformSystem::Update` when the scene changed: `PhysicsSystem::SynchronizeBodies`, then `Physics2DSystem::SynchronizeBodies`, the rebuilds of steps 5 and 7a for the components EnTT's signals marked, without their kinematic moves and teleports), then runs `OnStart`, in canonical order, for every instance created or enabled since the last flush; an instance the round's own callbacks create (an `OnStart` that spawns, an `OnCreate` it runs) waits for the next round of the same flush. This is the only start flush during a session (the frame phase runs none) besides the startup flush of the session and of each `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload`, so an entity created during the session starts here, in the step view of its tick, with the fixed delta, its destroy and disable requests flushed at that tick's step 8 (a startup flush's, by the destroy flush that follows it at once). The body synchronization applies every physics component and `Active` change, not only a new entity's: one made after a tick's pre-step (a physics callback, an `OnDestroy`, the frame phase, between ticks) is in force at the next tick's `OnFixedUpdate`. So an entity first runs `OnStart`, then `OnFixedUpdate`, at the same tick however the ticks are grouped into frames, its `OnStart` reads and does the same, and it has its body from its `OnStart` on. A flush runs at most `MaxScriptStartRounds` (16) rounds: an instance still waiting then belongs to a runaway `OnStart` chain, and is reported as a script error of its `OnStart` and disabled.
   - 2a. UiEvents (M22 C22.2, decision 27): the queued UI events reach their `OnUi*` callbacks, each bubbling from its element through its ancestors per behaviour (ADR 0031 decision 18), after `OnStart` and before `OnFixedUpdate`. Play only.
3. Script `OnFixedUpdate(fixedDt)` for every enabled instance, (`ExecutionOrder`, canonical, slot) order (the slot of an entity's Script list, §11.3); the iteration list is snapshotted at phase start.
4. Task scheduler resumes `Task.Wait*` and `Task.Delay` threads due at this tick (simulation time), then the running test case thread, if any (§11.10).
   - 4a. NativeStep, only in Play with a native module (§11.11; ADR 0030 decision 28): the module's systems in registration order, each reading the latched step input as `OnFixedUpdate` does; when the phase ends, every native component a system changed, added or removed is written back to the scene as canonical JSON. A value its type rejects or an exception that escapes a system stops the session fatally, and no later system, phase or tick runs.
   - 4b. SpriteAnimation, in Play and Simulate (`SpriteAnimationSystem`, ADR 0032 decision 5): every playing `SpriteAnimator` of an effectively enabled entity with a `SpriteRenderer`, in canonical order, advances one tick of the clip `Clip` of the renderer's sprite sheet: the current step's frame is written to `SpriteRenderer.Frame` (through `Entity::Patch`, so the change tracker sees it), each step shows for exactly its `Ticks`, and past the last step a looping clip restarts while a held one stops on its last frame and clears `Playing`. The playback state (`Step`, `StepTicks`, `Playing`) is component data, so the state hash covers it with no block of its own. It runs after the tick's gameplay code, so a clip started in `OnFixedUpdate` or by native code shows its first step at that tick, while one started in a contact callback or `OnDestroy` advances from the next. A clip the sheet lacks, or a sheet that is missing or does not load, changes nothing and is `SPRITE_UNKNOWN_CLIP`, logged once per entity and clip name. A session without an asset manager has no sheets, so the phase changes nothing there.
   - 4c. AnimationSystem (M23, ADR 0034 decision 29), in Play and Simulate: every effectively enabled Animator in canonical order (one pending destruction skipped) advances its layers' times (written back through the scene), samples and blends its pose into its runtime `AnimationPoseComponent` and moves its Transform by the root motion with `RootMotion` Apply (a pose or a moved Transform that would hold a value that is not finite is never written: the pose is dropped and the Transform kept, with one warning per Animator; ADR 0034's milestone review); the SkinnedMeshes' `ANIMATION_*` findings are raised once per entity (§13.7); then (M41, ADR 0058 decision 3) every `BoneAttachment` of an effectively enabled entity, in canonical order (parents first, so an attachment below another sees its parent's new pose), is placed on its joint of the nearest Animator above it, its `Translation` and `Rotation` written through the scene only when they differ bit for bit, and one that cannot attach keeps its Transform with `ANIMATION_ATTACHMENT_INVALID` once per entity; then, after every Animator was stepped and every attachment placed, the tick's animation events reach `OnAnimationEvent` (Play) in (canonical entity, layer, firing) order, at most 256 per Animator, an event of an entity a callback destroyed or disabled dropped, so a callback's changes take effect from the next tick whatever the entities' order. A scene without an Animator, a SkinnedMesh or a BoneAttachment is unchanged and hashes as before.
5. `TransformSystem::Update`, then `PhysicsSystem::PreStep`: create, rebuild or remove bodies for changed components, then create, change in place or remove joints after them (M37, §9.10), then vehicles (M44, §9.11); teleport bodies whose world pose was changed by script, native code, root motion or automation (including writes made in steps 3–4c of this tick, which the transform update has just propagated); `MoveKinematic` for kinematic and implicit sensor bodies; then each vehicle's driver input from its `WheeledVehicle`, in canonical order, waking a sleeping vehicle for a throttle or a new input (M44); then the characters.
6. `PhysicsWorld::Step(fixedDt, collisionSteps)` (§9.3).
7. `PhysicsSystem::PostStep`: break the joints over their thresholds (M37, §9.10); write dynamic poses back (world → local), then each vehicle's wheels' poses into their `VehicleWheel` entities' local Translation and Rotation (M44, §9.11); dispatch sorted collision and trigger events (§9.4), then the joint breaks (`OnJointBreak`).
   - 7a. `Physics2DSystem::PreStep` (M21, §9.9; ADR 0032 decision 10): first `TransformSystem::Update` when the scene holds 2D physics components and step 7 may have changed a transform (the 3D world holds a body or a character, or the scene changed since the last update), since the pre-step reads world matrices and detects teleports from local writes; then step 5's work for the 2D bodies. A scene without 2D physics components skips the update, so a 3D game steps as before.
   - 7b. `Physics2DWorld::Step(fixedDt, collisionSteps)`.
   - 7c. `Physics2DSystem::PostStep`: write 2D poses back (world X, Y and the rotation about Z; the entity keeps its world Z); dispatch the sorted 2D collision and trigger events (`OnCollisionEnter2D` …, §9.9). 3D callbacks see an unstepped 2D world, 2D callbacks a stepped and written-back 3D world.
8. Destroy and disable flush: `OnDestroy`, then synthesized `OnCollisionExit`/`OnTriggerExit` to surviving contact partners of destroyed or newly disabled entities (§9.4), then body/voice/instance removal, then entity destruction, children first. `PhysicsSystem::FlushDestroyed` (synthesized exits, then body and character removal), followed in every pass by `Physics2DSystem::FlushDestroyed` (M21), runs before `Scene::FlushPendingDestroys` and repeats until a pass finds nothing, since its callbacks may destroy or disable more; `AudioSystem` releases voices from its destroy signals.
9. `TransformSystem::Update`.
10. UiLayout (M22, ADR 0033 decision 3): `UiSystem::LayoutStep` lays the scene's UI out at the session's scene resolution (§8.3, `Scene/UiLayout.h`: the scene resolution of its game view, `ComputeGameViewOutputMapping`, the view's size, or a primary camera's PixelPerfectCamera reference resolution, which the game view draws the UI at; M22's landing, one function for the session and render extraction), after every phase that can change UI data, so the layout matches the state the step left. Play and Simulate.

Frame phase (once per frame; once per tick in lockstep and with `ManualClock`):
1. `PlayInput::LatchFrame()`: the frame view (§4.3), which in live play, neither lockstep nor recording, previews the device events queued for the next tick, so a frame that runs no step sees new device input (M22 W-CLOCK, ADR 0033 decision 12). No start flush (ADR 0038 decision 14): an instance created since the last fixed step starts at the next one's (step 2), and until then `OnUpdate` and `OnLateUpdate` pass it by.
2. Script `OnUpdate(frameDt)`, then `OnLateUpdate(frameDt)`; destroy flush; `TransformSystem::Update`. Transforms written in this phase get `InterpolationResetTag`. Then FrameUiLayout (M22): `UiSystem::LayoutFrame` lays the UI out again, so UI written in `OnUpdate` or `OnLateUpdate` is drawn in this frame; the session's current layout is the later of the two (`UiSystem::GetLayout`). Outside the phase list, `Activate` and a `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload`'s scene replacement at the end of a frame each run `UiSystem::LayoutStep` of the current scene before its startup callbacks and again after them, so the current layout always describes the current scene, in its `OnCreate` and `OnStart` too (ADR 0033 decision 3).
3. `AudioSystem::Update` (listener, source positions and velocities), then, while the session owns audio time (§10.1), one tick of frames for every tick run since the last pull, then the session's music's snapshot (M40, `SessionMusic::Update`: the voices the engine released forgotten, `Test.GetMusic`'s state taken). Play mode only.
3a. Particles (M26, ADR 0037 decision 6; ADR 0028's phase-3 ledger): `ParticleSystem::Step` advances every effectively enabled `ParticleEmitter`'s seeded simulation one fixed step per tick run since its last Particles phase (never by the frame's delta time; a state's first phase, whoever made it, steps it once and never catches up the ticks before it; at most `MaxParticleStepsPerPhase`, 60, a phase), in Play and Simulate, whether or not extraction is enabled, so particles are a function of the ticks and the emitters' poses at the frames alone; an entity that lost its `ParticleEmitter` or is effectively disabled loses its state there, and `ParticleEmitter:Emit` and `Clear` (§11.5) show at the next phase; it writes only the runtime `ParticleStateComponent`, so no simulation phase reads particles and the state hash never changes with them. An emitter's `ParticleLook` (M33, ADR 0048 decision 2) gives each new particle a start angle, a spin and a frame pick drawn from the emitter's second seeded stream, so its first stream, and every particle's motion, is the same with a look or without, and every step turns each particle by its spin.
4. Render extraction: interpolates `PreviousWorldTransform` → `WorldTransform` by `Alpha`, except for entities with `InterpolationResetTag` or a tagged ancestor, which render at `WorldTransform`.

**The world's phases and the UI's** (M35, ADR 0050 decision 2; ADR 0042's phase 5 execution order). Every phase is the world's or the UI's. While the world is paused (§5.6) the world's phases do not run, and the observer is not told of them: steps 4a NativeStep, 4b SpriteAnimation, 4c AnimationSystem, 5's `PhysicsSystem::PreStep`, 6, 7 and 7a to 7c in the fixed step, and 3a Particles in the frame phase; so bodies keep their velocities, animators, sprite animators, particles and the native module's systems hold, and a paused world draws as it stands, its interpolation held. Steps 3 and 4 and the frame's `OnUpdate` and `OnLateUpdate` reach only the behaviours that run while the world is paused, and step 4 only their tasks, the test case and the tasks without an instance owner (§11.3). Every other step is the UI's and runs as always: 0, 1, 1a, 1b, 2 (every `OnStart` and the body synchronization, so a menu creates its own entities), 2a (every `OnUi*` callback; `OnLocaleChanged`, M38, runs inside the `Loc.SetLocale` that delivers it, in whatever phase, and reaches every behaviour that defines it, paused or not), 5's `TransformSystem::Update`, 8, 9, 10 and the frame phase's 1, 2, 3 and 4. The session's tick counts every fixed step; the world's tick (`PlaySession::GetWorldTick`) only the steps the world ran, and the world's systems step on it (`SimStep::FromTick(worldTick, fixedDt)`; Particles steps each emitter to it), so the ticks the world ran before a pause took effect step at the first phase after it resumes. In a session that never paused both clocks agree. A phase a later milestone adds is classified when it lands.

**Creation and destruction semantics.** `Scene.CreateEntity` and `Scene.Instantiate` take effect immediately: the entity and components exist, script instances are created and `OnCreate` runs before the call returns (re-entrancy depth limit 16), and `OnStart` runs at the next start flush, before the instance's first update: the running one when the creator runs in a start flush (an `OnStart`, or an `OnCreate` it runs), the scene's startup flush when a startup `OnCreate` creates it, and otherwise the next fixed step's (step 2), never the frame phase, so `OnUpdate` and `OnLateUpdate` pass it by until then. The physics body, 3D or 2D, is created before that `OnStart`: at the flush's body synchronization (step 2), or at an earlier pre-step (step 5, and step 7a for a 2D body) when the entity was created before it in a fixed step. So an entity has its body from its `OnStart` on, wherever it was created: in a fixed step (an `OnStart`, a UI callback, `OnFixedUpdate`, a task, a test case, native code, an animation event, a physics callback, an `OnDestroy`), in the frame phase, between ticks by `script.eval` or another automation method, or by the startup callbacks of the session or of a `Scene.Load` or `Scene.Reload` (ADR 0038 decision 14, which closed friction F19's window; "PlaySession: an entity has its physics body from its OnStart on, wherever it was created"). Before that `OnStart` (in the callback that created it, for example) the body need not exist yet: `Physics.GetBodyBounds` returns nil and the body methods raise `has no physics body` (`RigidBody2D`'s `has no 2D physics body`). Entities created during a phase are not visited by that phase (a start flush's next round starts them). `Destroy` marks the entity with `PendingDestroyTag`: `IsValid()` returns false immediately and the scene's searches leave it out, but until the flush its reads keep working (every member registered as not mutating: its components' fields, `Name`, `ID`, its tags, `GetComponent` and the shortcuts, its place in the hierarchy), so a partner's collision callback can still read an entity destroyed earlier in the same dispatch. Its writes, and any access after the flush, raise a located `entity 5d1c1f0e9a8b7c6d was destroyed` error (an identity kept from a replaced scene reports `belongs to an expired scene` instead), and the body, character and audio functions refuse it at once, since its body and voices are leaving (ADR 0031 decision 4). The flush points above perform the destruction. A session holds at most `Simulation.MaxEntities` entities (default 65,536). Creating or instantiating beyond that raises a script error (`entity limit 65536 reached`) or an automation `InvalidState` error, never a crash. Entities destroyed in the current tick stay in the registry until the flush, so live, new and pending-destroy entities together stay within twice the limit as well, however many a script creates and destroys in one tick. Jolt's own body limit (§9.1) is checked with a diagnostic before it can be reached.

---

## 6. Serialization and file formats

All authored files are UTF-8 JSON, LF, tab-indented (per `.editorconfig`), written by the canonical `JsonWriter`:
- Header keys `"Format"` and `"Version"` first. Keys in registry order. Entities in canonical order. **PascalCase keys** in every authored file. (Automation envelopes use camelCase; component and asset data inside them keep PascalCase.)
- Floats: shortest round-trip representation of the `float` value (`std::to_chars` on `float`), `-0` written as `0`, NaN/Inf rejected. Default-valued fields are written: explicit beats implicit for agents reading files. A file read therefore gives a fractional number back as the double its float's shortest text reads as (`0.8`), not as the double the float widens to (`0.800000011920929`). JSON computed from typed fields that is then kept verbatim beside JSON read from files, as a prefab override's `Value` is (§5.5), takes that form first (`JsonWriter::ToWrittenForm`, what a load gives back from a write), so the two compare equal when a file would hold the same data (World Tree's brief 21).
- **Load → save is byte-identical.** A test asserts it for every authored file under `Projects/`, `Tests/Projects/` (the M16 dry-run game, ADR 0026 decision 8, and M19's native test game, ADR 0030 decision 35) and `Tests/Data`, except the fixtures that are never engine input: `Tests/Data/Lint/` (seeded lint defects) and `Tests/Data/Provenance/` (the audit's byte-hash fixtures, ADR 0026 decision 6). Line-oriented logs are exempt from the canonical writer and from this test: `.jsonl` files (batch scaffolds, `BuildLog.jsonl`) and everything under a project's `Automation/` folder. `Provenance.json` is still written canonically, but it is not engine-consumed.
- **Strict reader.** `JsonReader` errors carry JSON pointers. Unknown fields warn; unknown components warn and are **preserved** on save (forward compatibility), their numbers written as `float` like every authored number. A native component (`"Native.<Name>"`, §11.11) is preserved the same way but is not unknown: it is never reported as `SCENE_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT`, so a strict load keeps it too, and whether the loaded module registers it is the native layer's check (`NATIVE_COMPONENT_UNREGISTERED`, ADR 0030 decision 27). An unknown component holding a fractional number outside `float`'s range, which `JsonWriter` could not write back, is `SCENE_INVALID_COMPONENT` instead: an error in a strict load, dropped and reported by a repair load (ADR 0025). `Editor --strict` (§12.1) turns these warnings into errors for every project the editor opens (`--project`, `project.open`, `project.create`, recovery): unknown keys of the `.eproj`, and unknown keys, fields and components, and script field values that do not resolve or match, in its scenes and prefabs; and a settings patch (`ProjectSettingsCommand::CreateFromPatch`: `project.setSettings`, the inspector, the validator's fixes) naming a member the settings do not have is refused instead of dropped with a warning (§13.5). It also requires every scene and prefab under `Assets/` to load strictly when the project opens, so one that does not for any other reason (a structural defect, a file that cannot be read or parsed, a newer `Version`) refuses the project too, naming the file. The feature, determinism and export suites pass it over the committed FeatureTest (§15.8), and the Runtime always reads the project settings embedded in `Game.pak` strictly. `.meta` files are engine-written, so their reader refuses unknown members, and `Settings` holding a fractional number outside `float`'s range, with a Validation error (§6.4). A file whose `Version` is newer than the reader supports fails with `UnsupportedVersion`, naming both versions.
- **Structural pre-validation.** Scene and prefab loaders validate the whole entity graph **before** creating any entity. Merge results and hand edits are expected inputs, so each case returns a located `Result` (JSON pointer), never an assert: duplicate entity IDs, an invalid or zero ID, a `Parent` that does not exist (dangling) or forms a cycle, a `PrefabLink` whose `InstanceRoot` is missing or not an instance root, a member whose root lacks `PrefabInstanceComponent`, an `OuterPrefabEntityID` that names no enclosing instance and a nested instance root that records overrides (`SCENE_INCONSISTENT_PREFAB_LINK`), and a duplicated unique-per-scene component. A child listed before its parent is accepted and normalized to canonical order, with the warning `SCENE_NONCANONICAL_ORDER`. Asserts (`CreateEntityWithID`) are reserved for in-memory API misuse. Strict loading (Play copy, Runtime, export) fails on any error. **Repair loading** (`scene.open {repair: true}`, `project.validate {fix}`) applies deterministic fixes and reports each one: the later duplicate gets a fresh ID, orphans are reparented to the root, a cycle is cut at its first back-edge in file order, inconsistent prefab members are unpacked (an inconsistent `OuterPrefabEntityID` is cleared, a nested root's overrides dropped), and extra unique components are dropped (their JSON goes into the report). Each case has a fixture under `Tests/Data/Scenes/Invalid/`, in addition to the mutation fuzz test.
- **Migrations** are pure `json → json` functions: file-level (`Version`) and per component (`ComponentVersions`). Every migration has a golden fixture in `Tests/Data/Formats/`, and fixtures for every old version must keep loading. `project.upgrade` (§13.5) rewrites a project's files in the current canonical form and records the rewrite in provenance.
- **Enum spelling.** Files always contain the registry's PascalCase enum names. Readers of authored files are strict (exact case). Automation parses enum values case-insensitively (`"tap"`, `"Tap"`) and responses echo the canonical spelling.
- Extensions: `.eproj`, `.scene`, `.prefab`, `.material`, `.sfx`, `.meta`, `.replay`, `.spritesheet` (from M18), `.tilemap` (from M21), `.stringtable` (from M22), `.graph` (from M24), `.jsonl` (batch). M26's binary sources, `.irradiance` and `.heightfield`, and its imported `.cube` LUTs are not JSON (ADR 0037 decision 3), so the load-save identity of authored JSON does not cover them: a `.heightfield` (§6.12) is the 8-byte source header (`"EHFD"`, then the `uint32` version 1) and §6.8's heightfield payload, written byte for byte the same by every path that makes one. Generated JSON Schemas go to `Docs/Reference/Schemas/`.

### 6.1 Project (`RollingBall.eproj`, abridged)
```json
{
	"Format": "Project", "Version": 1, "Name": "RollingBall",
	"StartScene": "Assets/Scenes/Level1.scene",
	"Window": { "Title": "Rolling Ball", "Width": 1280, "Height": 720, "VSync": true, "Fullscreen": false, "Resizable": false },
	"Simulation": { "FixedHz": 60, "MaxStepsPerFrame": 5, "Seed": 27, "MaxEntities": 65536 },
	"Physics": {
		"Gravity": [0, -9.81, 0],
		"Layers": ["Default", "Ball", "Track", "Trigger"],
		"Collisions": [["Ball", "Track"], ["Ball", "Trigger"]]
	},
	"Input": { "Actions": {
		"MoveX": { "Type": "Axis", "Positive": ["Key.D", "Key.Right"], "Negative": ["Key.A", "Key.Left"], "Gamepad": "Gamepad.LeftX", "Invert": false },
		"MoveZ": { "Type": "Axis", "Positive": ["Key.W", "Key.Up"], "Negative": ["Key.S", "Key.Down"], "Gamepad": "Gamepad.LeftY", "Invert": false },
		"Restart": { "Type": "Button", "Bindings": ["Key.R", "Gamepad.Start"] }
	} },
	"Rendering": { "ShadowMapSize": 2048, "SsaoHalfResolution": false, "MaxShadedLights": 256, "SsrHalfResolution": false },
	"Scripting": { "MemoryLimitMB": 256, "CallbackBudgetMs": 1000, "PauseOnError": true, "BlockPlayOnTypeErrors": true },
	"Export": {
		"BuildScenes": ["Assets/Scenes/Level1.scene", "Assets/Scenes/Level2.scene", "Assets/Scenes/Level3.scene"],
		"Exclude": ["Assets/Tests/**"], "Icon": "", "Version": "1.0.0", "Company": "Engine Demos",
		"PruneUnreferenced": false
	},
	"Testing": {
		"Suites": [
			{ "Script": "Assets/Tests/Logic.test.luau", "Scene": "", "Modes": ["Editor", "Release", "Dist"] },
			{ "Script": "Assets/Tests/RollingBall.test.luau", "Scene": "Assets/Scenes/Level1.scene", "Modes": ["Editor", "Release", "Dist"] },
			{ "Script": "Assets/Tests/Frames.test.luau", "Scene": "Assets/Scenes/Level1.scene", "Clock": [0.1], "Modes": ["Editor", "Release", "Dist"] },
			{ "Script": "Assets/Tests/Autopilot/Level1.test.luau", "Scene": "Assets/Scenes/Level1.scene", "Modes": ["Editor"] },
			{ "Script": "Assets/Tests/Autopilot/Level2.test.luau", "Scene": "Assets/Scenes/Level2.scene", "Parameters": { "ElapsedTicks": 1500 }, "Modes": ["Editor"] },
			{ "Script": "Assets/Tests/Autopilot/Level3.test.luau", "Scene": "Assets/Scenes/Level3.scene", "Parameters": { "ElapsedTicks": 3600 }, "Modes": ["Editor"] }
		],
		"Replays": ["Assets/Tests/Replays/*.replay"],
		"CaseTimeoutTicks": 600, "SuiteTickLimit": 36000, "CoverageGates": false
	},
	"SortingLayers": { "Layers": ["Default"] },
	"Physics2D": { "Gravity": [0, -9.81] },
	"Localization": { "Locale": "" },
	"Ui": {
		"Navigation": false, "Submit": ["Key.Enter", "Key.Space", "Gamepad.South"], "Cancel": ["Key.Escape", "Gamepad.East"],
		"Up": ["Key.Up", "Gamepad.DPadUp"], "Down": ["Key.Down", "Gamepad.DPadDown"], "Left": ["Key.Left", "Gamepad.DPadLeft"],
		"Right": ["Key.Right", "Gamepad.DPadRight"], "Next": ["Key.Tab"], "StickNavigation": false
	}
}
```
Abridged from Rolling Ball's committed file: the file writes every member, each action's empty `Bindings`, `Positive`, `Negative` and `Gamepad` and each suite's `Parameters` (null when unset), `Isolation`, `Clock`, `Overrides` and `ExpectQuit` included. `Input.Actions` is a `Map` (keys sorted on save). `Scripting.CallbackBudgetMs` (minimum 10) applies in every configuration. Dist builds raise an effective budget below 5,000 ms to 5,000 ms, so slow player machines hitch instead of disabling scripts; test runs apply per-suite overrides exactly (§11.10). `Export.Icon` (a square PNG, ≥ 256²), `Version` (`major.minor.patch`) and `Company` (valid UTF-8 without control characters, U+FFFE or U+FFFF, at most `ExportSettings::MaxCompanyBytes` = 32,000 bytes, so `VS_VERSIONINFO` and `Info.plist`, an XML 1.0 document, can carry it on every host; a violation is a Validation error at `/Export/Company`, and the same text rule, `FindExportTextProblem`, checks every string of `Info.plist`; ADR 0025) go into the exported executable's resources (§14.2). `Export.PruneUnreferenced` (off by default) makes an export package only the assets that `StartScene`, `Export.BuildScenes` and a testing export's test content reach (§7.6; ADR 0030 decision 21). The `Testing` keys are defined in §11.10. `Localization.Locale` (M22, ADR 0033 decision 11) is the locale `Loc.Get` reads string tables in (§6.10, §11.5): empty, or a locale tag of §6.10's form (a Validation error at `/Localization/Locale` otherwise); it is the locale a play session starts in, unless the session is started in another (`play.start {locale}`, the Runtime's `--locale`, a suite's `Locale` or the run's, a replay's header; M38, ADR 0052 and ADR 0055 decision 3), and the edit evaluation's VM's; `Loc.SetLocale` changes a running session's (§5.6, §11.5), which supersedes ADR 0033 decision 11's VM fixed for its life. A suite's `Locale` is §11.10's. `Ui` (M22 C22.2, ADR 0033 decision 30) is the keyboard and gamepad navigation of the game's UI (§4.3, §5.7 step 1b): each of `Submit`, `Cancel`, `Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right` and `Next` lists the controls of its command in an input action's binding form, at most 16 unique, non-empty names (a Validation error at `/Ui/<list>` or `/Ui/<list>/<index>`), and a play session's start refuses a name that does not parse or names a mouse control or a gamepad axis, with a Validation error at `/Ui/<list>/<index>`, as an action's binding fails at `/Input/Actions`; `Navigation` false reads none of them and no stick, so focus moves only by the pointer and `Ui.SetFocus`, and `StickNavigation` false leaves the left stick out. Navigation moves focus only from a focused widget, or to a canvas's `DefaultFocus` while nothing has focus, so a game whose play uses the arrows and Space keeps them. `Physics.Layers` holds 1 to 16 names (§9.2; ADR 0014 decision 4, which amends ADR 0006 decision 11) and each `Physics.Gravity` component lies within ±1e12 m/s² (`MaxPhysicsGravity`, ADR 0014 decision 34). `SortingLayers.Layers` (M21; ADR 0032 decision 4) names the sorting layers sprites draw in, back to front: 1 to 32 unique non-empty names, the first `Default`, as `Physics.Layers`. A SpriteRenderer's `SortingLayer` names one; an undeclared name draws in the first (`SPRITE_UNKNOWN_SORTING_LAYER`). Every host copies the list into its render extraction request, as it copies `Rendering` (§8.2). `Physics2D.Gravity` (M21; ADR 0032 decision 9) is the 2D world's gravity, a `vec2` in m/s² whose components each lie within ±1e12 (`MaxPhysicsGravity`); the 2D world's layers are `Physics.Layers` (§9.9).

### 6.2 Scene (`Level1.scene`, an excerpt)
```json
{
	"Format": "Scene", "Version": 1, "Name": "Level1", "Seed": 0,
	"ComponentVersions": { "Transform": 1, "Prefab": 2, "PrefabLink": 1, "MeshRenderer": 1, "Camera": 1, "DirectionalLight": 1, "Environment": 1, "PostProcess": 2, "RigidBody": 1,
		"BoxCollider": 1, "SphereCollider": 1, "AudioSource": 1, "Script": 2, "UiCanvas": 1, "UiRect": 1, "UiImage": 1, "UiText": 1, "ParticleEmitter": 1, "Terrain": 1 },
	"Entities": [
		{
			"ID": "89e29e81b64dbde8", "Name": "Ball", "Parent": null, "Active": true, "Tags": ["Ball"],
			"Components": {
				"Transform": { "Translation": [0, 0.6, -3], "Rotation": [0, 0, 0, 1], "Scale": [1, 1, 1] },
				"Prefab": { "Prefab": "6fcd26eb0836aaac", "Overrides": [ { "Path": ["478096c60af9f02a"], "Kind": "Field", "Component": "Script", "Field": "Scripts/0/Fields", "Value": { "KillHeight": -8 } } ] },
				"PrefabLink": { "PrefabEntityID": "478096c60af9f02a", "InstanceRoot": "89e29e81b64dbde8", "OuterPrefabEntityID": null },
				"MeshRenderer": { "Mesh": "0000000000000102", "Materials": ["52eb3da5098abad7"], "CastShadows": true, "ReceiveShadows": true, "Visible": true },
				"RigidBody": { "Type": "Dynamic", "Mass": 1, "Friction": 0.8, "MotionQuality": "LinearCast", "Layer": "Ball", "MaxAngularVelocity": 120, "EnhancedInternalEdgeRemoval": true },
				"SphereCollider": { "Radius": 0.5, "Offset": [0, 0, 0], "IsTrigger": false },
				"AudioSource": { "Clip": "6d00294947a32653", "Volume": 0, "Loop": true, "PlayOnStart": true, "Spatial": true, "Group": "Sfx" },
				"Script": { "Scripts": [ { "Script": "392c104c7cf0be3c", "Fields": { "FallSound": "b20be608a1f8d9e2", "KillHeight": -8 }, "ExecutionOrder": 0 } ] }
			}
		}
	]
}
```
(An excerpt of Rolling Ball's committed scene: one of its entities, the ball, an instance of `Ball.prefab`, with the `RigidBody` and `AudioSource` field lists abridged; real files contain every entity and every field.) A game with a native module (§11.11) writes each native component under `Components` as `"Native.<Name>": { ... }` after the built-ins, with the `ComponentVersions` entry 1 (`NativeComponentVersion`): the entity keeps it as written, with or without the module loaded, among its preserved components (`UnknownComponentsComponent`). With the module loaded it is canonical, every field in registration order in its kind's form, and an entity's native components are sorted by name ahead of its unknown ones (ADR 0030 decision 27). The `Script` component (version 2) is a list of slots, each its own behaviour (§5.3). A prefab instance root, as the ball is, adds `"Prefab": { "Prefab": "<handle>", "Overrides": [ { "Path": ["<prefab-local id>"], "Kind": "Field", "Component": "Transform", "Field": "Scale", "Value": [1, 2, 1] } ] }` (`Prefab` version 2; keys in file order; §5.5 lists the kinds and the paths of nested instances' entities) and members, the root among them (its `InstanceRoot` its own id), add `"PrefabLink": { "PrefabEntityID": "<prefab-local id>", "InstanceRoot": "<root id>", "OuterPrefabEntityID": null }` (the id in the enclosing prefab on a nested instance root, §5.5), both under `Components`.

### 6.3 Prefab (`Block.prefab`)
Identical entity schema with `"Format": "Prefab"`, a `"Root": "<local id>"` key, and no `Seed`. Any entity but the root may hold `Prefab` and `PrefabLink` components: the live instances of other prefabs the prefab nests, expanded with their overrides as a scene holds them (§5.5; `PREFAB_NESTED_INSTANCE` on the root entity). The prefab importer lists every prefab a document nests in its import dependencies.

### 6.4 Asset metadata (`Track.glb.meta`)
Every asset file, native or foreign, has a sidecar. The registry is rebuilt by scanning `.meta` files; there is no central registry file to conflict in merges.
```json
{
	"Format": "AssetMeta", "Version": 1,
	"Handle": "3c9f2e7a11d04b88", "Type": "Prefab", "Importer": "Gltf", "ImporterVersion": 3,
	"Settings": { "Scale": 1.0, "GenerateMissingTangents": true, "ImportMaterials": true, "MergeMeshes": false,
		"AnimationEvents": [ { "Animation": "animation:0:Wave", "Name": "Step", "Time": 0.25 } ] },
	"SubAssets": [
		{ "Key": "mesh:0:Straight", "Handle": "77e1a0c4d2b95f01", "Type": "Mesh" },
		{ "Key": "material:0:TrackPBR", "Handle": "77e1a0c4d2b95f02", "Type": "Material" },
		{ "Key": "texture:0", "Handle": "77e1a0c4d2b95f03", "Type": "Texture" }
	]
}
```
Sub-asset keys are stable glTF identities (kind, index, name), so reimporting a modified file keeps every handle. `AnimationEvents` (GltfImporter version 3, ADR 0034 decision 25) lists the named events of the imported animation clips by clip key, since glTF has none; a meta written before version 3 has no such field and reads as no events.

Files that a glTF references (external `.bin` buffers, and images that have no meta of their own) get a **dependency meta** instead of an importer of their own: `{"Format": "AssetMeta", "Version": 1, "Handle": "…", "Type": "Dependency", "Owner": "<gltf handle>"}`. A dependency is never loaded on its own, never imported a second time by `TextureImporter`, and moves, is deleted and is trashed together with its owner. An image that already has a `Texture` meta is not converted: the glTF's material references that standalone texture handle instead of creating a `texture:` sub-asset, so the same texture is never imported twice.

### 6.5 Material (`Red.material`)
```json
{
	"Format": "Material", "Version": 2,
	"BaseColor": [0.9, 0.15, 0.15, 1], "BaseColorMap": null, "BaseColorUVSet": "UV0", "Metallic": 0, "Roughness": 0.45,
	"MetallicRoughnessMap": null, "MetallicRoughnessUVSet": "UV0", "NormalMap": null, "NormalUVSet": "UV0", "NormalScale": 1,
	"OcclusionMap": null, "OcclusionUVSet": "UV0", "OcclusionStrength": 1,
	"Emissive": [0, 0, 0], "EmissiveStrength": 1, "EmissiveMap": null, "EmissiveUVSet": "UV0",
	"AlphaMode": "Opaque", "AlphaCutoff": 0.5, "DoubleSided": false, "UVScale": [1, 1], "UVOffset": [0, 0]
}
```
Material version 2 (M23, ADR 0034 decision 10) puts each map's texture coordinate set (`TextureCoordinateSet`: `UV0`, the mesh's first set, or `UV1`, its second, §6.8) after the map; one `UVScale` and `UVOffset` still transform every map, and the vertex colour, which has no field, always multiplies the base colour (§8.5). A version 1 file loads with every set `UV0` and saves as version 2, so `Editor --upgrade` rewrites it canonically; materials are not in the scene serialization, so the upgrade changes no state hash.

### 6.6 Sound effect (`LineClear.sfx`)
A procedural audio source, so agents can create sound without external files (§10.3). It cooks to 48 kHz mono 16-bit PCM.
```json
{
	"Format": "SoundEffect", "Version": 1, "Seed": 7, "Volume": 0.8,
	"Layers": [
		{ "Wave": "Square", "DutyCycle": 0.5, "Notes": ["C5:0.06", "E5:0.06", "G5:0.06", "C6:0.18"],
		  "Envelope": { "Attack": 0.005, "Decay": 0.05, "Sustain": 0.6, "Release": 0.08 } },
		{ "Wave": "Noise", "Duration": 0.05, "StartFrequency": 4000, "EndFrequency": 800, "Volume": 0.3,
		  "Envelope": { "Attack": 0.0, "Decay": 0.05, "Sustain": 0.0, "Release": 0.0 } }
	]
}
```
A layer may also set `LowPass` (the one-pole low-pass of §10.3) and `Delay` (its start offset in seconds). A note is `"<Name><Octave>:<seconds>"` in equal temperament (A4 = 440 Hz) or a rest `"R:<seconds>"`, played back to back, with at most 7 digits before and 8 after the decimal point; a layer without notes is a tone of `Duration` sweeping exponentially from `StartFrequency` to `EndFrequency`, holding `EndFrequency` during its release. Each note has its own linear ADSR whose release follows the note's end (tails overlap and sum); Noise is a seeded sample-and-hold at the frequency that draws its first value at each note's start; the low-pass runs over the layer's span, from its delay to the end of its last release. Every duration is converted to whole frames once, F(s) = floor(double(s) × 48000 + 0.5), and lengths are sums of frames, so synthesis is bit-exact. Limits: 1 to 16 layers, 256 notes per layer, at least one frame per layer and at most 10 s (480,000 frames) per sound; range checks compare with the bounds rounded to float, as the type registry does. `Audio/SoundSynth.h` holds the full semantics (ADR 0015 decisions 11 and 23). The shipped `engine://Audio/LineClear` preset plays this example's square layer at `Volume` 0.6 and the sound at 0.7, because the overlapping release tails clip at the example's levels (ADR 0015 decision 24).

### 6.7 Input replay (`Opening.replay`) and automation batch (`Scaffold.jsonl`)
```json
{
	"Format": "Replay", "Version": 5,
	"Scene": { "Handle": "8a61c0d2e4f31b77", "Path": "Assets/Scenes/Level2.scene" },
	"Parameters": { "Time": 61.25 },
	"Seed": 7, "FixedHz": 60, "EngineVersion": "0.8.0", "Config": "Editor", "Locale": "",
	"SaveData": { "BestWave": 12 },
	"Fingerprint": {
		"Entities": [ { "Id": "1d0b3c5e7f9a2b4c", "Path": "/Ball", "Hash": "6c1e0f9a3b5d7e21", "Components": { "Transform": "0a4f6e2c8d1b3957", "Script": "c3e5a7f9b1d2046e" } } ],
		"Assets": [ { "Handle": "5f2e8a1c3b7d9046", "Path": "Assets/Scripts/Ball.luau", "Type": "Script", "Hash": "e9b7c5a3f1d20864" } ]
	},
	"Events": [
		{ "Tick": 0, "Type": "Action", "Name": "MoveZ", "Value": 1.0 },
		{ "Tick": 40, "Type": "Action", "Name": "MoveX", "Value": 0.35 },
		{ "Tick": 90, "Type": "Action", "Name": "MoveX", "Value": 0.0 },
		{ "Tick": 100, "Type": "Action", "Name": "Jump", "State": "Tap" },
		{ "Tick": 140, "Type": "Key", "Key": "Escape", "State": "Down" },
		{ "Tick": 141, "Type": "Key", "Key": "Escape", "State": "Up" },
		{ "Tick": 145, "Type": "Signal", "Name": "FrameTimeExceeded" }
	],
	"Expect": [ { "Tick": 150, "Luau": "return Scene.GetName() == 'Level3'" } ],
	"Checkpoints": [ { "Tick": 60, "StateHash": "9b1d5e0c27a4f381" }, { "Tick": 120, "StateHash": "51c7a0e9d2b64f18" } ],
	"FinalTick": 150, "FinalStateHash": "3e0c91a2b4d5f607"
}
```
- **Header.** `Scene` names the start scene by handle (authoritative) and path (readable; a moved scene still resolves). `Parameters` are the `Scene.Load` parameters the scene starts with, so Level 2 and Level 3 replays begin exactly as they would after the previous level. Like every authored file (§6), the header stores floats as float; a recording therefore starts its session from the parameters in that stored form (a value outside the float range is refused when the recording starts), so the recorded run and its replays read identical `Scene.GetLoadParameters()` values. `EngineVersion` is the version of the engine that recorded the replay: every recorder writes `EngineVersionString` (`session.hello`'s `engineVersion`), never the build id, which lives in session results, `Engine.pak` and `Game.json` (ADR 0030 decision 13), so a commit rewrites no replay; replays recorded before ADR 0038 (friction F10) hold `0.1.0`, which every recorder wrote until then. It is informational: no verification and no state hash reads it, so a committed replay keeps the version it was recorded with (Tetris's, Breakout's and NativeTest's `0.1.0`; Rolling Ball's `0.5.0`, recorded again by its session S5 after M27's bump, ADR 0038's session record). A version bump changes the header of every new recording, FeatureTest's replays included, which its scaffolds record and `Scaffold.py --check` compares byte for byte, so the bumping commit regenerates FeatureTest (ADR 0038 decision 13). `Config` records where the replay was made: it is the run mode of the recording process (`Editor`, `Release` or `Dist`), never the build configuration, so a Debug and a Release build record byte-identical replays (ADR 0022 "Integration"). With cross-configuration determinism (§9.1), it is informational, and a replay verifies in every configuration. `FinalStateHash` is the state hash at `FinalTick`. `input.replay {verify: true, strictHash: true}` compares it, and the determinism stage always does (§15.8).
- **SaveData** (version 4, M28, ADR 0043 decision 7) is the session's save-data store at the recording's start (its values by key, `{}` when empty), which seeds every playback's store, so a replay verifies whatever the machine's store holds; unlike every other authored number it stores the store's numbers as doubles, written exactly (`JsonWriter`'s `JsonNumbers::Double`, in the file and the cooked replay), so a recording starts from the store as it is and a large count or a timestamp keeps its value. A file of version 1 to 3 migrates with an empty one.
- **Locale** (version 5, M38, ADR 0055 decisions 4 and 5) is the locale the recorded session started in (empty or a tag, never null in a recording), which every verification path starts its playback in (`input.replay`, `input.record`'s stop verification, `test.run`, the Runtime's `--feature-test` and `--replay`); `ReplayPlayer::Begin` refuses a session started in another, naming both. A file of version 1 to 4 migrates with a null `Locale`, which plays in the project's `Localization.Locale`, and `project.upgrade` writes it so.
- **Checkpoints** (version 2, M16 friction S2-01) are the state hashes the recording observed along its run: the recorders (`input.record`, `test.run {record}`) store one at every positive multiple of `ReplayCheckpointInterval` (60) ticks before `FinalTick`, taken at the completed-tick boundary each fixed step starts from (`ReplayRecorder::CaptureCheckpoint`), which the previous tick's frame phase and pending `Scene.Load` complete: a step that follows the previous one in the same frame, as under a FeatureTest suite's scripted `Clock` that runs several steps per frame, starts from no completed boundary, so its tick gets no checkpoint even at a multiple of 60 (ADR 0026, milestone review R17); a reader accepts any strictly increasing ticks between 0 and `FinalTick`. Under `strictHash`, every verification path (`input.replay`, `test.run`'s replay rows, the FeatureTest runner in every mode, the Runtime's `--replay --verify` and the Dist `--feature-test` player through the cooked replay, the determinism and games suites) compares each checkpoint as playback reaches its tick, after that boundary's expectations, and stops at the first that differs, naming the tick and both hashes; with `continuePastCheckpoint` (the input checks, §13.6) it plays on to `FinalTick`, counting every checkpoint that differs and keeping the first. Without checkpoints a replay whose run ends where it began (an autopilot that restarts in place before `FinalTick`) would verify while proving nothing about its play. A version 1 file has no `Checkpoints`; it is read with none (only `FinalStateHash` is compared), and `project.upgrade` rewrites it (§13.12). The cooked replay (FormatVersion 3) carries the checkpoints and the fingerprint.
- **Fingerprint** (version 3, M19, ADR 0030 decision 2) is what the recording's session held at tick 0, so a playback whose state hash differs names what changed: every entity of the scene sorted by id, with its own members' hash (id, name, parent, active flag, tags) and each component's hash in the order scene files write them, and every asset an `AssetRef` value of those components names (a Script component's script and its asset fields among them), sorted by handle, with the XXH64 of its cooked artifact (`AssetManager::GetCookedHash`, which an exported pak's table of contents shares). Every hash is XXH64 as 16 lowercase hex digits, taken from the scene's minified canonical serialization, the document the state hash covers; paths are readable and never compared. Every recording writes it (`test.run`'s concatenated recording keeps its first segment's), so a recording whose session references an asset whose cooked hash cannot be taken (an import that failed) is refused, naming the asset (`input.record`'s `start`, `test.run {record}` as an invalidated recording; in the editor, an asset in error that the scene references already refuses play and with it `input.record` and `input.replay`, §12.4); a playback with its input whose checkpoint or final hash differs compares it with its own and names each entity added, removed or changed, then each component, then each asset, at most 16 lines (`changes` in `input.replay`'s result, the first ending its error's message, a checkpoint's stop reason and `test.run`'s `Checkpoint@<tick>` and `FinalStateHash` rows). A playback's own fingerprint only explains a difference: when it cannot be taken, the playback still plays to its verdict, and a hash that differs names that error as its one change (`not known, because the playback's start fingerprint could not be taken: <error>`; the review of W19.1). Only direct references are fingerprinted (an accepted limit). A version 1 or 2 file reads as version 3 with a null `Fingerprint`, which names nothing until the replay is recorded again.
- **Events** use exactly the event set of automation input (§13.6), with PascalCase keys and enum values in the file: `Action {Name, State | Value}`, `Key {Key, State}`, `MouseButton {Button, State, Position?}`, `MouseMove {Position}`, `MouseDelta {Delta}`, `Scroll {Delta}`, `GamepadButton {Gamepad, Button, State}`, `GamepadAxis {Gamepad, Axis, Value}`, `Text {Text}`, and from version 4 `Signal {Name}` (M28, ADR 0043 decision 6: a frame-time signal, `Input.PostSignal`). `State` is one of `Down`, `Up` and `Tap`. A recording writes the events that were actually applied at step 1 of each tick, whatever their source (§13.6).
- **Expect** entries are Luau expressions whose value must be truthy JSON: one that is not JSON fails its expectation with its Script error, a vector, `Color` or `Quat` included, which only `script.eval` returns as the array of its components (§13.6; ADR 0038's milestone review), so a mistaken `return position` fails instead of holding. The editor compiles them at record time and on every save, so a syntax error is a located diagnostic.
