- **Headless.** No surface, no swapchain; the final image lands in an `OffscreenTarget`, read by `Readback::ReadTexture(texture) -> Result<Image>` (staging texture with `CpuAccessMode::Read`, `copyTexture`, `mapStagingTexture`).

Directional shadow casters are pancaked per fragment in the shadow shader, with no Vulkan feature (§8.7): NVRHI does not expose `depthClampEnable`, and the engine requests no `depthClamp` feature. `GraphicsSpecification::DisableDepthClamp` turns pancaking off (`GraphicsDeviceInfo::DepthClamp` false), so casters are clipped at the extended light near plane instead. It defaults to false, applies in every configuration and has no CLI option. This permits deterministic testing of the extended-near shadow fallback (§8.7, §15.3; ADR 0017).

### 8.2 Frame structure and the render snapshot
`Scene/RenderExtraction` builds a plain `RenderSnapshot` per view; the renderer never sees the ECS, so it is tested with synthetic snapshots.
```cpp
struct RenderSnapshot
{
	bool HasCamera;                          // false: no camera (clear to the default colour, screen texts only)
	CameraData Camera;                       // view, projection (reverse-Z), position, viewport, exposure
	std::pmr::vector<MeshDrawItem> Meshes;    // world matrix, mesh handle+version, material per submesh, flags, PickID; M31: material parameters
	std::pmr::vector<LightData> Lights;       // directional, point, spot (≤ Quality.MaxShadedLights shaded after CPU culling)
	RenderEnvironment Environment;            // handle, intensity, rotation, ShowSkybox, SkyboxBlur, FallbackColor
	PostProcessSettings Post;
	float Alpha;                              // the interpolation alpha the poses were extracted at (§5.2)
	std::pmr::vector<TextItem> Texts;
	DebugDrawList DebugDraw;                  // the view's ordinary debug primitives (scripts, gizmos)
	DebugDrawList AnnotationDraw;             // labels, bounds, axes, colliders (M9, RenderAnnotations)
	RenderDebugView DebugView;                // Lit, except a viewport.screenshot with debugView or the editor's debug view
	std::pmr::vector<UUID> PickTable;         // PickID - 1 → entity UUID (snapshot-local; M9)
	RenderViewFlags Flags;                    // EditorOverlays, Grid, Selection, Colliders, Icons, Picking, Wireframe (M9), Navigation (M30)
	std::vector<UUID> SelectedEntities;       // the selection outline's and "selected" labels' entities (M9)
	RenderAnnotations Annotations;            // capture annotations: labels, bounds, axes (M9)
	RenderQualitySettings Quality;            // ProjectSettings.Rendering: ShadowMapSize, SsaoHalfResolution (M9), MaxShadedLights (M29), SsrHalfResolution (M32)
	std::pmr::vector<RenderIcon> Icons;       // procedural world glyphs (M9)
	uint64_t FrameIndex, SceneRevision;       // host stamps echoed by statistics and picking (M9)
	RenderOutputSettings Output;              // scene resolution, pixel-art colour path, letterbox (M18, ADR 0029)
	std::pmr::vector<SpriteItem> Sprites;     // world matrix, sheet, frame, texture, colour, flips, pixels per unit, layer, order, lit, normal map (M21)
	std::pmr::vector<TilemapItem> Tilemaps;   // world matrix, tilemap, colour, pixels per unit, layer, order, lit, DrawPosition among Sprites (M21)
	std::pmr::vector<Light2DItem> Lights2D;   // the 2D lights in canonical order: type, rendered position, colour, intensity, radius, falloff, height (M21)
	UiDrawList Ui;                            // the UI's images and texts in scene pixels (a World canvas's in its own), draw order (M22, ADR 0033)
	RenderFog Fog;                            // the scene's Fog, after M26's members: Enabled and its fields (M32, ADR 0047; §8.6)
	std::pmr::vector<PlanarReflectionItem> PlanarReflections; // M42: the visible mirrors at their rendered pose, canonical order (§8.3)
};
class SceneRenderer
{
public:
	static Result<Scope<SceneRenderer>> Create(GraphicsDevice&, SceneRendererPipelines&, GpuResourceCache&, AssetManager&,
		const SceneRendererSpecification&);
	Status Resize(uint32_t width, uint32_t height);
	Status Render(nvrhi::ICommandList& commandList, const RenderSnapshot& snapshot);
	void OnSubmitted(uint64_t frameIndex, uint64_t submissionId); // after the list holding the Render executed
	nvrhi::ITexture* GetFinalTexture() const;   // RGBA8_UNORM, display-encoded, at the view's size
	// M9: GetEntityIdTexture, RequestPick/PollPick/CancelPicks, GetViewGeneration, GetRenderStats.
	RenderOutputMapping GetOutputMapping() const; // M18: the last Render's view-to-scene mapping (§8.3, the output stage)
};
// The passes every view of a device shares (§8.12): Create; M18's CreatePipelines (the one creation entry: startup, the
// shader reload and the device-loss recovery), GetGeneration and ReloadShaders.
class SceneRendererPipelines;
```
`DebugView` is a member of its own rather than a view flag, because a screenshot sets it independently of the view's flags; the pick table, the view flags and the other M9 members are defined by ADR 0017. `Render` returns an error without recording for an invalid `DebugView` or `Quality.ShadowMapSize`; partial errors (a non-finite matrix, invalid overlay data, a binding-set creation failure) still record the view and return the first error. Data the schemas accept is never a render error (a shadow-casting light the shadow planners reject stays lit without shadows, §8.7). `HasCamera` is false for a view without a camera (a game view without a primary camera), which clears to the default colour and draws only screen texts. `TextItem` carries a text's fields as extracted (space, anchor, pivot, offset, alignment, billboard, font, colour, size, the rendered world matrix and the entity); a World text's em is `Size / WorldTextPixelsPerMetre` (100) metres before the entity's scale. `DebugDraw` is empty after extraction and its producers append to it (§8.10; ADR 0013 decisions 5 and 6). `Sprites` (M21; ADR 0032 decisions 3 and 4) lists every effectively enabled SpriteRenderer in draw order, not canonical order: sorted stably by (sorting layer, `OrderInLayer`), so equal keys keep canonical order; a sprite's layer is its name's index in the request's `SortingLayers` (the project's `SortingLayers.Layers`, which every host copies as it copies `Rendering`: the play session's game view, the editor's views and thumbnails, `viewport.screenshot`, the FeatureTest runner and the Runtime), 0 for an undeclared name. Extraction never touches assets: the renderer resolves the sheet's frame, the texture and a lit sprite's `NormalMap`. `Tilemaps` (M21; ADR 0032 decision 24) lists every effectively enabled TilemapRenderer with a `Tilemap`, each placed in the one 2D draw order by its `DrawPosition`: it draws before `Sprites[DrawPosition]` (after every sprite at `Sprites.size()`), sorted with the sprites by (sorting layer, `OrderInLayer`, canonical entity order), so `Sprites` keeps its meaning; its tiles draw as sprites of their palette entries' frames (§8.3, the Sprites stage). `Lights2D` (M21; ADR 0032 decisions 20 and 22) lists every effectively enabled Light2D in canonical order, its position the rendered world matrix's translation; only lit sprites and tilemaps take them (§8.3, the Sprites stage).

The pixel-perfect camera (M21, `Docs/Decisions/0032-m21-contract.md` decision 6): `Output` keeps its defaults (the scene at the view's size) unless the view's camera entity, through the Primary or Entity camera source, holds a `PixelPerfectCamera`. Then extraction (`ComputePixelPerfectView`, `Scene/PixelPerfectCamera.h`) sets `Output` to the reference resolution with the 2D colour path and the component's letterbox colour, makes the projection orthographic with a half height of `ReferenceHeight / (2 PixelsPerUnit)` at the reference resolution's aspect whatever the Camera's own projection, takes the reference resolution as the camera's viewport, and snaps the camera's position so the view's left and bottom edges lie on the pixel grid (multiples of `1 / PixelsPerUnit`, rounded half away from zero; Z unchanged). The output stage then upscales the scene image by the largest integer factor that fits the view, in the letterbox; the editor's scene view (the Explicit source) ignores the component. Picking, `viewport.pick` and captures map view pixels through the snapshot's output mapping as for any output settings, and scripts' `Camera:ScreenToWorldRay` and `WorldToScreen` map their view coordinates through the same mapping (`MapViewPointToScenePoint`), so a ray through a view pixel passes through the scene pixel it shows, and a letterbox pixel's ray passes beside the image.

A frame: `BeginFrame` (wait on the event query of frame N-2, acquire or pick the offscreen target) → record the scene command list → record ImGui or blit → execute → present → `runGarbageCollection()`. The pass list is fixed (no render graph): NVRHI's automatic state tracking places barriers, and immutable resources (IBL cubes, LUTs, material textures) are `keepInitialState` textures in `ShaderResource`, so every command list starts and ends with them there while copies out of them (readback in tests) stay legal. Pass targets come from `RenderTargetPool` keyed by `TextureDesc`. Each pass is wrapped in `beginMarker` and a pooled timer query (`GpuProfiler`).

### 8.3 Pass list
Depth is **reverse-Z** everywhere: `D32_FLOAT`, clear 0, compare `GreaterOrEqual`, infinite far plane for perspective (`m[0][0] = f/aspect; m[1][1] = f; m[2][3] = -1; m[3][2] = zNear`). Orthographic cameras use a finite reverse-Z range, `d = (zFar + z_view) / (zFar − zNear)` (1 at the near plane, 0 at the far plane, linear in view depth). Every pass that reconstructs view-space data takes the projection type from `ViewConstants` (`ProjectionKind`, `OrthoHalfExtents`, `Near`, `Far`), never assuming perspective. Linear depth is `zNear / d` for perspective and `zFar − d · (zFar − zNear)` for orthographic. The view ray is `normalize(ndc.xy · tanHalfFov · aspect, −1)` for perspective, while orthographic uses the constant direction (0, 0, −1) and the origin `(ndc.xy · OrthoHalfExtents, 0)`. CPU tests cover both mappings and both reconstructions. Projections never flip Y: NVRHI's Vulkan backend gives every viewport a negative height (`VKViewportWithDXCoords`), so clip space has +Y up as in D3D, and pipelines use `frontCounterClockwise = true` to keep glTF's counter-clockwise front faces; a GPU test renders a CCW triangle with back-face culling and checks that it is visible and upright.

| # | Pass | Type | Output (format) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Prepare | CPU | constant/structured buffer uploads | frustum culling against submesh AABBs; opaque sorted by pipeline → material → mesh → submesh; transparent back-to-front, ties by UUID; light list ≤ `Rendering.MaxShadedLights` (256 by default; M29), chosen with hysteresis at the cap; one instance record per submesh draw (M23, below) |
| — | Skinning | compute | each deformed item's vertices (`MeshVertex`) and previous positions (`float4`) | M23 (ADR 0034 decision 27): one dispatch per skinned or morphed item a pass draws, one thread per vertex, before every pass that draws meshes (below) |
| 2 | Directional CSM | graphics | `ShadowCascades` D32_FLOAT 2048² × 4 array (`Rendering.ShadowMapSize`) | stable cascades (bounding-sphere fit + texel snapping), practical split λ, per-fragment pancaking (§8.7), slope-scaled bias × cascade texel size |
| 3 | Spot shadow atlas | graphics | `ShadowAtlas` D32_FLOAT 4096², ≤ 16 tiles of 1024² (8 before M29) | shadowed spot lights by screen importance; over budget → unshadowed + one-time warning |
| 4 | Depth/normal prepass | graphics | `SceneDepth` D32_FLOAT; `SceneNormals` RG16_FLOAT (octahedral, view space, normal-mapped); `EntityId` R32_UINT (views with `Picking`); M26's `SceneVelocity` RG16_FLOAT (motion vectors) and `SceneRoughness` RG32_UINT (SSR's composite inputs, ADR 0037 decision 14) | alpha-mask materials discard here; runs in wireframe too, so hidden edges are depth tested and picking stays geometric; M26: the targets' order is SceneNormals, (EntityId,) SceneVelocity, SceneRoughness, cleared to zero, written by the prepass and picking prepass (below) |
| 5 | Depth pyramid | compute | `ViewDepth` R16_FLOAT, 5 mips (linear view depth, projection-aware) | GTAO input; M26's SSR traces over it (recorded for SSR without GTAO too) |
| 6 | GTAO + denoise | compute | `AmbientOcclusion` R8_UNORM (full res; half on Low or `SsaoHalfResolution`) | §8.8 |
| — | Light clusters | compute | `LightClusterMasks` (structured buffer, `MaxShadedLights / 32` `uint` words per cluster: 8 by default, M29) | M23 (ADR 0034 decision 5): the clustered light loop's ordered bitmasks, one thread per cluster and word, no atomics; recorded when the light list holds a point or spot light and the Lit view's forward passes or the LightCount view read the masks |
| 7 | Forward opaque | graphics | `SceneColor` RGBA16_FLOAT | depth `GreaterOrEqual`, writes off; PBR + IBL + shadows + AO; the lights of the pixel's light cluster; M26: the baked probes' indirect term inside their boxes (§8.6); M32: the scene's fog over the result (§8.6) |
| — | TerrainForward | graphics | `SceneColor` | M26 (ADR 0037 decisions 13 and 22): the terrains' LOD chunks shaded like meshes (light loop, probes), after Forward opaque and before the skybox; their prepass, TerrainDepthNormal, follows pass 4 into its final targets |
| 8 | Skybox | graphics | `SceneColor` | pixels at depth 0; skybox cube at `SkyboxBlur` LOD; M32: fogged as the sky at infinite depth with the fog's `FogSkybox` (§8.6), and recorded too, drawing the camera's clear colour fogged as the sky, in a view fogged with `FogSkybox` whose cleared pixels no skybox draws over |
| — | SSR | compute, then graphics | `SsrColor` RGBA16_FLOAT, composited into `SceneColor` | M26 (ADR 0037 decision 18, `Renderer/SsrPass.h`): only with `SsrEnabled` in a Lit view outside the wireframe, before the transparent pass. The trace (compute) follows each pixel's reflection (a surface whose `SceneRoughness` roughness is at most `SsrMaxRoughness`, from one pixel's footprint above it) at most `SsrMaxDistance` metres across the depth pyramid's cells, a coarse cell whose nearest depth is behind the ray skipped whole, down to `SceneDepth`'s pixels, where a surface the ray passes within `SsrThickness` behind its depth, facing it, is its hit; `SsrColor` holds the hit's `SceneColor` radiance and a confidence fading with the distance, the screen's edge and the roughness (0 for a miss). The composite (added into `SceneColor`) evaluates the forward pass's probe or environment specular term from `SceneNormals` and `SceneRoughness` (ADR 0037 decision 14) and replaces it by the traced radiance times the same factor, in proportion to the confidence times `SsrIntensity`, so where a ray misses the probes' reflection stays; SSR off records nothing. M32 (ADR 0047 decisions 10 and 11): the cost follows the glossy area: a classification (compute) lists the trace image's 8 × 8 tiles that hold a tracing pixel, and the trace and the composite run indirectly over the listed tiles only (the image is the same: an unlisted tile traced nothing and added 0); `Rendering.SsrHalfResolution` traces at half resolution (each trace pixel the scene pixel at its footprint's centre, over the full-resolution pyramid) and the composite reconstructs each tracing pixel's reflection from four bilateral taps with GTAO's weights; three pipelines. In a fogged view the composite's addition is multiplied by `1 − a`, the fog's remaining transparency at the pixel (§8.6) |
| 9 | Forward transparent | graphics | `SceneColor` | sorted, alpha blend; material AO only (GTAO describes the opaque surface behind, §8.8); M32: fogged before it blends (§8.6) |
| 9a | Sprites | graphics | `SceneColor` (+ `SceneDepth`, tested without writes) | Lit view only, and not with the Lit view's `Wireframe`, which replaces the shaded image (M21): the snapshot's sprites in its draw order (painter's order), one `QuadBatcher` quad each in world space with the Point sampler, `Color` times the texel, unlit runs with the Hdr pipeline and lit runs with HdrLit, which also multiplies by 9b's light at the pixel, both in the view's fog (M32, §8.6); a quad wholly outside the view is culled. Tilemaps (C21.2, ADR 0032 decision 24) draw in the same order, each before the sprite its `DrawPosition` names: every tile a quad of the sprite of its palette entry's frame at the tilemap's world matrix times the translation to its cell's centre (byte-identical to the same tiles drawn as sprites), in the tilemap's cell order (rows from the top down, each left to right, across chunks), of the chunks whose bounds (the union of their tiles' quads, kept between renders and rebuilt when the tilemap, one of its sheets or `PixelsPerUnit` changes; released by a render that draws no 2D item) meet the view; at most `SceneRenderer::MaxTileQuadsPerView` (2^19, two `QuadBatcher` batches) tiles a view, the first in that order, the rest counted (`SceneRenderStats::DroppedTiles`) and logged once per view while every sprite still draws, and no quad vector kept beyond one batch after the render (M21's milestone review) |
| 9b | Lights2D | graphics | `Lights2DNormals` RGBA16_FLOAT (+ `SceneDepth`, tested without writes), `Lights2DLight` RGBA16_FLOAT, at the scene resolution | only when a drawn sprite or tile is lit (M21, ADR 0032 decision 22), recorded before 9a's quads: the lit quads' world normals, then every 2D light that reaches the view added into the light accumulation (below) |
| — | Particles | graphics | `SceneColor`, and `SceneVelocity` with TAA (`SceneDepth` read as a texture, never written) | M26 (ADR 0037 decision 7, `Renderer/ParticlePass.h`): after the sprites and 2D lights, Lit view only, and not with the Lit view's `Wireframe` (as 9a): the snapshot's particles, each a quad of its size by its emitter's alignment (M33, ADR 0048 decisions 3 to 6: Camera, a square facing the camera, its edges along the view's right and up axes turned by the particle's angle; Velocity, stretched along its velocity across the view; Flat, a square in the emitter's local XZ plane) in its colour (its RGB times its `ParticleLook`'s `Intensity`, so above 1 for HDR) times its emitter's texture (null: the built-in `engine://Textures/Particle`, a soft white disc; a missing one its placeholder) or, with a flipbook, its phase's frame of the look's sprite sheet blended toward the next, sampled Linear (Point in pixel-art mode); emitters in snapshot order, an Alpha emitter's particles back to front in the view (ties in particle order) with the `ParticlesAlpha` pipeline (straight alpha), an Additive emitter's in their order with `ParticlesAdditive` (colour times alpha added); a particle wholly outside the view is culled and one with a non-finite position, colour or angle or a size not above 0 is skipped. M33 draws them with a program of its own, `Particles` (three pipelines, none with a depth attachment: §8.3 never attaches `SceneDepth` read-only, so the fragments read it as a texture and cover nothing behind the scene's depth, the test the QuadBatcher's pipelines made, and a soft particle fades over its `SoftDistance` of view depth before the surface behind it), on the jittered grid of the 3D passes (`ViewConstants::ViewProjection`); with TAA the same quads again with `ParticlesVelocity` write the motion each particle was drawn with since the view's previous render (its previous position matched by emitter and serial, `RenderViewHistory`) where its alpha is at least 0.5; its pipelines, samplers and buffers are `SceneRendererPipelines`', its binding sets the view's |
| — | TAA | compute | `SceneColor` resolved, `TaaHistory` RGBA16_FLOAT (two images, ping-ponged) | M26 (ADR 0037 decisions 10 and 17, `Renderer/TaaPass.h`): the jittered HDR image resolved against its history reprojected by the motion vectors, clamped to the current 3 × 3 neighbourhood in YCoCg, with a fixed feedback (0.9) and no random term, then copied back into `SceneColor`; first in HdrPost, only with `AntiAliasing` Taa in a Lit view outside the wireframe and pixel-art mode (below) |
| — | Overdraw | graphics | `Overdraw` RGBA16_FLOAT | the Overdraw data view only: additive geometric coverage of every draw, depth-independent; replaces passes 7–9 |
| 10 | Bloom | compute | `Bloom` R11G11B10_FLOAT (RGBA16_FLOAT when unsupported as storage, §8.1), 6-mip chain from half res | 13-tap downsample, Karis average on the first mip, 3×3 tent upsample, `lerp(scene, bloom, BloomIntensity)` |
| — | Exposure | compute | the renderer's histogram and adapted-exposure buffers | M26 (ADR 0037 decision 15): the luminance histogram of the image Tonemap exposes and the adapted exposure, after Bloom, only with `ExposureMode` Auto outside pixel-art mode |
| 11 | Tonemap + encode | compute | `LdrColor` RGBA8_UNORM | exposure 2^EV (M26: times the adapted exposure with Auto), tonemapper, M26's grading LUT, sRGB OETF in shader, blue-noise triangular dither (±1 LSB) |
| 12 | FXAA 3.11 | compute | `LdrColor` (ping-pong) | optional |
| 13 | Text | graphics | `LdrColor` (+ `SceneDepth`, tested without writes) | game text, SDF: world (depth-tested) then screen, at the scene resolution (M18: before the editor overlays; M22's UI after it) |
| — | Ui | graphics | `LdrColor` (+ `SceneDepth`, tested without writes for World canvases only) | M22 (ADR 0033 decision 7): the snapshot's UI draw list at the scene resolution, laid out in scene pixels, in draw order: images and 9-sliced sprite sheet frames through the QuadBatcher's Ldr pipeline (a missing sheet, reported once as an asset diagnostic, or a frame it lacks, draws nothing), texts laid out by the text-measurement layer and drawn as the Text pipelines' glyph runs (screen vertices on top), each run clipped by its scissor (a scroll view clips its descendants and moves its content by its clamped scroll position in the layout), then the capture's UI annotations unclipped. Extraction resolves the theme (C22.2, decision 25): a widget's own image takes its canvas's `UiTheme` tint of its state (Disabled, Pressed, Focused, Hovered, else Normal, from the play session's interaction state; outside a session Normal or Disabled), and a text without a font takes its canvas's `Font`, so the pass draws the items' colours and fonts unchanged; no pipeline of its own (its quad binding sets are the view's `UiQuadBindings`, its glyph runs share the Text pass's), and a stats row only when it records. C22.3 (ADR 0033 decision 51): World canvases' items, in their canvases' own pixels, are cut to their clips and canvas rectangles on the CPU and drawn first, canvas by canvas from the farthest to the nearest (the view-space depth of each canvas's centre), placed in the world by the canvas's matrix at its render pose and depth-tested against `SceneDepth` without depth writes (the QuadBatcher's `LdrDepth` pipeline, the Text pipelines' world vertices), untonemapped like world Text; a view without a camera draws none; the editor's scene view draws World canvases and no Screen canvas |
| — | Upscale | graphics | `OutputColor` RGBA8_UNORM (+ `OutputDepth` D32_FLOAT when an editor overlay draws), at the view's size | the output stage (M18, below), only when the scene resolution differs from the view's |
| 14 | Overlays | graphics | `LdrColor`, or `OutputColor` after an upscale (+ `SceneDepth` or `OutputDepth`, tested without writes) | wireframe edges (Lit view with `Wireframe`, replacing the shaded image), selection outline from `SelectionMask` R8_UNORM, debug lines and annotations (depth-tested and on-top pipelines), editor grid and icons, then the debug and annotation labels (the Text pipelines, under their own `Labels` row), at the view's resolution |
| — | Letterbox | graphics | `OutputColor` | after an upscale with a letterbox only: the letterbox bars painted again, so the overlays end clipped to the scene image (below) |
| 15 | ImGui or blit | graphics | swapchain BGRA8_UNORM or `OffscreenTarget` | editor UI; Runtime non-Dist F1 overlay |

**Stages** (M18; ADR 0029 decision 1). `SceneRenderer::Render` runs one stage function per `RenderStage` (`Renderer/RenderStage.h`), in this order, each a GPU zone `Stage:<name>` its passes' scopes nest in and a CPU zone of the process profiler (§4.13), whether or not it records anything; a later milestone appends a pass to a stage through its declaration in `Renderer/RenderPassDeclaration.h` (name, stage, pipelines, programs, stats rows, targets) and adds a stage only by a frozen-header change. There is no render graph.

| Stage | Passes (stats rows) | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Prepare | Prepare (CPU) | — |
| Deform | Skinning (M23: one dispatch per deformed item, below; ADR 0034 decision 27) | vertices |
| Shadows | DirectionalShadows, SpotShadows, PointShadows (M23: each shadowed point light's six cube faces with the Shadows declaration's caster pipelines, ADR 0034 decision 3) | shadow maps |
| DepthNormal | DepthNormal (prepass or picking prepass), then TerrainDepthNormal (M26: the terrains' prepass into the same targets; ADR 0037 decisions 13 and 22) | scene |
| Ambient | DepthPyramid, GTAO, GTAODenoiseHorizontal, GTAODenoiseVertical, LightClusters (M23: the cluster masks, below; ADR 0034 decision 5) | scene |
| Forward | PlanarReflection0 to PlanarReflection3 (M42: the view's planar reflections, one row per drawn mirror by rank, each timing that mirror's whole view; ADR 0059 decision 3), ForwardOpaque, TerrainForward (M26), Skybox, SSR (M26, only with `SsrEnabled`; ADR 0037 decision 18), ForwardTransparent, or Overdraw | scene |
| Sprites | Sprites, then Lights2D (M21; the QuadBatcher's pipelines are declared here); Lights2D records before the lit sprites that sample it (below); then Particles (M26, ADR 0037 decision 7; its own `Particles` program since M33, ADR 0048 decision 4) | scene |
| HdrPost | TAA (M26, only with `AntiAliasing` Taa in a Lit view outside the wireframe and pixel-art mode), Bloom, then Exposure (M26, only with `ExposureMode` Auto outside pixel-art mode; ADR 0037 decisions 10, 15 and 17) | scene |
| Tonemap | Tonemap, or the data views' composite under the same row | scene |
| LdrPost | FXAA | scene |
| SceneOverlay | Text (game texts, world then screen), then Ui (M22) | scene |
| Output | Upscale (only when the scene resolution differs from the view) | view |
| EditorOverlay | SelectionMask, SelectionDilateHorizontal, SelectionDilateVertical, SelectionComposite, Wireframe, Overlays, Labels, Letterbox (after an upscale with a letterbox) | view |

There is no temporal noise, and the temporal effects (M26's TAA and auto-exposure, opt-in) never break reproducibility: a capture resets its view's history and renders a fixed warm-up (ADR 0037 decision 10), so a capture of a deterministic scene, and without those effects its frame N, is exactly reproducible on a given device, which golden tests rely on. The data views (AO, ShadowCascades, Overdraw and M23's LightCount) replace pass 11 by one compute composite (`SceneDataView`) and show neither the snapshot's ordinary `DebugDraw` nor editor overlays or texts, only its `AnnotationDraw` (ADR 0017). Statistics list the recorded passes in the declared stats order, `RenderStatsOrder` (`Renderer/RenderPassDeclaration.h`: every pass declaration's rows in table order, ADR 0029 decision 2), whatever the recording order (the wireframe is recorded before the selection composite but listed after it): Prepare, Skinning, DirectionalShadows, SpotShadows, PointShadows, DepthNormal, TerrainDepthNormal, DepthPyramid, GTAO, GTAODenoiseHorizontal, GTAODenoiseVertical, LightClusters, PlanarReflection0, PlanarReflection1, PlanarReflection2, PlanarReflection3 (M42, ADR 0059 decision 3), ForwardOpaque, TerrainForward, Skybox, SSR, ForwardTransparent, Overdraw, Sprites (M21, ADR 0032 decision 4), Lights2D (M21, ADR 0032 decision 22), Particles, TAA, Bloom, Exposure, Tonemap, FXAA, Text, Ui, Upscale, SelectionMask, SelectionDilateHorizontal, SelectionDilateVertical, SelectionComposite, Wireframe, Overlays, Labels, Letterbox: 41 rows (37 before M42) (phase 2's ledger fixes the places of M21's Sprites and Lights2D and M22's Ui, ADR 0028; M23's Skinning row is declared by C23.3, ADR 0034 decision 27; phase 3's ledger fixes the places of M26's TerrainDepthNormal, TerrainForward, SSR, Particles, TAA and Exposure, declared by C26.1, ADR 0037 decision 13).

**Temporal anti-aliasing** (M26, R-TAA-VEL, R-TAA; ADR 0037 decisions 10, 11, 14 and 17). What a view remembers between its renders is snapshot data, filled by the view's `RenderViewHistory` (`Renderer/TemporalHistory.h`) right before each render: `CameraData::PreviousViewProjection` (the previous render's unjittered view-projection), each `MeshDrawItem::PreviousWorld` matched by entity, `DeltaTime` and `Jitter` (the Halton (2, 3) point of the frame since the last reset, 8 in a cycle, in scene pixels in (−0.5, 0.5), with `AntiAliasing` Taa outside pixel-art mode). A reset (a view's first render, a scene opened, closed or swapped, play started or stopped, a camera cut: another camera entity, projection kind or viewport size) empties them. The hosts keep one history per view: the editor's scene and game views (`EditorHostViewports`, the delta time the seconds since the view's last render), the Runtime's game view (its frames' unscaled seconds since its last render) and every capture (`ViewportCapture`, below). The renderer keeps only its GPU history (TAA's two `TaaHistory` images, the adapted exposure), which it starts afresh when the snapshot's history was reset or its previous render did not run the pass. A render with TAA (`AntiAliasing` Taa in a Lit view with a camera outside the wireframe and pixel-art mode, where Taa acts as None) folds the jitter into the scene passes' `ViewConstants` (the clip-space translation of `Jitter` pixels applied after the projection; `ViewConstants::Jitter` and `PreviousViewProjection` appended), so every pass before the HDR chain rasterizes jittered, while game text, the UI and the editor overlays draw with unjittered constants and never shake. The prepass writes the motion vectors into `SceneVelocity`: each fragment's current pixel minus its surface point's previous one, both interpolated clip positions (the vertex's `SV_Position`, and its previous local position through the instance record's `PreviousWorld` and `PreviousViewProjection`, which the renderer moves by the frame's jitter as it moves `ViewProjection`, so the jitter cancels; a deformed item that continues its history reads its previous deformation, the Skinning pass's previous positions, through vertex binding 2 of the 12 prepass pipelines, `DrawFlagPreviousPositions`; `Common/Motion.slang`), computed with the same NoContraction products, so a still scene seen by a still camera has exactly none; terrains add no motion of their own (a kept limit, Backlog §6). Particles (M33, ADR 0048 decision 6) write theirs after the prepass, in the Particles pass of a view with TAA: the motion each was drawn with since the view's previous render, where its alpha is at least 0.5. The TAA pass then resolves first in HdrPost, so bloom, exposure and the tonemap read the resolved image. A capture resets its history and, when its snapshot needs temporal state (`NeedsTemporalWarmup`: TAA or auto-exposure in a Lit view with a camera outside the wireframe and pixel-art mode), renders the same snapshot `CaptureWarmupFrames` (8) times with delta time 0, keeping the last image: two captures of one scene are byte-identical, at eight renders per temporal capture. `editor.screenshot` follows the rule (M26's milestone review): the fresh UI frame it asks for is a capture, so each editor view it shows renders the capture's warm-up (`ViewportCapture::RenderWarmup`: its history reset, the warm-up's renders submitted on their own, the frame's own render the last) instead of its live history, and the live frames after it go on from that history. A recovered device's renderer starts its temporal state afresh (a reset), so a capture after a loss equals one before it (ADR 0037 decision 29).

**Clustered lights** (M23, R-CLC; ADR 0034 decisions 4 and 5). The view is divided into 64 × 64-pixel tiles of the scene resolution (partial at the right and bottom edges) times 24 slices of view depth, exponential between the camera's near and far clip (the first slice from the camera, the last open beyond the far clip; a clip range that is not finite and positive gives one slice of every depth), for both projections (`Renderer/LightClusters.h`, `Shared/LightClusterConstants.h`). Each cluster holds `MaxShadedLights / 32` `uint` words (`LightClusterGrid::WordCount`, `Grid.w` of the constants: 8 at the default 256, 64 at 2,048), one bit per entry of the light list. M29 (ADR 0044 decisions 1 and 3): `Rendering.MaxShadedLights` (256, 512, 1,024 or 2,048; `RenderQualitySettings::MaxShadedLights`) caps the light list, which `CullLights` fills by importance; where more point and spot lights are visible than the cap leaves places for, a light the view's previous render shaded ranks with its importance times 1.25 (`LightHysteresis`, keyed by entity and type) so lights at the cap stop popping, and the chosen lights keep the plain importance order. The hysteresis reads the previous render only when the render continues its view's temporal history (a camera with `PreviousViewProjection`), so a capture ranks afresh. The light buffer is created for 2,048 lights once per renderer, and the shaders read the word count from `Grid.w`, so a larger cap renders a scene within the smaller one byte for byte. The LightClusters pass (`Renderer/LightClusterPass.h`, the end of the Ambient stage) dispatches one thread per cluster and word; each tests its 32 lights against its cluster's view-space box conservatively (the tile widened by a pixel, the slice's depths by a thousandth, the light's sphere of `Range` by a hundredth and by the rounding of the world positions; directional lights are in every cluster) and is the only writer of its word. The forward passes' light loop (`Common/LightLoop.slang`) shades the set bits of the pixel's cluster in ascending order, the light list's order. A light outside a pixel's cluster contributes exactly zero there (the windowed falloff is 0 beyond `Range`, a spot's cone factor 0 outside its outer cone), and the loop adds nothing for a light whose direct light is exactly zero, so the clustered image equals the brute-force image byte for byte: `RenderQualitySettings::ClusteredLights` false (tests only) loops over every light of the list through the same body, and the pass is not recorded then, nor when the light list holds only directional lights (every cluster would hold the whole list) or no pass reads the masks. The masks and the grid's constants are each renderer's (grown to the scene resolution's clusters, dropped with its state by a device loss), the pass is the pipeline set's (§8.14). The LightCount data view shows each pixel's cluster's light count: 0 black, 1–2 blue, 3–4 cyan, 5–8 green, 9–16 yellow, 17–32 orange, more red (the whole list's count when the loop is brute force).

**Instancing** (M23, R-INST; ADR 0034 decision 2). Every mesh draw is instanced, with no vertex binding of its own: the Prepare stage writes one instance record (`Shared/InstanceRecord.h`, 144 bytes until M31 and 208 since, std430: `World`, `PreviousWorld` for M26's motion vectors, `MeshDrawItem::PreviousWorld` or `World` without one, the pick id, the draw flags and, from M31, the item's material parameters, below; from M42 its former `Padding0` holds `PlanarReflectionSlot`, read with the draw flag `DrawFlagPlanarReflection` (16)) per submesh draw of the view into the per-view `Instances` structured buffer (`t10` of set 0, written once per view with the other per-view constants), in this order: the opaque draws, the transparent draws, the shadow casters (`ShadowPass::PrepareCasters`, sorted so that equal casters are adjacent, since a depth-only pass's result does not depend on its order), the selection mask's draws and (M42) each drawn planar reflection's mirror-view draws in slot order. Each pass splits its draws, in its recording order, into maximal runs of adjacent draws with equal keys (`GroupMeshInstances`: pipeline variant, material, mesh, submesh, vertex stream: 0 for a mesh's own vertices, a deformed item's own otherwise, below), whose records are adjacent, and records each run as one draw of that many instances; a shadow face records, of each run, the sub-runs its frustum does not cull. The vertex shaders read instance `i` (`SV_VulkanInstanceID`, counted from 0 within the draw) at `Instances[FirstInstance + i]` (`DrawConstants` version 2). Vulkan rasterizes a draw's instances in order, so an instanced render equals the render that `RenderQualitySettings::Instancing` false records with one draw per submesh draw, byte for byte ("SceneRenderer: an instanced render is byte-identical to the per-draw render"). `RenderPassStats::DrawCalls` counts the instanced draws and `SceneRenderStats::MeshDraws` the submesh draws. The Scene program has four vertex entries with the same position products, one per set of outputs its fragment shaders read (`VSMain` for the forward passes, M26's `VSPrepass` with the previous clip position, `VSPicking` with the previous clip position and the pick id, and `VSOverdraw`, which reads only the position and texture coordinates and the attribute stream, the attributes the overdraw pipelines bind), because the validation layer reports an output a fragment shader does not read and a vertex attribute a vertex shader does not read; the overdraw pipelines bind a set 0 of their own since M26, without the prepass's DFG LUT.

**Material parameters** (M31, `Docs/Decisions/0046-m31-material-parameters.md` decisions 2 to 7). A `MaterialParameters` component (§5.3) reaches its item as `MeshDrawItem::Parameters`, resolved by render extraction at the request's `SimulationTime` (`ResolveMaterialParameters`: the emissions times their strengths, `UVOffset` plus `UVScroll` times the time, wrapped into [0, 1) in double precision, the dissolve's edge only while it dissolves); the play session passes the rendered time of the world's clock (§5.6's world pause), `(WorldTick − 1 + Alpha)` fixed steps, `WorldTick` fixed steps at any alpha while its last fixed step held the world, and 0 before the world's first tick, for its game view and `ExtractView` (the world's, so a scrolling surface holds behind a world pause: batch 1's landing of M31 with M35), and every edit-time request 0, so a scroll moves smoothly in play and edit-time images show `UVOffset` alone. Parameters that are not the neutral defaults ride in the item's instance records (`Opacity`, `DissolveAmount`, `Tint`, `DissolveEdgeWidth`, `Emissive`, `DissolveNoiseScale`, `DissolveEdge`, `UVOffset`) with `DrawFlagMaterialParameters`, so items that differ only in them share instanced draws, and the Scene program's fragment shaders read them, from the record whose index the vertex shader hands on flat, only under that flag, so an item without them computes exactly what it did before M31. Under the flag the tint multiplies the base colour's RGB, the emission adds to the material's, the offset adds to every map's coordinates after the material's own UV transform (a Mask caster's alpha test included, so a scrolling cut-out's shadow moves with it), a dissolve clips the fragments whose noise (`engine://Textures/DissolveNoise` at `t16`, sampled at the first texture coordinates times `DissolveNoiseScale`) lies below `DissolveAmount` and adds the edge's emission just above it, and a fade clips by a 4 x 4 ordered dither of `Opacity`, its thresholds moved by a whole eighth at each frame of TAA's 8-frame jitter cycle (the phase `floor((Jitter.x + 0.5) × 8)`), so every pixel is covered in `Opacity` of the cycle's frames and TAA resolves a uniform fade; the noise is sampled at level 0, so the prepass, the forward passes and the casters read the same value. The clips run in the Mask variants: an Opaque material's draw takes them while its item dissolves or fades (its shadow casters only while it dissolves: a faded entity keeps its whole shadow, its depth and its opaque sort), chosen by `SelectMeshAlphaMode`, and the Mask variants test a material's alpha only for a Mask material; so no pass, pipeline or program is added. A Blend material's item stays in the transparent pass, its alpha multiplied by `Opacity` and 0 where it dissolves. The selection outline, the Overdraw data view, terrains, sprites, particles, text and the UI ignore the parameters (Backlog §6); the picking prepass clips with them. The renderer binds the noise texture's mirror while an item of the snapshot dissolves and its neutral white R8 texture otherwise.

**Deformation** (M23, C-SKEL and C-MORPH; ADR 0034 decision 27). A snapshot item is deformed when its mesh has a skin that its `JointPalette` covers (one matrix per skin joint, from the mesh's bind space into the item's space, which render extraction takes from the driving Animator's pose) or morph targets with a resolved weight that is not 0: `ResolveMorphWeights` gives one weight per target, the item's `MorphWeights` where it has one and the target's `DefaultWeight` (glTF's mesh weights, which travel with the GPU mesh in `GpuMesh::DeformBounds`) where it has none. A non-empty palette shorter than the skin draws the bind pose with one `RENDER_SKIN_MISMATCH` warning per renderer, kept across a device loss; an empty one is the bind pose without a warning (an edit scene, a mesh without an Animator). The Prepare stage culls a deformed item by its deformed bounds (`ComputeDeformedBounds`: each joint's box of the vertices it weights, widened by the morph reach and carried by its palette matrix's eight corners) and, when one of its draws survives (the camera's, a shadow caster's, which every face may draw, or the selection mask's), acquires the item's deformed state: its vertices, previous positions, palette and morph weights, kept by the renderer by entity and mesh from render to render and released at the end of a render that did not draw the item, with a vertex stream of its own, so deformed draws never share an instanced draw. The Skinning pass (`Renderer/SkinningPass.h`, `Passes/Skinning.slang`) then records one compute dispatch per deformed item, in snapshot order, all in one pass scope (one profiler scope, however many items), before any pass draws: one thread per vertex morphs the vertex (the deltas of every target of non-zero weight, in target order), skins it (the palette matrices of its four influences blended by weight; the position by the blend, the normal and tangent by its upper 3 × 3, then normalized; texture coordinates and the bitangent sign kept) and writes it into the item's vertex buffer of `MeshVertex` layout, which every pass binds as vertex binding 0 instead of the mesh's (the attribute stream stays the mesh's), so the 24 mesh pipelines and the vertex layouts stay; before it writes, each thread copies the position of the item's previous deformation (on its first, the new one) into the previous positions, M26's input for motion vectors. Each thread is the only writer of its outputs, so no atomic decides a value. The CPU reference `DeformMeshVertices` (`Asset/MeshDeform.h`) performs the same operations in the same order; the GPU's result equals it within 1e-4 per component (fused multiply-adds and the GPU's square roots, "SkinningPass: the deform equals the CPU reference, and the previous positions hold the last deformation"), and the scene view's wireframe draws it. Normals are transformed by the blended matrix, not its inverse transpose, so a joint with a non-uniform scale shades approximately, and `scene.raycast` tests a deformed mesh's bind-pose triangles (Backlog §6). `stats.get` lists the `Skinning` row, one dispatch per deformed item, only while a deformed item is drawn.

**Planar reflections** (M42, ADR 0059 decision 3; `Renderer/PlanarReflections.h`, `Renderer/SceneRendererReflections.cpp`, `Renderer/PlanarReflectionPass.h`, `Common/PlanarReflections.slang`). A `PlanarReflection` (§5.3) on the entity whose `MeshRenderer` draws a flat glass reaches the snapshot as a `PlanarReflectionItem` at its mesh's rendered pose (§8.2). In a Lit view with a camera outside the wireframe, a reflection is a candidate when its world plane (the local `Normal` and `Offset` through the item's world matrix) faces the camera and a draw of its entity survived the view's culling; the candidates rank by their glass's rectangle on screen, the largest first, ties by entity, and at most `MaxPlanarReflectionsPerView` = 4 are drawn (the drop is logged once per renderer); one past the cap, out of view, seen from behind, whose objects cannot be created or in a view whose probe constants could not be created draws exactly as without the component, with the probes and SSR. Each drawn reflection is a mirror view, rendered first in the Forward stage under its row `PlanarReflection<k>`: the camera mirrored in the plane (`S · View · R`, rigid, so every winding and face rule holds; the main view's unjittered projection), at `ResolutionScale` of the scene resolution, its draws culled by that camera cropped to the glass's rectangle widened by the blur's footprint (two texels of the chain's last level) and by the plane, clipped at the plane offset 1 cm toward its reflecting side by `SV_ClipDistance0` (`ViewConstants::ClipPlane`; every other view clips at (0, 0, 0, 1), nothing), rasterized within that rectangle, mirrored: its prepass and the terrains', its light clusters (inside its row), ForwardOpaque, TerrainForward, the skybox, ForwardTransparent and, in play scenes, the particles, then the colour's mip chain (each level the area mean of the whole level above, as deep as the level curve reaches at the view's `SsrMaxRoughness`). It binds the main view's shadow maps and constants (a directional cascade chosen by the main camera's depth of the point, `ViewConstants::CascadeDepthPlane`; a light only the mirror sees is unshadowed), environment, probes and instance buffer, its own light list (the main view's first, at their indices), fog from the glass on, and the neutral reflections (no recursion); SSR, GTAO, TAA, exposure, bloom, the tonemap, FXAA and every 2D, text, UI and overlay pass stay out, so the reflection is pre-exposure radiance the main view's post chain exposes. The main view's forward passes then replace the prefiltered radiance on the glass's draws (their records carry `DrawFlagPlanarReflection` and the slot) with the reflection sampled at the shaded point's projection by the mirror camera, blurred through its mips by the GGX alpha and faded back into the probes' term over the upper half of the roughnesses up to `SsrMaxRoughness`, under the same energy terms; the prepass writes a zero `SceneRoughness` multiplier there, so SSR neither traces nor composites over the glass. `stats.get` reports the drawn, dropped and culled reflections (§13.7).

**Terrain** (M26, C-TERR; ADR 0037 decisions 13, 22 and 29; `Renderer/TerrainPass.h`, `Renderer/TerrainLod.h`, `Passes/Terrain.slang`). Every snapshot terrain whose heightfield mirrors (`GpuResourceCache::GetHeightfield`: its samples as an R16_UNORM texture) is drawn as chunks of 32 cells (the last row and column smaller when the cells do not divide), each at a level of detail l (its vertices every 2^l-th sample and its corners) chosen by the camera's distance to the chunk's bounds in the terrain's local space over 32 cells' size times `LodBias` (`floor(log2)`, exactly, at most 5), neighbouring levels at most one apart; a chunk next to a coarser neighbour collapses its edge vertices the neighbour lacks onto the vertex before them, so both sides of every edge use one vertex sequence and no crack opens (`TerrainLod: a chunk's triangles cover it exactly once at every level and stitch`). A chunk's mesh, in chunk-local samples, depends only on its cells, its level and its coarser sides, so a view keeps one vertex and index buffer per such key, made the first time it draws one and released when it draws it no more; each chunk draws its key's mesh with its first sample pushed, the vertex shader placing every sample by `Asset/TerrainGeometry.h`'s rule from the heightfield texture, with the heightfield's central-difference normal (shared by chunks that share a vertex) and NoContraction products as the mesh passes. TerrainDepthNormal (its prepass and picking prepass, after the mesh prepass, into the same targets: normals, the camera's motion alone in `SceneVelocity`, since a terrain has no previous world, the forward pass's specular inputs in `SceneRoughness`, and its pick id, after the meshes' in the pick table) and TerrainForward (after Forward opaque, with the mesh forward passes' set 0: the light loop, the shadows it receives, the image-based lighting, the probes and GTAO) share the program `Terrain`: up to four layers weighted by the splat map's channels over their sum (layer 0 alone without a splat map), each layer's base colour, tint and tangent-space normal map tiled every `Tiling` metres in local XZ and its roughness and metallic constants; the pipelines cull nothing, and a back face is shaded with its normals flipped. A material debug view shades it from its constants (no specialized pipeline). A terrain casts no shadows (Backlog §6), and the Overdraw data view, the wireframe's edges and the selection outline leave it out (kept limits), while its depth occludes what is behind it. `stats.get` lists the `TerrainDepthNormal` and `TerrainForward` rows, one draw per chunk in view, only while a terrain is drawn.

**The Sprites stage** (M21; `Docs/Decisions/0032-m21-contract.md` decisions 4, 21 and 22). In a Lit view with a camera (not the wireframe), the stage lays out every sprite of the snapshot (and every tile, M21's tilemaps) as one QuadBatcher quad in the one 2D draw order, culling the quads wholly outside the view, then records in this order. When a drawn quad is lit, under the `Lights2D` row: (1) `Lights2DNormals` cleared to the flat normal (0, 0, 1) with 0 in w and, when a lit quad has a normal map (a lit sprite's `NormalMap` mirror, its placeholder when missing or failed, as a material's), the lit quads drawn into it in draw order with the QuadBatcher's Normals pipeline, depth-tested against `SceneDepth`, so each pixel keeps the world normal of its topmost lit item, with 1 in w (one normal per pixel: a kept limit, Backlog §6); (2) `Lights2DLight` cleared to zero and each light the view draws added into it with the `Lights2DPass` pipeline (blending one, one), one draw each: a Point light's square of side 2 `Radius` around it in its plane, projected by the view with its depth held inside the clip range (so a light beyond the camera's depth range still lights an orthographic view), a Global light's triangle over the target; each fragment evaluates `Renderer/Light2DShading.h`'s model at the point of the light's plane its pixel shows, reading the normal at its pixel. The view draws the first `MaxVisibleLights2D` (1,024) of the snapshot's lights, in their order, that reach it (`Light2DReachesView`: a Global light always; a Point light unless its projected square lies wholly outside the clip rectangle), skips the rest and logs the first skip once per renderer; a light whose values are not valid gives no light and does not count. Then, under the `Sprites` row, (3) the quads in their one draw order, each run of one lit-ness one QuadBatcher record: unlit runs with the Hdr pipeline, lit runs with HdrLit, which multiplies the texel's RGB by `Lights2DLight` at the fragment's pixel. Without a lit quad nothing of (1) and (2) is recorded and the light targets are not created, so unlit sprites keep their texels and a scene without a lit item renders exactly as before; a lit pixel without any light is black. The targets are the renderer's (its pool's, kept until the scene resolution changes, as the other lazily created targets) at the scene resolution, the PixelPerfectCamera's reference resolution, so lights accumulate at the reference resolution.

The overlay passes (13, 14) attach `SceneDepth` as an ordinary depth attachment with depth writes disabled, not as a read-only one: NVRHI stores a read-only depth attachment with `VK_ATTACHMENT_STORE_OP_STORE`, which synchronization validation counts as a write, and keeping `SceneDepth` in `DepthWrite` from the prepass to the overlays needs no transition (ADR 0013 decision 20). The forward passes test against the prepass depth without writing it, which needs bit-identical clip positions across the pipelines. Slang 2026.8 cannot decorate the position `Invariant`, so `Scene.slang` emits the vertex shader's two matrix products as `OpVectorTimesMatrix` decorated `NoContraction`, which no driver may fuse differently per pipeline (ADR 0013 decision 27).

**The output stage** (M18; ADR 0029 decisions 1, 5, 6 and 8). A view renders its scene at the scene resolution of the snapshot's `RenderOutputSettings` (the view's size by default) and the output stage brings it to the view: `ComputeRenderOutputMapping` takes the largest integer scale at which the scene fits the view (1 when it does not, which crops it) and centres the scaled image with offsets `floor((view − scale · scene) / 2)` (integer arithmetic; an odd leftover pixel goes to the right or bottom letterbox, an odd surplus is cropped on the left or top). Game text (pass 13's world and screen texts) draws at the scene resolution into the scene image, before the upscale, and M22's UI after it; then `UpscalePass` clears the view-size `OutputColor` to the letterbox colour and copies each scene pixel into a Scale × Scale block with `texelFetch` (point sampling), its viewport the scaled scene rectangle and its scissor that rectangle clipped to the view, and copies the scene depth into `OutputDepth` the same way when an editor overlay draws; then the editor overlays (pass 14 with the debug and annotation labels, under the `Labels` row) draw at the view's resolution, so lines stay one pixel wide and labels keep their pixel size. They draw over the whole view with the overlay camera, whose projection maps the scene's clip volume onto the scaled scene rectangle, so inside it they land where that rectangle's viewport would put them; last, the `Letterbox` row paints the letterbox bars again with the colour the upscale cleared them to (`UpscalePass::RecordLetterbox`), so an overlay that crosses the scene camera's frustum (a grid line, a debug line, a label, a dilated selection outline) ends clipped to the scene image, as the rectangle's scissor would clip it. At the identity mapping nothing is upscaled and the editor overlays draw into the scene image, so the default renders exactly as before the output stage. Picking, `viewport.pick`'s CPU ray and captures take view pixels and map them to scene pixels with `MapViewPixelToScenePixel` (`ComputeOutputPixelRayInterval`); a letterbox pixel shows no scene and picks nothing. UI is laid out and hit-tested in scene pixels (`MapViewPointToScenePoint`). The 2D colour path is §8.5's.

### 8.4 Binding model and shared structs
Shaders use HLSL register syntax compiled by Slang with `-fvk-t-shift 0 all -fvk-s-shift 128 all -fvk-b-shift 256 all -fvk-u-shift 384 all`, matching NVRHI's default `VulkanBindingOffsets` (SRV 0, sampler 128, CBV 256, UAV 384). Every `nvrhi::BindingLayoutDesc` sets `registerSpace = N` with `registerSpaceIsDescriptorSet = true`, so `spaceN` is descriptor set N.

| Space (set) | Frequency | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | per view | `b0 ViewConstants` (incl. projection kind and ortho extents, §8.3), `b1 ShadowConstants` (cascade matrices, splits, texel world sizes, penumbra scales), `b2 EnvironmentConstants` (SH9, intensity, rotation), `b3 LightClusterConstants` (M23: the cluster grid and the loop's mode, §8.3); `t0 Lights` (StructuredBuffer), `t1 ShadowCascades`, `t2 ShadowAtlas`, `t3 EnvSpecular` (cube), `t4 EnvSkybox` (cube), `t5 BRDFLut`, `t6 AmbientOcclusion`, `t7 BlueNoise`, `t8 ViewDepth` and `t9 SceneNormals` (the depth-aware AO upsample), `t10 Instances` (StructuredBuffer of `InstanceRecord`, M23, §8.3), `t11 LightClusterMasks` (M23: StructuredBuffer of `uint`, §8.3), `t12 PointShadowMaps` (M23: the point lights' cube array, §8.7), `b4 ProbeConstants`, `t13 IrradianceProbes` (StructuredBuffer of `float4`) and `t14 ReflectionProbeCubes` (cube array) (M26: the view's baked probes, §8.6), `t15 PointShadowMapsHalf` (M29: the Half tier's point-shadow cube array, §8.7), `t16 DissolveNoise` (M31: the dissolve noise, §8.3; also in the prepass's set 0 and the Shadow program's Mask casters' set 0, and declared unread by the Terrain program, which shares the forward set), `b5 FogConstants` (M32: the view's fog, also bound by the skybox and the SSR composite, §8.6), `b7 PlanarReflectionConstants` and `t17 PlanarReflections0` to `t20 PlanarReflections3` (M42: the view's drawn planar reflections, a neutral 1 × 1 black texture for a slot without one and in every mirror view; declared unread by the Terrain program; §8.3); `s0 LinearClamp`, `s1 ShadowCompare` (`GreaterOrEqual`), `s2 AnisoWrap`; plus the layout's `PushConstants` item (16 B) for the per-draw constants below, whose NVRHI slot is `b6` since M32 (`b5` before; NVRHI counts it as a constant-buffer slot; Vulkan ignores it) |
| 1 | per material | `b0 MaterialConstants`; `t0 BaseColorMap`, `t1 MetallicRoughnessMap`, `t2 NormalMap`, `t3 OcclusionMap`, `t4 EmissiveMap`; one cached `BindingSet` per (material, version); empty slots bind White/FlatNormal/Black |
| push | per draw | `DrawConstants { uint FirstInstance; uint Padding0; uint2 Padding1; }` (16 B, version 2 since M23: the draw's first instance record in `t10 Instances`, whose `World`, pick id and flags version 1 held; the normal matrix comes from the cofactor of the record's `World` in the shader). NVRHI requires push constants to be declared as a `BindingLayoutItem::PushConstants` in a binding layout; it lives in the set-0 layout of every graphics pipeline that draws meshes (and the matching set-0 binding sets), and Slang declares it `[[vk::push_constant]] ConstantBuffer<DrawConstants> Draw;`. Values are set per draw with `ICommandList::setPushConstants` |

Structs shared between C++ and Slang live in `Resources/Shaders/Shared/*.h` (the common subset, `ENGINE_SHADER` guards), included by both sides (`Resources/Shaders` is an include path of Engine). C++ adds `static_assert(sizeof(...))`; the test `Shaders.SharedStructsMatchReflection` compares every member offset in slangc's `-reflection-json` with `offsetof`. A GPU test checks the matrix convention (column-major glm, `-matrix-layout-column-major`, `mul(M, v)`) by transforming known vectors. Slang names: types and functions PascalCase, resources PascalCase without prefix, constant buffers end in `Constants`, locals camelCase.

Every `RWTexture*` declares its storage format explicitly with `[vk::image_format("r11f_g11f_b10f" | "r16f" | "r8" | "rg16f" | "rgba16f" | "rgba8" | "r32ui")]`, so the SPIR-V never relies on `shaderStorageImageWriteWithoutFormat`. `Shaders.LayoutsMatchReflection` also checks the reflected image format against the texture format the C++ pass creates.

**Blue noise** (`t7`, 64² R8) is generated in code: a seeded void-and-cluster implementation in `Renderer/BlueNoise.cpp`, run by `--bake-engine-assets` into the engine cooked cache (§7.5) and shipped in `Engine.pak`. A CPU test compares the hash of the output with a committed value, so no third-party texture or license is involved.

**Shared layouts and per-view binding sets** (ADR 0013 decisions 7, 20, 21 and 27). NVRHI accepts a binding set only for the pipeline's own layout objects, so `PipelineFactory::CreateBindingLayouts` creates each set's layout once and `GraphicsPipelineSpecification::SharedBindingLayouts` hands it to every pipeline that binds that set (the prepass shares set 1 with the forward pass for its Mask variants). The passes every view of a device shares (skybox, bloom, tonemap, FXAA, debug lines, text) keep no binding sets of their own: each record takes the view's `PassBindingCache`, which finds a set by its layout and exact `BindingSetDesc` and holds it; a `SceneRenderer` releases at the end of every render what that render did not bind, so views never evict each other's sets and no pass keeps a resized or destroyed view's targets alive. Material binding sets are cached per view by (handle, generation) the same way, except that a material whose every draw a render culls keeps its set while it stays in the snapshot and its mirror is current, so a material that leaves the view and returns makes no new set (M18, R-MATSET; ADR 0029). A renderer clears all of its binding sets and material sets before its first render after `SceneRendererPipelines::CreatePipelines` replaced the binding layouts they were made for (`GetGeneration`, §8.12). The forward layout binds `b0` to `b5`, `t0` to `t3`, `t5`, `t6`, `t8` to `t16`, `s0` to `s2` and the push constants (M29 added `t15`, the Half tier's point-shadow cubes, ADR 0044 decision 2; M31 `t16`, the dissolve noise, to it and to the prepass layout, ADR 0046 decision 6, the next register after M29's at batch 1's landing) (M8 bound `b0`, `b2`, `t0`, `t3`, `t5`, `s0`, `s2` and the push constants; M9 added `b1`, `t1`, `t2`, `t6`, `t8`, `t9` and `s1`; M23 `b3` and `t10` to `t12`, moving the push constants' NVRHI slot from `b3` to `b4`, and `t10` to the prepass layout's `b0`, `s2` and push constants; M26 `b4`, `t13` and `t14`, moving the push constants' slot to `b5`, ADR 0037 decision 16, and `t5` and `s0` to the prepass layout for `SceneRoughness`'s specular inputs, the overdraw pipelines keeping the prepass layout's former items in a set-0 layout of their own, decision 14; M32 `b5` (`FogConstants`), moving the push constants' slot to `b6`, ADR 0047 decision 5). The Shadow and SelectionMask programs bind `t10 Instances` in their own set-0 layouts. The Skinning program (M23, §8.3) binds its own set 0: `t0` the mesh's vertices, `t1` its skin and `t2` its morph deltas (raw buffers, `ByteAddressBuffer`, since `MeshVertex`, `MeshSkinVertex` and `MeshMorphDelta` have no std430 layout; a mesh without a skin or morph targets binds its vertices there, unread), `t3` the item's palette (`StructuredBuffer<float4x4>`) and `t4` its morph weights, `u0` its deformed vertices (raw) and `u1` its previous positions (`float4`), with the push constants `SkinningConstants` (vertex, joint and target counts and the first-deformation flag). `t4 EnvSkybox` is bound only in the skybox pass's set 0 and `t7 BlueNoise` only in the tonemap pass's, each in its own layout. The transparent pass binds a second forward set with the neutral white AO and far depth in `t6` and `t8`. `ViewConstants` ends with `LightCount` (400 bytes), then M26's `PreviousViewProjection` and `Jitter` (480 bytes, ADR 0037 decisions 11 and 17), then M42's `ReflectionView` (in the former `Padding4`), `ClipPlane` and `CascadeDepthPlane` (512 bytes, ADR 0059 decision 3: 1, the biased glass plane and the main camera's depth plane in a mirror view; 0, (0, 0, 0, 1) and unread in every other view); `t0 Lights` is a structured buffer of `Shared/ShaderLight.h` (std430); `InstanceRecord::Flags` holds `DrawFlagMirrored`, `DrawFlagReceiveShadows`, M26's `DrawFlagPreviousPositions` (a deformed item's motion vectors read its previous positions) and M31's `DrawFlagMaterialParameters` (the fragment shaders apply the record's material parameters, §8.3), and `InstanceRecord::EntityId` the instance's pick ID (`DrawConstants` held them before M23); `MaterialConstants` holds the §8.5 factors and `Flags` (`MaterialFlagEmissiveMap`; M23: `MaterialFlag<Map>UV1` for each map that samples the second UV set and `MaterialFlagNormalMapTwoChannel`); the debug view is the specialization constant `SceneDebugViewConstantId`; the post and bake passes take push constants (`TonemapConstants`, `BloomConstants`, `EnvironmentBakeConstants`, M26's `ExposureConstants` and `TaaConstants`). `SharedStructsMatchReflection` covers every constant-buffer and push-constant struct and the element structs of structured buffers (`ShaderLight`, `InstanceRecord`). Every pipeline that draws meshes (the Scene program's, the debug views', the shadow casters and the selection mask) takes two vertex bindings (M23, ADR 0034 decision 9; M26's 12 prepass pipelines a third, below): binding 0, `MeshVertex` (48 bytes), and binding 1, the attribute stream (`MeshVertexAttributes`, 24 bytes: `TEXCOORD1` `RG32_FLOAT` at offset 0 and `COLOR` `RGBA32_FLOAT` at offset 8, at the two locations after the pipeline's binding 0 attributes), which `GpuMesh::AttributeBuffer` supplies: the mesh's own stream, or the `GpuResourceCache`'s one shared default stream (`TexCoord1` (0, 0), opaque white) for a mesh without one, as long as the largest such mesh and bound at offset 0, since all its entries are equal. The prepass and picking prepass pipelines add binding 2 (M26, ADR 0037 decision 11): `PREVIOUSPOSITION` `RGB32_FLOAT` at offset 0 with a 16-byte stride, a deformed item's previous positions (the Skinning pass's `float4`s), read only with `DrawFlagPreviousPositions`; any other draw binds its own vertex buffer there, never read as positions, every fetch inside it.

### 8.5 PBR material model
glTF 2.0 metallic-roughness: base colour (sRGB texture × factor × the vertex colour, RGBA, M23), each map sampled with its UV set (`UV0` or `UV1`, Material version 2, M23), metallic-roughness (G = roughness, B = metallic), tangent-space normal map with scale (a two-channel BC5 map's z reconstructed as `sqrt(saturate(1 − x² − y²))`, `MaterialFlagNormalMapTwoChannel`, M23), occlusion (R) with strength, emissive (sRGB) × `EmissiveStrength`, alpha modes Opaque/Mask/Blend, double-sided, UV scale and offset. BRDF: GGX NDF, height-correlated Smith visibility, Schlick Fresnel, Lambert diffuse, multi-scatter energy compensation from the DFG LUT, perceptual roughness clamped to ≥ 0.045, geometric specular anti-aliasing from screen-space normal variance. Lights use artist units: unitless intensity multiplied by colour, windowed inverse-square falloff up to `Range` (point/spot), smoothstep cone attenuation, `SourceRadius` widening roughness (representative point) and driving PCSS. Exposure is manual (2^`ExposureEV`); with artist units HDR values stay well inside FP16, so no pre-exposure is needed. The mesh pipelines created at startup are the prepass, the picking prepass and the forward opaque pass for {Opaque, Mask} × {CullBack, CullFront, CullNone}, the transparent pass (Blend) and the overdraw pass for the three cull modes, 24 in all (`SceneRendererPipelines::MeshPipelineCount`): a mirroring world matrix (negative determinant) draws with CullFront and `DrawFlagMirrored`, which flips normals and `SV_IsFrontFace`, and double-sided materials draw with CullNone. With the passes' own pipelines (skybox 1, bloom 3, tonemap 1, FXAA 1, debug lines 2, text 2, DFG LUT 1, shadows 6, depth pyramid 2, GTAO 2, selection 8, the data-view composite 1, from M18 the QuadBatcher 2 and the output stage's upscale 2, from M21 the QuadBatcher's lit 2 and the 2D lights' 1, from M22 the QuadBatcher's `LdrDepth` 1, from M23 the light clusters 1 and the skinning 1, and from M26 the Exposure pass's 2, the histogram and the adaptation, the TAA pass's 1, the SSR pass's 2, the trace and the composite, and the terrain pass's 3, its prepass, picking prepass and forward pass, from M32 the SSR tile classification 1 (ADR 0047 decisions 10 and 14), and from M33 the Particles pass's 3, its two colour pipelines and its motion vectors' (ADR 0048 decision 4; M26's QuadBatcher `HdrAdditive` 1, which drew the additive particles until then, was removed at M33's merge, decision 10)) that makes 76 at startup (`SceneRendererPipelines::StartupPipelineCount`, the sum of the pass declarations' counts, `GetDeclaredPipelineCount`; ADR 0029 decision 2). The material debug views (M8: Albedo, Normals, Roughness, Metallic, Emissive) are a Vulkan specialization constant through `IDevice::createShaderSpecialization`; such a view's nine forward variants are created the first time a snapshot asks for it (`SceneRendererPipelines::EnsureDebugView`) and kept, so a debugging path does not cost every device, fixture and exported game 45 pipelines (an exception to §8.12's startup rule). Creating them is a debug-view switch, a request after startup (M18, ADR 0029 decisions 42 and 44): an out-of-memory creation is trimmed for and retried once, and when it runs out of memory again `Render` records the view in the debug view the renderer last rendered and returns `OutOfMemory` as a partial error (one warning per renderer and view; the editor sets its scene view's setting back, and a capture fails with `OutOfMemory`), never `FatalError(OutOfMemory)`. On a lost device a `Gpu` error there is the loss: `Render` returns it and the view is created on its first render after the recovery (ADR 0029 decision 28). M9's data views (AO, ShadowCascades, Overdraw) and M23's LightCount use the startup overdraw pipelines and the data-view composite, never forward variants. A debug view's post chain is fixed: no skybox, bloom, FXAA or dither, exposure 1, Linear, the OETF only for Albedo and Emissive, so a data view stores v as round(255 v). The 2D colour path (`RenderOutputSettings::PixelArt`, M18; ADR 0029 decision 7) fixes a Lit view's chain the same way with the OETF: Linear at exposure 1, no dither, bloom or FXAA whatever the snapshot's post-processing says, so the linear value of an 8-bit sRGB texel drawn into `SceneColor` reaches the output unchanged; GTAO still follows the post-processing. Both pipeline counts are logged and asserted by a test (ADR 0013 decisions 7 and 12). Mask materials drop fragments by writing `SV_Coverage = 0` (Slang compiles `discard` to `OpDemoteToHelperInvocation`, whose feature `GraphicsDevice` does not enable); `MaterialFlagEmissiveMap` tells the shader whether an emissive map multiplies the factor; a light of radiance C·I delivers π·C·I illuminance to a surface facing it, so a white Lambertian surface lit head-on by a directional light of intensity 1 has radiance 1; specular anti-aliasing follows Tokuyoshi and Kaplanyan with Filament's variance and threshold, diffuse occlusion Jimenez's multi-bounce fit and specular occlusion Lagarde's, with horizon occlusion for normal maps (ADR 0013 decision 21).

### 8.6 IBL pre-filtering (Poly Haven HDRIs)
`EnvironmentBaker` (Renderer, implements `IEnvironmentBaker`) runs at **import time** in the editor (GPU compute); results are cooked into the `.envmap` payload, so neither the editor at load nor the runtime ever re-bakes.
1. `stbi_loadf` (`.hdr`) or tinyexr (`.exr`, M23) → RGB32F equirect, at most 8,192 texels wide (keeping the upload at most 512 MiB); non-finite texels rejected; optional `ClampLuminance` import setting (default off).
2. Equirect → `EnvSkybox` RGBA16F cube, face `min(1024, width/4)`, full mip chain by compute downsampling (skybox and `SkyboxBlur`).
3. Specular prefilter → `EnvSpecular` RGBA16F 256² × 7 mips, mip *i* = perceptual roughness *i*/6, GGX importance sampling with **filtered importance sampling** (source mip chosen by PDF, Křivánek & Colbert), Hammersley sequence, 64–512 samples per mip. This tames Poly Haven sun texels (> 50,000) without ad-hoc clamping. With `Compression` `Auto` (M23, the default) the importer then stores the skybox and specular cubes as BC6H blocks (`BC6H_UFLOAT` on the GPU, an eighth of RGBA16F's memory, or the decode fallback's RGBA16F on a device without BC support, §8.1), every face of every level compressed through CMP_Core; the SH9 of step 4 is the same either way (ADR 0034 decisions 14 and 15).
4. Diffuse irradiance → **SH9** (L2) by a compute reduction with exact texel solid angles in a fixed order, over the first skybox level of at most 64², then normalized, convolved with the cosine lobe over π and windowed (**Hanning**, w = 4) against ringing from small bright sources; negative results clamped in the shader. Baked texels are clamped to 65,504, the largest finite binary16 value.
5. DFG/BRDF LUT RG16_FLOAT 128², Filament's multi-scatter form `(∫ Fc·Gv, ∫ Gv)` over (NdotV, perceptual roughness), generated once at device startup by compute (< 1 ms), state permanent. It depends only on the BRDF and belongs with it (`Renderer/BrdfLut`), not with the bake.

Shading: diffuse IBL `SH(N) · albedo · (1 − F_ms) · multiBounce(AO)`; specular IBL split sum with multi-scatter and specular occlusion (Lagarde, from AO, NdotV and roughness) plus horizon occlusion for normal-mapped surfaces. `Rotation` rotates the lookup vector; `Intensity` scales both terms. More HDRIs: `Scripts/FetchAssets.py hdri <id> --res 2k --dest <Project>/Assets/Environments` then `asset.import`.

**Baked probes: the shading** (M26, R-GI-PROBE; ADR 0037 decisions 8 and 16). An `IrradianceVolume` (an `IrradianceVolume` asset: a grid of 2 to 16 probes per axis over its box, each the SH9 of the irradiance it receives in `EnvironmentData`'s convention) and a `ReflectionProbe` (an `Environment` asset, whose prefiltered specular cube is the probe's) replace, inside their boxes, the image-based terms above: the forward passes' indirect term (`Common/Probes.slang`, after M23's light loop and outside it) starts from the Environment's SH9 irradiance and prefiltered specular (or the constant ambient) and blends each probe over them, weighted 0 outside its box and rising linearly to 1 at `BlendDistance` metres inside its nearest face (1 inside with `BlendDistance` 0): a volume's irradiance is its eight probes around the point, the coefficients trilinear in its grid (the corner probes at the box's corners) and evaluated at the shading normal, a reflection probe's specular its cube sampled at the reflected direction at the roughness's lod, box-projected with `BoxProjection` (the ray to the face it leaves the box through, seen from the probe's origin, where its cube was captured), each times its `Intensity` (clamped like the environment's). The probes blend from the largest box (world volume) to the smallest, ties in snapshot order, so where boxes overlap the smaller wins and fades into the larger at its faces. A view shades with at most 8 volumes and 8 reflection probes (`Shared/ProbeConstants.h`), the first of the snapshot's, in its canonical entity order, that have a box (a finite, invertible world matrix and a positive size), are not culled against the view (their box's corners, as a mesh's bounds) and whose data loads; one more is dropped, logged once per renderer. The renderer writes `ProbeConstants` (`b4`) per view and copies the volumes' coefficients from their `GpuIrradianceVolume` mirrors (the cache's place 3, `CountX × CountY × CountZ × 9` `float4`s) into one per-view structured buffer (`t13`) and the reflection probes' cubes from their `GpuEnvironment` mirrors into one per-view cube array (`t14`) (place 2, ADR 0029 decision 27), only when the view's probes change; the cube array takes the first probe's format (`RGBA16_FLOAT`, or `BC6H_UFLOAT` for an Environment imported with `Compression` `Auto` on a device with BC support), so a reflection probe whose cube differs (another `Compression`) is dropped, logged once per renderer. Only the Lit view outside the wireframe view uses probes, and never a bake's captures (`RenderQualitySettings::Probes` false: one bounce, and a second bake byte-identical to the first). Without probes nothing changes, so a scene without them renders as before.

**Conventions** (`Asset/EnvironmentData.h`, shared by the shaders and the CPU references): right-handed, +Y up; the equirectangular centre is −Z and u = 0.75 is +X; cube faces and texel directions follow Vulkan's face selection; `IrradianceSH9` holds the coefficients of irradiance / π, so a constant environment evaluates to its radiance; `Rotation` turns the environment by +Rotation about +Y. The skybox face is `max(1, min(1024, width / 4))` or an explicit power of two up to 1024, and specular mip 0 is the skybox resampled to the specular size; `EnvironmentBaker::BakeWithOptions` bakes the oracle tests' small cubes. `Intensity` is at most 65,504 and the renderer clamps it, zeroing any scaled SH coefficient that is not finite (ADR 0013 decisions 7, 9, 21 and 27).

**Baked probes: the bake** (M26, R-GI-PROBE; ADR 0037 decision 8). `lighting.bake` (`EditorCore/Lighting/LightingBake.h`, the editor's Tools > Bake lighting through the same method) bakes a saved edit scene's effectively enabled `IrradianceVolume`s and `ReflectionProbe`s in canonical order from one extracted snapshot. `Renderer/ProbeCapture` renders the snapshot six times around a point through a `SceneRenderer` of its own over the editor's shared pipelines and cache (created at startup like the `ViewportCapture`, injected with `EditorContext::SetProbeCapture`; none with `--renderer none`, where the bake is refused): 90-degree faces with an exact unit projection in Vulkan's face order, each a rotation looking along the face's major axis with `-Sc` right and `-Tc` up (a reflection would flip every triangle's winding), so the read-back columns are mirrored back on the CPU; `Quality.Probes` false (one bounce), no particles, sprites, UI, texts or overlays, every temporal input reset, TAA and SSR off (SSR, a view-dependent screen-space effect, would trace each face within its own image and seam the cube; ADR 0037's W26.2 review), GTAO as the scene sets it, cleared to black where no environment's skybox draws; it reads `SceneColor` (`SceneRenderer::GetSceneColorTexture`, linear HDR before the post chain) back and keeps finite texels in [0, 65,504]. Each capture collects the garbage of its own submissions before it returns, and so does each environment bake, which a reflection probe's import runs on the GPU (`EnvironmentBaker`), both through `GraphicsDevice::CollectCompletedSubmissions` (§8.14 item 2), so what a capture or an import used and dropped (each face's read-back staging texture, what a face's culling stopped drawing, an environment bake's cubes and read-backs) is released during the bake, not at the end of its frame: a bake holds one capture's and one import's device allocations whatever its probe count, and a bake straight after another adds none (World Tree's brief 21, where the bake of a 13 x 3 x 13 volume ended with 23,521 native allocations until its frame's garbage collection). An irradiance probe (16 texels a face) is projected to SH9 with each texel's exact solid angle (`DetMath::ATan2`), the cosine lobe over pi and the Hanning window above, in double precision and a fixed order; a reflection probe (its `Resolution`) is resampled bilinearly into an equirectangular image of 4 x 2 faces (`DetMath` directions) and written as flat RGBE Radiance HDR. Every probe is checked before the first capture (a volume's counts and `Size`, a reflection probe's `Resolution`), so a probe out of its ranges refuses the bake with Validation, nothing rendered or written. The files go to `Assets/Lighting/<the scene's path below Assets/, without its extension>/<entity id>.irradiance` or `.hdr` (`Assets/Scenes/Room.scene` into `Assets/Lighting/Scenes/Room/`, so scenes of one name in different folders, even a copy that kept the entity ids, never share a file; ADR 0037 decision 31; the `.hdr` imported by `EnvironmentImporter` with default settings), rewritten only when their bytes change, a new source getting its `.meta`, and imported; the probes' `Data` is then set in one undo step ("Bake Lighting"), none when no `Data` changes.
