The world keeps each body's list (`PhysicsWorld::SetColliderSurfaces(body, {collider, Friction, Restitution, SurfaceVelocity in body axes})`, refused with `InvalidArgument` for a non-finite or out-of-range value, a collider the shape lacks or a duplicate) in the body records its contact listener reads. In `OnContactAdded` and `OnContactPersisted` (which Jolt calls with freshly combined settings for every new, cached and continuous-collision contact) a contact of which a side's collider has a surface gets its `ContactSettings` from both sides, each side's value its surface's or else its body's, by Jolt's own rules: friction `sqrt(f1 · f2)`, restitution `max(r1, r2)`, and `mRelativeLinearSurfaceVelocity = R2 v2 − R1 v1` (each body's rotation at that moment times its side's body-space velocity), which Jolt applies through the contact's friction, so a surface whose combined friction is 0 carries nothing. A contact neither of whose colliders has a surface keeps exactly what Jolt combined, so bodies without surfaces simulate bit for bit as before ("PhysicsWorld: contacts between bodies without surfaces stay bit-identical", with the 200-body pile's committed hash). The session sends each body's list from the components: a `ColliderSurface`'s signals mark its entity in a set of their own and never compose the scene, so a belt written every tick keeps its body's handle and shape ("PhysicsSystem: a surface write keeps the body's handle and shape and composes nothing"); PreStep, after its rebuilds, sends the lists of the bodies that hold a marked entity's colliders, the velocity turned from the entity's axes into the body's (the owner's inverse world rotation times the entity's, rotation only), and a created or reshaped body gets its list at once. A write in the fixed step is in force at that tick's PreStep, one in the frame phase at the next tick's. A collider whose values really changed wakes the bodies inside its bounds, so debris asleep on a stopped belt rides it once it starts, and an unchanged write wakes nothing. Under Jolt's manifold reduction (on for every body) a body lying across the seam of two coplanar pieces takes the surface of the sub-shape its merged manifold is named after (§9.4 "Collider events"): ice or marble, never a blend, deterministic (`Docs/Backlog.md` §6). Surfaces are 3D only, with no angular velocity and no per-triangle materials (§2 of the Backlog).
- **Seams.** Jolt removes ghost contacts on internal edges only within one shape, so separate bodies bump at shared edges. Tracks use the shared-static-body pattern (§5.3), and rolling bodies set `EnhancedInternalEdgeRemoval`, which makes Jolt collide such a body against a compound with its `InternalEdgeRemovingCollector`. Test: a 0.5 m sphere rolled at 6 m/s across 20 adjacent 1 m boxes of one static compound keeps `|v.y| < 0.05 m/s` throughout. A control case with 20 separate bodies documents the bump the pattern avoids. Measured with the integrated world, Jolt's own collector is not enough: with its default convex radius the boxes' rounded edges form a groove at every seam, and with flush faces its 1-degree face test still keeps the ball's contact with the next box's leading edge. Boxes therefore have no convex radius, and every world collides body pairs through `Detail::CollideBodiesWithEdgeRemoval`: Jolt's default collision for pairs without enhanced internal edge removal, and for the others the same algorithm with the face test at 0.1 degree and a total order on equally deep delayed contacts (ADR 0014 decision 26).
- **Triggers** (`IsTrigger`) are Jolt sensors (`mIsSensor`), created **Kinematic** and kept active, so they also detect sleeping bodies (Jolt docs: static sensors only see active bodies). They also set `mCollideKinematicVsNonDynamic`, so they detect kinematic platforms and character inner bodies (§9.6). Implicit sensor bodies (§5.3) follow their entity with `MoveKinematic`. A sensor `RigidBody` of Type Static is created as a Kinematic sensor for the same reason and follows its entity the same way.
- Bodies are (re)built at `PreStep` when RigidBody, a collider or `Active` changes (EnTT signals mark them dirty), so component order does not matter; such a change made before a start flush is already applied by the flush's body synchronization (§5.7 step 2, `PhysicsSystem::SynchronizeBodies`: the same rebuild without the moves and teleports; ADR 0038 decision 14), so a new entity has its body from its `OnStart` on. Bodies are created in canonical order. A body is also rebuilt when a gathered collider moved relative to its body, the hierarchy changed above or below a collider, the world scale of an owner or gathered collider changed (scale is baked in), the `MeshRenderer.Mesh` a mesh collider falls back to changed, a collider's mesh got a new version, or a `TerrainCollider`'s `Terrain` changed or its heightfield got a new version (M26: `terrain.edit`, a reimport). A rebuild that keeps the motion type and sensor flag uses `PhysicsWorld::SetShape` (handle, pose, velocities and contacts kept); any other destroys and creates the body with its current velocities (ADR 0014 decision 11). A `ColliderSurface` change never rebuilds anything (M36, "Collider surfaces" above).
- **Layers.** Up to 16 named project layers plus a symmetric collision matrix. Object layer = `(layerIndex << 2) | kind` with kind ∈ {Static, Moving, Sensor, Character}; broad-phase layers `NonMoving`, `Moving` (Moving and Character), `Sensor`. The pair filter is `matrix[a >> 2][b >> 2] && !(both Static) && !(Sensor and Static) && !(both Sensor)`, and a Character (a character's inner body, M34, §9.6) pairs with a Sensor only, so sensors never pay for static geometry or each other, as Jolt recommends, and the solver never resolves a contact between an inner body and another body (ADR 0049 decision 1). Three small engine classes implement Jolt's filter interfaces. Masks are 32-bit (`PhysicsLayerMask`, the width of Luau's `bit32`; bits at or above the layer count select nothing; ADR 0014 decision 4). Queries take a layer mask (`Physics.LayerMask("Track", "Default")`).

### 9.3 Fixed step and sync
- `Step(fixedDt, collisionSteps)` with `collisionSteps = max(1, ceil(60 / FixedHz))`, computed in integers: `1.0 / 60 × 60` need not round to exactly 1, and an extra collision step would change results (ADR 0014 decision 3).
- **PreStep** runs right after a `TransformSystem::Update` (§5.7 step 5), so world matrices include every Transform write made earlier in the same tick. A body the start flush's synchronization created (§5.7 step 2) is first swept or teleported by the next PreStep, as one created at session start is. Kinematic bodies call `MoveKinematic(target, fixedDt)` (correct velocities, so moving platforms carry the ball). So is a Kinematic body on an entity a `BoneAttachment` placed in the tick's AnimationSystem phase (M41, ADR 0058 decision 3): a swinging staff is swept with its bone and pushes what it meets, while solid colliders on an attached entity without a Kinematic body of its own would rebuild an ancestor's compound or teleport a static body every tick (`ANIMATION_ATTACHMENT_INVALID`). Teleports are detected exactly: a Dynamic body or a character whose owner's local `Translation` and `Rotation` differ bit for bit from the values PostStep wrote (a pose decomposed from the world matrix would differ in the last bits and wake every body every tick), and a Static body whose world matrix differs from the one it was created or last teleported at, is teleported in the same tick with `SetPositionAndRotation` and woken, keeping its velocity unless the script also set it. A character is moved with `CharacterController::SetPose` before its update; a Kinematic body whose entity carries `InterpolationResetTag` at PreStep is placed with `SetPose` instead of swept, so it does not fling what rests on it. A Transform written beyond `MaxPhysicsCoordinate` is not applied: the entity's local values go back to the body's (ADR 0014 decisions 11 and 34). Test: "Transform write in OnFixedUpdate teleports the body in the same tick".
- **PostStep:** every Dynamic body that is active or has a parent writes its world pose back as local transforms (through the parent inverse), so the entity always shows where the body is. Bodies are visited in canonical order, never in `GetActiveBodies` order. Render interpolation does not depend on PostStep; it uses the per-step snapshot of every entity (§5.2). A dynamic body under a moving parent raises `PHYSICS_DYNAMIC_UNDER_MOVING_PARENT`. It is simulated in world space, not carried by the parent.
- **Body control** (ADR 0014 decisions 13 and 34). Every body function takes the owner's UUID and returns a `Result`: NotFound without a created body (or for an owner pending destruction or disabled), InvalidArgument for non-finite or out-of-range values, InvalidState for the wrong motion type. `MoveKinematic(entity, position, rotation)` sets the entity's world pose and the next PreStep sweeps the body there, so the Transform stays the single source of a kinematic body's pose. A Kinematic body's velocities are those of its last sweep (the pose change over one fixed delta): in the tick of a `MoveKinematic` made before its `PreStep` (in `OnFixedUpdate`, a task or a test case), the rest of that fixed step still reads the previous tick's sweep, while that tick's physics callbacks, the frame phase, an evaluation between ticks and the next tick's fixed step read the new sweep's, and a step that does not move the body leaves them zero (ADR 0038, friction F18; "PlaySession: a Kinematic body's velocities are those of its last physics step, so a MoveKinematic shows in them from its tick's physics step on"). `Teleport` sets the entity's and the body's world pose at once, tags `InterpolationResetTag` and keeps the velocity. Forces and impulses need a Dynamic body, and so do `SetLinearVelocity` and `SetAngularVelocity`, since every PreStep sets a Kinematic body's velocities through `MoveKinematic`; Static bodies take no velocity.

### 9.4 Collision and trigger events
`ContactListener` callbacks run on Jolt worker threads during `Update`. `OnContactAdded` appends `{Added, BodyA, BodyB, SubShapePair, Point, Normal, RelativeNormalSpeed, Touching}`, `OnContactPersisted` appends one `{Touched, …}` the first time a contact added without touching touches, and `OnContactRemoved` appends `{Removed, SubShapePair}` to a mutex-guarded buffer; nothing else happens on workers. After `Update` the main thread:
1. maps body IDs to UUIDs and collapses sub-shape contacts into body-pair begin/end events with a per-pair reference count (a pair begins only once it holds a touching contact, see "Speculative contacts" below), and into the collider-pair events of scripted gathered colliders (see "Collider events");
2. **sorts events by the canonical order key** `PhysicsEventOrderKey` (lower body owner UUID, higher body owner UUID, type, receiving collider: the null UUID for a body event), because Jolt documents callback order as non-deterministic;
3. drops events whose entities were destroyed;
4. dispatches a body event to scripts on **both** entities, and a collider event to the scripted gathered collider alone: `OnCollisionEnter(other, contact)`, `OnCollisionExit(other)`, and for sensor pairs `OnTriggerEnter(other)`, `OnTriggerExit(other)`. `other` is the body owner. `contact = {Point, Normal, RelativeSpeed, Collider, OtherCollider}`, where `Collider` and `OtherCollider` are the collider entities of the first sub-shape pair that touched, resolved through the sub-shape user data (§9.2). They differ from the owner for compounds, for example the track piece under a level root.

Body events are per body pair: a ball rolling from one piece of a compound track to the next stays in contact with the same body and gets no new `OnCollisionEnter`. M37's joint breaks (§9.10) are dispatched after a PostStep's pair events, in UUID order of the joints' entities. A piece whose own script needs its collisions is a scripted gathered collider and gets collider events of its own.

**Speculative contacts** (ADR 0031 decision 3). Jolt adds a contact as soon as two shapes are within its speculative contact distance (2 cm), still apart, so a ball gliding 1 cm past a brick used to enter and exit without touching it (ADR 0026 P03). A contact touches when its manifold's penetration depth is at least 0, or when Jolt's solver acts on it within the collision step: its relative normal speed times the collision step's delta time (the step's delta over its collision steps) is at least its separation, Jolt's own test for applying a speculative contact's impulse and restitution, so a ball that bounces or stops on a speculative contact touches at that step, on both sides of the restitution threshold. Sensor contacts (Jolt adds them only for overlapping shapes) and character contacts (`CharacterVirtual` reports only what its update collided with) are recorded touching. A contact added without touching counts for its pair's lifetime but cannot start it: a pair enters at the first PostStep after which it holds a touching contact, its enter's contact being the first touching contact of that step; a pair whose contacts all end before one touched reports nothing; an entered pair exits when its last contact, touching or not, ends. The rule runs inside PostStep and changes no world state, so the simulation's state hashes stay as they were; scripts that see fewer or later enters change theirs.

**Collider events** (ADR 0031 decision 2, ADR 0026 P01). A scripted gathered collider is an entity whose Script component names a script and whose solid colliders are gathered into another owner's body (a `RigidBody`'s compound or an implicit static body's tree). The system reads the component alone, never the script or a VM, so a Simulate session decides the same way. Its collider pairs, keyed by (the collider entity, the partner's body owner, kind), count only the contacts of its own sub-shapes and follow every body-pair rule (the pending enter, dormant contacts, rebuilds and unconfirmed pairs, the drop rules, synthesized exits at the destroy and disable flushes of either side); a collider pair is a collision or a trigger pair as its body pair is. Its event's `Self` is the collider, `SelfBody` its body's owner, `Other` the partner's body owner, and the contact names the collider and the partner's collider of the first sub-shape pair, the normal pointing from the collider's body towards the partner. The partner and the body's owner keep their body events unchanged, so a scene without scripted gathered colliders dispatches exactly as before. A collider that stops being one (its Script component removed or naming no script, a `RigidBody` of its own, moved out of the body) ends its collider pairs at the next PostStep with synthesized exits, and one that becomes one while touching enters at the next PostStep. A compound rebuilt in place (`SetShape`) can move a persisting contact's sub-shape ID to another collider, so the system resolves the colliders of a rebuilt body's contacts again (`PhysicsWorld::GetSubShapeCollider`). Collider pairs never wake bodies and are not counted in `stats.get` or `physics.bodyInfo`. A collider pair sees the sub-shape contacts Jolt reports: with Jolt's manifold reduction (on for every body), the contacts of one body pair whose normals agree are merged into one manifold, named after the first sub-shape pair Jolt found, so a body resting flat across two coplanar pieces (or a ball on the seam between them) touches only one of them as far as collider events go; pieces whose contacts face different ways (a floor and a wall) each get theirs.

**Exit on destroy, disable and character contacts.** Jolt reports a destroyed body's `OnContactRemoved` only at the next step, with the stale handle, so the session keeps the set of active pairs and closes a destroyed body's contacts itself (ADR 0014 decision 25). At each destroy/disable flush (§5.7 step 8 and the frame-phase flush), every active pair involving a destroyed or newly disabled entity is closed: the surviving partner receives `OnCollisionExit(other)` or `OnTriggerExit(other)`, with `other:IsValid() == false` for a destroyed entity and `other:IsActive() == false` for a disabled one. Teleporting out of a trigger is reported by Jolt's next step as a normal exit. A checkpoint trigger therefore never keeps a stale "inside" state after a respawn.

Scripts never run on physics threads. Destroying an entity inside a callback is deferred (§5.7).

**Dispatch details** (ADR 0014 decisions 11, 12 and 25; ADR 0031 decision 2). The system delivers one `PhysicsEvent` per receiving entity of a pair event (`{Type, Self, Other, Contact, Synthesized, Tick, SelfBody}`, the normal from `Self`'s body towards `Other`; `SelfBody` is `Self` for a body event and the collider's body owner for a collider event) to an `IPhysicsEventListener`, which M13's dispatcher implements; pair events are sorted by `PhysicsEventOrderKey`, a body event is dispatched first to the lower UUID, and a pair's collider events follow its body event of the same type. M21's 2D world and M26's height fields dispatch with the same key. Events of a pair with an entity already pending destruction or disabled when the dispatch starts are not dispatched (an enter is dropped and the pair never becomes active; the exit is the flush's). A callback whose `Self` an earlier callback of the same dispatch destroyed or disabled is dropped, while its partner's is still delivered; a side that got the enter gets exactly one exit unless its own entity goes first. Pairs are keyed by owner UUIDs and kind, so they survive rebuilds: a rebuilt body's pairs become unconfirmed, and at PostStep a pair that no contact re-established ends with a synthesized exit. Jolt also reports `OnContactRemoved` when two touching bodies fall asleep and `OnContactAdded` when they wake; such contacts stay **dormant** (still counted for their pair), so sleeping never ends a pair, and are dropped only after a step that began with one of their bodies awake and did not report them again. `FlushDestroyed` repeats its close, dispatch and remove pass until a pass finds nothing. Run-time diagnostics are logged once and passed to `IPhysicsEventListener::OnPhysicsDiagnostic`, which M13 turns into the script error for a refused body (§9.1).

### 9.5 Queries
`Raycast`, `RaycastAll`, `SphereCast` (`CastShape`), `OverlapSphere`, `OverlapBox` through `NarrowPhaseQuery` on the main thread, filtered by layer mask, results sorted by distance then UUID. Hits report the collider entity and the owning body entity. Bounds: `GetBodyBounds(entity)` returns the world AABB of the body the entity owns, and `GetColliderBounds(entity)` the world AABB of that entity's own collider sub-shapes, whether they form a standalone body or part of an ancestor's compound. Both are nil when there is none. Queries include sensors, so a game can ask whether a point lies inside a checkpoint (ADR 0014 decision 7). `Raycast` casts all hits and returns the first after sorting by distance, then collider UUID, then body UUID; `SphereCast` keeps the world's single closest hit, ties broken by body handle (handles follow the canonical creation order); a world-level overlap returns one entry per (body, collider). Scene-level queries validate their input (radii and half extents within [`MinColliderSize` / 2, `MaxColliderSize` / 2], points within `MaxPhysicsCoordinate`; InvalidArgument otherwise) and leave out entities pending destruction or disabled; world-level ones assert on invalid input (ADR 0014 decisions 30 and 34).

### 9.6 Character and ball control
- `CharacterControllerComponent` wraps `JPH::CharacterVirtual` with `ExtendedUpdate` (stair stepping, floor sticking), updated in PreStep from the desired velocity set by `CharacterController:Move(velocity)`. `IsGrounded()`, `GetGroundNormal()`, `GetVelocity()`. A `CharacterVirtual` is not in the broad phase, so the character gets an inner body: an ordinary Kinematic capsule of the controller's size created by `PhysicsWorld::CreateBody` (not Jolt's `mInnerBodyShape`, which the world's records, limits and filters would miss), on the controller's layer and in its collision group, with the owner's UUID as user data, never sleeping, and the world's next body in the canonical creation order, so its ID is deterministic. The controller places it at the padded base after every update and teleport (ADR 0014 decisions 8 and 23). Raycasts, overlaps and sensors therefore see the character through its kinematic inner body. A `CharacterContactListener` records character-vs-body contacts into the same buffer, so the character's script and the other body receive `OnCollisionEnter`/`OnCollisionExit` with the same sorting and exit rules (§9.4).
- **Characters and Dynamic bodies** (M34, ADR 0049 decisions 1 and 2; World Tree's brief 11). Placed rather than swept, the inner body would push a Dynamic body it overlaps with infinite mass, driving light bodies through the floor and launching the character that stands on one. So its object layer has the Character kind (§9.2), which pairs with sensors only: the solver never resolves a contact between an inner body and a Dynamic, Kinematic, Static or other inner body, while queries and sensors see it as before and the character's own collision meets other characters' inner bodies as Moving bodies, so characters still block each other. A character pushes Dynamic bodies only through `CharacterVirtual`'s own contacts, with at most `Mass` × 9.81 N (`mMaxStrength`; no push-strength field). A Dynamic body lighter than the character's `Mass` never moves it: it cannot push it (`mCanPushCharacter` off), it does not carry the character up its upward-facing surfaces (its contact is a vertical wall to the character's slide, `OnContactSolve`, except the walkable ground the character stands on, which it walks along as on any ground; what the wall leaves moving into a steep face slides along the face instead of hanging the character there), its velocity is not the character's ground velocity (so standing on one never launches the character), it is never a stair (the controller runs `ExtendedUpdate`'s walk-stairs step itself without light bodies, so the character pushes a light body below `StepHeight` instead of climbing it) and it carries at most its own weight from the character (the controller puts the weight on a Dynamic ground itself, `min(Mass, m)` × the gravity's part along the ground normal × dt). A Dynamic body at least as heavy as the character pushes it, carries it and is climbed as before. Collision events between a character and a Dynamic body come from the character's own contacts alone. A Dynamic body moving into a character (ADR 0049 decision 3; `Docs/Backlog.md` §6): a light one is stopped by the character's own push (the character's update meets a body approaching within 0.1 m and pushes it back with at most `Mass` × 9.81 N for the tick) and passes into the capsule only when it outruns that look-ahead within one tick or is driven harder than the push; a light platform never lifts or carries a character (it rises through one it is driven up under, and gives no ground velocity, with `InheritGroundVelocity` or without); a heavy one shoves the character through its contacts and overlaps it only when the character is pinned against static geometry or under the body. A projectile that must hit a character is a trigger or a cast, which see the inner body. Test: "CharacterController: a character walking at 6.5 m/s through fifteen 0.35 kg Dynamic shards on the floor stays below 0.1 m over 60 ticks, and no shard goes below -0.05 m: the shards are pushed aside along the ground".
- **What a character stands on** (M36, `Docs/Decisions/0053-m36-contact-surfaces.md` decisions 4 and 5; World Tree's briefs 15 and 16). The ground state names the body and the collider the character stands on, from Jolt's ground body and sub-shape of the update itself (no query): `CharacterController:GetGroundCollider() -> Entity?` (another character's entity when it stands on one; nil in the air, or when that entity is disabled or pending destruction), `physics.bodyInfo`'s `groundCollider`, and `Physics.GetSurface(collider) -> SurfaceInfo?` the values its contacts use (its `ColliderSurface`'s friction and restitution and its velocity in world space, as the component holds them now, or its body's material with no velocity; nil for nil, for a disabled entity and for one without a solid collider in a body, a character's capsule included; a destroyed entity is an error), so a game reads its footing as `Physics.GetSurface(controller:GetGroundCollider())`, nil in the air. The ground collider's surface velocity, its part along the ground alone (projected onto the plane of the ground normal, as a body takes a surface velocity only through friction along the contact; the lead's decision on the W36.2 review, ADR 0053), joins the ground's velocity (`CharacterGroundState::GroundVelocity`): its vertical part (an inclined belt's) as every ground's, and its horizontal part carries a grounded character whatever `InheritGroundVelocity` says, added to the velocity its script asks for, so a belt carries the Warden 2.5 m in a second while it walks ("CharacterController: a belt carries a grounded character whatever InheritGroundVelocity says"); `InheritGroundVelocity` stays about ground that really moves. A Dynamic body lighter than the character gives none, surface or not (M34's rule). `CharacterVirtual` has no friction, so the engine makes no character slide on ice: a game reads the ground's friction and slides its own character.
- **Pushes and the squeeze** (M36 W36.2, `Docs/Decisions/0053-m36-contact-surfaces.md` decisions 11 and 12; World Tree's brief 16). A Kinematic body, or a Dynamic body not lighter than the character, moving into a character pushes it along the contact's normal at the body's velocity, through `CharacterVirtual`'s moving contact planes: a body within the character's look-ahead (0.1 m) at its update, so up to 6 m/s at 60 Hz, never enters the capsule; a faster one overlaps it for one tick, by at most its step beyond the look-ahead, and pushes it out at the next update; one beyond about 0.1 m plus `Radius` a tick can pass through it (`Docs/Backlog.md` §6). Measured by "CharacterController: a Kinematic piston pushes a character at its velocity" at 2 and 8 m/s; the push moves the character, which its position shows, while `CharacterController:GetVelocity()` stays the velocity its update asked for. A character such a body cannot move out of the way is **squeezed**: after its update, the contacts of its last pass name the bodies that push it (not sensors, able to push it, not Static, moving towards it faster than 1 mm/s), and one shape query of the character's capsule against those bodies alone, at the position the update left it, measures each: a body whose push over the step would leave it more than `CharacterSqueezeTolerance` (1 cm) inside the padded capsule squeezes it (the floor under a press, a wall behind a piston). `CharacterController:IsSqueezed()` and `:GetSqueezingBody() -> Entity?` (the squeezing body's owner; the one with the lowest body handle when several squeeze it, a deterministic choice) read the last update, so a script sees a squeeze in the next fixed update; `physics.bodyInfo` reports `squeezed` and `squeezedBy`. A body at rest (a resting ram a belt carries the character into), one moving away, the character's own walk into a wall, a corner or a steep face, and a press's first contact while still above the head never squeeze. There is no callback, no escape and no damage: the engine invents no sideways escape from under a flat face, whose contact normal is vertical, and the game crushes or shoves what is squeezed. The squeeze is derived from the character's state each update, like `IsGrounded`, and not hashed.
- The rolling ball (Rolling Ball 3D, §13.11) is a Dynamic sphere with `LinearCast`, `EnhancedInternalEdgeRemoval`, friction 0.8 and `MaxAngularVelocity` raised to 120 rad/s (Jolt's default 47 rad/s caps a 0.5 m ball at ≈ 23 m/s). Its script steers it in the fixed step relative to the ball's own heading, which it keeps there: while the ball is grounded (a downward `Physics.Raycast` on the track's layer) and faster than a threshold, the heading turns towards the horizontal velocity by a bounded angle a tick. The move direction is right(heading) × `MoveX` + forward(heading) × `MoveZ`; on the ground the script applies `AddTorque(cross(up, moveDir) * torque)`, and in the air a small `AddForce` for air control. The follow camera reads that heading in `OnLateUpdate`, and the simulation never reads the camera's frame-phase pose, so live play does not depend on the frame rate (§11.2, §11.3). Each level root carries a `Static` `RigidBody`, so all track pieces form one static compound without seams (§5.3). Moving platforms are kinematic bodies driven by `RigidBody:MoveKinematic`. Checkpoints and the goal are triggers with explicit sensor bodies: a sensor `RigidBody` of their own on the `Trigger` layer, Type Static, which the engine creates as a Kinematic sensor that follows its entity (§9.2). An implicit sensor body would take the layer of its nearest ancestor `RigidBody` (§5.3), under the level root the `Track` layer, and every `Track`-masked query (the ground probe, the main-path support check) would see it, since queries include sensors (§9.5). The kill plane is a height check in the ball's script, not a trigger: below its level's kill height the ball is teleported to its spawn with `RigidBody:Teleport` and both of its velocities are zeroed, since `Teleport` keeps them.
- **Character conventions** (ADR 0014 decisions 8, 23 and 34). The entity's origin is the capsule's base, and `Height > 2 × Radius` (else `PHYSICS_INVALID_SHAPE`). `Move(velocity)` is consumed by one PreStep: a script moves its character by calling it in every `OnFixedUpdate`, and a jump is one `Move` with an upward part. A step's velocity is the desired velocity's horizontal part plus, while grounded (Jolt's `OnGround` while the character does not move away from the ground faster than 0.1 m/s), the ground's vertical velocity and the desired vertical part, and in the air the previous vertical velocity plus gravity × `GravityFactor` × dt; with `InheritGroundVelocity`, while grounded, also the ground's horizontal velocity (Jolt's ground velocity, read before the step: a kinematic platform's velocity, a rotating body's surface velocity under the character), so a platform moving at v carries the character v × t, and the character walks relative to it; it is clamped to `MaxCharacterSpeed` (500 m/s), and `MoveCharacter` refuses a desired velocity with a larger component. `StepHeight` sets both the stair step-up and the floor step-down. A gravity whose squared length underflows counts as none; the weight a character puts on a Dynamic ground is capped at 1e10 N s (and at the body's own weight for a body lighter than the character, M34); an update that would carry the character beyond `MaxPhysicsCoordinate` leaves it where it was with no velocity and warns once. The ground's horizontal velocity carries the character only with `InheritGroundVelocity` (off by default, so a character keeps only the ground's vertical velocity) and only while grounded (a collider surface's velocity carries it either way, M36): a character that jumps off a moving platform moves in the air as its `Move` tells it, and no binding exposes the ground's velocity (`Physics.GetSurface` exposes a collider's surface velocity alone). A change in play of `GravityFactor` or `InheritGroundVelocity` applies in place; one of any other `CharacterController` field creates the character again with its velocity, and a new character is not grounded during its first step (ADR 0030 decision 36; ADR 0025 decision 11).

### 9.7 Determinism tests
A 200-body pile stepped 600 times gives the same `ComputeStateHash()` across repeated runs and with Jolt thread counts 0, 1 and 8. Contact-event order is identical across runs. The same pile's final hash is a committed constant checked in the Debug and Release unit runs, and the `determinism` stage compares a 600-tick physics-and-script replay across Editor Debug, Editor Release, exported Release and exported Dist (§15.8). Contact-event order, collider events included, is identical at Jolt thread counts 0, 1 and 8 (ADR 0031). Other tests: free fall vs analytic, rest height (0.48 with slop), restitution bounce, trigger enter/exit exactly once (including a sleeping body), layer matrix (incl. no Sensor–Static/Sensor–Sensor pairs), teleport honoured in the same tick, kinematic platform carry, CCD prevents tunnelling at 200 m/s, destroy inside a callback is safe, seam test (§9.2), compound contacts name the child collider, synthesized exits on destroy and disable, trigger detects a character (inner body), invalid shapes, all-DOF-locked and Dynamic-trigger bodies are rejected with diagnostics and never assert; a speculative contact that never touches reports no enter, one that bounces or stops a body enters at that step on both sides of the restitution threshold, and a scripted collider gathered into a compound receives its own enter and exit, also across an in-place rebuild of the compound. M36: a Kinematic piston pushes a character at its velocity at 2 and 8 m/s, a press brought down onto a grounded character and a piston pressing one against a wall report it squeezed by them, a character carried into a resting ram stops against it and is not squeezed, and a character's own walk into a wall, a corner or a steep face is never a squeeze; a collider surface's friction and restitution replace its body's for contacts with that collider, contacts between bodies without surfaces stay bit-identical (the committed pile beside a surface), a surface velocity carries what rests on it turned with its body, shards struck alike travel farther on ice than on marble of one static compound, a surface write keeps the body's handle and shape and composes nothing, and a belt carries a grounded character whatever `InheritGroundVelocity` says. M37's joints (§9.10): each type against an analytic case (a pendulum's period, a motor reaching its target, limits holding, a weld reading and breaking at its load), kept frames across body rebuilds, every body removal path, two histories stepping identically, and a chain, a motored hinge, a limited slider and a breaking weld at Jolt thread counts 0, 1 and 8 with a committed hash. M44's vehicles (§9.11): a centre-of-mass offset that moves the centre of mass and keeps the origin's pose, bodies without one bit for bit as before; a vehicle at rest on every wheel within 1 cm of its analytic rest length, full throttle at the analytic top speed within 2 %, a full-lock turn at 15 m/s that rolls a buggy over without its lowered centre of mass and not with it, a 2 m drop onto its wheels, a wheel's grip following its ground's friction, refusals before Jolt's asserts, every body removal path, kept wheel frames through a body made again, a reparent and components added back, two histories stepping identically on one island, and twenty-four vehicles (Jolt steps vehicles in jobs of eight) and a convoy at Jolt thread counts 0, 1 and 8, the convoy with a committed hash.

### 9.8 The 2D world (`Physics/Physics2DWorld`, M21)
`Physics2DWorld` (ADR 0028 decision 6; ADR 0032 decision 8) is a second `PhysicsWorld`, owned by the play session's 2D system, whose API speaks 2D: `Physics2DPose` (a position in the plane and an angle about +Z), planar forces, impulses and velocities, scalar torques and angular velocities about Z. No library is added and the frozen `PhysicsShape.h` does not change.
- **Plane locks.** A Dynamic body allows translation along X and Y and rotation about Z only (`Physics2DDofs`; `Physics2DTranslationDofs` with `FixedRotation`), Jolt's `EAllowedDOFs`: Jolt masks the locked velocity components and position steps, so a body's Z, its rotation's X and Y and its off-plane velocities stay exactly zero. Kinematic bodies move only to planar targets and Static ones never move; every pose, force and velocity the world is handed is planar (`ToPhysicsPose`: z = 0 and the rotation of the angle about +Z through DetMath).
- **Shapes** (`MakeBody2DShape`) are the existing variant laid in the XY plane: a circle is a sphere that turns about Z as a disc (`BodyDescription::SpheresAsDiscs`: its moment about Z m r^2 / 2, not a sphere's 0.4 m r^2; M21's milestone review), a box a box and a polygon the hull of its points at z = -h and z = h, each collider extruded by its own half depth h (`GetPhysics2DHalfDepth`): the diagonal of its bounding rectangle after its scale (a circle's radius). Every body lies on z = 0, so two shapes overlap along Z by more than their deepest overlap in the plane, and Jolt's minimum-penetration axis, the contact normal, lies in the plane however deep they overlap; a box's or hull's inertia about Z is its 2D one at every size. The depth counts against `PhysicsShape::MaxColliderSize`, so a box or polygon whose diagonal exceeds 50 km is refused (Backlog §6).
- **Reads are planar.** `GetPose` is the pose's X, Y and the twist of its rotation about Z (`ToPhysics2DPose`, in (-pi, pi]); ray hits (`Raycast`, `RaycastAll`, in the plane z = 0) and drained contact records have their points at z = 0 and their normals in the plane, which removes the spread of a manifold's points over the extruded depth and the rounding that leaves a little Z in some contact normals. `Overlap` takes a box (laid with its half depth) or a circle.
- **Everything else is `PhysicsWorld`'s** (§9.1): validation (a void mutator asserts and ignores a pose that is not finite), `PHYSICS_*` codes, handles in creation order, unsorted contact records with M20's touching rule, determinism in every configuration and at every Jolt thread count ("Physics2DWorld: a 2D pile ends in the same state with 0, 1 and 8 Jolt threads", its sorted contact records included), main thread only. "Physics2DWorld: a dynamic body never leaves its plane" checks positions, rotations and velocities bit for bit on a pile of boxes, circles, polygons and compounds after 600 steps; "Physics2DWorld: a body sunk deep into a box is pushed out in the plane" checks the depth rule.

### 9.9 2D physics in the scene (`Scene/Physics2DSystem`, M21)
The 2D world (§9.8; ADR 0028 decision 6, ADR 0032 decisions 8 to 13), a second Jolt world beside the 3D one, is created only at a session's first 2D body, so a session without one holds one world and costs as before. `Physics2DSystem` is `PhysicsSystem`'s design in the plane, rule for rule: RigidBody2D in RigidBody's place and `BoxCollider2D`, `CircleCollider2D` and `PolygonCollider2D` in the colliders' (§5.3's composition: compounds, implicit static and sensor bodies, collision groups, canonical body order), the same rebuilds (the start flush's body synchronization included, §5.7 step 2), pairs across rebuilds, kinematic moves, teleports, write-back, events (M20's pending enter, dormant contacts and collider events, sorted by `PhysicsEventOrderKey`), flushes, diagnostics and queries (sorted by distance, then UUID).
- **One world per entity.** An entity holding a 2D and a 3D physics component is `PHYSICS2D_MIXED_WORLDS` (Error): it keeps its 3D body and its 2D components make no 2D body, so the 3D world is unchanged. The two worlds never collide with each other.
- **The plane.** A body takes its owner's world X and Y and the twist about Z of its world rotation; an owner (or a gathered collider's entity) rotated about X or Y is `PHYSICS2D_OFF_PLANE` (Warning). The write-back writes X, Y and a rotation about Z alone, keeping the entity's world Z (free for draw depth); a Transform write that leaves the planar pose as it is (a new Z) moves and wakes nothing, whatever the body's motion type: the pre-step compares the planar pose of the owner's Transform with the one it had at the body's last creation, placement, kinematic move or write-back, bit for bit, never with the body's own pose, whose angle the round trip through the quaternion may move by an ulp. Contacts and query hits are reported in the plane (Z 0).
- **Callbacks** `OnCollisionEnter2D(other, contact)`, `OnCollisionExit2D(other)`, `OnTriggerEnter2D(other)` and `OnTriggerExit2D(other)` reach every slot of the receiving entity as the 3D ones do (§11.3); the script surface is `RigidBody2D`'s methods and the `Physics2D` module (§11.5), the automation surface `physics2d.raycast` and `physics2d.overlap` (§13.5, a play session needed).
- **Settings.** The project section `Physics2D` holds `Gravity` (vec2, default (0, -9.81), each component within ±1e12 m/s²); the layers and the collision matrix are `Physics`'s.
- **Tilemap colliders** (C21.2, ADR 0032 decision 25). A `TilemapCollider` collides with its `Tilemap`, or its entity's `TilemapRenderer.Tilemap` when it names none, loaded through the session's asset manager (`project.validate` loads it through the editor's, so both report alike): its merged boxes (§5.3) are `BoxShape2D` sub-shapes of the cells' rectangles in the entity's plane, scaled and placed as the other 2D colliders, built in canonical order in integers, so the shape is the same in every configuration. A collider without a tilemap, with a missing or failed one, or with more than `MaxTilemapColliderBoxes` (65,536) boxes is `PHYSICS_INVALID_SHAPE` (`Component` TilemapCollider, `Field` Tilemap) and its body is not created; a tilemap without a solid cell adds no box, and a body left without any is not created, without a diagnostic. Every rebuild records the version of each creatable body's tilemaps, and the pre-step rebuilds when one changes (`tilemap.paint`, a reimport), so the shape is rebuilt in place (`PhysicsWorld::SetShape`: pose, velocities and pairs kept), a body erased down to no solid cell is removed and one painted back is created again; a `TilemapRenderer` change counts only for a `TilemapCollider` on its entity that takes the renderer's tilemap. A body rolling across the boxes' seams sets `RigidBody2D.EnhancedInternalEdgeRemoval` (§9.2 "Seams"). A scene without a `TilemapCollider` loads no tilemap and hashes as before.
- **The state hash** gets a physics2d block after M19's native block: every 2D body in canonical order of its owner (solid before sensor), its owner's UUID, position, angle, linear and angular velocity as little-endian float bits, and its sleeping flag; nothing without a 2D body, so every existing replay keeps its hash. Tested at Jolt thread counts 0, 1 and 8, a tilemap collider's terrain included.

### 9.10 Joints (`Scene/PhysicsJoints`, `Scene/PhysicsSystemJoints.cpp`, M37)
Joints (M37, ADR 0054; World Tree's brief 16) join two bodies, or a body and the world, through Jolt's hinge, slider, distance and fixed constraints, from the `HingeJoint`, `SliderJoint`, `DistanceJoint` and `FixedJoint` components (§5.3, category Joints; one per entity).
- **Which bodies.** `ComposePhysicsJoints` (`Scene/PhysicsJoints.h`, beside the body composition and never changing it; the session, `project.validate` and the debug view share it): a joint's body is the body of the RigidBody at or above its entity (its own, else its nearest ancestor's, with no CharacterController on the way), so a joint sits on a body's entity or a child of it and a body may hold several; `ConnectedBody` names the other end by the same rule or, without a RigidBody at or above it, the implicit static body its solid colliders belong to, the whole of it (an ancestor's, when the ancestor gathers them, so `CollideConnected` false then keeps the joined body apart from every collider of that body); null joins the body to the world. A joint that cannot be made is `PHYSICS_JOINT_INVALID` (§13.7): the joint is not created and its bodies simulate unjoined.
- **The world** (`PhysicsWorld.h`'s joints section, `Physics/PhysicsJoint.h`): joints by `JointHandle`, created from frames in each body's space relative to its origin (the world converts them to Jolt's centre-of-mass space), changed in place, measured and destroyed. Nothing invalid reaches Jolt: equal limits without a spring, limits of the wrong sign, axes that are not unit, invalid motor settings and unbounded springs or targets are refused or clamped (§9.1). `DestroyBody` destroys a body's joints first, since a Jolt constraint holds raw body pointers, and `SetShape` tells them that the body's centre of mass moved. A joint whose `CollideConnected` is false keeps its two bodies apart in both of Jolt's collision passes (the body-pair hook, and a simulation shape filter for continuous casts), so no contact or collision event is ever made between them; a change of it makes the pair collide afresh at the next step.
- **The session.** Joints are created after every body of a rebuild, in UUID order of their entities, and synchronized in PhysicsPreStep and the start flush's synchronization whenever a joint component changed or a body was created or removed (§5.7). A change of the motor, a target, a limit, friction, the spring, `CollideConnected` or a threshold applies to the live joint in place and wakes its bodies, without recomposing the scene, so a script may write a motor target every tick. A hinge's, slider's or fixed joint's two frames are formed when it is first made, from the poses of that moment (the authored pose is the hinge's angle 0 and the slider's position 0), and kept: a body created again (a RigidBody change, a re-enabled entity) gets its joints back at the same frames, so a door that swung keeps its zero and its limits; a change of `ConnectedBody`, `Anchor`, `Axis`, the bodies the ends resolve to or the joint entity's place in the hierarchy forms them again from that moment's poses. A distance joint reads both anchors from the scene at every creation, and a change of `ConnectedBody`, either anchor, the bodies its ends resolve to or its entity's place in the hierarchy makes it again. Every joint in force solves at its entity's rank in UUID order (Jolt's constraint priority), so the solve order is a function of the state, never of Jolt's add-and-remove history. A body's joints are destroyed before it on every removal path; a joint whose entity or connected end leaves play (disabled or destroyed) keeps what it has until the destroy and disable flushes, as their bodies step until then, and the flushes remove it.
- **Breaking.** At the start of PhysicsPostStep, each joint in force with a `BreakForce` or `BreakTorque` compares the force and torque of the last collision step (the length of its linear and of its angular constraint impulses, the motor's and the friction's left out, divided by the collision step's duration) with them; one over either is removed, its bodies woken, `Broken` written true into its component (scene data, so hashed) and its break dispatched after the step's pair events. A `Broken` joint is never made; `Broken` written false mends it at its kept frames, which the solver reaches gradually from wherever the bodies are. Below 60 Hz a tick has several collision steps, so a joint at the edge of its threshold may break on another tick at another rate (deterministic in every configuration).
- **The state hash.** The physics block's joint part follows its bodies and characters: every joint whose frames the session keeps, in canonical order of its entity, its UUID and its two kept frames' bits; nothing without a joint, so every existing replay keeps its hash.

### 9.11 Vehicles (`Scene/PhysicsVehicles`, `Scene/PhysicsSystemVehicles.cpp`, M44)
Wheeled vehicles (M44, ADR 0062; Skerries' brief S02) drive a Dynamic body on Jolt's `VehicleConstraint` with its `WheeledVehicleController`, from a `WheeledVehicle` on the body's entity and a `VehicleWheel` on each wheel entity below it (§5.3, category Vehicles). A `MassProperties` beside the body's `RigidBody` lowers its centre of mass (§9.2 "Mass overrides").
- **Which body and wheels.** `ComposePhysicsVehicles` (`Scene/PhysicsVehicles.h`, beside the body composition and never changing it; the session, `project.validate` and the debug view share it): a vehicle drives its own entity's Dynamic, non-trigger body, and its wheels are the `VehicleWheel` entities whose nearest `WheeledVehicle` it is, with no `RigidBody` or `CharacterController` on the way, in canonical order (the world's wheel index). A wheel carries no collider (the chassis would gather it): it finds the ground by its cast. `PHYSICS_VEHICLE_INVALID` (Error) reports one reason per vehicle, the first of `body`, `wheels`, `wheel`, `collider`, `suspension`, `engine`, `transmission`, `differential`, `bar` and `curve`, at edit time and in play alike, and `refused` in play for a description the world refuses; such a vehicle is not created, and its body moves as a plain body. A disabled wheel of the vehicle is no wheel (a differential's side drives nothing, a bar is left out) without a word while the vehicle stays drivable; disabled wheels that leave it undriven, or its driven shares off 1, are `differential`, named. Destroying a wheel that a differential or bar names makes the vehicle invalid: disable a wheel to take it off.
- **The world** (`PhysicsWorld.h`'s vehicles section, `Physics/PhysicsVehicle.h`): vehicles by `VehicleHandle`, described in the body's space (its origin; radians), created, changed in place, read and destroyed. Forward is the body's local -Z and up its +Y; every suspension runs along the body's -Y from an attachment point `SuspensionMaxLength` above the wheel's authored centre, and steers about its +Y; the wheel's authored rotation gives its camber and toe, its axle along its local X. The cast is `Ray`, `Sphere` (Jolt's sphere tester has one radius: the vehicle's smallest wheel `Radius`) or `Cylinder` (each wheel's radius and width), on the body's object layer, skipping sensors and the vehicle's own body. Nothing invalid reaches Jolt's asserts: every value is finite and bounded (the registry's ranges are the world's), and the rules across fields (decision 3's list, Jolt's torque-share rule within 1e-6 among them) are refused with nothing created. `DestroyBody` destroys a body's vehicle before its joints and the body, since a Jolt vehicle holds a raw body pointer; reads name a wheel's ground by its body ID, never the step's pointer. A wheel's grip is `sqrt(tyre × ground)` in each direction, the ground's friction its collider's `ColliderSurface`'s, else its body's (`Detail::ResolveGroundFriction`, the hook M54's terrain layers join). Vehicles solve after the joints: the session ranks the joints in force from 0 in UUID order, then the vehicles, so no two constraints share a priority (Jolt sorts by priority, then index, within an island).
- **The session.** Vehicles are synchronized after the joints in every rebuild, in PhysicsPreStep and in the start flush's synchronization whenever a vehicle component changed or a body was created or removed. A write of driver input alone composes nothing (item 4b applies it). A change of the engine, the transmission, the differentials, a bar's stiffness or `MaxPitchRollAngle` applies in place; a change of a wheel's field, the wheel set, the cast or the bars' wheels, or the body made again, makes the vehicle again on its body, carrying over its RPM, gear, clutch and each wheel's spin and angle (the rest of its drivetrain state, its constraint's warm start and Jolt's previous step time, starts afresh). Each wheel's frame (its authored centre, up and forward in the body's space, the vehicle's world scale included) is formed when the vehicle is first made with it and kept for the session while the wheel belongs to the vehicle, so a vehicle made again, a reparent below it or a component removed and added back finds every wheel where it was authored, never where the engine last wrote it.
- **Driving it** (PhysicsPreStep item 4b, after the kinematic moves and before the characters): each vehicle in force, in canonical order, takes its `WheeledVehicle`'s `Throttle`, `Steering` (+1 is full right lock), `Brake`, `HandBrake`, `Gear` and `Clutch`; a sleeping body wakes for a throttle or any new input, since Jolt keeps a vehicle awake only while its wheels spin. `Auto` shifts by `ShiftUpRpm` and `ShiftDownRpm` and reverses for a negative `Throttle` when it has a reverse gear; `Manual` drives by `Throttle` in [0, 1] in its `Gear`'s direction (clamped to the ratios) through its `Clutch`. The `Differentials` that name a wheel share the engine's torque by `EngineTorqueRatio`, summing to 1; a vehicle that drives nothing (a trailer) has one differential, in `Manual` at `Gear` 0. Jolt keeps the engine's torque at `MaxRpm`, so a `TorqueCurve` that falls to 0 there is a rev limiter: only then is the top speed `MaxRpm × 2π / 60 / (top gear ratio × differential ratio) × radius`.
- **Wheel poses** (PhysicsPostStep, after the write-back and before the pair events): each wheel entity of a vehicle in force gets its wheel's pose (suspension, steer and spin) as its local Translation and Rotation through the vehicle's world scale and the chain of local matrices below it, written only when a bit differs, so collision callbacks see the wheels placed and render interpolation draws them in the rendered pose; its Scale stays its own.
- **Reads.** `WheeledVehicle:GetSpeed`, `GetEngineRpm`, `GetGear` and `IsShifting`; `VehicleWheel:IsTouching`, `GetContact` (point, normal, collider entity), `GetSuspensionLength`, `GetSuspensionForce`, `GetRotation` ([0, 360) degrees), `GetSteerAngle` (degrees, positive right), `GetAngularVelocity` (degrees per second, positive rolling forward) and `GetSlip` (the slip ratio and the slip angle in degrees), all after the last physics step (§11.5); `physics.vehicleInfo` reports the same (§13.5). A vehicle not in force raises "entity has no vehicle in force".
- **The state hash.** The physics block's vehicle part follows its joint part: every vehicle whose wheel frames the session keeps, in canonical order of its entity, its UUID, each kept frame's wheel UUID and bits, and while it is in force its engine's and transmission's saved state and each wheel's spin, angle, steer and suspension length; then each placed wheel's authored pose. Nothing without a vehicle, so every existing replay keeps its hash. Vehicles step in Jolt's step-listener jobs, each writing only its own vehicle; twenty-four vehicles step alike at Jolt thread counts 0, 1 and 8, and a convoy's hash is committed (§9.7).
- **The debug view** (`Scene/VehicleDebugDraw`): under the Colliders flag, after the joints, each wheel's circle with one spoke at its pose, its suspension's travel and, in play, its contact's normal, in pink, or rust for a vehicle the session did not make (or, at edit time, would not); lines only.
- **Limits** (`Docs/Backlog.md` §6): wheels never meet characters (their casts use the chassis's layer); until M54 a terrain's grip is its `TerrainCollider`'s; a wheel turning more than half a turn per tick aliases on screen; a sleeping vehicle's wheels keep turning by their last spin, slowed by their `AngularDamping`, and their entities creep.

---

## 10. Audio (miniaudio 0.11.25)

### 10.1 Engine
- `AudioEngine` (ECS-agnostic, one per application) wraps `ma_engine` whose resource manager uses a **custom `ma_vfs` backed by the engine VFS**, so loose files in the editor and `Game.pak` entries play through identical code. Groups (`ma_sound_group`): Master → Music, Sfx, Ui.
- **The engine never owns the device.** `ma_engine` is **always** created with `noDevice = MA_TRUE`, 2 channels at 48 kHz, in every mode. Windowed runs add a separate engine-owned `ma_device` (playback, f32 stereo, 48 kHz; miniaudio converts to the native format). Its data callback only calls `ma_engine_read_pcm_frames(&engine, out, frameCount, nullptr)`, the pattern miniaudio documents for caller-owned devices. Headless runs and tests have no device and pull frames themselves. Because the node graph never references a device, device loss or a reroute re-initializes **only the `ma_device`**: every `ma_sound`, group and voice keeps its state and playback position.
- **Device notifications.** The device config's `notificationCallback` only queues the notification; `AudioEngine::Update` handles the queue on the main thread, on the frame clock's time (never the wall clock). `rerouted` (default device changed, e.g. headphones unplugged) is logged. An unexpected `stopped` uninitializes the `ma_device` and re-creates it on the current default device after 1 s, up to 3 attempts, then gives up with one warning and keeps running with no device. If no device can be created at startup, the engine runs device-less with a warning. A `Rerouted` or `Started` after a `Stopped` cancels it (WASAPI stops, reroutes and restarts the device on a default-device change); a `Stopped` still pending a delay later re-creates the device only if it has not started again (ADR 0015 decisions 4 and 28).
- **Time ownership.** Three time sources, one reader at a time: `Device` (the callback reads in real time), `Simulation` and `Host` (no device: `Update` pulls the frames of each frame's unscaled delta with a fractional accumulator). While simulation time is owned the device callback outputs silence and does not read the engine, and the engine pulls one tick of frames per `AdvanceSimulationTick` into a discard or capture buffer: after n ticks at F Hz exactly round(n × 48000 / F) frames, half up and in integers (800 per tick at 60 Hz). The play session owns simulation time while it is in lockstep (§13.6) and, for its whole life, when it is a test run (`PlaySessionSpecification::OwnsAudioTime`, which M13's FeatureTest runner sets for every suite, `ScriptedClock` ones included); its `AudioUpdate` phase pulls one tick for every tick run since the last pull, never per frame, and ticks run before it took time are never pulled. A paused session that is not in lockstep does not take time: its voices are paused. Voices pause before time goes back to the device and resume only after the session has taken it (ADR 0015 decisions 5 and 13). Voices therefore advance with simulation time, and `play.step {ticks: 600}` no longer plays a burst out of sync. Normal play reads in real time through the device.
- **Deterministic decoding.** In test runs and headless processes, the resource manager is created with `MA_RESOURCE_MANAGER_FLAG_NO_THREADING` (which implies non-blocking) and `jobThreadCount = 0`. Before each pull, the `AudioEngine` processes pending resource-manager jobs inline (`ma_resource_manager_process_next_job` until empty), so streamed and async-loaded clips decode at the same simulation point in every run. Ordinary windowed Runtime keeps miniaudio's job thread. Windowed Editors construct the deterministic decoder from startup so in-process test runs do not replace a resource manager underneath loaded clips; playback devices remain available (ADR 0019 decision 6). A pull longer than 480 frames is read in chunks of at most 480, with the pending jobs processed before each, and `Update` processes them too, so a stream's next page is decoded before the mixer needs it (ADR 0015 decision 23). Test entry points select deterministic decoding before AudioEngine construction. `Test.CaptureAudio(n)` measures the exact sample interval of n ticks starting with its current step; with grouped fixed steps it waits for the containing AudioUpdate and resumes at the next phase 4, trimming earlier/later samples without an extra pull (ADR 0019 decision 6).
- **Clips** (ADR 0015 decision 6). A clip is named by its handle's 16 hex digits and registered per version under `"<16 hex digits>@<version>"` (miniaudio never replaces the data of a registered name), reference-counted (each `RegisterClip` balanced by `UnregisterClip`); a hot-reloaded version is a new registration while voices of the old one play on. An encoded clip that does not stream (at most `MaxDecodedClipSeconds`, 10 s, by default) is decoded once at registration (`Audio/AudioDecoder`'s `DecodeEncodedAudio`, interleaved f32) and registered with `ma_resource_manager_register_decoded_data`, as synthesized PCM is; `register_encoded_data` is not used, since every voice on encoded data would run its own decoder. A streamed clip (`MA_SOUND_FLAG_STREAM`) is decoded by the resource manager to the same f32, its bytes served by the `AudioVfs` as a memory file under the resource name (every other name resolves through the engine VFS), so streamed and decoded playback are sample-identical. Its bytes pass the decoder's container checks at registration all the same (`CheckStreamedAudio`, pages and headers only: an Ogg file's pages, an Ogg Vorbis file's comment and setup headers and an Ogg Opus file's single logical stream, as the import and the decode at registration check them), so a cooked clip stb_vorbis or opusfile would read past their buffers is refused before a voice opens it (ADR 0034's milestone review). The bytes are shared, never copied, and kept until the registration is removed and its last voice has ended.
- **Decoders** (ADR 0015 decision 2; ADR 0034 decision 16). WAV, FLAC and MP3 decode through miniaudio's built-in decoders, Ogg Vorbis through stb_vorbis compiled into the miniaudio project, and Ogg Opus through miniaudio's unmodified libopus decoding backend (`Vendor/miniaudio/extras/decoders/libopus`) over opusfile, libopus and libogg. That backend is a custom `ma_decoding_backend_vtable`, which `Audio/AudioDecoder` and the resource manager (for streamed clips) both register, wrapped by `Audio/Private/MiniaudioOpus.h` so that it claims only data whose first Ogg packet is an Opus identification header and asks for 16-bit samples: libopus is built fixed point without run-time CPU detection or intrinsics, so `op_read`'s samples, converted to f32 exactly by miniaudio, are identical in Debug, Release and Dist and on every CPU, whether the clip decodes at registration or streams. Ogg Opus always decodes at 48 kHz. `AudioDecoder` refuses an Ogg Opus file that is not one logical stream before opusfile reads it, since miniaudio sizes its buffers for the first link's channel count.
- **Voices** (ADR 0015 decisions 7, 23, 24 and 28). `HandlePool<Voice>` of 64 `ma_sound`s, each started with `ma_sound_init_from_file` on its registration's resource name, which shares the data buffer node (what `ma_sound_init_copy` does inside). When full, the voice with the lowest priority is stolen, then the farthest from the listener (non-spatial voices count as distance 0), then the oldest, but only when its priority is not above the new voice's; otherwise `PlayVoice` fails with InvalidState. Priorities, fixed when a voice starts: 0 for effects (Sfx and Ui sources and one-shots), 1 for music (Music sources and one-shots, M40's Music one-shots included, and the session's music), 2 for the editor's preview, so effects never steal the soundtrack or a stinger. A voice at the end of a non-looping clip is released at the end of the pull that played its last frame. The engine plays a voice at a pitch of at most 16 and reduces its Doppler factor so the Doppler pitch stays within [1/3, 3], and replaces every non-finite output sample with silence. `AudioVoiceInfo::CursorFrames` counts the frames the engine has mixed of the voice: exact while the engine pulls its own frames, miniaudio's cursor while a device reads. Captures (`StartCapture`/`StopCapture`, `Test.CaptureAudio`) record only the frames the engine pulls itself, up to 10 minutes.
- **Fades** (M40, ADR 0057 decision 3). A voice's level, a multiplier of its `Volume`, moves linearly from one value to another over a number of the voice's own mixed frames (48 kHz) on miniaudio's per-voice fader: `AudioVoiceDescription::Fade` starts a voice with one, set before it starts so no frame plays at another level, and `FadeVoice(voice, target, frames, end)` starts one from the level the voice has reached, replacing a fade in progress. A fade counts the voice node's clock (`ma_node_get_time`, the frames the mixer has output of the voice), so a paused voice's fade holds and a fade follows the time source as cursors do: simulation time in lockstep, test runs and replays, real time while the device reads. The engine keeps its own record of each fade and computes the level with the fader's formula, exact while it pulls its own frames, within a device period while a device reads (`AudioVoiceInfo::FadeVolume`, `FadeTarget`, `FadeEnd`). Every pull (and `Update`, for the device's reads) ends the fades it completed: an `AudioFadeEnd::Release` fade releases its voice at the end of the pull that completes it, and a `Hold` fade holds its target on the fader, re-armed from its start (off for 1) and again every `MaxFadeFrames` (about 12.4 hours), so the fader's 32-bit cursor, which stops writing frames after about 24.8 hours, never runs out. A level lives on the fader alone, never on the voice's volume, and the engine hands miniaudio at most one fader setting per voice per pull and per `Update`, the last one winning (miniaudio's hand-off is four separate atomics), so a device reading a voice never mixes a frame at a level the voice never had. A voice that never faded never touches the fader.
- **Chained voices** (M40, ADR 0057 decision 11): a voice whose description names a `Next` clip plays its clip once, then `Next` from the first frame after the clip's last, sample-accurate, decoded or streamed (an opening and its loop shipped as two files). It owns one resource-manager data source per section, linked with `ma_data_source_set_next` and read by one `ma_sound` (`ma_sound_init_from_data_source`); its `Loop` is set on the `Next` section's own looping flag (a stream loops inside its decoder, a decoded clip in its buffer's connector), never on the head, whose looping would stop the chain; when a looping stream's decoded pages run out (a loop shorter than a page, a second: miniaudio's page fill stops at its second end), the section re-enters itself through the chain and seeks to its start, as a looping voice of one clip does, with the seek's gap that `Docs/Backlog.md` §6 records, and a section that read nothing since its start ends the chain. A voice that loops is created looping (its `Next` section for a chained voice), since a stream decodes its first two pages when it opens, with the looping it has then. Both sections share one sample rate, channel count and sample format (InvalidArgument otherwise: a sound effect's 16-bit PCM and a decoded file's 32-bit float never chain, since miniaudio reads the chain in its head's format), since the voice's resampler follows its head. `AudioVoiceInfo` reports the section playing (`InNext`, `NextClip`), and its cursor and length are that section's: frames read ahead across the boundary but not yet mixed are the head's tail, exact while the engine pulls its own frames, the section miniaudio reads while a device does.

### 10.2 Components and spatialization (`Scene/AudioSystem`)
`AudioSystem::Update` runs after transforms in the frame phase: it creates/destroys voices for `AudioSourceComponent`s (EnTT signals), applies fields (volume, pitch, looping, attenuation model, min/max distance, rolloff, Doppler factor, group), sets position, direction and velocity (from the delta of the rendered pose, below) for spatial sources, and feeds `ma_engine_listener_set_position/direction/velocity` from the primary `AudioListenerComponent` (the first in canonical order when several are primary, `AUDIO_MULTIPLE_PRIMARY_LISTENERS`), falling back to the primary camera (validation `AUDIO_NO_LISTENER` when neither exists and sources are spatial). Non-spatial sources use `MA_SOUND_FLAG_NO_SPATIALIZATION`. `Audio.PlayOneShot(clip, position?, volume?, group?)` is non-spatial when `position` is nil, spatial at `position` otherwise, and uses the `Sfx` group unless one is given; its priority follows its group, as a source's does (M40, ADR 0057 decision 13: music priority in the `Music` group, so a stinger is never stolen by effects). A session's `AudioSystem` admits at most 1,024 one-shot requests per frame (`MaxAudioOneShotsPerFrame`: the requests between two `AudioSystem::Update` calls, so a frame's fixed steps, `OnUpdate` and `OnLateUpdate`; evaluations while no frame runs count toward the next one); a later request in the frame starts nothing and fails with InvalidState, which a script receives as a located error. The system keeps only the handles of live one-shot voices, dropping ended and stolen ones at every request and every update, so it never tracks more than the pool's 64. Play-mode pause pauses all session voices; Stop releases them. Edit mode is silent except asset-browser previews. `Attenuation::None` keeps a sound positioned (panned and Doppler-shifted) without distance falloff (miniaudio's inverse model with a rolloff of 0, since its own "none" turns spatialization off).

**Lifecycle** (ADR 0015 decisions 12, 13 and 28). One `AudioSystem` per Play session (none in Simulate and none without an engine), owned by `PlaySession` (`GetAudioSystem`). `Start` plays the `PlayOnStart` sources in canonical order; a source created later with `PlayOnStart` starts at the first Update after it exists; a source whose entity becomes effectively disabled is released, and a `PlayOnStart` one starts again when re-enabled; removing the component or destroying the entity releases its voice at the destroy flush; a changed `Clip` restarts a playing voice and a null `Clip` plays nothing; values a script writes out of range are clamped. A spatial source and the listener are heard where they are drawn: at their rendered pose (§5.2, `ComputeRenderedWorldMatrix` at the frame's alpha), whose position delta over the frame's delta is their velocity (0 for a zero delta). Physics and `OnFixedUpdate` scripts move entities only inside the fixed steps, of which a frame runs 0 to `MaxStepsPerFrame`, so the world pose of a body at a constant speed stands still on some frames and jumps on others; the rendered pose moves at that speed on every frame, so it has no frame-rate Doppler warble and a follow camera placed from `Transform.RenderPosition` hears its ball without a shift. No velocity is reported on the frame a pose stops interpolating (the entity or an ancestor gains `InterpolationResetTag`: a teleport, a respawn, a creation, an enable, or a first write outside the fixed steps; a pose written outside them on every frame, such as a camera in `OnLateUpdate`, keeps its velocity), nor for a move at or above the speed of sound in one frame (a camera cut) (ADR 0016 decision 8). The listener is the first active primary `AudioListener` in canonical order, else the primary camera, else the origin. Clips load through `GetOrPlaceholder` (a missing clip records its diagnostic once and plays the silent clip). `SetPaused` pauses every voice of the system; M35's `SetWorldPaused` (ADR 0050 decision 3, amended by M40's ADR 0057 decision 14) pauses the world's voices, those of every group but `Music` and `Ui` (today the `Sfx` group's), while the world is paused with the `sounds` choice `Pause` (§5.6), such voices started meanwhile starting held, so a menu's `Ui` sounds, `Music` sources and one-shots and the session's music play on (with `Finish` the world's voices play on to their end); a voice is paused while either pause or its source's own `Pause` holds it; destroying it is Stop. `InitializeMix` records the engine's Music, Sfx and Ui volumes and sets them to 1 before startup callbacks. The mix belongs to the session, not to a scene (M28, ADR 0043 decision 9): at `Scene.Load` and `Scene.Reload` the replaced scene's system hands the volumes it recorded to the new scene's (`TakeMix`, `AdoptMix`) instead of restoring them, so a volume a script set before the replacement holds after it and the recorded volumes come back once, when the session ends. `Start` invokes it idempotently for standalone callers, then starts voices without overwriting script-authored gains. Destroying the system restores the original mix even when no voices started, so a game's mix (`Audio.SetGroupVolume`, §11.5) never leaks into Edit mode, the preview or later sessions; the Master volume stays the host's. Session replacement first performs fallible `PlaySession::Prepare` without callbacks or shared audio ownership, retires the old session only after preparation succeeds, and calls `Activate` once on the installed replacement (ADR 0019 decision 10). Audio is not simulated state and never reaches the state hash.

**The session's music** (M40, ADR 0057 decisions 4 to 6; World Tree's brief 20). A track that outlives a scene is the play session's, not a scene's: `Scene/SessionMusic`, which `PlaySession` makes in `Activate` in every Play session (none in Simulate, which runs no scripts), after the first `AudioSystem`, and keeps to its end (a session without an engine has one too, which records the scripts' requests and starts no voice: the feature host's scratch sessions discover test suites by starting each suite's scene, whose startup callbacks ask for their track there as anywhere), while each `Scene.Load` and `Scene.Reload` replaces the `AudioSystem`. Its clips load and register through its own registrations (`Scene/Private/AudioClipRegistry`, which each `AudioSystem` also holds), so a scene going never drops them. `Audio.PlayMusic(clip, {Volume, FadeSeconds, Loop, Intro})` (§11.5) plays a non-spatial voice in the `Music` group at music priority, its `Volume` 1 and its level on the voice's fade: with no music playing the clip starts (after its `Intro`, played once and followed seamlessly by the clip, a chained voice of §10.1, when one is given and both load; an intro whose sample rate, channel count or sample format differs from the clip's is refused on every call), its level rising from 0 to `Volume` over `FadeSeconds`; with the clip already playing its voice is kept, never restarted, its level fading from where it is to `Volume` (a duck) and `Loop` applied, whatever the scene, so each scene of a chain asks for its track and the track goes on through the doorway; another clip crossfades (the playing voice fades to 0 and is released at the fade's end while the new one fades in), and a voice of the clip still fading out is taken back and fades up again. At most four music voices play (`MaxMusicVoices`: the current one and those fading out; a new one past it releases the oldest fading one at once). `Audio.StopMusic(fadeSeconds)` fades the current voice out and ends the request; `Audio.GetMusic()` reports the request as scripts made it, never the voice's progress, so it reads the same in every run of a replay. The engine's failures (a full pool of higher-priority voices) are logged, never raised. The music's voices are held from `Activate` to the first `AudioUpdate` and while the session is paused and not in lockstep (in the order of §10.1's time ownership), never at a scene transition (whose new `AudioSystem` is held to the next `AudioUpdate`, which in Device time would silence a carried voice) and never by the world pause; destroying the session releases them before the `AudioSystem` restores the mix and before time goes back. Each `AudioUpdate` phase ends with the music's snapshot, which `Test.GetMusic` reads (§5.7 step 3).

### 10.3 Procedural sound effects
`Audio/SoundSynth` turns a `.sfx` description (§6.6) into PCM deterministically: layers of Sine/Square/Triangle/Saw/Noise oscillators, note sequences (`"C5:0.06"`) or frequency sweeps, ADSR envelopes, optional low-pass, per-layer volume and a seeded noise generator. It runs at import (cooked PCM), so runtime cost is zero. Agents create sounds with `asset.create {type: "SoundEffect", values: {...}}`; ten presets ship as `engine://Audio/*`. The exact semantics (note grammar, whole-frame timing, the sweep's release, the first noise draw, the low-pass span, float-rounded range checks) are those of §6.6 and `SoundSynth.h`; synthesis uses Core/DetMath in double precision, so the presets' committed hashes hold in every configuration and on every platform (ADR 0015 decisions 11 and 23).

### 10.4 Tests
On a device-less engine: a playing clip has non-zero RMS; a source panned hard right has right RMS > left; volume 0 is silent; attenuation is monotonic with distance; streamed and decoded playback of the same clip are sample-identical (no-threading resource manager); captured PCM of a fixed scene is bit-identical across runs; a missing clip yields a diagnostic and silence; synthesis is bit-identical across runs. Device handling uses miniaudio's Null backend (`ma_backend_null`) as the real device plus a fake notification source: a `stopped` notification re-creates only the device, and a voice keeps playing with an unchanged cursor; three failures leave the engine device-less with one warning; in lockstep the device callback reads nothing and voices advance by exactly 800 frames per tick. The fake notification source is `AudioEngine::InjectDeviceNotification` (thread-safe; an injected `Stopped` counts as unexpected), with `InjectDeviceCreationFailures` for re-creations and `AudioEngineSpecification::InjectedDeviceCreationFailures` for the startup creation; the re-creation delays run on `Update`'s clock, so tests pass chosen times. Applications never use them (ADR 0015 decision 4).
