| `AutomationPanel` | connected clients, live request log with timings, pause-agent toggle, deny-mutations switch, "Allow AI automation" preference (lets agents attach to this editor, §13.8), external source editor preference (executable plus one argument per line, `{path}` and `{line}` substituted without a shell; written to `user://Editor.json` at the next safe point) |
| `UndoHistoryPanel` | the active scene's history (each open scene has its own, §12.3): command labels, `[agent]` prefix for automation-originated commands |
| `SaveDataPanel` | M28 (ADR 0043 decision 8; closed by default, opened from the Window menu; `EditorPanel::SaveData`, named "SaveData"): editor play's save data, the store a live play session starts with and `SaveData.Commit` writes: lists its values, sets one from a key and JSON text, deletes one and clears them all, as `savedata.get`, `savedata.set` and `savedata.clear` do |
| `NativePanel` | M19 (ADR 0030 decisions 29 to 31; closed by default, opened from the Window menu; `EditorPanel::Native`, named "Native"): the user's "Allow native code" preference (`AllowNativeCode` in `user://Editor.json`, off by default), whose checkbox only queues the change for the next frame boundary, where `NativeModuleHost::Update` writes it keeping every other member of the file; no automation method takes, writes or changes it, and `native.status` only reports it. While it is off nothing native is built or loaded, a game with `Native/` does not export, and turning it off unloads the module at the first frame boundary without a play session. The game's module sources and builds; Build and Load queue `native.build` and `native.load`; the loaded module's types; the selected entity's native components, read-only (`native.getComponents`; agents edit them with `native.setComponents`). **Load and hot reload** (`EditorCore/Native/NativeModuleHost`): each build goes to a new `Library/Native/Builds/<8-digit sequence>/`, since Windows does not let a loaded library be replaced; a load takes the newest successful build of the editor's configuration whose source hash is current, loads its library (`SharedLibrary`, §4.3), registers the module and only then replaces the loaded one, so a load that fails at any step leaves the previous module and the open scenes as they were. Loads happen only at frame boundaries without a play session (Play or Simulate). A reload whose layout hash is unchanged rewrites nothing, so the scenes stay byte-identical; a load whose layout changed (every first load, one after an unload included) migrates the native components of every open scene by field name (§11.11), each checked before any changes so that one scene's error leaves them all as they were (M20's merge with M19, ADR 0031 "Merge with M19"), marks each scene modified whose canonical form changed and clears every open scene's undo history, whose entity snapshots hold the previous layout's values or the values as written, keeping a scene modified when it was. The previous module's types go last, which unloads its library; the host keeps the loaded build and the newest, removing older ones. A project's opening loads the newest current build when the preference is on and builds nothing; a scene that opens with a module loaded gets canonical native components; a `--strict` editor refuses a project whose scenes and prefabs hold a native component the loaded module does not register (every one while none is loaded), rejects or would migrate. Closing the project cancels a running build and unloads the module |
| `AnimationPreviewPanel` | M23 (ADR 0034 decision 32): the "Animation Preview" window, shown while the active edit scene's selection is one entity holding an `Animator` or a preview of the active scene runs, never in play: the entity's path, Preview, Play and Pause, Stop and a time slider over the longest loaded clip, every control one `animation.preview` request. The preview (`EditorCore/Animation/AnimationPreview`, the `EditorContext`'s) poses that Animator in its edit scene at its layers' times plus the preview's time (`PoseAnimator`), writing only the runtime `AnimationPoseComponent`, so the scene's revision, history and file never change while the scene and game views, thumbnails and `viewport.screenshot` show the pose; edit scenes otherwise draw skinned meshes in their bind pose. One preview at a time, belonging to its open scene: previewing another entity or scene, switching the active tab, closing the scene or the entity losing its Animator ends it and removes the pose; the editor's frame (`EditorApp::OnUpdate`) advances a playing preview by the frame's unscaled time (presentation only) |
| `GraphEditorPanel` | M24 (ADR 0035 decision 15): the "Graph Editor" window, a first-party canvas on Dear ImGui that `EditorLayer` draws while a graph is open in it (one at a time; not an `EditorPanel`, so `editor.state` and the saved layout do not change), opened by the content browser, the inspector and the Diagnostics panel. It shows the graph `graph.read` gives (rounded node boxes with their pins coloured by type, Bezier links, a grid, each node's findings as its outline) with the kinds `graph.nodes` lists, and a side panel of the behaviour's name, fields and variables (M39: and its "Runs while the world is paused" checkbox and a Methods section, each method's name, parameters and result, added, renamed and removed through `graph.setMembers`; ADR 0056 decision 13) and of the selected node's input literals, one field per pin type. Every action that changes the graph submits its method through `EditorActions` (`EditorCore/Graph/GraphEditorActions` and `GraphEditorRequests`): the node menu (right-click; searchable, by category) `graph.addNode`, a link dropped on empty canvas then a kind chosen one `edit.batch` of `graph.addNode` and `graph.connect`, a link dragged between pins `graph.connect`, Alt+click on a link or a link dragged off its input onto empty canvas `graph.disconnect`, a link dragged off its input onto another input one `edit.batch` of `graph.disconnect` and `graph.connect` (one undo step, which a refused connect leaves undone), a drag's release `graph.moveNodes`, Delete `graph.removeNodes` (a selection of more nodes than one call takes, 1,024, as one `edit.batch` of such calls, one undo step), Ctrl+D and Ctrl+V one `edit.batch` of `graph.addNode` and `graph.connect` ops, the literal fields `graph.setValues`, the members panel `graph.setMembers`, Undo and Redo `edit.undo` and `edit.redo`. A link or literal on a pin the node's kind no longer has (a binding's parameter renamed or removed) shows as a pin of its own in the error colour, its tooltip saying why, and goes as any other does (`graph.disconnect`; the side panel's Clear literal, `graph.setValues` with null); a field being edited keeps its text or drag across a read that arrives meanwhile (ADR 0035's milestone review). Panning (middle or right button), zooming (wheel), framing (F), hovering, selecting (click, Ctrl/Shift, box) and Ctrl+C are presentation, without a method (decision 16). While a play session that runs behaviours plays (a test run's included), the window polls `graph.liveValues` once a frame, read at the editor's next safe point between frames (`EditorCore/Graph/GraphLiveView`, decision 14), for the play entity selected or else the first holding the graph: under each node its outputs' last values and the retained script errors its code raised (that node outlined as an error), and in the side panel the members' values, none of them when the slot read holds another graph of the same behaviour name, which the toolbar names; reading them changes no state, the state hash included (§11.12). A finding opened in the graph already open selects and frames its node as in a graph opened anew. The canvas's geometry, node menu and target resolution are UI-free (`EditorCore/Graph/GraphCanvas`, `GraphNodeMenu`, `GraphEditorTarget`) |
| `ProjectLauncher` | recent projects (the host's memory snapshot of `user://Editor.json`, read at startup and after each project open or close, never while drawing), New from template (Empty, Basic3D), Open; the location and the project file through the FileDialog API (`Editor/FileDialog.h`): the operating system's dialog in a windowed editor on Windows, the ImGui picker headless and on Linux and macOS; each dialog only fills the path that `project.create` and `project.open` take (presentation, ADR 0029 decisions 19 and 20) |

### 12.3 Commands and undo
```cpp
class Command
{
public:
	virtual ~Command() = default;
	Command(const Command&) = delete;
	[[nodiscard]] virtual Status Execute(EditorContext& context) = 0;   // atomic: fully applies or leaves state unchanged
	[[nodiscard]] virtual Status Undo(EditorContext& context) = 0;      // atomic: restores the exact prior state, or fails (file I/O) still applied
	[[nodiscard]] virtual std::string_view GetLabel() const = 0;
	[[nodiscard]] virtual std::string_view GetMergeKey() const { return {}; }   // equal non-empty keys and origins may merge
	[[nodiscard]] virtual bool MergeWith(const Command& next) { return false; }  // gizmo drags, slider scrubs
	[[nodiscard]] virtual bool ChangesScene() const { return true; }            // false: settings commands, no dirty scene
	[[nodiscard]] virtual size_t GetMemorySize() const = 0;                     // the history's 256 MB bound
	[[nodiscard]] virtual Status ReplayOnSceneCopy(Scene& scene, bool after) const;  // scene.diff against a revision
	CommandOrigin GetOrigin() const; void SetOrigin(CommandOrigin origin);     // User | Agent; set by EditorContext::Execute
private:
	CommandOrigin m_Origin = CommandOrigin::User;
};
```
Almost every operation uses one generic implementation, **`SceneEditCommand`** (snapshot undo): `SceneEdit edit(context, "Reparent")` begins tracking, the operation mutates the scene through the normal `Scene`/`Entity` APIs, and `edit.Commit()` builds the command from the scene's change tracker: for each touched entity, the canonical JSON before and after (absent = created or destroyed) plus parent and sibling index. Undo and redo restore through the heavily tested serializer. Debug builds verify after each commit that the canonical JSON of every untouched entity, the state hash's input, is unchanged (ADR 0008 decision 34). Other command types: `AssetEditCommand` (file bytes before/after, for materials, sound effects, scripts written through automation and import settings), `ProjectSettingsCommand` (settings JSON before/after), `AssetMoveCommand`, `AssetDeleteCommand` (moves file + `.meta` to `Library/Trash/`; never a permanent delete) and `CompositeCommand` (transactions and `edit.batch`; atomic: if a child fails, executed children are undone in reverse).

Continuous edits begin on `IsItemActivated` or gizmo mouse-down and commit on release (one undo step). `CommandHistory` is bounded at 1,000 entries or 256 MB (configurable through `EditorContextSpecification::HistoryLimits`, for the property test), keeps a save point for the dirty flag, and records `EditorContext::GetRevision()`, the editor's never-repeating revision, before and after each command's first execution; undo and redo never change those values, and a merge keeps the first one (ADR 0008 decision 28). There is one history per open scene. An `EditorTransaction` collects the commands executed inside it into one `CompositeCommand`, and a nested transaction joins the outermost one (ADR 0008 decisions 13, 18 and 29). Property tests: for random sequences of 10,000 operations over random scenes, undo-all restores byte-identical JSON and redo-all reproduces the final state; per command type, Execute → Undo equals the original and Execute → Undo → Redo equals Execute.

### 12.4 Play mode, assets, projects
- Toolbar: Play, Simulate, Pause, Step, Stop; lockstep indicator. Behaviour per §5.6. Play is refused only for a scene that references an asset in error (and for type errors when configured). World Tree brief 14 (ADR 0042 decision 2) narrowed the gate from any asset error of the project to the played scene's: `play.start`, `input.record` and `input.replay` (`EditorPlayController::ValidatePlayRequest`) refuse with `InvalidState` naming the first asset in error (an Error-severity diagnostic that describes the asset's state, `AssetManager::GetErrorDiagnostics`) that the scene they play (the open scene with its unsaved edits, or the file) references directly or through other assets: its components' asset references, a Script component's fields typed by the project's script field schemas, and transitively what the dependency graph records for each (§7.5: prefab to meshes and materials, material to textures, script to required scripts; `EditorAssetManager::FindReferencedAssetErrors`). Every other scene plays, and test runs, which never had the gate, run. The graph knows the edges of the imports the editor has run, as the editor knows the errors themselves only from imports that failed. A Scene asset is neither checked nor followed, whether a Script field names it (the next level) or a script passes it to `Scene.Load`, so the answer never depends on which scenes the session has loaded; nor is an asset a script loads at run time (`Assets.Load`): such a load fails in the script as at any time (`Docs/Backlog.md` §6). The narrower gate is kept beside the deferred environment bake (§7.4), which alone would leave every other kind of asset error stopping the whole project: a broken test suite, a work-in-progress texture or one bad import now stops only the scenes that use it.
- Ordinary Play consumes `Application.Quit` at the editor safe point through the normal Stop path. Test, replay, recording and lockstep drivers retain control of their sessions. Script environment queries use the live borrowed window, including its headless state, except the window size, which is the session's view (view coordinates, §4.3: the Game image for ordinary play, the project's window size for test, replay, recording and lockstep sessions); cursor changes use that window and restore the editor baseline on Stop or replacement. Focus loss releases capture. Native input and viewport focus-loss input changes respect exclusive test/replay ownership, while authored test input remains effective (ADR 0019 decision 10).
- Autosave and recovery per §4.13.
- New-project templates write the folder skeleton `Assets/{Scenes,Scripts,Prefabs,Materials,Models,Textures,Audio,Fonts,Tests}`, `.luaurc`, `.gitignore` (`Library/`), an `AGENTS.md` stub and, for Basic3D, a scene with camera, sun, environment, post-process and ground. Script templates: `Behaviour` (the class pattern of §11.2), `Module` (a plain table module), `Test` (a suite, §11.10); each is type-checked by a fixture.
- `SceneChangedOnDisk` (§7.5) shows a banner offering reload; it never reloads silently.

### 12.5 Editor design quality

The editor's functional gates and its product design are separate acceptance obligations (ADR 0020). Editor changes must be reviewed in actual rendered, populated screens and exercised through the corresponding editing workflow. Screenshot comparisons guard a reviewed design against regressions; an unchanged screenshot alone is not a design approval.

- Use the committed Inter font, shared `Editor/Ui` style and a restrained dark palette. Size controls from font/style metrics, keep keyboard focus visible and apply display scaling to both text and spacing without compounding it across monitor changes. Account for framebuffer scaling so Retina displays do not apply the monitor scale twice. Game input ownership suspends UI keyboard navigation until focus returns to the editor.
- Distinguish the menu, primary toolbar, panel tools and status. The project, current scene, unsaved state and play mode must be understandable without opening a diagnostic panel. Friendly panel titles are presentation names; automation names remain stable, and existing saved layouts are migrated when their ImGui IDs change.
- Inspector labels precede their controls in aligned rows. Ordinary transforms expose position, Euler rotation and scale; raw quaternion and derived values remain available under advanced disclosure. Show readable entity and asset names with paths/identifiers on demand. Removal and other occasional actions belong in component menus rather than competing with every editable field.
- Property editing never rounds a stored value to its display format. Drags and typed numbers stay inside the field's range and step over its excluded magnitudes, and a multi-edit changes only the vector components the user touched. Every rotation edits as Euler degrees, with the raw quaternion components renormalized after an edit. Runtime (Play) content carries the play accent. Which panels are open persists with the saved workspace layout, and the undo, redo and save shortcuts work from any panel.
- Browsing scenes, importing assets and opening projects must have discoverable selection flows. Import and project-opening pickers also accept typed paths. Empty, busy, failed, read-only and agent-controlled states explain what happened and what the user can do next.
- Review populated and empty screens at 1280×720 and 1600×900, and at a larger display scale. Required controls must remain reachable at narrow widths through wrapping or scrolling. Review selection, property editing and undo, asset browsing, scene opening and Play/Stop with the production command paths.

---

## 13. AI automation

### 13.1 Topology
```
Claude Code ──MCP (stdio)──▶ Tools/MCP bridge (Python, official mcp SDK) ──JSON-RPC 2.0 / TCP 127.0.0.1──▶ Editor AutomationServer
                              launch / attach / supervise / relaunch            I/O thread: framing, auth
                              catalog from the method registry                  main thread: Pump() → MethodRegistry
                              crash reports, output capping, transcript         → Commands / PlaySession / Renderer
```
The engine owns a stable, semver'd JSON-RPC protocol; MCP lives only in the thin Python bridge, so MCP revisions are absorbed by the pinned official SDK, the bridge survives editor crashes, and the same protocol serves Python tests, batch files and the Runtime.

### 13.2 Protocol, transport, security
- **Framing:** LSP-style `Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n<UTF-8 JSON>`; frames over 64 MB, invalid UTF-8 or nesting depth over 128 close the connection. A first line that is not a `Content-Length` header (e.g. `GET / HTTP/1.1`) closes the socket immediately, which defeats browser-based localhost attacks and DNS rebinding.
- **Transport:** TCP bound to `127.0.0.1` only, port 0 (OS-assigned) or `--automation=<port>`. The editor writes `<UserData>/<Product>/Automation/Sessions/<pid>.json` `{pid, port, token, protocolVersion: "1.0", engineVersion, build, projectPath, headless, startedAt}` (`build` is the editor's build id, `<version>+<12-hex commit>[.dirty]`, which `session.hello` and `session.info` report too beside `engineVersion`; ADR 0030 decision 13) with user-only permissions (0600 on POSIX; per-user `%LOCALAPPDATA%` ACL on Windows); deleted on clean exit; stale files (dead pid) are ignored. Clients read the file at any moment, also while the server's rename publishes or replaces it: the server renames with `PublishedFile::Replace` (on Windows a POSIX-semantics rename, which replaces a file that readers hold open sharing deletion) and every client reads with full sharing (`SessionFile::Read`, `PublishedFile::Read`; the Python client's `read_shared_bytes`), so a read never fails while the rename's handle is still open on the file and a rewrite never fails while a client reads it (ADR 0040). A client that starts an editor (`engine_client.launch_editor`, which the MCP bridge, the Python tests and the scripts use) waits up to 300 s for its session file, a hang bound (ADR 0040 decision 5).
- **Handshake:** the first request must be `session.hello {token, protocolVersion, client: {name, version}}`. The 256-bit token (OS CSPRNG) is compared in constant time; 3 failures close the connection; a major-version mismatch is rejected listing both versions.
- **Availability:** the server runs only with `--automation`, `--headless` or the editor preference "Allow AI automation". It does not exist in Dist builds.
- **Threading:** the I/O thread decodes frames into a queue; `AutomationServer::Pump` executes requests on the main thread between input and update, so handlers see a consistent frame and need no locks. Up to 4 clients; requests from one client run in order; mutations from all clients serialize through the single `CommandHistory`.
- **Disconnect.** When a client's connection closes, cleanly or not, the server cancels that client's pending operations (each resolves internally as `Cancelled`). If the client owned lockstep, it releases lockstep and pauses play, so the session never stays locked in "Agent controls time". It stops any recording that client started, marking the file invalid and not writing it, and logs one `AutomationClientDisconnected` event. Python tests cover a kill during `play.step`, during `input.replay` and while recording.
- **Pending operations:** handlers return `MethodResult = std::variant<nlohmann::json, Error, Scope<PendingOperation>>`; `PendingOperation::Poll(MethodContext&) -> std::optional<Result<nlohmann::json>>` runs once per frame until it resolves (`play.step`, `play.waitFor`, `asset.import`, `asset.reimport`, `project.export`, `test.run`, `input.record`, `input.replay`, `editor.screenshot`), with optional `$/progress` notifications.
- **Progress** (Skerries' brief S20). A pending operation that reports its work (`PendingOperation::GetProgress`: `test.run`, `input.record`'s Stop and `input.replay`) sends its client `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "$/progress", "params": {id, method, work, stage, subject, tick, finalTick, step, steps, runs, message}}`: `id` and `method` are the request's; `work` grows whenever the operation advances (a test run counts its runner units, a replay its ticks) and never otherwise; `stage` is `suite`, `replay`, or a recording's runs, `record` (run 1, the recorded suite), `verify` (run 2, replayed strictly with its input) and `inputCheck` (run 3, replayed without it), which only a recording with input events has, so `runs`, the recording's runs once known, is 3, or 2 for one without input events, whose verification ends the call (0 while `test.run`'s recorded run has not ended, and for any other stage); `subject` names the suite (`<suite>/<case>` while a case runs) or the replay's path; `tick` is the stage's session tick, `finalTick` a replay's or recording's final tick (0 when unknown), `step` of `steps` the suite's or replay's place among those selected; `message` says it in one line (`recording Record.Hops, run 2 of 3 (replayed strictly with its input): tick 120 of 480`). The Dispatcher sends the first as the handler returns the operation, then one after each Poll whose stage or step changed and otherwise at most one a second (`DispatcherSpecification::ProgressInterval`), and each new stage begins in a frame of its own, so every client hears each of a recording's runs. TCP clients get them, the Runtime's too; in-process clients only when they ask (`DispatcherClientOptions::Progress`). A client bounds such a call by whether its work advances (`engine_client.ProgressDeadline`): the wait ends `timeoutSeconds` after the request or after the last notification whose `work` grew, so a run of any length ends with its answer while it advances, and one that stops advancing is cut off after the same `timeoutSeconds` that bounded the whole call before (any single unit of its work, a suite's collection or one tick of the largest scene, is far shorter; the clients and the MCP bridge, §13.8).
- **Watchdog:** if the main thread has not pumped for 5 s, the I/O thread itself answers new requests with `Busy` (−32007) including the main thread's current phase from an atomic phase marker (`"Script:Board.OnFixedUpdate"`, `"AssetImport:Track.glb"`) and the request that holds it (`data.request`, the method whose handler, Poll or Cancel runs, `Watchdog::GetRequest`): the message then names that request and says to retry once its current step ends (`a test.run request is running a long step on it ... retry once that step ends`): the main thread answers again when that step (a suite's collection, a scene load) ends, while the request itself may run on, and a refused `session.hello` is sent again on the same connection before its handshake deadline or on a new one (Skerries' brief S20); with no request it says to retry later. An agent never hangs on a frozen editor. Play sessions report every protected gameplay script entry to their host, which sets the script phase `Script:<script file stem>.<callback>` (`Task` for a resumed task, `Test.Case` for a case body) over whatever request or pending operation is current, wherever the session is advanced from; one-shot evaluations keep the request's phase.
- **Paths:** every path argument resolves through `VfsPath` inside `project://`. Runtime recording is a narrow exception because its project mount is a read-only pak: relative `input.record` output paths are confined below `user://Replays/`, and Runtime `input.replay` also accepts the returned canonical path there. Absolute paths, traversal and other schemes remain rejected (ADR 0019 decision 7). Two methods may read an absolute source path, read-only: `asset.import`, and from M26 `terrain.importHeightmap` (ADR 0037 decisions 20 and 31), which converts that one file into a `.heightfield` below `Assets/` and copies nothing; each records what it writes in provenance under its request, whose transcript line carries the source. `asset.import` copies the importable file and, for a `.gltf`, its **dependency closure**: every buffer and image URI, which must be relative and inside the source's directory tree (no `..`, no absolute paths, no schemes other than `data:`). Relative paths are preserved under `destDir`, and each copied dependency gets a dependency meta (§6.4). Nothing else is copied. `project.export` writes only under `<Project>/Build/` or `--export-root` given on the command line. No method runs a process, a shell command or code that a request names: the only processes a method starts are `project.export`'s runs of the exported game, its smoke test (`smokeTest`) and its feature test (`featureTest`, a testing export's suites and replays), and, on macOS, `codesign` in its Sign phase (§14.2), each by a fixed path with fixed arguments. The one exception is a game's native module (Windows only): while the user's "Allow native code" preference is on, the open project's `Native/` sources, which `native.write` may author, are built by the fixed-path `Scripts/BuildNative.py`, run by the interpreter the workspace was generated with (`native.build`, and `project.export`'s NativeBuild step), and the build is loaded into the editor's process (`native.load` and the project's opening) and linked into the games the editor exports. That preference therefore grants every connected automation client code execution in the editor and in its exports: it is the user's alone, set in the editor's Native panel, and no method can change it (ADR 0030 decisions 29 to 33). `script.eval` runs in the Luau sandbox.

### 13.3 Error codes
JSON-RPC standard codes plus: −32000 `Internal`, −32001 `NotFound`, −32002 `InvalidState`, −32003 `ValidationFailed`, −32004 `Conflict`, −32005 `Timeout`, −32006 `ScriptError`, −32007 `Busy`, −32008 `Unauthorized`, −32009 `Unsupported`, −32010 `Cancelled`. `error.data` carries `errorCode` (the engine `ErrorCode` name) and `issues[]`, each `{pointer, message, hint?, suggestions?}`. `Internal` also answers the environment's failures, `errorCode` naming which: `Io`, `Gpu`, and from M18 `OutOfMemory`, a request that ran out of GPU memory again after its trim and retry and failed alone (`Docs/Decisions/0029-m18-contract.md` decision 45; no code is added, so the protocol version is unchanged):
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":8,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Invalid params","data":{"errorCode":"Validation",
 "issues":[{"pointer":"/components/RigidBody/Mas","message":"unknown field 'Mas' on 'RigidBody'","hint":"did you mean 'Mass'?"},
           {"pointer":"/components/RigidBody/Friction","message":"must be >= 0 (got -0.2)"}]}}}
```

### 13.4 Conventions every method follows
- Names `domain.verb`; params and results are JSON objects with **camelCase** keys; embedded component/asset data keeps registry PascalCase. Enum values are parsed case-insensitively and echoed in canonical PascalCase (§6). Each method's params and result are **reflected C++ structs**, so parsing, defaults, validation and the JSON Schemas (2020-12, with `$defs` per component) are generic; there is no hand-written JSON plumbing. Every method has a description, `exposeAsTool`, `mutates`, `supportsDryRun`, `availableInRuntime`, `availableInLauncher` and `timeoutSeconds` metadata.
- **`EntityRef`** params (a method param that names an entity, such as `entity.update`'s `entity` or `entity.create`'s `parent`) accept a 16-hex UUID, a unique UUID prefix (≥ 6 hex digits) or a path (`/Game/Board`, `/Track/Piece[3]`); ambiguous paths fail and list candidates. Inside a batch a path also names an entity an earlier op created (`"parent": "/Game"`), and unlike a `$ref` index it does not shift when an op is inserted. An `EntityRef` **inside component data** (a component field, a script's `Field.Entity()` value reached through a script slot's `Fields`, an element of an array or map of them) takes the same forms (M19, ADR 0030 decision 7): `MethodRegistry::Invoke` rewrites a prefix or a path to the entity's id through the host's `IEntityReferenceResolver` before the data is validated, so the stored value keeps the handle pattern (ADR 0010 decision 32). The schemas that describe component data in params (`rpc.discover`'s and `Methods.json`'s params, `component.schema`, `script.fields`) give such a value the pattern `^([0-9a-fA-F]{6,16}|/.+)$` (`JsonSchema`'s `EntityReferenceSchema::IdOrPath`), while file and result schemas keep the 16-hex one. The editor resolves it in the scene the request addresses (the edit scene of its `scene` target or of the active scene, or the play scene with `target: "Play"`; "Scene target" below), looked up at each reference, so a batch op's component data names an entity an earlier op created by its path; an entity path is the `/`-separated names from a scene root and continues through prefab instances' members, nested ones included. A reference that names no entity counts with the unresolved asset references (`NotFound`), an ambiguous one is an `InvalidArgument` issue at its pointer with the candidates as suggestions. A host without a resolver (the Runtime, which writes no components) refuses anything but the 16-hex id, `InvalidArgument` at its pointer (`expected a 16-digit hex UUID string`) with the hint `an Entity value in component data takes the entity's 16-hex id; use {"$ref": "<op>.entity.id"} in a batch or the id entity.get returns` (ADR 0027 decision 3, A4). **`AssetRef`** per §7.1, a path resolving inside component data too. Responses always include canonical ids plus readable names/paths.
- **Seed.** A play session started without `seed` (`play.start`, `input.record {action: "Start"}`), every test suite and every recording uses the **session seed**: the project's `Simulation.Seed` XOR the scene's `Seed` (an empty scene's is 0; §4.12); a replay restarts with its header's seed. So `play.start {lockstep: true}` without a seed shows the piece order and spawns that suites and recordings of the same saved scene see.
- **Target.** `target: "Edit" | "Play"`. Reads default to the play scene while playing. Mutations of the play scene must say `target: "Play"`; they are transient (no undo) and the response says so.
- **Scene target** (M20, ADR 0031 decisions 14 and 16). The editor keeps several scenes open, one of them active (§12.1). Every method that addresses one open scene (`entity.*`, `prefab.*`, `edit.*`, `scene.tree`, `scene.query`, `scene.get`, `scene.raycast`, `scene.save`, `scene.diff`, `scene.activate`, `scene.close`, `project.validate`, `script.eval`, `script.errors`, `viewport.screenshot`, and M19's `native.getComponents` and `native.setComponents`) takes the reserved member `scene`, as it takes `dryRun`: an open scene's project path or its id from `scene.list` (an integer from 1 to 2^32 − 1, the only way to name a scene never saved), listed in the method's schemas. Absent, the request addresses the active scene, so a transcript without targets behaves exactly as with one open scene. With one, the request's whole stretch addresses the named scene while the active scene stays: its permission checks, `ifRevision` (each open scene has its own revisions, which never repeat across scenes), the dry run's copy, the handler with its entity paths, batch `$ref` (positional or named) and the entity references in its component data (M19's resolver), its undo history and `_meta`. `scene.activate` requires the target (`RequiresSceneTarget`, the one method that does: absent, `InvalidParams` names `scene`), and `scene.activate` and `scene.close`, whose subject the target is, change which scene is active. A path or id that names no open scene is `NotFound` at `/scene`; any other method refuses the member as unknown (`play.start` and `input.record` keep their own `scene`, a scene file); an op of `edit.batch` runs in the batch's scene and cannot carry its own. The play scene belongs to the open scene the session started from: without a scene target `target`'s rules reach the session from any tab, while a target naming another open scene addresses that scene's edit scene and refuses `target: "Play"` with `InvalidArgument` at `/scene`. The Runtime, which has no open scenes, refuses `scene` with `InvalidState`.
- **Undo.** An edit-scene mutation is exactly one `Command` per call (one `CompositeCommand` per `edit.batch`), labelled `[agent] …`; the result includes `undoIndex`.
- **`dryRun: true`** validates and returns the would-be result without applying it, and is accepted only by methods with `supportsDryRun`. Others return `Unsupported`; this includes `project.export`, `play.*`, `input.*` and `test.run`, and `asset.import` without `replace` (a first import). A pending method that supports it (`asset.import {replace: true}`, World Tree brief 08) answers a dry run at once: `MethodRegistry::AddPending` polls its operation once inside the invocation, so the sandbox never outlasts the request, and an operation that would need another poll is cancelled and the request fails with `Cancelled`. Scene mutations execute then undo inside a sandboxed history. **File-writing methods** (`asset.create`, `asset.setProperties`, `script.write`, `script.create`, `prefab.create`, `project.setSettings`) write into an `OverlayMount` (§4.10) layered over `project://` for the duration of the call: parsing, compiling, type-checking, registry updates and `$ref` results all happen in memory, and nothing touches the disk, the file watcher, the trash or provenance. `edit.batch {dryRun: true}` rejects a batch containing an op without `supportsDryRun` before running anything, reporting `failedOp: k` and `Unsupported`.
- **`ifRevision: N`**: optimistic concurrency; if the addressed open scene's revision (`_meta.revision`; the active scene's without a scene target) moved since, the call fails with `Conflict` and the current revision. The revision counts changes to that scene and the project settings only: creating or writing asset and script files leaves it unchanged, so `ifRevision` guards the scene and the settings, not asset files (ADR 0026, friction S1-14).
- **Atomic batch.** `edit.batch {label, ops: [{method, params}], dryRun?}` runs inside one `CompositeCommand`; if op *k* fails, ops 0..k−1 are undone and the error reports `failedOp: k`. `{"$ref": "<opIndex>.<jsonPath>"}` substitutes earlier results (e.g. `"3.entity.id"`). An op may carry a `name` (an identifier `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` of at most 64 characters, unique within the batch, checked with the other op checks before any op runs: `InvalidArgument` at `/ops/<k>/name`, `failedOp` k), and `{"$ref": "<name>.<jsonPath>"}` then names that op's result, which does not shift when an op is inserted; a name no earlier op bears is `InvalidArgument` (`no op named '<name>' before this one`, its hint listing the earlier names after "did you mean"), a later op's name a forward reference (M19, ADR 0030 decision 8). A path that names no member is `InvalidArgument` naming the object inspected (`no member 'ids' in '3.prefab' (in the result of op 3)`, or `in the result of op 3` for the result itself), with a hint that lists at most 32 of its members and how many more, after "did you mean" for close ones (ADR 0026, milestone review R27).
- **Diagnostics delta.** Every response carries `_meta: {revision, dirty, undoLabel?, tick?, playState, diagnostics: {newErrors, newWarnings, newScriptErrors, logCursor, firstNew: [≤ 3 entries]}}`, so an agent learns about problems without polling. A failed `script.eval`'s own log entry is neither counted nor quoted: it is the caller's error, which the response already answers (ADR 0038, friction F13).
- **Bounded output.** Lists take `limit` (default 100, max 1,000) and `cursor`; any result over 48 KB (minified, `_meta` excluded) is written to `Library/Automation/Out/<pid>-<startSeconds>-<seq>.json` (`user://Automation/Out/` in the launcher state and for read-only editors) and returned as `{path, truncated: true, summary}`. The summary lists the result's members in order, each verbatim when its minified JSON is at most 512 bytes (numbers, booleans, paths, codes, counts and short name lists such as `test.run`'s `counts`, `failedCases` and `jsonPath`) and otherwise as its type with its length or count, a longer array whose elements are all strings adding `first`, its leading strings within 1,536 bytes (`MaxOffloadSummaryListBytes`), so an offloaded `test.run` still names its first failing cases (ADR 0026, milestone review R26); it stays below 4 KB (a `first` that would not fit is left out). Every file a server writes to that directory, offloaded results and output files (screenshots, test reports) alike, takes its name from one per-server sequence (`<seq>`, at least 8 digits, from 1), so no two share a name; a file is created exclusively, never replaced (`VirtualFileSystem::WriteNewFile`, §4.10: a taken name is `AlreadyExists`, also one another process took a moment before), so nothing there is overwritten and no `.bak` is made. A server's first write to the directory removes every file a server whose process no longer runs left there, whatever its extension, with the `.bak` and `.tmp-*` leftovers of older or interrupted writes; a server that shuts down removes exactly the offloaded results it wrote and keeps its output files, so a test run's reports and a `--batch` run's screenshots outlive it (ADR 0026, friction S1-02 and S1-03). A screenshot taken with `keep: true` (`viewport.screenshot`, `editor.screenshot`) goes instead to `Library/Automation/Kept/` (`user://Automation/Kept/` without a writable project and in the Runtime), with the same per-server naming and sequence, created exclusively, and no server ever prunes it: `Kept/` is the one automation output this rule does not bound, growing with every kept file until the user removes files (an accepted limit, M19, ADR 0030 decision 9). Screenshots are downscaled to `maxDimension` (default 1024).
- **Provenance.** The editor records every file it writes under `Assets/`, under `Native/` (the game's native module, whose sources `native.write` writes; ADR 0030 decision 35), the root `.eproj` and the root `.luaurc` in the project's **committed** `<Game>/Automation/Provenance.json` (`<Game>/` is the project directory: `Projects/<Game>/`, or `Tests/Projects/Breakout/` for the M16 dry run): `{"Format": "Provenance", "Version": 1, "Entries": [...]}`, one entry per path, `{Path, XXH64, Method, RequestId, Client, TranscriptLine}` with PascalCase keys like every canonical file (§6; ADR 0008 decision 10). `XXH64` is the seed-0 hash of the bytes written (16 hex digits), `RequestId` the JSON-RPC id as sent, `Client` the `session.hello` client name (or `batch`, `cli`, `test`, `ui`), and `TranscriptLine` the request's 1-based line in `BuildLog.jsonl` (§13.8), null for a request that carried none (a `--batch` run writes no transcript). Entries are kept sorted by path and written canonically. Writes by the windowed UI are recorded with `Method` and `Client` `"ui"`, and only they have a null `RequestId`; the audit rejects them for demo projects. A `cli` entry (`Editor --upgrade`, §12.1) carries its own request's id and transcript line. The `.meta` writes an import publishes after its request returned keep the attribution of the request that started the import (ADR 0026 decision 10). A move (`asset.move`) carries a file's entry to its new path, with the move's attribution, only when the old path had an entry whose `XXH64` equals the moved bytes; otherwise the destination gets no entry, so a file the editor did not write (no entry, or bytes changed since its entry) stays an audit finding after a move (ADR 0026, milestone review R02). Dry runs never record. `project.upgrade` records its rewrites with `Method` `"project.upgrade"` (§13.12).

Both screenshot methods return `{path, mimeType, width, height}`; `viewport.screenshot` adds `view` and, with `inline`, PNG base64 `data` when the PNG is at most 30 KB. Larger images report `inlineOmitted: true` so the result stays below the offload threshold. Output PNGs outlive the server, including a `--batch` run. Viewport captures use the requested camera, target scene, project rendering quality, debug view and strictly validated annotations. All M9 data views are supported. `editor.screenshot` is a pending operation: it requests and waits for a UI frame completed after admission, then reads back the whole UI with its embedded viewport textures. This includes earlier changes in the same automation pump. A minimized editor renders that fresh frame offscreen at the last usable extent, without acquiring a swapchain image, and without publishing the views' extents (they stay unavailable to `viewport.pick` until the window is restored). A frame whose viewport textures were withdrawn after it was built (the window was minimized in between) is never captured: the request asks for another frame. A frame request the host cannot schedule fails the request at once. Cancellation releases the request; failure to publish a fresh frame within the method's 60-second deadline returns Timeout. Both methods return Unsupported with `--renderer none` (ADR 0017 and ADR 0018). A capture that runs out of GPU memory again after its trim and retry fails alone, never returning an image of another size or debug view: both methods answer Internal with `error.data.errorCode` "OutOfMemory" (§13.3), the editor goes on, and the next capture tries again (M18; §8.14 item 7, `Docs/Decisions/0029-m18-contract.md` decisions 44 and 45). A capture that a device loss or a reset hang ends answers `Gpu`; a client retries it after the `GpuDeviceLost` event.

**Runtime subset** (Runtime Debug/Release with `--automation`; handlers shared from `Engine/Automation/Methods`): `session.*`, `rpc.discover`, `scene.tree`, `scene.query`, `scene.get`, `scene.raycast`, `entity.get`, `entity.bounds`, `play.pause`, `play.resume`, `play.step`, `play.state`, `play.waitFor`, `play.setTimeScale`, `input.*`, `viewport.screenshot` (game view), `log.read`, `events.read`, `stats.get`, `physics.bodyInfo`, `physics.jointInfo` (M37), `physics.vehicleInfo` (M44), `physics2d.raycast`, `physics2d.overlap`, `physics2d.bodyInfo`, `audio.stats`, `script.errors`, `script.eval` (play context), `ui.tree` (M22). Handlers reach the host's audio engine through `AutomationMethodContext::GetAudioEngine()` (the Runtime's comes from `RuntimeAutomationServerSpecification::Audio`; ADR 0015 decision 15).

### 13.6 Lockstep, input injection, replays, batches
- `play.start {lockstep: true, seed: 42}` decouples simulation from the wall clock (without `seed` the session runs with the session seed, as suites and recordings do, §13.4); ticks advance only through `play.step` (one tick = fixed step + frame phase). `play.step {ticks: 600, render: "Last"}` fast-forwards 10 s of game time and renders one frame. A `play.step` is a pending operation that runs as many ticks per editor frame as fit a **50 ms budget** (at least one), so the UI, the watchdog and other clients stay responsive during long fast-forwards. Its result carries the final `tick` and `stateHash`. The UI keeps drawing and shows "Agent controls time". Lockstep is owned by one client; others get `InvalidState`. A disconnect releases it (§13.2). Audio advances by simulation time while lockstep owns time (§10.1).
- Input events are stamped with a tick offset relative to the step start: `{"tick": 0, "type": "Action", "name": "MoveLeft", "state": "Tap"}` (`Tap` = down on that tick, up on the next, so both edges are observed). Types: `action {state | value}`, `key`, `mouseButton {position?}`, `mouseMove`, `mouseDelta`, `scroll`, `gamepadButton`, `gamepadAxis {value}`, `text`. Type and state names are case-insensitive; files use PascalCase (§6.7).
- `play.waitFor {until: "return Scene.FindByName('GameOver'):IsActive()", timeoutTicks: 3600}` evaluates the predicate in the play VM after every tick and returns `{satisfied, tick, value}`. Its value, like a replay expectation's (§6.7), must be JSON: a vector, `Color` or `Quat`, which `script.eval` returns as the array of its components (ADR 0038 friction F01), ends the wait with its Script error instead of holding at once (ADR 0038's milestone review).
- **Recording** always starts at tick 0, so a replay can reproduce it. `input.record {action: "Start", scene?, parameters?, seed?}` is accepted in Edit mode: it starts a lockstep play session of the scene (default: the open scene) with the given load parameters and seed (default: the session seed, the project's `Simulation.Seed` XOR the scene's `Seed`, §13.4), and records from tick 0. The session plays the saved scene asset the replay header names, so the open scene must be saved: with unsaved changes `start` fails with `InvalidState` (save first). `start` takes the recording's start fingerprint (§6.7), so a scene that references an asset whose cooked hash cannot be taken (an import that fails when the fingerprint cooks it) is refused with that asset's error, naming it, and no recording starts (`test.run {record}` invalidates its recording the same way); an asset in error that the editor already knows and the scene references refuses play itself first (`InvalidState` naming it, §12.4). The parameters start the session in the header's stored form (§6.7). While playing, `start` requires `restart: true`, which restarts the session at tick 0 with the recorded seed; otherwise it fails with `InvalidState` ("recording must start at tick 0"). The recording's own owner may restart an active recording this way. The recorder captures **every event applied at step 1** of each tick (§5.7), whatever its source: `play.step` input, `input.inject`, `Test.Inject*` from test threads, and real devices in the game viewport. `input.record {action: "Stop", path, expect?}` writes the replay with its full header (§6.7), its checkpoints and `FinalStateHash`. Every recording is first **verified with its input** (ADR 0027 decision 3, A1; one without input events too since M19, ADR 0030 decision 4): the play session restarts from the candidate's header, as for the input check, and plays it with its events (`verify` and `strictHash`, evaluating `stop`'s `expect`). Unless that playback reproduces every checkpoint and the final hash, satisfies every expectation, stops nowhere early (a quit or a fatal error) and raises no script error (as `test.run {record}`'s ordinary-play verification requires; once the playback has reached its final tick with nothing else failed, its scripts are stopped and an error their `OnDestroy` raises counts too, named `(at teardown)`, M19, ADR 0030 decision 5), `stop` refuses with `Validation` at `/path`: `refusing to write '<path>': replayed with its input, the recording does not reproduce itself: <reason>; nothing was written`, `<reason>` naming the first failure in tick order (a checkpoint's observed and recorded hashes, an expectation that is false or raised, the final hash, where playback stopped, or, only when the playback otherwise passed, the first of its script errors), with a hint naming the usual causes and the playback's outcome as error data `verification`; the recording is ended, and the session is the verification's, paused where it stopped (after a teardown error with its scripts stopped: `script.eval` in the play context is refused, `scene.query` and `entity.get` read its final state, and `play.stop` ends it). This catches what nothing detects when it happens: a `script.eval` or `play.waitFor` that writes script state (a `self` field, a module table) during the recording, an expectation that is false or raises, a script that reads the host, and any other nondeterminism. A failure to start or run the verification keeps its error's code, writes nothing and ends the recording. A candidate with input events then gets the **input check** (the recording guard, M16 friction S2-01): the play session restarts for the candidate as for `input.replay` and plays it with none of its events (`ReplayPlaybackOptions::WithoutInput`, expectations compiled from their source), on past any checkpoint that differs to `FinalTick` (`ContinuePastCheckpoint`, M19, ADR 0030 decision 3); when that run passes the candidate's verification (every checkpoint, the final hash and every expectation), the recording's outcome does not depend on its input and `stop` refuses it with `Validation` naming the replay, a hint (end the recording while the played state is still in the scene) and the check's outcome as error data `inputCheck`, writing nothing. Since a checkpoint that differs fails that verification, the check refuses only a recording whose input never shows in the world at a checkpoint, at `FinalTick` or in an expectation: one shorter than one checkpoint interval that ends idle, input that changes only script state, or input that acts only after the last checkpoint and is undone by the end. A longer recording that ends with a restart is accepted, its checkpoints having seen the play, but its `FinalStateHash` then proves only the restored state and the play after its last checkpoint is unchecked (M16 friction S3-01), so recordings end while the played state is in the scene; when the check's run differed at a checkpoint yet satisfied every expectation and reached the recorded final hash, the recording is written with one warning in `warnings` (`MakeFinalHashIndependentWarning`: its final state hash does not depend on its input, so only its checkpoints prove the play; ADR 0030 decision 3). Either way the session is then the check's, paused where it ended, and `inputCheckTick` is the first checkpoint tick that differed, else where it ended. A recording without input events is a pure determinism replay: `stop` writes it once its verification passed, with `inputCheckTick` 0, and the play session is the verification's. **One rule decides input independence everywhere** (the recording guards of `input.record` and `test.run {record}`, and the input check of the games and determinism suites): a replay is input-independent when its input-free run passes verification (every checkpoint, the final hash, every expectation), whatever script errors that run raised; a script error that only the input-free run raises does not let the recording through. A hot reload or a play-scene mutation during recording (an edit with target `Play` from automation, the inspector or a gizmo; a dry run excepted; a `script.eval`, `play.waitFor` or test case that calls a mutating engine API, such as a component write, `SetActive`, a session `Random` draw or `Scene.CreateEntity`, `Scene.Instantiate`, `Scene.Destroy` or `Scene.Load`, while `Scene.FindByName` and the other `Scene` queries only read) invalidates it: `stop` then fails with the reason, writes nothing and ends the recording, so `start` (with `restart: true`), `test.run` and `input.replay` are accepted again.
- **Replays** are checked with `input.replay {verify: true}`: a fresh session of the header's scene starts with its parameters and seed, events are applied by tick, every `Expect` must hold, and `strictHash: true` also compares every checkpoint as playback reaches it (the first that differs stops the replay there with `checkpointFailed`, the tick and both hashes, and counts in `checkpointsFailed` and `firstFailedCheckpointTick`, as below; M25's friction F12, ADR 0036) and `FinalStateHash`; with `continuePastCheckpoint: true` (which requires `strictHash`) it plays on to `FinalTick`, compares the final hash too and reports `checkpointsFailed` and `firstFailedCheckpointTick`, the replay still failing (M19, ADR 0030 decision 3). `withoutInput: true` applies none of the events: the check that a replay depends on its input, which must fail for a replay with events (the games and determinism suites run it for every committed replay with events). Like `strictHash` it requires `verify` (`InvalidArgument` at `/withoutInput` otherwise, since an unverified run checks nothing and would always pass), so the input check is `input.replay {verify: true, strictHash: true, withoutInput: true}` (ADR 0026, milestone review R19). A checkpoint or final-hash failure of a playback with the recording's input carries the divergence hint (the world differs from the recording: a serialized component of the scene, the look's included, a script, the game's native module, an asset or the engine changed since it was recorded, or the play is not deterministic; re-record it with `test.run {record}`), and for a replay recorded with a start fingerprint (format 3, §6.7) its `changes` name each entity, component and directly referenced asset that changed since the recording, the first ending the error's message, but never the native module's code or its resources' starting values, which the fingerprint does not record (ADR 0030 decision 2); a `withoutInput` playback carries neither, since failing is its expected outcome. The games and determinism suites' input checks pass `continuePastCheckpoint` and print the final-hash warning above for a replay whose run without input reached its final hash anyway, a warning that never fails a step. `input.readReplay` reads a replay's header, its events in `play.step`'s input form with absolute ticks (a page at a time), its expectations and checkpoints (M19, ADR 0030 decision 14). Gameplay that quits or stops fatally before `FinalTick` fails the replay with `stopReason`, the tick it reached and its later expectations unevaluated (`Validation` with the outcome in error data), never `Cancelled`. They double as regression tests (§15.7) and run in exported builds through the cooked replay player (§14.4).
- **Autopilot workflow** (documented in the `game-building` skill). Steering a physics ball blind with tick-stamped injections is impractical, so the agent writes a test-only **autopilot suite**, `Assets/Tests/Autopilot/Level1.test.luau`, bound to the level scene with `Modes: ["Editor"]`. Its single case reads the ball's state, follows an authored list of waypoint entities with a PD controller, and injects analog `MoveX`/`MoveZ` actions with `Test.InjectAction` every tick until the goal is reached. The case only reads the scene and injects input. It never mutates entities and never uses the session's `Random` stream, so the run is identical to a player pressing the same inputs. `test.run {filter: "Autopilot.Level1", record: "Assets/Tests/Replays/Level1.replay"}` records the run. The replay is then verified **without** the autopilot (`input.replay {verify: true}` and `Testing.Replays`), which proves that plain input reaches the goal. `Level2` and `Level3` suites set `Parameters` (e.g. the carried timer), which the replay header stores.
- **Recording publication** (ADR 0019 decision 6). `test.run {record}` verifies the candidate in fresh ordinary gameplay without the test driver, including every checkpoint and the original final hash, before writing; a candidate with input events then gets the input check in another fresh session (the rule above), and one whose outcome does not depend on its input fails the run with `Validation` (its context names the replay; the case rows and reports are kept). It preserves all input from case-isolated segments with cumulative tick offsets, without encoding resets. `test.run {record, expect}` (M19, ADR 0030 decision 6) compiles each expectation in the editor (chunk `=test.run`, located at `/expect/<i>/luau`), writes them into the recording and evaluates them in the verification, where each must hold, and in the input check; one after the recording's final tick is `Validation` at `/expect/<i>/tick`. The recording block reports `expectations` and the input check's `warnings`. A non-reproducible start, clock grouping or reset returns located Validation with no recording file; ordinary test runs remain supported. Verification is cancellable and counts toward the explicit run-wide tick limit, not case ticks or coverage.
- **Recording suites.** Every replay of a demo is recorded by a **recording suite**: a `Modes: ["Editor"]` suite with a single case, either an autopilot as above or a case that injects a planned input list at fixed ticks with `Test.InjectAction` (a Tetris opening), with `Test.Expect` on what only the input causes; its name occurs in no replay path (`Record.Opening`, not `Opening`), so `test.run {filter: "<its exact name>", record}` selects it and no committed replay (a selected replay row that fails refuses the recording and is named, §13.5). Re-recording is then one call, and the input plan stays readable through `script.read`. A replay made with `input.record` is re-recorded from its own events, which `input.readReplay` returns in `play.step`'s input form (M19, ADR 0030 decision 14); no method reads the transcript back.
- **Re-recording.** When an engine change legitimately alters simulation results (a physics or gameplay fix), the agent re-runs the recording suites with `test.run {record}` through automation, so provenance and the transcript record the new replays. The change's review must state why the hashes changed. After a gameplay change a replay is re-recorded when it must cover the new behaviour: a matching hash means only that the worlds matched at each checkpoint and at the end (§5.1).
- Batch files per §6.7.

### 13.7 Observability
- **Screenshots** (§8.13): fresh frame after `WaitIdle`; `annotate: {labels: "all"|"selection"|[ids], colliders, bounds, axes, navMesh}` draws entity names and short ids so a vision model can tie pixels to entities (M30: `navMesh` draws the scene's baked navigation mesh as polygon edges, one colour per agent type, `RenderViewFlags::Navigation`, ADR 0045 decision 12); from M22 `bounds` also outlines every drawn UI element in yellow and the labels name UI elements, in scene pixels over the UI, with or without a camera (`AppendUiRenderAnnotations`, ADR 0033 decision 9). The MCP tool returns an image content block plus the saved path.
- **`scene.tree {format: "Text"}`**, the token-efficient outline:
```
Main.scene  rev 58  dirty  14 entities
├─ Camera      7c1f09a2  Transform Camera(Ortho 11.5)            (7.5, 10, 20)
├─ Sun         09bb1e2f  Transform DirectionalLight              (0, 10, 0)
└─ Game        8f3a2c1d  Transform Script(Scripts/Game.luau)     (0, 0, 0)
   ├─ ScoreText 1d2e3f4a Transform Text("Score 0")
   └─ … 3 children (depth limit)
```
- **`ui.tree {format: "Text"}`** (M22, ADR 0033 decisions 8 and 31), the UI's outline in scene pixels: a header line, each canvas in draw order with its sort order and scale (scene pixels per canvas unit; a World canvas also `world <w>x<h>`, its canvas pixels, in which its elements' rectangles are, C22.3 decision 53), and below it its elements in draw order with their UI components (`UiRect`, which every element holds, left out; the widgets as `UiButton`, `UiToggle(on|off)`, `UiSlider(<value as read>)`, `UiScrollView(<x>,<y>)`, its position as read, and C22.3's `UiTextInput("<text>")`), their rectangle `(x,y wxh)`, `clipped` (a clipping ancestor clips it) or `hidden` (it covers no pixel), `inactive` for an inactive canvas or element that `includeInactive` lists (M25's friction F10, ADR 0036), `overflows` when its text's laid-out box reaches beyond its rectangle (M25's friction F02), and then the interaction markers in one group: `disabled` for a widget that is not interactable, and `focused`, `hovered` and `pressed` from the play session's interaction state (`UiSystem::GetInteraction`; the edit scene has none). The JSON format adds each element's path, parent, depth, clip and text (a text input's own Text, C22.3), its `widget` (`TextInput` for a text input) and `interactable` and the play session's `focused`, `hovered` and `pressed`, and (M25's F02) its text's `textBounds` (from its lines' leftmost pen start to their rightmost advance end and from the block's top to its bottom, in the rectangle's pixels; all 0 when it draws no text) and `textOverflows`, (M25's F11) every element's `scale`, its canvas's, and (M25's F10) `active`. The edit scene is laid out at `width` x `height`, by default the project's window size; the play scene's is the session's current layout (`UiSystem::GetLayout`):
```
Main.scene  rev 12  1600x900 scene pixels  4 elements
Hud  9a1c03f2  UiCanvas(sort 0, scale 2)
├─ Panel  4be2d7a0  UiImage(Ui/Panels.spritesheet#0)  (20,10 80x40)
│  ├─ Score  77c0e15b  UiText("Score 0")  (28,14 48x32)  clipped
│  └─ Lives  0f3d9e21  UiText("Lives 3")  (104,14 40x32)  clipped  hidden
└─ Pause  5c2e81aa  UiImage(none) UiButton  (120,10 80x40)  focused hovered
```
- **Logs and events** are structured with source locations and entity context, read by cursor so nothing is lost between polls. **Script errors** are deduplicated with tracebacks and pause play on the first error; the agent then inspects with `script.eval {context: "Play", entity: "/Game", code: "return self:BoardToAscii()"}`.
- **Graphs** (M24, ADR 0035 decisions 8, 13 and 14): a graph behaviour's compile, type and runtime errors name a line of its transpiled text, and the editor maps every finding to its node: `graph.read` lists the graph's `GRAPH_INVALID` and `GRAPH_UNREACHABLE_NODE` findings and the import's script findings each with its node, and with `luau` the text and its line map; during play `graph.liveValues` reads each node's last output values, the members and the instance's errors by node between frames without changing the state hash (§11.12), which the Graph Editor shows beside its nodes.
- **`scene.diff {against: "Saved"}`** gives the agent a precise self-review. `entity.bounds` and `physics.bodyInfo` support layout and physics reasoning (gaps between track pieces); in scripts and test suites the same questions are answered by `Entity:GetWorldBounds()`, `Physics.GetColliderBounds()` and `Physics.Raycast` (§11.5).
- **`project.validate`** returns `{id, severity, code, message, entity?, component?, field?, asset?, file?, line?, hint, autoFixable}`. `fix: true` applies every safe fix, and `fix: [ids or codes]` applies only the selected ones (the editor's per-item buttons use the same path); either way the fixes form one undoable command. Codes (generated into `Docs/Reference/Validation.md`): `SCENE_NO_PRIMARY_CAMERA`, `SCENE_MULTIPLE_PRIMARY_CAMERAS`, `SCENE_DUPLICATE_UNIQUE_COMPONENT`, `SCENE_NONCANONICAL_ORDER`, `SCENE_INVALID_HIERARCHY` (dangling or cyclic parent), `SCENE_INCONSISTENT_PREFAB_LINK`, `ENTITY_DUPLICATE_ID`, `ENTITY_DANGLING_REFERENCE`, `COMPONENT_FIELD_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `COMPONENT_MISSING_REQUIREMENT`, `COMPONENT_CONFLICT`, `ASSET_MISSING`, `ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH`, `ASSET_IMPORT_FAILED`, `ASSET_ORPHAN_META`, `ASSET_DUPLICATE_HANDLE`, `ASSET_ORPHAN_DEPENDENCY`, `ASSET_TANGENTS_APPROXIMATED`, `ASSET_UNSUPPORTED_UV_SET`, `ASSET_VERTEX_COLORS_IGNORED` (retired by M23: no longer reported), `ASSET_CONTENT_SKIPPED`, `PATH_CASE_MISMATCH`, `PREFAB_MISSING_ASSET`, `PHYSICS_NONCONVEX_DYNAMIC`, `PHYSICS_MIXED_TRIGGER`, `PHYSICS_DYNAMIC_TRIGGER`, `PHYSICS_ALL_DOFS_LOCKED`, `PHYSICS_INVALID_SHAPE`, `PHYSICS_ADJACENT_STATIC_BODIES`, `PHYSICS_UNKNOWN_LAYER`, `PHYSICS_NONUNIFORM_SCALE`, `PHYSICS_DYNAMIC_UNDER_MOVING_PARENT`, `PHYSICS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `SCRIPT_COMPILE_ERROR`, `SCRIPT_TYPE_ERROR`, `SCRIPT_NOT_A_BEHAVIOUR`, `SCRIPT_UNKNOWN_FIELD_OVERRIDE`, `SCRIPT_FIELD_TYPE_MISMATCH`, `INPUT_UNKNOWN_ACTION` (string literals passed to `Input.*Action*`/`GetAxis`, found by AST scan), `AUDIO_NO_LISTENER`, `AUDIO_MULTIPLE_PRIMARY_LISTENERS`, `RENDER_NO_LIGHTING`, `RENDER_LIGHT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (more enabled lights than the project's `Rendering.MaxShadedLights`; M29), `RENDER_SPOT_SHADOW_BUDGET` (more than 16 shadowed spot lights; 8 before M29), `BUILD_START_SCENE_MISSING`, `BUILD_SCENE_MISSING`, `TEST_SUITE_INVALID` (a `Testing.Suites` entry whose script is not a TestSuite or whose scene is not a registered Scene asset; ADR 0024 decision 6), `SCRIPT_COMPUTED_ASSET_LOAD` (only while `Export.PruneUnreferenced` is on: an `Assets.Load` whose reference a script below `Assets/` that `Export.Exclude` leaves in computes, which a pruned export cannot follow, at the script's line; an unfixable warning, §7.6; ADR 0030 decision 21), `PREFAB_CYCLE` (a prefab that nests itself, directly or through other prefabs: an error on each prefab on the cycle; ADR 0031 decision 8), `SPRITE_UNKNOWN_SORTING_LAYER` (a SpriteRenderer, or from C21.2 a TilemapRenderer, naming a sorting layer that `SortingLayers.Layers` does not declare, drawn in the first layer), `SPRITE_FRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` (a SpriteRenderer whose Frame its sprite sheet lacks, which draws nothing) and `SPRITE_UNKNOWN_CLIP` (a `SpriteAnimator` whose `Clip` names no clip of its `SpriteRenderer`'s sprite sheet, when the sheet loads or there is none), these three unfixable warnings, then `PHYSICS2D_MIXED_WORLDS` (an entity holding both 2D and 3D physics components, which keeps its 3D body only; an unfixable error) and `PHYSICS2D_OFF_PLANE` (a 2D body whose world rotation is not a rotation about Z alone, which takes its rotation about Z; an unfixable warning), M21's five codes in ADR 0032 decision 12's order, then its `TILEMAP_FRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` (a tilemap's palette entry naming a frame its sprite sheet lacks, whose cells draw nothing; an unfixable warning on the `.tilemap` file, field `Palette[<i>].Frame`, once per entry; ADR 0032 decision 30), then its milestone review's `SPRITE_FRAME_OUTSIDE_TEXTURE` (a sprite sheet's frame that extends past its texture's size, its imported width and height, reported on the sheet file, field `Frames[<i>].Rect`, and a tilemap's palette entry naming such a frame, on the `.tilemap` file, field `Palette[<i>].Frame`, once each; the texels past the edge sample the texture's edge; an unfixable warning). M22's codes follow: `UI_ELEMENT_WITHOUT_CANVAS` (an entity with a `UiRect` and no `UiCanvas` on an ancestor, which layout leaves out: an unfixable warning on the element; M22, ADR 0033 decision 13), `UI_IMAGE_FRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` (a `UiImage` whose `Frame` is not an index of its loaded sprite sheet's `Frames`, which draws nothing: an unfixable warning; ADR 0033 decision 13), `UI_WIDGET_PART_INVALID` (a `UiToggle` `Graphic`, `UiSlider` `Fill` or `Handle`, `UiScrollView` `Content`, or `UiTextInput` `TextElement` or `Placeholder` (C22.3, decision 53) that names an entity of the scene that is not a UI element below its widget in its canvas, which the widget ignores: an unfixable warning on the widget's field; a part the scene lacks is `ENTITY_DANGLING_REFERENCE`'s; ADR 0033 decision 35). M23's codes follow: `RENDER_POINT_SHADOW_BUDGET` (more than 16 shadow-casting point lights enabled in a scene, four before M29: an unfixable warning on the scene file; ADR 0034 decision 18, ADR 0044 decision 6), `ANIMATION_NO_ANIMATOR` (a `SkinnedMesh` whose mesh has a skin with no Animator on its entity or an ancestor) and `ANIMATION_SKELETON_MISMATCH` (a `SkinnedMesh` whose mesh skin addresses more joints than its Animator's Skeleton holds), unfixable warnings on the `SkinnedMesh`, each drawing its bind pose, which the AnimationSystem phase also raises once per entity (ADR 0034 decision 30). M24's codes follow, the graph checks of the validator's own read of every Graph-imported source (a `.graph` file, a Script asset of the Graph importer; with the Scene scope, of the graphs the scene's script slots hold, which the script source rule sends there and never to the Luau check): `GRAPH_INVALID` (a graph that does not read or breaks a rule of the node library, `ValidateGraph`'s unfinished inputs included: an unfixable error per problem, field its JSON pointer and message naming its node; the graph does not import, and this code is its import failure, never a second `ASSET_IMPORT_FAILED`) and `GRAPH_UNREACHABLE_NODE` (a statement node that no event's flow reaches, so it never runs: an unfixable warning at `/Nodes/<i>`, reported while the graph has no problem but unfinished inputs, as `graph.read` reports it); `SCRIPT_COMPUTED_ASSET_LOAD` also covers a graph's computed loads, found in its transpiled text as the exporter finds them, at the text's line and its node's pointer (ADR 0035 decisions 5 and 24). M26's codes follow M24's: `PROBE_NOT_BAKED` (an `IrradianceVolume` or `ReflectionProbe` whose `Data` is null or does not load as its type: an unfixable warning on the component's `Data`, the probe lighting and reflecting nothing until `lighting.bake` bakes it; `Scene/ProbeValidation.h`, ADR 0037 decision 9). Its terrain codes follow it: `TERRAIN_NO_HEIGHTFIELD` (a `Terrain` whose `Heightfield` is null or does not load as one, which draws nothing and whose `TerrainCollider` makes no body) and `TERRAIN_SPLAT_NOT_RAW` (a `Terrain` whose `SplatMap` is a Texture not imported as a data texture, the Texture importer's Usage Linear and Compression None: its weights would be decoded as sRGB colour or blurred by block compression, and `terrain.edit` cannot paint it; a built-in texture is not checked), unfixable warnings on the `Terrain`'s field (`Scene/TerrainValidation.h`, ADR 0037 decision 9); M34's `INPUT_INVALID_ACTION` (an action of `Input.Actions` that `play.start` refuses: an unknown binding name, a stick axis among a button list, a `Gamepad` that is not a gamepad axis or a field its type does not have), an unfixable error at the action's field (ADR 0049 decision 7); M33's `PARTICLE_FRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` (a `ParticleLook` whose flipbook range, `FirstFrame` and `FrameCount` or to the sheet's last frame, is empty or ends past its loaded `SpriteSheet`'s frames, so its particles draw nothing), an unfixable warning on `FirstFrame` or `FrameCount` (`Scene/SpriteValidation.h`, ADR 0048 decision 9); M30's `NAV_MESH_NOT_BAKED` (the scene's `Navigation` has no `NavMesh`, or it does not load as one: every navigation query finds nothing) and `NAV_MESH_STALE` (the bake input's hash, recomputed from the scene's static colliders, `NavModifier`s and `Navigation` settings, differs from the one the mesh stores, or the input can no longer be read), unfixable warnings on the `Navigation`'s `NavMesh` that name the scene's file (`Scene/NavigationValidation.h`, ADR 0045 decision 9). Phase 6's follow (ADR 0052's ledger): M36's `PHYSICS_SURFACE_UNUSED` (a `ColliderSurface` whose entity holds no solid collider of a body the scene creates: no collider, triggers only, a character's capsule, 2D colliders only, or a body a composition error refuses: `PHYSICS_MIXED_TRIGGER`, `PHYSICS_DYNAMIC_TRIGGER`, `PHYSICS_NONCONVEX_DYNAMIC`, `PHYSICS_ALL_DOFS_LOCKED`, `PHYSICS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`), an unfixable warning on the `ColliderSurface` (`Scene/PhysicsSurfaceValidation.h`, its code in an array of its own, ADR 0053 decision 6), then M37's `PHYSICS_JOINT_INVALID` (a `HingeJoint`, `SliderJoint`, `DistanceJoint` or `FixedJoint` that cannot be made: no RigidBody with a collider at or above its entity, a `ConnectedBody` naming no entity or no body, an end under a CharacterController or a RigidBody2D, both ends one body, a zero `Axis`, equal limits while `UseLimits` holds, or a `MinDistance` above `MaxDistance`; an unfixable error on the joint, which is not created; the play session raises the same once per joint as a physics diagnostic, so as a script error; `Scene/PhysicsJoints.h`, ADR 0054 decision 9). Phase 7's follow (ADR 0058's ledger, with M42's allocations from ADR 0059's): M41's `ANIMATION_ATTACHMENT_INVALID` (a `BoneAttachment` that cannot attach its entity: no Animator above it, an empty `Bone`, a Skeleton without the joint `Bone` names, with up to three close joint names, or at run time an Animator without a pose; or an attached entity whose physics fights its placement: a `CharacterController`, a Dynamic `RigidBody`, or solid colliders without a Kinematic body of its own), an unfixable warning on the `BoneAttachment`, which the AnimationSystem phase also raises once per entity; an entity that is not attached keeps its Transform (`Scene/BoneAttachments.h`, ADR 0058 decision 3), then M42's `RENDER_REFLECTION_INVALID` (a `PlanarReflection` whose entity has no `MeshRenderer` with a `Mesh`, or whose mesh's bounds reach farther than `PlanarReflectionMaxMeshDistance`, 5 cm after the entity's scale, from its plane, with a hint naming the local axis along which the mesh is thinnest and the `Offset` of its face there, or a mesh too thick for any plane), an unfixable warning on the component's field (`Scene/PlanarReflectionValidation.h`, its code in an array of its own, ADR 0059 decision 3), then M44's `PHYSICS_MASS_UNUSED` (a `MassProperties` whose entity's `RigidBody` makes no Dynamic body: Static, Kinematic, triggers, or no body the scene creates), an unfixable warning on the `MassProperties` (`Scene/PhysicsMassValidation.h`, its code in an array of its own, ADR 0062 decision 3), then M44's `PHYSICS_VEHICLE_INVALID` (a `WheeledVehicle` that cannot be made: its `RigidBody` makes no Dynamic body, no `VehicleWheel` below it or more than 16, a wheel on the vehicle's entity or under another `RigidBody` or a `CharacterController`, a solid collider on or below a wheel, or fields that contradict each other: a suspension, the engine's RPM, the gears and shift points, a differential or bar naming a wheel that is not the vehicle's, no differential naming a wheel, driven torque shares that do not sum to 1, a curve whose X does not increase; one per vehicle, its first reason as the Subject `body`, `wheels`, `wheel`, `collider`, `suspension`, `engine`, `transmission`, `differential`, `bar` or `curve`), an unfixable error on the `WheeledVehicle`, which is not created; the play session raises the same once per vehicle, and `refused` for a description the world refuses (`Scene/PhysicsVehicles.h`, its code in an array of its own, ADR 0062 decision 3). Later milestones append their codes in landing order (ADR 0028's, ADR 0042's, ADR 0052's, ADR 0058's and ADR 0059's ledgers). Severities where the list leaves them open: the physics codes as ADR 0014 decision 9 gives them (`PHYSICS_ADJACENT_STATIC_BODIES`, a warning fixable by a Static `RigidBody` on the nearest common ancestor unless it is missing or has trigger colliders of its own; `PHYSICS_NONUNIFORM_SCALE` and `PHYSICS_DYNAMIC_UNDER_MOVING_PARENT`, warnings; `PHYSICS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, a warning past 90 % of a limit and an error at it; the others errors whose body is not created, except `PHYSICS_UNKNOWN_LAYER`, whose body goes to layer 0); `AUDIO_MULTIPLE_PRIMARY_LISTENERS`, a warning fixable in the open scene by clearing `Primary` on each extra listener, and `AUDIO_NO_LISTENER`, an unfixable warning (ADR 0015 decision 12); `RENDER_LIGHT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, an unfixable warning on the scene file that counts its effectively enabled lights (ADR 0013 decision 7).
- **`stats.get {views?}`**: measured FPS, CPU frame and per-pass CPU/GPU timings (`views: false` leaves the per-view statistics out, for a counter read such as a soak check's, ADR 0038 friction F09), dropped simulation time, entity/body/voice counts (`bodies`: the play session's 3D and 2D worlds' bodies together, M21's milestone review), native Vulkan allocation counts, from M18 the GPU device losses the host recovered from (`deviceLosses`; each recovery is also a `GpuDeviceLost` event, after which a client retries a request the loss failed with `Gpu`), and, from M25's landing, the committed bytes of the heap the C runtime allocates from (`processHeapAvailable`, `processHeapCommittedBytes`: on Windows the process heap's, its large blocks included, through `Platform/ProcessHeap`; unavailable on Linux and macOS, and when the query fails), which the hardening soak's memory rule measures (`Docs/Decisions/0036-m25-tetris-pixel-art.md`, "The soak"), and from M28 (ADR 0043 decision 4) the play session's awake bodies of both worlds and live particles (`activeBodies`, `particles`) and each view's shaded and dropped lights and deformed skinned meshes (`lights`, `droppedLights`, `skinnedMeshes`), M42's planar reflections drawn, dropped past the cap of 4 or for want of their GPU objects or the view's probe constants, and culled, and the drawn ones' entities in slot order (`planarReflections`, `droppedPlanarReflections`, `culledPlanarReflections`, `planarReflectionEntities`; each drawn one's cost is its pass row `PlanarReflection<k>`, ADR 0059 decision 3; the readout's `PlanarReflections` and `DroppedPlanarReflections`), the counters the performance readout (`Application.GetStats`) shares through `Session/SessionStatistics`, which Dist has. Scene and game views have independent histories; transient screenshot captures never replace them. The views are the editor's displayed viewport panels: a panel that is not displayed is not rendered and its view reports unavailable, and a headless editor displays the Scene view only, so its game view is unavailable (ADR 0027 friction F08), unless it was started with `--headless-game-view`, which renders the Game view every frame as a displayed Game panel would, at the game resolution or the project's window size (M19, ADR 0030 decision 11). Each view also reports the quality settings its recorded frame rendered with (`shadowMapSize`, `ssaoHalfResolution` and, from M32, `ssrHalfResolution`: the project's `Rendering` settings, also in an exported Runtime), from M32 the SSR trace's area in a completed frame (`ssrAreaFrame`, `ssrTiles`, `ssrTracedTiles`, `ssrTracedPixels`: the trace image's 8 × 8 tiles, those the trace covered and the trace pixels that traced, read back without waiting as the GPU timings are; ADR 0047 decision 13), and its shadow counts: `shadowDraws`, `shadowedSpotLights`, `droppedSpotShadows` and, from M23, `shadowedPointLights` and `droppedPointShadows` (ADR 0034 decision 18), and from M26 `historyFrames`, the renders since the view's temporal history (§8.3's temporal anti-aliasing paragraph) last started afresh, 0 at its first render and after a scene change, play starting or stopping, or a camera cut (ADR 0037's W26.2 review), and from M29 `maxShadedLights`, the shaded-light cap the frame rendered with, and `cachedPointShadows` and `cachedSpotShadows`, the shadowed lights whose maps the static shadow cache reused (ADR 0044 decisions 4 and 5).
