the script heap's lowest post-collection trough in the last quarter within max(128 KiB, 10 %) of its lowest trough in 0.25 to 0.75, a window without a collection failing unless its samples bound the growth, counters flat; a collection cycle longer than about a quarter of the soak can leave the heap rule inconclusive depending only on its phase, which a longer soak, `Hardening.py --soak-frames N`, confirms), Release perf capture (warning-only); the fuzz step's shard count and timeout follow the per-target costs its previous run measured (ADR 0028 decision 16), and it needs as many logical CPUs and GiB of available memory as its minimum shard count (14 with M17's measured costs) and otherwise refuses to start (exit code 3) | `CI.py --milestone` (or `--stages hardening`) | every milestone gate from M15 to M17, and from M18 each phase's last lander (local; ADR 0024 decisions 12 to 19, ADR 0028 decision 12) |

### 15.2 Unit tests per module (representative, not exhaustive)
- **Core:** `ENGINE_TRY`/context chaining; UUID hex round trip, prefix matching, seeded generator; XXH64 test vectors; `HandlePool` generation reuse; VFS escape, reserved-name and case rejection; `OverlayMount` never writes through; atomic writes under injected failure; `JobSystem(0)` ordering; `FixedStepScheduler` tables; `ScriptedClock` cycling; DetMath accuracy (≤ 1 ULP of correctly rounded references) and committed output hash; JsonReader error paths with pointers; canonical float formatting; `BinaryReader` bounds; deterministic mutation fuzzing (seeded byte flips, truncations) of BinaryReader, JsonReader, pak and cooked-header readers with a never-crash, always-`Result` oracle.
- **Platform:** input latching tables (taps between steps, multiple steps per frame, zero steps per frame); action/axis resolution incl. up-positive stick Y and `Invert`; null-platform window event path; crash child (`Tests --crash-child` writes a report and exits 4); `Editor.lock` exclusivity (a second lock attempt fails; the lock is released when the child is killed).
- **Reflection/Scene:** registry-parametrized component and struct tests (§5.4) incl. `Map`/`Variant` and non-finite rejection; hierarchy ops and cycle rejection; canonical order independence from insertion history; TransformSystem vs reference math; byte-identical re-save; every migration; `UnsupportedVersion` for a newer file; one fixture per structural defect (duplicate IDs, dangling and cyclic parents, child before parent, inconsistent prefab links, duplicate unique components) in strict and repair mode; prefab derived IDs, overrides surviving a prefab edit, user children preserved, external references intact; deferred destroy; serializer-copy state hash equality; interpolation snapshot rules (§5.2: script-moved, kinematic, frame-phase-written, teleported, created).
- **Asset:** Khronos glTF sample fixtures (textured, normal-mapped, alpha modes, embedded/data-URI, external `.bin`/`.png` closure); URI rejection (`..`, absolute, `http:`); `TEXCOORD_1` and `COLOR_0` in the attribute stream and a `TEXCOORD_2` texture's diagnostic (M23); dependency metas move and trash with their owner; a standalone texture referenced by a glTF is not duplicated; required-extension rejection; stable sub-asset handles after reimport; double-import hash equality; cache corruption recovery; registry diagnostics; pak round trip, tamper detection and determinism; `SoundSynth` bit-exactness; hot-reload races (no echo reimport after an editor write, stale job completion dropped, `SceneChangedOnDisk` raised and never auto-applied, reload deferred during lockstep).
- **Renderer (CPU):** device scoring (incl. storage-format support and the Bloom fallback); projection math (perspective and orthographic reverse-Z mappings, linear-depth and view-ray reconstruction for both, clip-space +Y up without a Y flip); cascade splits, frustum-corner fit for both projections, texel snapping; GTAO radius for both projections; atlas allocation; light culling; transparent sort ties; tonemapper CPU references; blue-noise hash.
- **Physics, Audio:** §9.7 and §10.4. **Scripting:** one test per registered function, method, property, operator and constructor (enforced by comparing the test registry with `ScriptApiRegistry`); every callback; sandbox escape suite (`getfenv`/`setfenv`, `setmetatable(_G)`, writing library tables or another module's globals, `string.dump`, `debug` access, `gcinfo`/`collectgarbage`, `require` outside `Assets/`); load-time VM (multi-file require graph, shared budget, engine API at module top rejected, classification of Behaviour/Module/TestSuite); yield rule (§11.3); watchdog (including during GC-heavy loops and nested callbacks inheriting the deadline); memory soft limit, second breach and hard limit; error-message format and locations (callbacks and resumed threads); hot reload (behaviour state, module patch plus dependents, chain rollback); `math.random` and DetMath-rebound `math` and `vector.angle` determinism; bounded host copies of script strings (log size and rate, debug text, names, tags); test runner (suite collection, sequential cases, per-case timeout, isolation, quit handling, filter, result schema); type-checker fixtures (§11.9). **Play-session fuzz:** 10,000 seeded random calls through the bindings and automation (NaN, ±Inf, 0, negative, huge, subnormal, wrong types, destroyed entities) never crash, assert or reach Jolt; every rejection is a located script or protocol error. A fixed corpus with exact expectations is followed by calls whose arguments are generated from the seed for Transform and collider writes, `AddComponent` values, `Scene.Instantiate` position, rotation and parent (including parents whose scale or translation make a finite position unrepresentable) and `SetParent` on physics entities; after each, every transform in the scene and every body stays finite.
- **EditorCore:** command property tests (§12.3); composite atomicity; dirty tracking; validator codes (incl. selective fixes); exporter validation; automation framing, auth, schema validation, `dryRun` (overlay, `supportsDryRun`, no provenance), `ifRevision`, `$ref`, bounded outputs, case-insensitive enums; an in-process round trip for every method.

**Test infrastructure** (`Tests/Source/Support`): custom doctest main (`DOCTEST_CONFIG_IMPLEMENT`) that creates the `ProcessContext` (headless platform) and parses `--require-gpu`, `--death-test=`, `--windowed-child=`, `--update-golden`; the recording assert handler and death-test helper (§4.5); the `ExpectLog` listener (§4.4); `TempDirectory` RAII; seeded `UUIDGenerator`/`Random`; `HeadlessGpuFixture` (skips with a reason when no Vulkan 1.3 device exists unless `--require-gpu`, which `CI.py` and `PreCommit.py` pass unless `--gpu-optional`; fails a test on any validation or NVRHI error or warning and on any object still alive; `Test::ProbeGpuForProcess` for tests whose code under test creates its own device); per-test timeout watchdog (it ends the exit watch before its exit with code 5); the exit watch: the main begins the crash handler's exit watch for doctest's run and ends it after (§4.13; Windows, in a process that writes crash reports), so an exit during the run, through `exit()` on any thread or through `ExitProcess` (a driver's or a library's included), writes a crash report naming the exiting thread, its stack down to its start routine, the exit code where `ExitProcess` gave it and, through the `TestCase` breadcrumb the test case tracker sets as each case starts, the running test case, and prints its reason on stderr; a process that is not a child also logs `Test case of process <pid>: <name>` at Trace, flushed, as each case starts (`Test::FormatTestCaseLogLine`; the log file names a line's thread, not its process), and `Test.py` names the last such case of a run that ended with a non-zero exit code and no crash report, with that thread's last log lines (§2.3), which on Windows leaves, besides the binary's own announced exit codes 2, 3, 4 and 5, `TerminateProcess` (from inside the process or outside it) or an exception status no handler saw as the end; doctest's own fatal-condition handler stays on during each case (it replaces the crash handler's unhandled-exception filter and `SIGABRT` handler, prints `CRASHED` and calls `std::exit(1)` on the faulting thread), and the exit watch reports that exit too: its report names the faulting thread, its stack down through the exception's dispatch to the faulting frame and the crashed case (the tracker keeps a crashed case's `TestCase` breadcrumb), and its minidump's exception stream names that thread (M23's landing, R-GPUCRASH, "TestMain: an access violation on another thread during the doctest run leaves a report naming that thread on Windows"); an `exit()` during a case also ends in doctest's `CRASHED: SIGABRT`, after the watch's report, once static destruction meets the timeout watchdog's running thread; glm helpers `ApproxEqual(a, b, epsilon)` plus `doctest::StringMaker` specializations for vec/quat/mat.

### 15.3 GPU correctness tests (device-independent oracles)
Shadow fallback coverage also creates a device with `GraphicsSpecification::DisableDepthClamp`: the reported pancaking capability is false, and real caster/receiver tests exercise the extended-near path under both API caps. The next default device pancakes again (§8.7; ADR 0017).

Clear and exact readback; compute arithmetic; matrix convention; winding/culling; octahedral pack/unpack vs CPU; **white furnace**: BRDF energy ≈ 1 with multi-scatter compensation, prefiltered constant environment = 1 ± 0.5% in every mip, SH irradiance constant; DFG LUT vs CPU reference; GPU prefilter vs CPU reference at 16²; equirect-to-cube seam continuity; tonemapper curves vs CPU at 1,024 points; shadow stability under a 0.37-texel camera move; picking returns the expected UUID at known pixels; ImGui texture protocol; pipeline count; zero leaks at device destruction; host-image-copy and staging uploads read back identically (§8.1); the swapchain state machine (windowed child process) recovers from out-of-date and minimize; fault injection (§8.14 item 8): the fatal faults (`device-lost-unrecoverable`, `hang`, and out-of-memory at startup under `ENGINE_GPU_FAULT_AT_STARTUP`) exit 4 with a crash report and, in the editor, an autosave, while from M18 `device-lost`, `hang-reset` and `hang-reset-persistent` run on after a recovery at the frame boundary and the `oom-*` faults fail only their request (§8.14 items 6 and 7); every GPU owner survives a device loss (M18): one loss test per owner through the shared helper `Test::RunDeviceLossTest` (`Tests/Source/Support/DeviceLossTest.h`) proves the same output, the same tracker counts and one recovery after an injected loss, and an owner that presents proves its loss in a windowed child instead; each test also runs with `--vulkan-api=1.3`. The GPU stage enables `VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION_EXT` together with standard validation, and any validation or synchronization-validation message, error or warning, fails the test: in process through `HeadlessGpuFixture`, which reads the device's counts after its teardown, and in the Editor and Runtime processes a test starts through `--expect-no-gpu-errors`. A meta-test provokes a real hazard and a real validation error to prove the wiring.

### 15.4 Golden images
Deterministic scenes of `Projects/FeatureTest` (the golden scene list, `Test::ListGoldenScenes`: `Golden.jsonl`'s kept `Assets/Scenes/Golden/*.scene` and the golden scaffolds' scenes, below), rendered headless at 640×360 at fixed ticks with FXAA on and fixed noise: PBR roughness × metallic sphere grid under the Studio HDRI, IBL only, CSM PCSS near/far cascades, orthographic-camera shadows (`ShadowsOrtho`), spot shadows, point-light shadows (`PointShadows`), textures block-compressed and uncompressed side by side (`TextureCompression`), clustered lights over instanced meshes and their LightCount view (`ClusteredLights`), a skinned and morphed glTF posed by a clip (`SkinnedPose`), alpha and additive particles after a fixed number of lockstep ticks (`Particles`), a room's baked colour bleed and box-projected reflection (`Probes`), automatic exposure, a colour-grading LUT, TAA and SSR (`AutoExposure`, `Lut`, `Taa`, `Ssr`), a sculpted terrain of splatted layers across levels of detail (`Terrain`), M29's 1,000 small point lights and twelve shadowed point and spot lights at a shaded-light cap of 1,024 (`ManyLights`), one mesh untouched, tinted, glowing, its texture offset, half dissolved and half faded by per-entity material parameters (`MaterialParameters`, M31), M32's fog (`FogPillars`, `FogHollow`, `FogSunGlow`, `FogTransparent`: pillars receding into distance fog, height fog in a hollow under an isometric orthographic camera, the sun glow over a fogged skybox, a transparent pane and a sprite in fog), M33's particle look (`ParticleLook`: a turning, blended flipbook flame meeting the floor softly, sparks stretched along their velocity, flat discs on the ground and blooming embers; `ParticlesInFog`: alpha smoke and additive embers receding into distance fog, from M33's merge), M42's planar reflections (`PlanarReflections`, `Scaffold/GoldenPlanarReflections.jsonl`, IdSeed 3902: a sharp mirror showing a figure's back, with a marker only the mirror sees and a box behind the glass clipped away, the sky and fog in the glass, a rough mirror's blurred reflection of the figure and a turned-away mirror's fallback; ADR 0059), GTAO on/off and with an orthographic camera (`GtaoOrtho`), each tonemapper, bloom, alpha mask/blend, debug draw, selection outline, SDF text, an imported glTF fixture, M22's UI (`GoldenUi/Ui.scene`: a sprite frame at 1:1 and scaled, a 9-sliced clipping panel holding a stack and wrapped text, and a second canvas over the first), M22's widgets at rest (`GoldenUiWidgets/UiWidgets.scene`: an enabled and a disabled button in the canvas's Disabled tint, a toggle on and one off, a horizontal and a vertical slider at a quarter, and a list scrolled within its clip), M22's scripts (`GoldenUiScripts/UiCjk.scene`, `UiArabic.scene` and `UiHebrew.scene`: Japanese, Arabic and Hebrew UI texts, shaped, ordered by the bidirectional algorithm and in mixed-direction lines, through a copy of Inter whose `Fallbacks` are the Noto fixtures, imported with `Ranges` of the texts into `Assets/Fonts/GoldenUiScripts/`), M38's direction-following alignment and mirrored rows (`GoldenUiDirection/UiDirection.scene`, ADR 0055 decision 13: Arabic and Latin labels at Start and at End, a block of an Arabic and a Latin paragraph at Start, and an options row of a caption, a slider at a quarter and its value laid out HorizontalReverse above the same row laid out Horizontal, in `GoldenUiScripts`' copy of Inter and its Arabic fallback), M22's World canvas (`GoldenUiWorld/UiWorld.scene`: a World canvas turned in a lit scene, partly behind a mesh, under a Screen HUD), the combined 2D/UI scene of M22's landing (`Combined2DUiGolden/Combined2DUi.scene`: sprites and a Screen canvas with a button and labels under a PixelPerfectCamera at scale 3, the UI laid out at the reference resolution and upscaled with the sprites), the default editor layout (`editor.screenshot`). Goldens live in `Tests/Golden/<DeviceClass>/` (device class = vendor + driver major, e.g. `nvidia-58x`). Comparison: fail if more than 0.1% of pixels differ by more than 2/255 or any pixel by more than 24/255 (thresholds tunable per test); failures write `actual`, `expected` and `diff` PNGs to `bin/TestResults/Golden/`. On a device class without goldens the suite runs in **smoke mode** (renders, zero validation errors, finite pixels, luminance statistics within loose bounds) and reports "goldens missing" as a warning, never a pass of the comparison; but when another device class of the same vendor has the image's golden, the driver's major version changed, and the test fails with "device class changed" instead (M18's device-class check; the rename procedure is `Tests/Golden/README.md`'s). `Test.py --update-golden` writes candidates that must be reviewed (skill `golden-images`) before commit. No software rasterizer goldens and no cross-device comparison. The scenes are written by committed scaffolds (§15.5; the fixtures they import sit in `Scaffold/Sources` as byte-identical copies of `Tests/Data/Assets`, which a test checks): the eight M8 scenes by `Projects/FeatureTest/Scaffold/Golden.jsonl`, whose outputs regeneration keeps (exactly the files `Scaffold/Baseline/Provenance.json` records, with its bytes; they change only through a recorded regeneration, ADR 0028's ledger, or through the project's recorded upgrade, a canonical rewrite whose provenance entries replace their baseline entries, as M23's Material version 2 did, ADR 0034 decision 21), and later ones by **golden scaffolds**, `Scaffolds.json` entries with `GoldenDirectories` that write only below directories of their own, outside the kept ones, and that `Scaffold.py` regenerates and checks like every other scaffold (§2.3). The first is `Scaffold/GoldenRendererII.jsonl`: M18's recorded regeneration (T-FTPROV) moved `Golden.jsonl`'s M9 part into it, so its nine scenes (`AnnotatedScreenshot`, `GtaoOff`, `GtaoOn`, `GtaoOrtho`, `SelectionOutline`, `ShadowsFar`, `ShadowsNear`, `ShadowsOrtho` and `SpotShadows`, in `Assets/Scenes/GoldenRendererII/`) and three materials (`Assets/Materials/GoldenRendererII/`), each with its `.meta`, have `Provenance.json` entries from its seeded run; up to M17 those 24 files were copied in from a unit test's replay and had none (ADR 0022 review fix M11; ADR 0025). M21's `Scaffold/Sprites2DGolden.jsonl` writes `Sprites2DPixelArt` (`Assets/Scenes/Sprites2DGolden/`, its texture and sprite sheet in `Assets/Textures/Sprites2DGolden/`): unlit sprites in the project's sorting layers, flipped sheet frames, a whole texture and the four built-in sprite shapes under a `PixelPerfectCamera` whose 200 × 120 reference resolution the golden view upscales 3 times in a letterbox, in the 2D colour path, so without the FXAA, bloom and dither the other scenes render with (§8.2; ADR 0032 decision 17). M21's `Scaffold/Lights2DGolden.jsonl` writes `Lights2DPixelArt` (`Assets/Scenes/Lights2DGolden/`, its normal map, sprite sheet and tilemap in `Assets/Textures/Lights2DGolden/`) in the same view and colour path: a lit wall under a dim global light and three point lights of falloff 0, 0.5 and 1, two unlit sprites, one inside a light and one outside every point light, a lit sprite, a normal-mapped one beside a raised point light and a lit tilemap (ADR 0032 decision 32). M23's first is `Scaffold/GoldenPointShadows.jsonl` (IdSeed 2104): its scene `PointShadows` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenPointShadows/`), two shadow-casting point lights whose shadows cross several cube faces, and its three materials (`Assets/Materials/GoldenPointShadows/`; ADR 0034 decision 3). Its second is `Scaffold/GoldenTextured.jsonl` (IdSeed 2103): its scene `TextureCompression` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenTextured/`), a colour photo, an alpha-masked texture, a normal map and a metallic-roughness map, each imported twice (`Assets/Textures/GoldenTextured/Auto/` and `None/`, `Compression` Auto and None) and drawn on quads side by side through its eight materials (`Assets/Materials/GoldenTextured/`; ADR 0034 decisions 13 and 17). Its third is `Scaffold/GoldenClusteredLights.jsonl` (IdSeed 2106): its scene `ClusteredLights` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenClusteredLights/`), a grid of blocks and orbs (two kinds of one mesh and one material each, so each pass draws each kind as one instanced draw) under three shadow-casting point lights, thirty small point lights and two spot lights, and its three materials (`Assets/Materials/GoldenClusteredLights/`); its goldens are the lit image, which the per-draw render and the brute-force light loop equal byte for byte, and its LightCount view (`ClusteredLightsLightCount`; ADR 0034 decisions 2, 5 and 17). Its fourth is `Scaffold/GoldenSkinnedPose.jsonl` (IdSeed 2108): it imports `Skinned.gltf` into `Assets/Models/GoldenSkinnedPose/` and writes its scene `SkinnedPose` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenSkinnedPose/`), the strip "Posed" playing the fixture's Wave clip at tick 24 of FeatureTest's 64 Hz (its second joint turned and the clip's Bulge weight at 0.75) beside the strip "Morphed" at its rest pose with its `SkinnedMesh`'s own Bulge weight 1, lit; edit scenes draw skinned meshes in their bind pose, so its test poses the scene's Animators as the editor's animation preview does (`PoseAnimator`, through `GoldenSceneOptions::PrepareScene`) before it renders (ADR 0034 decision 33). M26's `Scaffold/GoldenParticles.jsonl` (IdSeed 2402) writes its scene `Particles` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenParticles/`): the alpha emitter "Smoke", grey puffs rising from a cone, growing and fading, its base behind a block, and the additive emitter "Embers", a burst and a stream of sparks from a sphere, over a lit floor; edit scenes simulate no particles, so its test steps the emitters through the Particles phase's system for 64 ticks of FeatureTest's 64 Hz (`ParticleSystem`, through `GoldenSceneOptions::PrepareScene`) before it renders, and checks that the image differs from the scene without them (ADR 0037 decisions 7 and 25). M26's `Scaffold/GoldenProbes.jsonl` (IdSeed 2404, a rendering scaffold) writes its scene `Probes` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenProbes/`, its three materials in `Assets/Materials/GoldenProbes/`): a room open at the front, its left wall red and the rest white, lit by one point light close to the red wall, with a chrome ball, an `IrradianceVolume` over the room and a box-projected `ReflectionProbe` of the room's box, which it bakes through `lighting.bake` into `Assets/Lighting/Scenes/GoldenProbes/Probes/` (the volume's `.irradiance` and the reflection's `.hdr`, a golden directory of its own); the golden shows the red wall's light bouncing onto the white surfaces and the room reflected in the ball, and its test checks that the image differs without the volume and without the box projection and that the far white wall turns red only through the volume (ADR 0037 decisions 8, 16 and 25). M26's post-processing goldens are the scenes of four golden scaffolds (ADR 0037 decision 25): `Scaffold/GoldenAutoExposure.jsonl` (IdSeed 2406) writes `AutoExposure` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenAutoExposure/`, its three materials in `Assets/Materials/GoldenAutoExposure/`), a dim room under the Studio environment at 5 % with a bright emissive lamp, exposed by `ExposureMode` Auto (its test checks it far brighter than its manual exposure); `Scaffold/GoldenLut.jsonl` (2407) writes `Lut` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenLut/`, its four materials in `Assets/Materials/GoldenLut/` and its copy of the `Warm.cube` fixture in `Assets/Luts/GoldenLut/`), red, green and blue spheres graded by that LUT (its test also renders the built-in identity LUT within one level of the ungraded image); `Scaffold/GoldenTaa.jsonl` (2408) writes `Taa` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenTaa/`, its two materials in `Assets/Materials/GoldenTaa/`), a fan of thin poles and a turned block anti-aliased by TAA instead of FXAA; and `Scaffold/GoldenSsr.jsonl` (2409) writes `Ssr` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenSsr/`, its three materials in `Assets/Materials/GoldenSsr/`), a mirror-like metal floor reflecting two red blocks and a blue ball through SSR, the Studio environment where a ray misses. The temporal ones (`AutoExposure` and `Taa`) are captured after the fixed warm-up from a reset history (`CaptureWarmupFrames` renders, ADR 0037 decision 10), so two captures are byte-identical, which each of the four tests checks. M26's `Scaffold/GoldenTerrain.jsonl` (IdSeed 2411) makes the flat 129 × 129 heightfield of `asset.create` in `Assets/Heightfields/GoldenTerrain/`, sculpts it (three hills and a pass) and paints its splat map with `terrain.edit`, and writes its scene `Terrain` (`Assets/Scenes/GoldenTerrain/`): the 64 m terrain's four splatted layers (a tiled checker under a grass tint, rock, sand and snow) seen from beyond a corner along its diagonal with `LodBias` 0.25, so its chunks draw at five levels of detail, stitched without cracks; its test also checks the levels the view selects and that the painted splat map changes the image (ADR 0037 decisions 22, 23 and 25). The scenes are rendered by `Test::RenderGoldenScene` from a temporary copy of the project (an `EditorAssetManager` with the engine resources, an `EnvironmentBaker` and the editor's generators, then `ViewportCapture`), which fails on any load or scan error and on any Error-level asset diagnostic instead of rendering placeholders. The M8 golden scenes and the legacy LitScene fixture turn SSAO off and disable shadow casting, so M9's passes leave their images unchanged. M9 scenes explicitly enable the passes they exercise. The editor layout golden renders the actual Editor host at its full retained UI extent, rather than the 640×360 scene-capture extent. The DebugDraw golden appends its primitives to the extracted snapshot instead of running a script, so its image depends on the renderer alone. The committed goldens are those of device class `nvidia-62x`: ADR 0013 decisions 14, 21 and 24 committed them for `nvidia-61x`, and `Tests/Golden/README.md`'s procedure renamed them when the product owner took NVIDIA driver 621.14 (ADR 0028 decision 9, amended 2026-11-10).

Each scene below is bound to one or more suites in `Testing.Suites` (§11.10), and a row without a scene names a suite that runs in no scene of its own. Every suite runs in all three modes unless noted.

| `Golden/*.scene` and the golden scaffolds' scenes (`GoldenRendererII/*.scene`, `Sprites2DGolden/*.scene`, `Lights2DGolden/*.scene`, M22's `GoldenUi/Ui.scene`, `GoldenUiWidgets/UiWidgets.scene`, `GoldenUiScripts/*.scene` and `GoldenUiWorld/UiWorld.scene`, the combined 2D/UI test's `Combined2DUiGolden/Combined2DUi.scene` (M22's landing, whose `Combined2DUi.replay` presses its button through the PixelPerfectCamera), and M23's `GoldenPointShadows/PointShadows.scene`, `GoldenTextured/TextureCompression.scene`, `GoldenClusteredLights/ClusteredLights.scene` and `GoldenSkinnedPose/SkinnedPose.scene`, and M26's `GoldenParticles/Particles.scene`, `GoldenProbes/Probes.scene`, `GoldenAutoExposure/AutoExposure.scene`, `GoldenLut/Lut.scene`, `GoldenTaa/Taa.scene`, `GoldenSsr/Ssr.scene` and `GoldenTerrain/Terrain.scene`, and M29's `GoldenManyLights/ManyLights.scene`, 1,024 lights at the shaded-light cap that `Scaffold/LightLimits.jsonl` sets in `FeatureTest.eproj`, and M31's `GoldenMaterialParameters/MaterialParameters.scene`, and M32's `GoldenFog/*.scene`, and M33's `GoldenParticleLook/*.scene`, and M38's `GoldenUiDirection/UiDirection.scene`) | §15.4 |

**Settings coverage.** `Projects/FeatureTest/FeatureTest.eproj` uses non-default values wherever they are observable at run time (gravity, layers and matrix, fixed rate, seed, input actions with inversion, rendering, scripting limits, `MaxEntities`, and from M22 `Localization.Locale`, which the Localization suite reads (and M38's suites with a `Locale` of their own start elsewhere), and the `Ui` section's `Cancel` and `Next`, which add Backspace and the gamepad's right bumper and the UiWidgets suite drives). `Tests/Data/Project/AllSettings.eproj` sets **every** `ProjectSettings` field to a non-default value. A unit test loads it, applies it to an `EngineContext` and asserts each value is observed by its consumer (gate 8).

**Determinism replay.** `Assets/Tests/Replays/Determinism.replay` (600 ticks: a 50-body pile, a rolling ball on a compound track, scripted forces, script-side DetMath trigonometry and `^` with a non-trivial exponent) carries a committed `FinalStateHash`. It runs in every mode, and the `determinism` stage compares the hashes (§15.8).

FeatureTest scenes are produced by committed automation batch scaffolds (`Projects/FeatureTest/Scaffold/*.jsonl`, run with `Editor --batch --id-seed <n>` from `Scaffold/Baseline/` in the order and with the seeds of `Scaffold/Scaffolds.json`, by `Scaffold.py`; ADR 0022 decision 8), so they stay byte-for-byte reproducible and exercise the automation surface; test scripts live under `Assets/Tests/`. The harness (`Engine/Testing/FeatureTestRunner`, §11.10) runs every suite and replay in `Testing`, collects results in the shared schema, evaluates the coverage gates for the current mode (the project opts in with `Testing.CoverageGates`; only an unfiltered, non-recording run evaluates them) and writes JUnit XML plus `bin/TestResults/FeatureTest-<mode>.json` (the editor's `--junit <file.xml>` puts both beside each other elsewhere, so the Debug and Release editors do not collide); exit 1 on any failure (ADR 0022 decisions 3 and 7).

### 15.6 Coverage gates
- **Gate 1, components:** every registered component appears in FeatureTest scenes that are simulated or rendered, and every serialized field holds a non-default value somewhere.
- **Gate 1b, enum values:** every value of every enum reachable from a serialized component field (`Tonemap` AgX/ACES/PbrNeutral/Linear, `Attenuation`, `BodyType`, `MotionQuality`, `SsaoQuality`, `ClearMode`, `ProjectionType`, `TextSpace`, `TextAlignment`, `AudioGroup`, `PrefabOverrideKind`, …; ADR 0022 decision 4) appears in a simulated or rendered FeatureTest scene. Enums that only asset files hold (`AlphaMode`, `SoundWave`, import settings) are not gated per value; their importer and asset tests cover them, and gate 9 loads every format that carries them.
- **Gate 2, script API:** every `ScriptApiRegistry` counter is non-zero: functions, methods, properties, operators and constructors (§11.4), plus every per-value counter of string-enum parameters.
- **Gate 3, script callbacks:** every lifecycle callback was invoked at least once.
- **Gate 4, proxy fields:** every scriptable component field was read and written through a proxy at least once.
- **Gate 5, automation methods:** every registered method was called by `Tests/Automation` (the bridge-side client counts calls).
- **Gate 6, validation codes:** every `project.validate` code is triggered by a fixture in `Tests/Data/Validation/`, except the retired codes (`ProjectValidator::GetRetiredCodes`), which nothing reports any more and which keep their place so a code is never reused (M23: `ASSET_VERTEX_COLORS_IGNORED`, since `GltfImporter` version 2 imports `COLOR_0`; ADR 0034 decision 18).
- **Gate 7, descriptions:** every type, field, function, method, property and automation method has a non-empty description.
- **Gate 8, project settings:** every `ProjectSettings` field is non-default in `Tests/Data/Project/AllSettings.eproj`, and the settings test observes each one (§15.5).
- **Gate 9, formats:** every importer and every importable extension (`Asset/SourceFormats.h`; an extension an importer claims only to refuse would be excluded, and none is since M23's `EnvironmentImporter` version 2 imports `.exr`) is cooked and loaded in the run, as observed through the asset manager's load observer; only the loads of the run's own work count (inside `FeatureTestRunner::Advance`), never those of the editor's viewports or thumbnails in the host frames between, so no count depends on how many frames ran; the foreign formats' fixtures live in `Assets/Formats/` (ADR 0022 decision 5 and "Integration").

**Per-mode evaluation.** FeatureTest runs in three modes: editor headless lockstep (which also catches editor/runtime divergence), exported Release and exported Dist (cook and strip bugs). Each run records its counters in `FeatureTest-<mode>.json`. Gates 1–4, 1b and 9 are evaluated **per mode**: in each mode, every entry available in that mode (`RunModes::All`, plus `EditorOnly` in the editor) must be covered, and an `EditorOnly` entry counts only in the editor run. A merge step (`Test.py --merge-coverage`) then checks that the union over the three runs covers every registered entry, so nothing is exempt in all modes; it compares id sets per mode, never the registry fingerprint, which differs between modes by design (ADR 0022 decision 6). Gates 5–8 are mode-independent. Each gate has a seeded-gap fixture (`Tests/Data/CoverageGaps/`) proving that it fails and names exactly what is uncovered. Gates 1–4, 1b and 9 have one fixture per mode, for example an entry covered only by the editor run makes the Dist evaluation fail.

### 15.7 Automation and game tests
`Tests/Automation/test_*.py` (stdlib `unittest` + `Tools/Automation/engine_client.py`) start headless editors on temp projects: project lifecycle, launcher state, every method, scaffold batches, play/step/waitFor (incl. the 50 ms step budget and `stateHash`), recording rules (Edit-mode start, `restart`, capture of `Test.Inject*`, header parameters), replays, undo/redo byte-equality, dry runs (no file, watcher event, trash item or provenance entry; `Unsupported` for non-dry-runnable methods; batch rejection with `failedOp`), crash recovery, `Busy` watchdog (a script spin-loop under a raised budget), project lock (a second editor exits 3; `--read-only` opens), `editor_launch` attaching to a running editor, client disconnect (pending operations cancelled, lockstep released, play paused), `project.upgrade` provenance entries, security (bad token, HTTP probe, path escapes, oversized frame), export and run exported, and MCP conformance (the SDK's client lists tools with compact schemas, calls `scene_tree`, receives an image from `viewport_screenshot`), and the provenance audit of a project built through the bridge's launcher (`test_audit_provenance.py`, ADR 0026). Game suites run each staged demo's `Testing` suites and replays (`Test.py --suite games`, §15.8).

### 15.8 CI entry point
`python Scripts/CI.py` runs stages in order, each failing fast: `setup → generate → lint → build → bake → unit → gpu → golden → feature → automation → export → determinism → games → portability` (plus `hardening` at each phase's last lander: `CI.py --milestone`, `Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decision 12). Every stage names its configuration:

| Stage | Configuration(s) | Content |
|---|---|---|
| setup, generate, lint | n/a | toolchain checks, project generation, the static checks (`Scripts/Lib/scripts.py` `run_static_checks`, the list §15.9 gives): `CheckBuildConfig.py` with its fixtures, `Lint.py` (header self-containment included) and its self-test, `CheckRuntimeMap.py --self-test`, the provenance audit self-test (`AuditProvenance.py --self-test` over `Tests/Data/Provenance/`), the format check, the fixture generators' `--check`, the DetMath reference check (`GenerateDetMathReference.py --check`) and both `FetchAssets.py` checks |
| build | Debug, Release, Dist | all projects existing in each configuration (EditorCore, Editor, Tests have no Dist); after the Dist build, the step "Dist: map file contains no automation, Analysis, ImGui or AssetPipeline symbols" (§14.4) |
| bake | Release | `Editor --headless --renderer vulkan --bake-engine-assets` fills the configuration-independent `bin/EngineCache` (incremental; a no-op when nothing changed); without a device it fails, and with `--gpu-optional` it reruns with `--renderer none` (the environments left out with a warning) and ends as a warning |
| unit | Debug, Release | `Tests` (T0 static suite + T1), incl. committed-hash physics and DetMath tests |
| gpu | Debug, Release | `Tests --test-suite=GPU --require-gpu`, validation + synchronization validation, both API caps; the fixture fails a test on any validation or NVRHI error or warning (`--gpu-optional` drops `--require-gpu` on a machine without a Vulkan device) |
| golden | Release | `Tests --test-suite=Golden --require-gpu` (CPU inputs are configuration-independent per §9.1; SPIR-V flags are identical in Debug and Release, so the commit gate compares the same goldens in Debug) |
| feature | Debug, Release | `Editor --headless --run-tests --strict` on FeatureTest (editor mode; §6) |
| automation | Release | Python suites and MCP conformance against the Release editor (the bridge's default); `--require-gpu` like gpu for the tests that start a rendering editor (the screenshot methods), `--gpu-optional` drops it |
| export | Release editor → Release and Dist testing exports | from a `--strict` editor, exports a copy of FeatureTest with `testing: true` into `bin/Exports/<Config>/FeatureTest/`, runs `--feature-test` in both, evaluates each mode's gates, then merges coverage over the three modes with the feature stage's Editor report (§15.6); `--require-gpu` like gpu (ADR 0024 decision 9) |
| determinism | Debug, Release editors (`--strict`); exported Release and Dist | compares the final state hash of `Determinism.replay` and of every FeatureTest replay across all four runs and with the committed `FinalStateHash` (each run compares the checkpoints as it plays); any difference fails. The editor runs also require every replay with input events to fail its verification without them (the input check, `continuePastCheckpoint` included, whose final-hash warning fails nothing, ADR 0030 decision 3; both FeatureTest replays fail it as required: `Determinism.replay` by its hashes and expectations, `Input.replay`, whose probe keeps its observations in script tables, by its expectations). The editor runs need no GPU; the exported runs' hashes come from the export stage's reports and, without them and without `--require-gpu`, are reported as not compared (a warning; ADR 0024 decision 10) |
| games | Debug, Release editors (`--strict`); Release editor → Dist exports | from M16 (ADR 0026 decision 8): every staged demo below `Projects/` and `Tests/Projects/` (FeatureTest excluded; one passed step, `games`, while none exists; staged demos that share an `.eproj` stem or a staged Name fail the `games` step before any runs, ADR 0030 decision 12): the provenance audit of its staged files (index mode, §13.12), then, in strict rendering Debug and Release editors on its staged blobs (for a demo with `Native/`, Windows only, each editor gets the user's preference and a current build of the module first, the Dist half's exporting editor included, ADR 0030 decision 35), the build-settings check first (a set `StartScene` that a non-empty `Export.BuildScenes` lists; ADR 0027 decision 4, B1), `script.check` and `project.validate` clean, the canonical re-save check (`project.upgrade {dryRun: true}` changes nothing) and its suites and replays at their committed hashes, at least one committed replay with input events and every one failing its verification without them (the input check, `continuePastCheckpoint` included, whose final-hash warning fails nothing, ADR 0030 decision 3), and a testing Dist export run with `--feature-test` whose hashes must equal the committed ones, the editor runs' and the export's own `featureTest.replays` (ADR 0030 decision 10), then a plain Dist export's smoke test; `--require-gpu` like gpu |
| portability | n/a | generation for other OSes (file lists, precompiled-header paths, xcode4 Dist LTO, the Runtime's link settings), clang-cl builds of Engine + Tests (Release) and of every Dist project |
| hardening | Release + ASan; Debug (the debug-heap gpu suite) | perf capture (plain Release, warning-only), soak (plain Release editor per scene of every project under `Projects/`, FeatureTest and the demos there, rendering each scene's game view with `--headless-game-view` beside the Scene view (a sample whose game view did not render failing the scene), a new script error failing the scene; and the exported Release FeatureTest, rendering its game camera), the AddressSanitizer workspace in `bin-int/Asan`, its unit suite (in shards sized from the measured per-case costs, several at a time, `Docs/Decisions/0060-skerries-engine-program.md` decision 3) and feature suite, the Debug gpu suite on the Windows debug heap with the GPU object lifetimes logged (`Docs/Decisions/0029-m18-contract.md` decision 37), long fuzz (`Scripts/Hardening.py`, `Scripts/Perf.py`; only with `--milestone` or an explicit `--stages`, ADR 0024 decision 19). Within a phase, only the last lander's milestone-end `CI.py` adds `--milestone` (the hardening stage: perf, soak, ASan, debug heap, fuzz), on the merged tree of all the phase's milestones, when any milestone of the phase touches core systems, file readers (fuzzed formats) or the renderer, as its plan or contract decides; every other milestone end runs `CI.py --require-clang-cl` without `--milestone`. The program's setup gate keeps its own rule (ADR 0028 decision 16), and M27, alone in phase 4, decides in its plan (ADR 0028 decision 12) |

Because simulation is deterministic across configurations (§9.1), replays and expected hashes recorded in any configuration are verified in all of them; the `determinism` stage is the mechanical proof. **Portability** (local, no remote needed): premake generation for `--os=linux gmake`, `--os=linux ninja` and `--os=macosx xcode4` must succeed with the expected file lists and project/configuration sets; the gmake and xcode4 precompiled-header paths must exist (xcode4's `GCC_PREFIX_HEADER` resolved as Xcode does), and the first-party xcode4 projects must enable LTO (`LLVM_LTO`) in Dist; the Runtime's generated link settings must hold in every configuration (`Scripts/Lib/portability.py`, ADR 0024 decision 18: the Linux `$ORIGIN` RPATH and map file in gmake and ninja, the Frameworks rpath, map file, deployment target 14.0 and tool product type in xcode4, `/MAP` and the subsystems in vs2026); then `clang-cl` builds (`toolset "clang"`) of Engine + Tests in Release and of every Dist project (asserts compiled out, so Clang reports helpers only asserts use), with warnings tolerated only in vendored code, when the VS Clang component is installed, otherwise reported as skipped (a failure with `--require-clang-cl`). Header self-containment is not a portability check: it is the `headers` step of `Lint.py` in the lint stage, because it needs the compilation database `Lint.py` generates. GitHub is only an off-site backup of the repository: GitHub Actions is not part of the process, and nothing reads or waits for its results. From the program's setup commit, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only when started by hand (`workflow_dispatch`), and no step of the process starts it. As written, it holds jobs for windows, ubuntu-24.04 with GCC 14 and Clang 19, and macos arm64, each running its stages through `CI.py` (the Windows job with `--require-clang-cl`; on Linux the lint stage in the Clang job only); the hosted runners have no GPU, so the Linux jobs run the gpu, golden and automation stages on Lavapipe (Mesa's software Vulkan driver, `mesa-vulkan-drivers`, which meets the Vulkan 1.3 feature set of §8.1) with the SDK's `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`, inside the unit stage's Xvfb display and with `--require-gpu`, golden images in smoke mode (§15.4: no software-rasterizer goldens), and the Windows and macOS jobs run them with `--gpu-optional`. Windows is the only verified platform. First-party code stays portable by rule (the `Platform/` layering, no Windows-only shortcuts, the local portability stage's premake generation and clang-cl builds), but Linux and macOS are never verified: the Linux/macOS catch-up was dropped by the product owner, because there is no Linux or macOS machine without GitHub. This replaces ADR 0011's non-blocking remote CI and the catch-up of ADR 0026 decision 1 (ADR 0028 decision 10). Results: JUnit in `bin/TestResults/`, a summary table on stdout, exit code per §4.1.

### 15.9 Commit gate and code review
Before every commit, the gate that fits it (`Docs/Decisions/0023-verification-without-duplicate-work.md`; `Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decisions 11 and 12). Wave and contract commits are checkpoint commits on the milestone branch: each is reviewed and runs only the tests and suites its change touches, never `PreCommit.py` or `CI.py`. The milestone end runs one `CI.py` on the milestone's final tree instead of PreCommit. Within a phase, only the last lander's milestone-end `CI.py` adds `--milestone` (the hardening stage: perf, soak, ASan, debug heap, fuzz), on the merged tree of all the phase's milestones, when any milestone of the phase touches core systems, file readers (fuzzed formats) or the renderer, as its plan or contract decides; every other milestone end runs `CI.py --require-clang-cl` without `--milestone`. The program's setup gate keeps its own rule (ADR 0028 decision 16), and M27, alone in phase 4, decides in its plan. (This supersedes ADR 0024 decision 19 in part.) CI runs every PreCommit stage (golden and automation in Release only, which covers them: CPU inputs and SPIR-V are configuration-independent and asserts stay on in Release). Commits straight to main outside a milestone run the targeted checks their change touches, as a checkpoint commit does, or for documentation-only edits the checks that read the edited files; `PreCommit.py` stays for a change too broad to scope, and main is pushed only at a tree a full gate passed (`Docs/Decisions/0051-gates-in-proportion.md`). PreCommit is green when these pass (generate; the full lint-stage list of static checks: `CheckBuildConfig.py` on the workspace and on every fixture workspace, `Lint.py` and its self-test, `CheckRuntimeMap.py --self-test`, the provenance audit self-test `AuditProvenance.py --self-test` (ADR 0026 decision 9), the format check, every `Tests/Data/Generate/*.py --check`, the DetMath reference check `GenerateDetMathReference.py --check` (its self-test, then a byte comparison of `Tests/Source/Engine/Core/DetMathReferenceData.h` with a fresh generation; ADR 0025), `FetchAssets.py defaults --check` and `FetchAssets.py fixture --check`; Debug build; the `references` check, `GenerateDocs.py --check --config Debug`, which fails when any file of the generated reference (`Docs/Reference/*`, `Resources/Scripting/Engine.d.luau`, `Tools/MCP/catalog.json`; ADR 0022 decision 13) is missing, stale or extra compared with what the built editor generates (ADR 0019 decision 9); unit, gpu, golden, feature, automation and games suites in Debug, the automation suite against the Debug editor and the games suite as its audit of every staged demo and their Debug editor half (no Dist half: PreCommit builds no Dist; ADR 0026 decision 8), and the gpu, golden, feature, automation and games suites with `--require-gpu` (§15.1 T2 runs on this machine's GPU; `--gpu-optional` only on a machine without a Vulkan device)), then a **recorded review**: the `commit-review` skill (§13.10) reviews the staged diff against `Docs/ReviewChecklist.md` (correctness, error handling per §4.6, ownership, threading, determinism, tests added and meaningful, generated files refreshed, style and naming, no TODOs masking defects, docs updated). Blocking: any failing check, any unresolved checklist item, any unfixed confirmed finding, a nit included, missing tests for new behaviour, a style violation. One review pass per wave: blocker and major findings are verified before they are fixed, every confirmed finding is fixed at once, minors and nits included (never batched or deferred), and there are no rechecks of rechecks. A contract checkpoint gets one review of the frozen interfaces; the wave's one review pass covers the integrated wave diff; neither is rechecked. Milestones run in phases: the milestones of a phase are developed in parallel, each on its own branch in its own worktree, and their milestone-end `CI.py` runs go one at a time on the one GPU. Milestone end: the milestone branch merges current main, then one review pass of the milestone diff with every finding fixed, then one `CI.py` on the final tree; main fast-forwards to the milestone branch only after that run is green. Phase end: once the phase's last milestone has landed, main is pushed to `origin` as an off-site backup, and the work pauses for the product owner's go-ahead. (ADR 0028 decisions 11 and 14.) The review and its fixes precede the gate. The commit message ends with a `Reviewed:` trailer summarizing the review outcome and the gate result (a checkpoint commit names its targeted runs). Documentation edits after a green gate keep the result unless a check reads the edited file, and a red gate reruns only its failed stages unless the fix changed production code, build files or shared test support (ADR 0023). PreCommit and the milestone-end `CI.py` are strict: no `ENGINE_CONTRACT_STUB` and no test case skipped outside the child-process targets (`Test::ChildTargetSuite`) may remain (the `contract` step of `Lint.py` and the skip check of `Test.py`, `Docs/Decisions/0004-contract-stub-gate.md`). A contract checkpoint runs its targeted checks in contract mode (`Lint.py --allow-contract-stubs`, `Test.py --allow-skips`); the wave's integration replaces every stub and skip of its contract, and the milestone-end `CI.py` is strict, so none reaches main (Roadmap rule 3).

## 16. Cross-platform concerns

| | Windows x64 | Linux x64 (Ubuntu 24.04+) | macOS arm64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status | **verified** on every change; the only verified platform | generation-checked locally (the portability stage); never verified (ADR 0028 decision 10) | generation-checked locally (the portability stage); never verified (ADR 0028 decision 10) |
| Toolchain | VS 2026 (v145, MSVC 14.51), `vs2026` | GCC 14 / Clang 19+, `gmake`/`ninja` | Xcode 26 (minimum), `xcode4`, deployment target macOS 14.0 |
| Windowing | Win32 GLFW | **X11 GLFW only** (vendored build); Wayland sessions run through XWayland; native Wayland deferred (steps in `Vendor/GLFW/VENDOR.md`) | Cocoa GLFW; framebuffer ≠ window size (Retina) |
| Vulkan | driver `vulkan-1.dll`, loaded dynamically | `libvulkan.so.1` (package `libvulkan1`) | loader + MoltenVK (Vulkan 1.3/1.4 near-conformant, macOS 14+); KosmicKrisp used when installed (Vulkan 1.4 conformant, needs macOS 26 + Apple silicon); portability enumeration + `VK_KHR_portability_subset` |
| Audio | WASAPI → DirectSound → WinMM | PulseAudio/PipeWire → ALSA → JACK (dlopen) | CoreAudio (linked, `MA_NO_RUNTIME_LINKING`) |
| Export | app-local CRT DLLs; icon and version resources patched | RPATH `$ORIGIN` | `.app` bundle with loader + ICD, rpath `@executable_path/../Frameworks`, `Info.plist` + `.icns`, ad-hoc signed |

GPU requirement (M42, ADR 0059 decision 4): `shaderClipDistance` is a required device feature (§8.1), which the planar reflections' clip at their plane needs; a device without it is refused at startup with the missing feature named. The development machine's device reports it; Linux and macOS devices are not verified (ADR 0028 decision 10).
| Native modules (§11.11) | built with MSVC (`Scripts/BuildNative.py`), loaded and hot-reloaded in the editor (`LoadLibraryExW`), linked into exports | none: build, load and the export of a game with `Native/` return `Unsupported`; the editor treats the module as not loaded | none, as on Linux |
| Durable save data (M28, ADR 0043 decision 8) | `PublishedFile::WriteDurably`: the store's temporary file flushed (`FlushFileBuffers`) before its atomic rename | none: `WriteDurably` reports `Unsupported` and the store falls back to the atomic write without a flush | none, as on Linux |
| Display settings (M28, ADR 0043 decision 3) | the monitor's video modes and the switch between Windowed, Borderless and Exclusive (`Platform/Windows/DisplayModesWindows.cpp`, GLFW's monitor modes, without `VK_EXT_full_screen_exclusive`) | none: `Platform/Posix/DisplayModesPosix.cpp` reports `Unsupported`, so scripts see no modes and a refused request | none, as on Linux |

Windows is the only verified platform. First-party code stays portable by rule (the `Platform/` layering, no Windows-only shortcuts, the local portability stage's premake generation and clang-cl builds), but Linux and macOS are never verified: the Linux/macOS catch-up was dropped by the product owner, because there is no Linux or macOS machine without GitHub. Windows backends only: a kept item's platform interface stays, so a later port can add backends, but no Linux or macOS backend is written, and on Linux and macOS the interface reports the capability as unavailable (`ErrorCode::Unsupported`) through the platform layer's existing error path. The rule covers the platform capabilities the program adds in first-party C++: existing POSIX backends (`Platform/Posix/`) keep compiling when their interface changes, and the Python tooling keeps its guarded POSIX branches. Vendored libraries' premake scripts stay portable (the portability stage generates gmake and xcode4 projects from them); their GCC, Clang and Apple Clang builds are never compiled. (`Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decision 10.) Common rules: precise floating point and `JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC` on every platform (§2.2); all binary formats little-endian (asserted); text LF; JSON UTF-8 without BOM; data paths always `/`; the VFS case policy protects case-sensitive filesystems; paths are UTF-8 internally and converted only in `Platform`; platform code lives only in `Platform/<OS>/` and `Graphics` device setup (lint-enforced), so the untested platforms concentrate risk in few small files. The renderer avoids features with weak Metal mappings (geometry shaders, wide lines, large bindless arrays). Shaders are SPIR-V 1.6 from one source on every OS. `std::stacktrace`, modules, `std::flat_map` and coroutines are not used (CodeStyle §13).

## 17. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Linux/macOS rot without local builds | platform code isolated; generation smoke tests and clang-cl/header checks every run; honest status labels: Windows is the only verified platform. First-party code stays portable by rule (the `Platform/` layering, no Windows-only shortcuts, the local portability stage's premake generation and clang-cl builds), but Linux and macOS are never verified: the Linux/macOS catch-up was dropped by the product owner, because there is no Linux or macOS machine without GitHub. (ADR 0028 decision 10) |
| ODR/ABI mismatch with vendored libs (NDEBUG, Jolt, spdlog, miniaudio) | `Use<Lib>()` copied from VENDOR.md; `CheckBuildConfig.py`; workspace-scope `NDEBUG`; `VerifyJoltVersionID` fatal at startup |
| NVRHI or Slang drift | pinned commits/versions; NVRHI only in Graphics/Renderer/ImGui; reflection checks CPU-only; slangc version in cache key and checked |
| Swapchain sync hazards | per-image render-complete semaphores; resize/minimize state-machine tests; validation on in every GPU test |
| Golden flakiness | no temporal effects (from M26, captures reset temporal history and render a fixed warm-up, ADR 0028), fixed noise, per-device-class goldens (nvidia-62x only, the driver's major version held at 62x during the program since the product owner took driver 621.14, ADR 0028 decision 9; a same-vendor class without goldens fails the run instead of smoke-testing, M18's device-class check), smoke mode elsewhere, device-independent oracle tests carry correctness |
| Non-determinism (threads, unordered iteration, Jolt callback order, time, build configuration) | canonical order, sorted events, seeded UUIDs/RNG, sim-time APIs, `JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC` + precise FP everywhere, DetMath on the simulation path, lint on unordered iteration in serialization and on CRT transcendental functions, thread-count hash tests, cross-configuration `determinism` stage |

## 18. Milestone plan (summary; details, acceptance tests and parallelization in `Docs/Roadmap.md`)

Every milestone ends with one `python Scripts/CI.py` green on Windows: every stage that exists, in the configurations of the §15.8 matrix, and the clang-cl builds. From M15 to M17 that was `CI.py --milestone` with the hardening stage (plain `CI.py` before; ADR 0024 decision 19). From M18 on (`Docs/Decisions/0028-backlog-program.md` decision 12): within a phase, only the last lander's milestone-end `CI.py` adds `--milestone` (the hardening stage: perf, soak, ASan, debug heap, fuzz), on the merged tree of all the phase's milestones, when any milestone of the phase touches core systems, file readers (fuzzed formats) or the renderer, as its plan or contract decides; every other milestone end runs `CI.py --require-clang-cl` without `--milestone`. The program's setup gate keeps its own rule (ADR 0028 decision 16), and M27, alone in phase 4, decides in its plan. A recorded review and a commit go with it. Milestones run in phases: the milestones of a phase are developed in parallel, each on its own branch in its own worktree, and their milestone-end `CI.py` runs go one at a time on the one GPU. Milestone end: the milestone branch merges current main, then one review pass of the milestone diff with every finding fixed, then one `CI.py` on the final tree; main fast-forwards to the milestone branch only after that run is green. Phase end: once the phase's last milestone has landed, main is pushed to `origin` as an off-site backup, and the work pauses for the product owner's go-ahead. Windows is the only verified platform. First-party code stays portable by rule (the `Platform/` layering, no Windows-only shortcuts, the local portability stage's premake generation and clang-cl builds), but Linux and macOS are never verified: the Linux/macOS catch-up was dropped by the product owner, because there is no Linux or macOS machine without GitHub. (ADR 0028 decisions 10 and 14.) A setup commit lands on main before phase 1 (ADR 0028 decision 16). The World Tree engine program, M28 to M35 in one phase, phase 5, keeps these rules but one: by the product owner's decision, every one of its milestone ends runs `CI.py --require-clang-cl` and none runs the hardening stage (`Docs/Decisions/0042-world-tree-engine-program.md`, the owner's answers 8 and 9). Its phase 6, M36 to M40, runs it once, at the phase's last batch gate (`CI.py --milestone`), and every other gate of the phase with `CI.py --require-clang-cl` (`Docs/Decisions/0052-world-tree-phase-6.md`, the owner's answer 5).

## Appendix A. Decisions for CodeStyle [Architecture] topics

| Topic | Decision (section) |
|---|---|
| Error handling | `Result<T>`/`Status` (`std::expected`), asserts for bugs, fatal exit codes; surfacing per §4.6 |
| Exceptions / RTTI | enabled; first-party code never throws (lint); `try` only in allowlisted boundary files; no `dynamic_cast`/`typeid` in first-party code |
| Warnings | `/W4 /WX` (MSVC), `-Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Werror` (GCC/Clang) for first-party; vendor via external includes, warnings off |
| Floating point | precise model everywhere (`/fp:precise`; GCC/Clang `-fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off`, clang-cl through `/clang:`), never fast-math; `JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC`; DetMath instead of CRT transcendental functions on the simulation path (§2.2, §4.12, §9.1) |
| `Ref` | `std::shared_ptr`; no `WeakRef` alias; `Scope` = `std::unique_ptr` (§4.7) |
| Log/assert macros | `ENGINE_CORE_{TRACE,INFO,WARN,ERROR,CRITICAL}`, `ENGINE_{…}`, `ENGINE_{CORE_}ASSERT`, `ENGINE_{CORE_}VERIFY` (active in Dist), `ENGINE_UNREACHABLE`; loggers Engine/App/Script (§4.4–4.5) |
| Bit-flag enums | `template<> inline constexpr bool EnableFlagOperators<T> = true;` enables constrained `| & ^ ~ |= &=` and `HasFlag(value, flag)` from `Core/Base.h` |
| Threading | §4.11; memory strategy §4.7 |
| Namespaces | `Engine` everywhere (also Editor, Runtime, Tests); sub-namespaces `Utils`, `Detail`, `Automation`, `ScriptBindings`, `Lua` (Scripting's checked helpers and protected VM entry points; ADR 0021), `Test` |
| Platform layout | `Engine/Source/Engine/Platform/{Windows,Posix}/` today (`Posix/` shared by Linux and macOS), `Linux/` and `MacOS/` when a difference grows, helpers both halves share in `Private/` (§3); selected by premake `filter "system:*"` and guarded by `ENGINE_PLATFORM_*` |
| PCH | Engine (`EnginePCH.h`), Editor/EditorCore (`EditorPCH.h`), Tests (`TestsPCH.h`); Runtime none |
| Minimum Xcode / libc++ | Xcode 26, deployment target macOS 14.0 (unverified locally) |
| Headless/GPU tests | `HeadlessGpuFixture`, skip-with-reason unless `--require-gpu` (§15.2); goldens §15.4 |
| glm test helpers | `ApproxEqual` + `doctest::StringMaker` (§15.2) |
| FeatureTest | §15.5–15.6 |
| JSON key naming | PascalCase in authored files; camelCase automation envelopes (§6, §13.4) |
| Luau API naming | PascalCase modules, functions, properties; native `vector` and value-type fields lowercase; enums as string literals (§11.4) |
| Slang bindings | HLSL registers + Slang shifts matching NVRHI offsets, `registerSpaceIsDescriptorSet`, set 0 view / 1 material / push per draw; PascalCase resource names (§8.4) |
| Python / Lua tooling | stdlib only (except the MCP venv); Python is PEP 8 with a 120-column limit (CodeStyle §15); `Lint.py` checks syntax with `ast.parse` (also against the Python 3.10 grammar) + AST checks; premake Lua reviewed against CodeStyle §15 |
| Naming enforcement | `.clang-tidy` `readability-identifier-naming` (classes/functions/enums/constexpr `CamelCase`, private/protected members prefix `m_`, statics prefix `s_`, globals `g_`, locals/parameters `camelBack`, macros `ENGINE_` prefix via regex) run by `Lint.py` on `compile_commands.json`; falls back to the `RegexNamingChecker` in `Lint.py` (regex rules reading the same `.clang-tidy` options: `m_`/`s_`/`g_` prefixes and cases) when clang-tidy is absent or `--mode regex` is given |

| Unachievable CI gates (nightlies, remote CI, lavapipe on Windows) | Windows-local gates, honest status, portability stage, smoke-mode goldens (§15) |

| Project-scoped `configurations` does not drop Dist | `removeconfigurations { "Dist" }` (§2.2) |
| Unshifted `[[vk::binding]]` vs NVRHI offsets | Slang shifts = NVRHI defaults + `registerSpaceIsDescriptorSet` (§8.4) |
| Custom Jolt job adapter | Jolt's `JobSystemThreadPool` (§4.11) |
| `os.time`/`os.clock` left, watchdog off in Dist | removed; watchdog 5 s in Dist (§11.1) |

| Input edges per frame vs fixed-step reads | phase-aware latching (§4.3) |
| No array script property | `Field.Array` (§11.2) |
| Tests compiling Editor sources | `EditorCore` static lib (§12.1) |
| Late automation | automation core in M4 (§18) |
| Agents writing scripts with file tools | `script.write` + provenance audit (§13.5, §13.12) |
| FeatureTest not run on shipping Dist | three-way runs, harness kept in Dist (§14.4, §15.6) |
| Lifecycle callbacks and proxy fields not gated | gates 3 and 4 (§15.6) |
| Demo audio sourcing | `.sfx` synthesizer + built-in presets (§10.3) |
| HDRI downloads inside the editor | `FetchAssets.py` script, allowlisted, md5 (§2.3) |
| Physics/Scene/Renderer coupling | ECS-agnostic Physics/Audio, CPU-only assets, RenderSnapshot (§3) |
| IBL baked at every load | baked at import, cooked (§8.6) |
| Hazel naming not enforced | clang-tidy naming (Appendix A) |
| Vulkan 1.4 usage undefined | §8.1 policy, concrete gated host-image-copy path, dual-API tests |
| Audio device loss | notification-driven recovery/fallback (§10.1) |
| Pre-commit review undefined | §15.9 |
| Friction per collider vs Jolt per body | on `RigidBody` (§5.3); per collider from M36 through a `ColliderSurface`, set on each contact by the world's contact listener (§9.2 "Collider surfaces", ADR 0053) |
| Reverse-Z Y flip winding | `frontCounterClockwise = true` + test (§8.3) |
| Import allowlist requiring human input | `asset.import` and `terrain.importHeightmap` (M26) read any absolute source path read-only (§13.2) |
| Editor spawning builds during export | never; error names the build command (§14.2) |
| Native file watchers | polling only (§7.5) |
| No clean error without a Vulkan loader | exit 3 + message box (§8.1, §14.3) |

| Native Wayland | X11 via XWayland; out of scope (ADR 0028) |
| Point-light shadows, TAA, auto-exposure, clustered lights, instancing | resolved: point-light shadows, clustered lights and instancing built in M23 (W23.1; §8.3, §8.7; ADR 0034 decisions 2, 3 and 5); histogram auto-exposure built in M26 (W26.1) and TAA in M26 (W26.2) (§8.3; ADR 0037 decisions 10, 15 and 17). |
| Faster registry-based Play copy | resolved: the faster serializer copy landed in M20 (W20.1; ADR 0031 decision 6, measured), its 30 ms budget still tracked warning-only by the perf capture (§5.6; ADR 0024 decision 16); the registry-based copy won't do (ADR 0028 decision 2). |
| Pak compression, reachability pruning | resolved: built in M19 (W19.2). Pak version 2 deflates each entry at a fixed level wherever that saves at least an eighth, byte-identical from the Debug and Release editors (§14.1); `Engine.pak` holds the built-ins the game reaches or the Runtime asks for, and the opt-in `Export.PruneUnreferenced` packages into `Game.pak` only what the build scenes reach, with `SCRIPT_COMPUTED_ASSET_LOAD` naming each computed `Assets.Load` (§7.6; ADR 0030 decisions 17, 20 and 21). |
| Second UV set and vertex colours in the mesh format | resolved: built in M23 (W23.2). Mesh format version 2 carries `TEXCOORD_1` and `COLOR_0` in an attribute stream on a second vertex binding of every mesh pipeline (still 24), Material version 2 picks each map's UV set, and the vertex colour multiplies the base colour; `ASSET_UNSUPPORTED_UV_SET` names only `TEXCOORD_2` and up, and `ASSET_VERTEX_COLORS_IGNORED` is retired (§6.5, §7.4, §8.5; ADR 0034 decisions 9, 10 and 18). |
| Further Vulkan 1.4 features (push descriptors, line rasterization) | not used; need NVRHI support (§8.1); won't do (ADR 0028, the vendored rule) |
| Multiple open scenes in the editor | resolved: M20 (W20.2) keeps up to 16 open scenes in tabs, one active, each with its own history, selection, revision and autosave, and an optional scene target on every scene-addressing method (§12.1, §12.2, §13.4; ADR 0031 decisions 13 to 16); tabs are editor-only, and additive runtime scenes are not built (§5.6). |
| Editor shader hot reload | resolved: built in M18 (W18.1): `shaders.reload` and the editor's Tools > Reload shaders swap in the rebuilt shaders without a restart, and a broken build output keeps the previous pipelines (§7.5, §8.12; ADR 0029 decision 3). |
| Profiler timeline export and GPU merge | resolved in M18 (W18.1; ADR 0029 decisions 4 and 11): each retired frame's stage and pass GPU zones reach the profiler's timeline (`RenderStatsHistory::PublishGpu`), and the editor's `profiler.capture` writes one Chrome trace with CPU and GPU zones, counting the zones its rings dropped (§4.13). |
| Per-frame arena for the render snapshot and debug draw lists | resolved: closed by M18 without adopting it. W18.1 measured the extraction at 10 to 27 µs per view and frame over the heap and 20 to 29 µs over a per-frame monotonic arena, of about 1.0 to 1.5 ms of frame CPU work: no gain, so the default allocator stays; the `std::pmr` parameter stays for a later measurement (§4.7; ADR 0025; ADR 0029 decisions 9 and 51). |
| Luau compiler objects in Dist | resolved: built in M19 (W19.2). The first-party `require` replaced Luau's Require library in every configuration, so Dist links no Compiler, Bytecode, Config or Require object (Parser and Ast stay for `ScriptApiRegistry`'s signature parsing), and the map check's `LuauCompiler` family keeps it so (§14.4; ADR 0030 decision 22, which replaces ADR 0025 decision 5's premise). |
| Build versioning | resolved: built in M19 (W19.1). The build id (`<version>+<12-hex commit>[.dirty]`, stamped by `Scripts/Build.py`) is in `session.hello`, `session.info` and the session files, `Engine.pak`'s metadata and `Game.json` (GameManifest v2), while a replay header records the version alone (`0.1.0` until ADR 0038's friction F10, the running engine's since, so a bump regenerates FeatureTest's scaffold-recorded replays, and a committed demo's replays keep the version they were recorded with); each phase's last lander bumps the minor version (§13.2, §14.1; ADR 0030 decisions 13 and 18). |
| Provenance of FeatureTest's 24 copied-in M9 golden files | resolved in M18 (W18.2): its recorded regeneration moved `Golden.jsonl`'s M9 part into the golden scaffold `GoldenRendererII.jsonl`, whose seeded run writes the 24 files with their `Provenance.json` entries, and `Scaffold.py` regenerates and checks them like every scaffold (§15.4; ADR 0022 review fix M11, ADR 0025, ADR 0028). |
| A character carried by moving ground | resolved: built in M19 (W19.1) as the opt-in `CharacterController.InheritGroundVelocity`, which while grounded adds the ground's horizontal velocity to the character's (§5.3, §9.6; ADR 0030 decision 36). |

## Appendix D. v1.1 principal-engineer review: findings and resolutions

| Finding (severity) | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Replays and hashes not reproducible across build configurations (critical) | `JPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC` + precise FP for Jolt and first-party code, checked by `CheckBuildConfig.py`; DetMath on the simulation path; `determinism` CI stage; stage-by-configuration matrix (§2.2, §4.12, §9.1, §15.8) |
| Exported FeatureTest cannot pass every gate (critical) | `RunModes` on registry entries, per-mode gates plus a union check with per-mode gap fixtures; testing exports include `Assets/Tests/**` and cook replays with precompiled expectations; the replay player stays in Dist; test-mode semantics of `Debug.Break`, `Application.Quit` and `IsEditor` (§7.6, §11.4, §11.10, §14.4, §15.6) |
| Test-script model undefined (critical) | `Test.Suite`/`Test.Case`, `Testing.Suites` bound to scenes or an empty scene, sequential threaded cases with timeouts, scene restart between suites, one result schema, filter semantics (§11.10) |
| Load-time VM lacks `require` and standard libraries | pure standard libraries + load-time `require` with a shared budget, require edges in the dependency graph, Module/Behaviour/TestSuite kinds, `SCRIPT_NOT_A_BEHAVIOUR` (§11.2, §7.5) |
| Yield across the C-call boundary | explicit yield rule with `lua_isyieldable` check and documented error; task and case bodies are threads (§11.3) |
| Class pattern fails strict mode | `local T = {}` … `return Script.Define(name, T)` with `Define<T>`; `GetScript(): any` + cast idiom; nil-guarded example; fixtures (§11.2, §11.9) |
| No map or dynamic `FieldType` | `FieldType::Map` and `Variant` with runtime schema resolvers; three named users (§5.4) |
| Replay recording semantics undefined | tick-0 recording, capture of all applied input, scene handle + parameters + version in the header, autopilot suite workflow, re-recording procedure (§6.7, §13.6) |
| `entity.bounds` check script not implementable | `Entity:GetWorldBounds`, `Physics.GetBodyBounds`/`GetColliderBounds`; main-path raycast support check in the Rolling Ball suite (§9.5, §11.5, §13.11) |
| Seams between implicit static bodies | shared Static body per level root, `EnhancedInternalEdgeRemoval`, `PHYSICS_ADJACENT_STATIC_BODIES`, collider identity in contacts, Sensor–Static/Sensor–Sensor filtered (§5.3, §9.2, §9.4) |
| Interpolation incomplete | per-step snapshot of every entity, frame-phase and teleport resets, `RenderPosition`/`RenderRotation`, `Time.GetInterpolationAlpha` (§5.2, §5.7) |
| Variable-rate frames never tested end to end | `ScriptedClock` and the `Timing` suite in all three modes (§4.2, §15.5) |
| Orthographic GTAO and shadows | projection-aware reconstruction, ortho GTAO radius, generic-corner cascade fit, CPU tests, `GtaoOrtho`/`ShadowsOrtho` goldens (§8.3, §8.7, §8.8) |
| Two editors on one project; orphaned lockstep | `Library/Editor.lock`, attach-instead-of-spawn, `editor_attach`, `--read-only`, disconnect cancels and releases (§4.13, §13.2, §13.8) |
| Provenance audit not reproducible | committed `Automation/Provenance.json`, `project.upgrade`, always-on transcript, re-recording procedure (§13.4, §13.8, §13.12) |
| Vulkan failure surfaces | `VkResult`-based swapchain, frame-boundary catch, bounded waits instead of `waitEventQuery`, null-checked creation, device fault data, fault injection, minimized throttle (§4.2, §4.6, §8.1, §8.14). Correction to the finding: NVRHI already catches `vk::DeviceLostError` inside `Queue::submit` and reports it through the message callback; the engine handles that path too |
| Script or automation values crash Jolt | finite-only values, `FieldMeta` minimums, `ShapeSettings::Create` results, new physics validation codes, entity cap, play-session fuzz (§5.3, §5.4, §9.1, §15.2) |
| Duplicate IDs on load assert | structural pre-validation with located results, `UnsupportedVersion`, repair loading, fixtures (§6) |
| Hot-reload races | no-echo writes, generation-checked jobs, `SceneChangedOnDisk`, deferral in deterministic sessions, module patching with dependents (§7.5, §11.8) |
| Audio device loss cannot keep voices | device-less `ma_engine` + engine-owned `ma_device`, simulation-time audio in lockstep, Null-backend tests (§10.1, §10.4) |
| glTF external files and texture duplication | dependency closure, dependency metas, URI rejection, UV1/colour diagnostics (§6.4, §7.4, §13.2) |
| Methods/properties not registered or gated | `ScriptApiRegistry::Type(...)` with methods, properties, operators, constructors; `Bindings/Script.cpp`; shortcut rule (§11.4) |
| Feature-level coverage not enforced | gates 1b, 8, 9 and per-value enum counters (§15.6) |
| Test module cannot observe what scenes promise | `GetScriptErrors`, `ExpectScriptError`, `CaptureAudio`, `ReloadScript`, `GetStateHash`; no-threading resource manager; per-suite overrides; runtime-only `Errors.scene` (§10.1, §11.5, §15.5) |
| Startup order contradictions | process-level vs per-context initialization; windowed GPU tests in a child process (§4.1) |
| Engine.pak HDRIs need a GPU | engine cooked cache, `--bake-engine-assets`, `Unsupported` under `--renderer none` without a bake, target-config SPIR-V (§7.5, §7.6, §14.2) |
| `dryRun` writes real files | `supportsDryRun`, `OverlayMount`, no provenance for dry runs (§13.4) |
| Storage image formats unchecked | `shaderStorageImageExtendedFormats` + per-format checks, Bloom fallback, `[vk::image_format]`, synchronization validation (§8.1, §8.4, §15.3) |
| Module placement ambiguities | `EditorAssetManager` in AssetPipeline, `IScriptDiagnosticsProvider`, explicit layer-5 DAG, NVRHI-free snapshot headers (§3) |
| Consistency items | world-transform rw rules, `PrefabEntityID` key, two scene/prefab importers, `Lint.py` CheckIncludes step, missing codes, budget precedence, `.jsonl` exemption, single open scene, manifest path, push constants in set 0, `imgui.ini` under `user://`, generated blue noise and icons, `StartScene`/`BuildScenes` in the walkthrough, case-insensitive automation enums |
| Automation ergonomics | compact MCP schemas, generated `.mcp.json`, `stateHash` in results, launcher state, headless throttle, selective fixes, `scene.open` dirty handling, 50 ms step budget (§13) |
| Exit semantics and CharacterVirtual | synthesized exits at flushes; inner body + `CharacterContactListener` (§9.4, §9.6) |
| Memory cap and nested deadlines | soft limit with headroom, second breach stops the session, nested callbacks inherit the deadline (§11.1) |
| PreStep teleport lag | `TransformSystem::Update` before `PreStep` (§5.7, §9.3) |
| Exported game naming and resources | user data from manifest `Name`, resource patching, `Export.Icon/Version/Company`, macOS rpath (§4.4, §14) |
| Vulkan 1.4 used only as `apiVersion` | gated host-image-copy upload path with dual-cap tests (§8.1) |
| Input and audio details | up-positive stick Y + `Invert`, replay events reuse the automation event set, `PlayOneShot` defaults (§4.3, §6.7, §10.2) |
